In Honduras, where one in five people already face some level of food insecurity in a normal year, the government has paid a Mexican company $750,000 for 20 flights to trigger rainfall. Meteorologists have routinely cast doubt on cloud seeding, saying weather modification is no solution to long-term drought. Some religious rural farmers see it as trying to play God with the weather.

“This is an experiment,” said Nabil Kawas, a meteorologist and former dean of sciences at the National Autonomous University of Honduras. “Now if you ask me whether I would have taken that $750,000 and invested it in an irrigation project or water reservoir … it would likely have a greater benefit to poor farmers who use the water for their crops.”

José Francisco Ordóñez, a spokesman for the Honduran Secretary of Agriculture, defends the flights as one of a number of climate mitigation projects being carried out by the government and international aid groups. Others include fortifying existing irrigation systems, building water reservoirs, and distributing food aid, fertilizer and seeds to farmers hit the hardest.

Ordóñez said the cloud seeding program has taken advantage of recent clouds and rainfall briefly breaking up the painfully dry season to make the most of the water before the drought stretches on.

He said the flights have boosted rainfall between 20% and 60% in key areas, compared to projected rainfall, and they hope to extend it. Kawas said a previous cloud seeding program in Honduras during comparable droughts boosted rain by less than 10%.

Subsistence farmers say they need wells to adapt

Carlos Alberto Hernández spends most of his days wondering if he and his wife will go hungry.

They have long lived off their small patch of bean crops in Nueva Concepcion, and like most people in the Dry Corridor, the 81-year-old farmer has never been able to afford an irrigation system, so they depend on the skies to yield their two yearly harvests.

As Honduran authorities issued a series of drought alerts this summer, he watched his first crop of the year die.

“We can’t afford to buy food. What we grow, that’s what we live off,” Hernández said. “Without water, we’re left with nothing.”

Ordóñez estimated that farmers like Hernández have lost 80% to 90% of their crops during this year’s drought.

Hernández, who joined hundreds at the WFP site, said he’s spent many nights with an empty stomach, preferring to save what food he had for the next day. Thursday’s food shipment, funded by WFP and coordinated with Honduras’ government, was the first such aid the community had received.

But Hernández dismissed the cloud seeding, saying what he and his neighbors need is help digging wells, so they can survive with or without the rain.

The drought’s effects are felt across Central America

In an attempt to fend off a deeper crisis, Salvadoran authorities declared a six-month state of emergency. Guatemala approved emergency measures to mitigate hunger in poorer indigenous communities, including importing staple grains without tariffs.

As for Nicaragua, where the government tightly controls information, the exiled opposition has criticized the lack of an emergency declaration or contingency plan. Nicaragua’s government did not respond to a request for comment.

The recent rainfall, which was expected before the cloud seeding began, has given farmers some hope. Hernández has planted bean seedlings. If more rain falls, they could provide him with steady food by December.

But the World Meteorological Organization now projects that El Niño will persist until February, and the U.S. National Weather Service predicted it will strengthen and likely break records. For the Dry Corridor, this likely means what little rain they usually get will fall elsewhere, feeding everything from floods to hurricanes in other regions.

In Nueva Concepcion, another crop failure would be a second blow in a year when families already sold whatever they could to buy food, and have few resources to recover, Zúñiga said.

Hernández keeps a close watch on his small patch of bean sprouts, peeking out from soil that had been cracked and dry.

“You go to bed at night, and you wake up in the morning praying to God that he sends water,” Hernández said.

——

Moises Castillo in Nueva Concepcion, Marlon González in Tegucigalpa, Honduras, Sonia Pérez D. in Guatemala City, and Marcos Alemán in San Salvador contributed to this report.

News.title: A chemical tank explodes in Ohio, forcing evacuations and prompting fears of another blast
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A chemical tank explosion in Toledo, Ohio, forced hundreds of residents to evacuate their homes or shelter in place Wednesday due to fears of a toxic release and the possibility of another explosion.

Video showed a plume billowing from the tank Wednesday morning, hours after the leak first erupted Tuesday night.

Some residents felt irritation in their eyes and throats, and one sheriff's deputy who responded to the blast drove himself to a hospital because he felt unwell, city officials said.

MC Tank Transport said the tank contained glycidyl methacrylate, which it described as “an industrial chemical used to make certain plastics, paints and coatings perform better.”

The leaking tank was in a largely industrial area. Nearly 1,000 residents were told to evacuate overnight within a 1-mile (1.6-kilometer) radius of the explosion, Mayor Wade Kapszukiewicz said at a news conference Wednesday morning.

A shelter-in-place zone order covering a 3-mile (4.8-kilometer) radius included neighborhoods along the Lake Erie shoreline and stretched just across the state line into Michigan.

Health officials said the chemical was mostly an irritant so far, causing watery eyes, and that tests were ongoing to determine how much toxicity was in the air.

Kristine Kowalinski, who lives just outside the impacted area, said she was staying inside because she’s sensitive to even wood burning outside. She said she’s worried about what’s in the air and on the ground.

“My main concern is how did that affect everything overnight when it was raining down on cars, houses, my garden,” she said.

Kapszukiewicz said the chemical is liquid inside the tank but becomes a gas when released.

“There is still concern that the tank is emitting this chemical and it has the potential within 12 hours of the incident to be explosive,” the mayor said, adding that it can hold 5,500 gallons of the chemical in liquid form. He said officials don’t know what caused the explosion.

People who come into contact with glycidyl methacrylate may feel as if their eyes, nose, mouth and skin are burning, the city fire department said. Overexposure can lead to headache, dizziness, tiredness, nausea and vomiting.

“It’s really toxic if you touch it, if you ingest it,” said Karim Baroudi, director of the Toledo-Lucas County Health Department. “Now we’re trying to kind of determine how much of a toxicity is in the air that the people are breathing so we can give better guidance.”

Baroudi advised residents to close their windows and that those who “feel irritation in the eyes, heavily breathing, just take a shower for now.” The fire department said those who experience symptoms should contact a medical professional.

First responders, hazmat and safety teams are not approaching the tank because of the risk of more explosions, and will reassess conditions later Wednesday morning, Kapszukiewicz said.

Arkansas-based MC Tank Transport said in a statement the company is working with the fire department and other emergency authorities. Company representatives were on their way to Toledo, Kapszukiewicz said.

“Our immediate and overriding concern is the safety of area residents, emergency responders and our employees,” it said. “Our immediate and overriding concern is the safety of area residents, emergency responders and our employees.”

___

McCormack reported from Concord, New Hampshire. Associated Press writer Dave Collins in Hartford, Connecticut, contributed.

News.title: Ebola case confirmed in Nigeria as outbreak spreads through Africa
News.content:
African ministers have been called to an urgent health summit after Nigeria confirmed its first case in the outbreak of the deadly Ebola fever tearing through eastern Congo.

Confirmation of a case in Africa’s most populous nation came days after a cluster was detected in Kenya and has heightened questions about border screening checks designed to stop the virus spreading from its epicentre in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

With cases now found in West Africa, Central Africa and East Africa, the epidemic “has already become the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak in history,” said Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the continent’s main public health body.

DRC has recorded close to 10,000 cases since an outbreak began in mid-May, with around half of them dying of the haemorrhagic fever.

The Nigeria case meant “Ebola is now affecting three regions of Africa,” warned Dr Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention.

“The situation demands urgent action and political leadership at the highest level,” he said, convening an online summit for next week.

News.title: One billion children at risk from heatwaves, WHO warns
News.content:
More than one billion children are exposed to increasingly severe heat waves, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

1.5 billion children under one experienced a fivefold increase in the number of heat wave days in 2024 compared with the 1986 to 2005 baseline period, jumping from roughly four days per year to a high of over 20, says the health agency. And these periods of high temperature are becoming longer, more frequent and more severe, the WHO warns.

According to the Met Office, this summer was the hottest on record in the UK, with five widespread heatwaves and 40 days where the temperature was above 30 degrees celsius. Europe also saw record-breaking temperatures, and Asia and Africa both experienced their warmest July on record, according to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

Four UN agencies, including the WHO, the WMO, Unicef and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), have urged countries to monitor how extreme heat affects pregnant women, newborns and children.

The new framework tracks preterm birth, stillbirths, low birthweight, pregnancy hypertension, child deaths and health facility visits.

“Heat is already affecting our most vulnerable populations, including pregnant women, newborns and children. But what health systems do not count, they cannot respond to,” said Dr Pascale Allotey, director of WHO’s department of maternal and child health.

“By tracking outcomes such as preterm birth, child deaths and illnesses, and health-facility visits alongside heat exposure, countries can identify potential impacts and take action to protect women and children,” she said.

High temperatures are particularly dangerous for pregnant women because the body has to work much harder to cool both the mother and the baby.

Intense heat can cause surface-level blood vessels to dilate, which in pregnant women can restrict blood flow to the placenta and reduce the amount of oxygen and nutrients that reach the foetus. Heat can also put strain on the cardiovascular system, increasing the risk of gestational diabetes, dangerously high blood pressure, and pre-eclampsia.

The odds of a preterm birth also increase by 26 per cent during heatwaves: for every one degree rise in heat exposure, the likelihood of giving birth early rise by roughly 4 per cent, according to a systematic review published in Nature Medicine.

The WHO has also urged countries to develop and implement tailored heat-health action plans that account for the needs of pregnant women, newborns and children, as well as strengthening early-warning systems to ensure timely action to heat risks, such as alert systems and personalised public messaging.

“As our world continues to heat up, it creates new risks for health, and older people, pregnant women, newborns and children are among those least able to escape them,” said Bruce Gordon, director of environment and climate change at the WHO.

“Our health systems need the data to recognise this reality and take action – from protecting people during heatwaves to embedding climate risk consideration into everyday health services,” he said.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Rio Ngumoha dazzles on coming-of-age night in Europe
News.content:
Iraola made major changes at half-time, substituting Araújo and playing without a conventional right-back for the second half. It was brave and changed the momentum of the game, pushing his team higher up the pitch in what looked like a man-to-man marking arrangement. It enabled Iraola’s players to deny Villarreal the space and possession they had enjoyed in the first half when they had taken a two-goal lead – chiefly because of the mistakes of the home team. However much that was destabilising for Liverpool, by half-time they were level.

“They are so good on the ball,” Iraola said of Villarreal afterwards. Indeed, Villarreal’s manager Iñigo Pérez, a former Athletic team-mate of the Liverpool manager, was a coach whom Iraola sought to appoint at Bournemouth. “People probably don’t rate them [Villarreal],” Iraola said, “but after Barça they are probably the best in La Liga. They have 61 per cent of possession. Probably they have not had the results they deserve. If you are not really aggressive, you are not going to get the ball.

“We didn’t take as much risk. We were struggling because it is not a team that you can just press a bit. Either you go all the way or you will struggle without the ball.” Once Liverpool had done so, he said, his team had “won a lot of duels”. He was right in that respect. With the space squeezed, it was the power of Liverpool’s midfield that was telling.

Virgil van Dijk gave the first goal to Villarreal’s small No 9 Georges Mikautadze who had looked up to that point like he was hopelessly mismatched against the Liverpool captain and Jérémy Jacquet. Van Dijk’s misjudged header back to Alisson let in the striker, who did well to gather the ball and then hit it early. The second Villarreal goal at the midpoint of the first half was a mistake from Kostas Tsimikas, who failed to step up and played both Mikautadze and Cardona onside from Nathan Saliba’s ball. Either might have tucked it in but it was the left-back Cardona who took it on.

News.title: Inflation jumps in run-up to Healey’s maiden Budget
News.content:
Inflation has jumped to its highest level in almost a year, underlining the challenges facing John Healey, the Chancellor, ahead of his first Budget next week.

The consumer prices index climbed from 3.1pc in August to 3.5pc in September, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS).

Inflation was ahead of the 3.4pc predicted by economists and is now at its highest level since October 2025.

The sharp rise was driven by soaring fuel costs as a result of the Iran war. The ONS said average petrol prices rose by 8.2p a litre in September and diesel by 10.7p. Both reached levels not seen since 2022, in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales, said: “Rising inflation is turning the Budget into a perilous high-wire act for the Chancellor, increasing pressure for cost-of-living support while pushing up government borrowing costs, which is shrinking fiscal headroom and narrowing his policy options.”

Britain spent more money on debt interest last month than in any September on record, official figures show.

The UK’s debt servicing costs rose to £10.9bn in September, the highest total for the month since at least 1997, according to the ONS.

This burden helped to push national debt above £3 trillion for the first time.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, said the unhappy milestone and the rise in inflation “show Labour has lost control of the economy”.

Public sector net debt has soared by 50pc since it first exceeded £2tn in June 2020.

Mr Healey insisted the British economy still had “momentum” and pointed to Wednesday morning’s approval of new drilling for gas in the North Sea as evidence of this.

He said: “We know that price rises from conflicts in the Middle East and Europe are hitting Britain and countries worldwide. Last week, the IMF said our UK fiscal discipline stands out with the lowest forecast deficit in the G7 by 2029.

“And today we’ve given the green light to getting North Sea gas from the Jackdaw field, investing the revenues in our clean energy future and supporting British workers.

“In my Budget next week, I will keep up this momentum. Maintaining our fiscal discipline and drive for growth in every postcode, while giving businesses and families some breathing space.”

September’s inflation figure is used for the annual uprating of welfare payments, with the state pension now in line to rise by almost £500 next year.

The figure is also used to calculate increases in business rates in England, with pubs, shops, offices and other hospitality businesses now facing a £1.1bn increase in the collective bill from April, according to tax firm Ryan.

News.title: England dealt harsh lesson in Pakistan collapse
News.content:
Brendon McCullum wants his team to learn how to adapt as they prepare for the World Cup and this was a lesson in how not to master a run chase.

Failing to overhaul 302 is not an embarrassment, but the way England threw away a good start with some brittle batting gives McCullum plenty to ponder.

Spin exposed familiar failings as left-armer Arafat Minhas added six for 40 to his 59 from 58 with the bat, but it was also short balls from the seamers that hurt England. A two-paced pitch made the back-of-a-length delivery tricky, as it had in the match between Sri Lanka and Pakistan on the same ground at the weekend, but England failed to find a way to adjust their tempo.

Ben Duckett, Joe Root and Sam Curran were all dismissed by seamers hitting the pitch hard and forcing them to play square while Arafat exposed limitations against spin. He bowled Harry Brook for five with a beauty that dipped and straightened as he mixed up his arm ball with consistent accuracy to deadly effect.

News.title: Fried chicken and sugary drinks: Tanzania battles a growing obesity problem
News.content:
In early 2025, Said Shukuru, 31, was experiencing life-threatening health concerns. He weighed 150 kg (over 20 stone); his body mass index (BMI) was over 40 and he had a blood pressure of 190/100.

“It was very serious,” says Shukuru. In April last year, he underwent a successful mini gastric bypass operation at the Aga Khan Specialised Polyclinic in Masaki, Dar Es Salaam. His weight has since halved.

Shukuru’s case may be extreme, but his story serves as a warning. Overweight and obesity levels are increasing fast across East Africa, and particularly in Tanzania. Unless the government responds properly, the country faces a looming public health crisis.

Overweight and obesity in Tanzania have grown over the past 40 years because of economic development and liberalisation, urbanisation and increasingly sedentary lifestyles. Traditional diets, based on whole foods, are being replaced by refined and processed products. To make matters worse, chicken and chips, known as kuku chips, and sugary drinks are everywhere.

“When you live in an urban area like Dar (Es Salaam),” says Shukuru, “junk food is cheaper than groceries.”

The origins of these developments lie in Tanzania’s economic history. During the colonial period, fruits and legumes were exported while high-energy, starchy foods like maize were produced for domestic consumption, says Joyce Kinabo, professor of nutrition at Sokoine University.

“Food security was considered as having a lot of maize,” says Kinabo.

News.title: US warns over travel in Kenya as Ebola cases mount
News.content:
The United States has urged citizens to reconsider travel to Kenya, raising its travel alert level after the country reported an eighth case of Ebola.

The East African nation has recorded a rash of cases linked to a Kenyan businessman who died after travelling from Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

DRC is currently enduring the second worst Ebola outbreak on record with more than 4,000 deaths since May, though the true toll is thought to be far higher.

“The level was changed from Level 2 to Level 3 due to health risks,” the US embassy in Kenya said, a day after the State Department issued renewed travel advice for its citizens.

“Reconsider travel in Kenya due to risk of health, crime, kidnapping, terrorism, unrest and traffic safety. Some areas have increased risk,” it said.

The alert came as Kenyan doctors leaders demanded better protective equipment against the highly infectious virus.

Three of the confirmed Ebola cases are reported to be health staff who cared for the businessman and the others are thought to be relatives who visited him.

News.title: US records first human case of H5N1 this year
News.content:
A man in Washington has tested positive for H5N1, marking the first human case of bird flu in the US this year.

The patient, who works on a dairy farm, was reportedly infected after being exposed to two infected cows.

H5N1 has become endemic on US dairy farms after ‘spilling over’ from birds in 2024, and has since infected more than 1,000 herds across dozens of states.

The person is not seriously ill and is isolating at home, according to the Washington State Department of Health.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 mutates and gains the ability to spread person-to-person, it could trigger the next global pandemic – and each new infection gives the virus more opportunities to replicate and change.

Last week, a 50-year-old man in Taiwan was infected with a different strain of bird flu, H7N7, genetic analysis of which showed the virus had undergone adaptations to spread more effectively between mammals.

Of the more than 1,000 people who have contracted H5N1 since it was first detected in the late 1990s, almost half have died.

Its “extraordinarily high” mortality rate means that, were it to gain the ability to spread between people, it would be of “enormous concern”, the World Health Organization (WHO) previously warned.

However, the strain circulating among US dairy cattle, clade 2.3.4.4b, has proven less lethal to humans.

Sports.title: Inside football’s most glam couple Diletta Leotta and Loris Karius’ lavish life with yacht trips and luxury holidays

DAZN queen Diletta Leotta has her king in husband Loris Karius.

The pair, who began dating in 2022 after meeting at Paris Fashion Week, are football’s most glam couple.



Not only are they blessed with good looks, they’ve been successful in their careers.

Delightful Leotta, 35, has established herself as the face of Italian football.



While, Karius, 33, is Bundesliga side Schalke’s No1, following stints at Liverpool and Newcastle.



Away from the pitch, they live a blessed life. They are parents to daughter Aria, born in 2023, and a son named Leonardo, who arrived this year.

Their jet-set lifestyle includes attending fashions shows, hiring luxury yachts and going on fancy holidays.

SunSport takes a peek at how the glamour couple live.

Sicilian wedding

Two years after they began dating, Leotta and Karius had a stunning wedding.



They tied the knot off the coast of Sicily at the five-star Therasia Resort, with 160 guests said to be present for the star-studded occasion.

Karius was seen wearing a white tuxedo and black bow tie and trousers combo while Leotta walked down the aisle in a beautiful white dress.



Leotta was given away by her father to the tune of John Legend‘s All of Me.

They exchanged vows in front of the Tyrrhenian Sea alongside their daughter Aria.

As the joyous day went into the night, Karius switched to a green suit as they cut a huge cake before sharing a kiss in front of a fireworks display.

The lavish occasion was the start of things to come.

Amazing holidays

Over the years, Leotta and Karius have proven to be global travellers – with no expense spared.



They have shared their holiday experiences on Instagram, showing the epic existences they lead.

Last summer, the pair enjoyed two Spanish getaways.

First, they went to Mallorca, where they hired a boat with pals and sunned themselves on deck.

They then went to Ibiza, again renting a luxury yacht, with Karius and Leotta entertaining a group of friends.



Not content with summer holidays, they also seemingly embrace winter with trips to the slopes.



Back in March, before Diletta gave birth to their son Leonardo, they rented a chalet in the millionaire’s alpine playground of St. Moritz.

They took walks on the snowy mountains, ate hearty meals, and enjoyed the incredible scenery with daughter, Aria.

Fashion shows

Being one of football’s most glamorous couples means you have to keep up appearances.

So, when it’s fashion week in Milan, you will see Karius and Diletta arm-in-arm in the front row watching a show.

They met at Paris Fashion Week in 2022, which Leotta described as “love at first sight”.



Since then, they’ve been spied together taking in major showcases like the Roberto Cavalli show during Milan Fashion Week.

Handsome Karius has even transcended football by becoming a model himself.

Back in 2024, he walked the catwalk for Hugo Boss at MFW, showcasing the brand’s Spring/Summer 2025 Ready-to-Wear collection.



Karius also partners with Longines, regularly promoting their timepieces on social media.

Managing a long-distance relationship

Rather than letting their careers hold them back, Karius and Leotta have managed to maintain their cross-border marriage and family life.

Leotta lives primarily in Milan, while Karius is based in Gelsenkirchen.

The couple frequently fly between Italy and Germany to spend time together, with Leotta sharing snaps of her relaxing in the quiet German countryside during Serie A breaks.



They view the distance as a positive that helps them “preserve their own spaces” until they eventually live under one roof.

Last year, Karius spoke about the difficulties of living miles apart from each other.

But, he revealed it’s something that Diletta is on board with and understands because of his football path.

He told Sport Bild: “Diletta even advised me to extend at Schalke.

“She thinks the club is great and she likes everything she has seen here so far.



“Diletta also thinks that royal blue is the perfect choice for my sporting success. She is fully behind this decision.”

However, Karius admitted it was tough not seeing his daughter every day and has to rely on FaceTime to talk with her.

“But that’s what FaceTime is for and we see each other regularly – as often as possible.”

LISANDRO MARTINEZ could be heading for the Manchester United exit door this summer as the club prepare for a major defensive overhaul.

The Argentine World Cup winner, 28, faces an uncertain future at Old Trafford according to a report in the Mail.



And his potential departure comes just days after he landed himself in hot water with United bosses over a controversial outburst about the club’s transfer policy.

Martinez publicly questioned United’s summer recruitment following their 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid last week.



The defender admitted he had expected more from director of football Jason Wilcox.

His comments did not go down well with the club’s hierarchy, who subsequently handed him a fine.



Martinez later apologised for the timing of his remarks and insisted everyone at United was working towards the same goal.

He said: “Everyone at the club is doing everything they can to make the team successful.”

However, reports suggest his potential departure is not linked to the controversial comments.

Instead, United are preparing to reshape their defence ahead of next season, with Martinez among those whose futures remain unresolved.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The former Ajax star joined United for £57million in 2022 and has been a regular on the left side of central defence when fit.

But injuries have severely disrupted his time in Manchester, keeping him sidelined for a combined 20 months.

Martinez suffered another setback during Sunday’s 1-1 draw with Leeds at Elland Road.

He was forced off at half-time with a thigh problem, raising fresh concerns over his fitness.

The Argentina international’s contract expires at the end of June and he is reportedly unlikely to agree a new deal.



However, United are reluctant to lose him for nothing and could activate a 12-month extension before attempting to sell him in the summer.

The Red Devils are also weighing up a fresh move for Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite.

United previously had two bids worth up to £50million rejected by the Toffees in 2024.



And the England international could return to their transfer shortlist as they look to strengthen their backline.

Meanwhile, uncertainty also surrounds the futures of Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw.

Shaw is approaching the end of his contract after 12 years at Old Trafford and does not have an option to extend his deal.

Maguire, however, has a 12-month extension clause in the one-year contract he signed in April.

United must decide whether to retain the experienced England duo or continue their defensive rebuild.



There are no such concerns over Matthijs de Ligt despite his lengthy absence through injury.

The Dutch defender has been sidelined for almost a year after undergoing surgery on a back problem.

He also forbade singing in the showers, thinking it “disrupts concentration levels”.



Presumably none of the Black Cats had time to offer a rendition of Ice Ice Baby after he was sacked five league games into the season.

POKE-NO GO

Jose Mourinho reportedly banned Manchester United players from playing Pokemon Go for the 48 hours before matches in 2016.

Ahead of their pre-season trip to China, the now-Real Madrid boss insisted that his stars focus solely on tactics.



It was claimed at the time: “He’s still finding his way around Old Trafford and treading carefully.

John Toshack’s menu at the Wales camp did not go down too well with Robbie Savage in 2004.

Writing in his autobiography, Savage ripped into his former boss after being refused gravy with his chicken dinner.

He recalled crawling under the table as he jokingly searched for sauces.



Savage wrote: “The waitress came in to take our order. Plain chicken, no sauce. Or spaghetti ­bolognese. Fried bananas or rice and ­broccoli.”

Toshack’s sympathy didn’t stretch far – only telling his midfielder that he should have used bolognese sauce.

SPACE JAM

In 1999, Stefan Schwarz had a clause in his Sunderland contract outlawing space tourism.



After dropping a hint that he was up for a trip in a rocket, the midfielder was forced to sign a deal that would be ripped up if he travelled out of the atmosphere.

Alexander Zorniger banned his Stuttgart players from wearing headphones in public in 2015.

He argued that a pair of oversized headphones looked absolutely ridiculous on the smaller stars.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic did exactly what everyone would have expected him to do when Pep Guardiola banned sports cars at Barcelona training.

STAR-CROSSED ENEMIES

SNOOD AWAKENING

Sean Dyche placed a ban on hats and snoods at training after arriving at Nottingham Forest in 2025.

But he did allow white socks, joking that his former players would give him grief for the concession.



THAT’S CAP

Fabio Capello is the most notorious condiment hater of them all.

He wasted no time removing all brown sauce, ketchup, and butter from the menu when he took the England job in 2007.

And before kick-off, a giant banner was held up by the home fans showing the Barcelona badge being destroyed by a chainsaw-wielding masked figure in a PSG shirt.

A Barcelona spokesman told Reuters they had reported the tifo to a Uefa match delegate after full time.

Uefa rules state “the use of gestures, words, objects or any other means to transmit a provocative message that is not fit for a sports event” may result in sanctions.

Clubs can be fined up to £8,300 for a first offence.

And it didn’t take long for him to leave his mark on the match.

The 17-year-old picked up the ball on the edge of Saints’ defensive third and drove towards the edge of the box.

The fuming fans then began to loudly boo the teenager, who did not seem to notice.

The stunning long-range finish drew comparisons among Juve fans to his father.

His boy’s strike against Southampton came from almost the exact same spot – though Marchisio Sr’s effort was a sneaky low drive across goal rather than a rocket into the top corner.

United were beaten 1-0 in the Manchester Derby by their bitter rivals in September after Haaland's winner was not chalked off. Enzo Fernandez was offside and interfering with play, but his involvement was not spotted by VAR Matt Donohue and his assistant Blake Antrobus.

‌



The incident was a huge blunder for Pro Ref, who were forced to apologise to United on two separate occasions. Donohue has not worked on Premier League matches since the game on September 13 but has now been reinstated for this weekend's round of fixtures.

‌



He will be the assistant VAR for Saturday’s match between Coventry and Fulham. Antrobus has already made his comeback as assistant referee for Aston Villa's 1-0 win over Newcastle on Saturday.

‌



Pro Ref chief Howard Webb later admitted that Donohue had got "tunnel vision" which meant he only focused on Haaland and not Fernandez's position. The high-profile mistake was a serious dent in the confidence of Pro Ref and their officials this season.

Appearing on Match Officials Mic'd Up last month, Webb admitted: "We felt it was important that we acknowledged an error in this situation. We know that Erling Haaland, who was penalised on field for offside, wasn't in an offside position.

‌



"But we also know that Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, almost certainly interfered with the Manchester United defence and probably the goalkeeper as well.

View 2 Images Matt Donohue will return as a VAR this weekend (Image: Tiego Grenho/Getty Images)

‌



"I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are. None more so than the officials themselves. They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they're obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation. They'll not be officiating again until after the international break. We've reached out to Manchester United and acknowledged the error, as we do when these things happen.

"They don't happen that often, but we want to ensure that we are transparent and open, and we've played the audio and the footage to the football club to let them know what happened, and we're going to review this situation to understand what elements of process fell down in this situation which meant we didn't get to the right outcome."

‌



While he has been absent from Premier League officiating for the last three match weeks, Donohue has been working in the Championship. He was referee for the 0-0 draw between Southampton and Bolton last Saturday and the 1-1 draw between Derby and Wrexham game on October 10.

Although he has only officiated five times in the Premier League, Donohue is an experienced referee with 190 Championship games under his belt.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino issued public apology as statement on FIFA president's salary claims made
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino issued public apology as statement on FIFA president's salary claims made

FIFA President Gianni Infantino has received a public apology as he continues to come under scrutiny from UEFA and other critics

View 2 Images FIFA released a statement after Gianni Infantino was offered an apology (Image: Robertus Pudyanto - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

FIFA have reaffirmed its belief that there is a concerted effort to undermine President Gianni Infantino, after an apology was issued over claims the world governing body boss was drawing a second salary. The governing body of world football criticised the 'damaging report'.

‌



‌



Infantino has come under increased scrutiny after his proposal to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors. The Swiss football politician has so far withstood a number of calls to stand down from his position ahead of the presidential election next year.

‌



Earlier this week UEFA called upon FIFA to release key documents, setting a deadline of November 2. In a letter, the European governing body asked 42 questions covering issues such as the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) private investment, the FIFA Peace Prize and the decision to suspend US star Folarin Balogun's ban at the World Cup.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

However, accusations that Infantino drew a second salary have proven to be unfounded, with the Times offering an apology for a number of the claims.

The Times said: "On 13 October 2026 (Sport), we reported that Gianni Infantino received a “second salary” from FIFA, which FIFA had failed to disclose. This is incorrect.

‌



"There was no “second salary”. Regulations do not require FIFA to include expenses and reimbursements received by Mr Infantino in its annual report as they are not considered “compensation” under Swiss reporting requirements.

"We also accept Mr Infantino did not purchase a property in Miami at a suspected undervalue as we reported and neither he nor his family are the legal or beneficial owners of Shadi LLC and have no control over that company, as we suggested. We are happy to make these corrections and apologise to Mr Infantino and FIFA for the errors."

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has come under pressure following shelved plans to sell shares of the World Cup. (Image: Omar Marques/Getty Images)

‌



FIFA highlighted the apology made by the Times and set out their stall to 'vigorously' challenge inaccurate reporting.

"FIFA takes note of an apology published by The Times following an inaccurate and damaging report," they said.

‌



"As FIFA stated in August, it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President. FIFA urges the media to act responsibly and carefully verify all sourcing to prevent the publication and subsequent reproduction of false and defamatory information.

"FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a license to amplify false allegations. Where reporting is inaccurate, misleading, or totally false, as in this case, FIFA will continue to challenge it directly and vigorously."

‌



Infantino is standing for re-election as FIFA president, with a deadline of November 18 for a rival candidate to make themselves known. Former Arsenal boss Arsene Wenger has been touted in some corners as a unity candidate.

Sports.title: Four issues Man Utd boss Michael Carrick must overcome against Como after 'toxic culture' claim
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is facing one of the biggest games of his Manchester United tenure on Wednesday night. If the rain allows the match to go ahead, then he simply must deliver a win.

United have won just two of their 10 games across all competitions this season and arrive in northern Italy on a six-game winless run. It should also be noted that their last victory came against Champions League debutants Sabah, while their first of the campaign was against newly-promoted Ipswich.

After landing the job on the strength of his stint as interim boss, Carrick is rapidly running out of the goodwill he had banked last season. On Wednesday he will be faced with Cesc Fabregas - a familiar opponent from his playing days. This time he will need to beat him as a manager in order to quiet the speculation swirling in stormy Como.

As he's already learned this season, that won't be a straightforward task. Here are the biggest issues at United that Carrick must overcome, starting now.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Injury crisis

The most obvious problem is availability. Carrick is without NINE first-team stars for the Como game: Lisandro Martinez, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Ayden Heaven and Marcus Rashford have joined long-term absentees Patrick Dorgu, Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte on the injury list, while Leny Yoro is suspended after being sent off in the 2-0 defeat against Atletico Madrid last week.

Most of the aforementioned players would be in Carrick's first-choice starting XI. The injury crisis has struck at the worst possible time and forced Carrick to tread carefully when asked in his pre-match press conference about United's failure to sign a left-back in the summer transfer window.

‌



"I think when we have injuries, you can always look at what could have been done and what we could have improved," he said diplomatically, no doubt acutely aware of being seen to echo Martinez's fiery criticism of the United hierarchy from last week.

View 4 Images Lisandro Martinez is unavailable after his explosive interview last week (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Injuries mean Carrick has little option but to throw Matthijs de Ligt into the fray immediately after returning from an 11-month absence due to a back problem. It is a nightmare situation for a defence that has been struggling enough, even when more players were available.

Leaky defence

United's only clean sheet this season came against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah. They have shipped 15 goals in 10 games in total and have been completely unable to shut up shop.

‌



"There's definitely parts of our game that we have to improve to make things easier, fully aware of that," Carrick said on Tuesday when asked about the issue. It's one thing being aware of it - how can you not be - it's another entirely to address it.

United did not sign a single defender in the summer, preferring to splash £155million on central midfielders. The result is a stale backline, with Shaw and Harry Maguire, in particular, appearing to be long past their best.

Harry Amass - a player United were open to loaning in the summer - could come in at left-back, with Shaw and Dorgu out, while Noussair Mazraoui's experience could be crucial alongside Maguire against Como, who have been in good goalscoring form this season, netting four against RB Leipzig and two against Feyenoord in the Champions League.

View 4 Images Manchester United's leaky defence has cost them points (Image: Getty Images)

‌



'Toxic culture'

Carrick could have done without ex-United boss Erik ten Hag giving his first interview since his sacking two years ago this week. The Dutchman had plenty to say, including accusing the club's hierarchy of fuelling a "toxic culture" inside the dressing room by giving players like Cristiano Ronaldo, Casemiro and Raphael Varane too much influence.

Carrick rejected those claims, stressing the "togetherness" and "determination" of his players. But the fact Martinez felt compelled to call out United director of football Jason Wilcox after the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid last week suggests Ten Hag may have a point.

United could really do with the sort of stand-out individual performance Bruno Fernandes has previously made a habit of tonight. The United skipper has four goals and one assist in 10 games this season, but all of those came in their two wins against Sabah and Ipswich.

View 4 Images Bruno Fernandes' form is becoming an issue for Michael Carrick (Image: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock)

‌



Midfield balance

United spent all their cash this summer to bring in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba and are yet to see the benefit. The balance in midfield was a constant problem last season, with Ruben Amorim unwilling to field Mainoo alongside Casemiro and Fernandes, and Carrick is yet to find the solution.

Carrick has fielded his three new midfielders together in the past two games, but it's yet to click. With Mainoo injured, Tielemans has been handed a more forward-thinking role, with Baleba and Santos sitting in front of the defence. It is a combination that will no doubt need time to settle. But, unfortunately for Carrick, time is not a luxury he currently has.

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag identifies the off-pitch area Man Utd lag behind rivals with INEOS dig
Sports.content:
Erik ten Hag identifies the off-pitch area Man Utd lag behind rivals with INEOS dig

Former Manchester United boss Erik ten Hag has taken a pointed dig at INEOS after claiming he offered them advice on how to improve the club's data department

View 2 Images Former Manchester United head coach Erik ten Hag (Image: Getty Images)

Former Manchester United head coach Erik ten Hag has taken another swipe at INEOS and revealed he offered them advice on improving their data department, only to be rejected - claiming that they believed 'they knew everything already'.

‌



‌



Ten Hag, who took charge of United in May 2022, was dismissed by INEOS bosses in November 2024 after a disappointing start to the campaign which saw just three victories from their opening nine Premier League fixtures. The Dutchman was understood to be 'completely devastated' by United's decision to axe him, just months after lifting the FA Cup and signing a new two-year deal at Old Trafford.

‌



Yet, despite last season's third-place finish under Michael Carrick, it's fair to say United have shown little improvement since Ten Hag's departure and INEOS' arrival at the club in February 2024. Sir Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS came on board after acquiring a 27.7% stake in United, immediately taking near-complete control of men's and women's football operations, academies, and securing board positions.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

When INEOS initially made their move to United, Ten Hag provided recommendations on strengthening the club's data operation, as he sought to attract superior talent to the Reds. However, speaking to The Athletic, the current FC Twente director has disclosed that INEOS turned down his proposal.

‌



"Data changed the whole world, and now it's coming, AI, and every organisation has to take this on board," Ten Hag said. "I think United miss some aspects. The moment I came in, they were starting. For instance, data was already a long time on board at Ajax.

"A manager should get, by the end, all the information. You need others in a club to collect all the information and make everything ready to make final decisions. Top organisations innovate continually and they're actually driving the innovations.

‌



View 2 Images Erik ten Hag during his time at Manchester United (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"I offered my knowledge and abilities to INEOS to help them to construct, but they were of the opinion that they knew already everything. They were convinced of, say, the philosophy, the strategy, the work methods. But they came from petrochemicals, from Formula 1, from cycling. Top football demands something totally different."

‌



Ten Hag added: "Seven points where I judge the player. Technical ability, for me, is most important. Second is game intelligence and cognition. Third, you need athleticism, then lifestyle. Determination. Resilience and robustness to play every third day. And then we want to be always offensive.

"For instance, when I came to United, we didn't have the scoring ability to be in the top four. I will not say football is mathematics, but a bit of logic is in it. For us at Twente, we need 70 goals if you want to be in fourth position. When you want to win the Premier League, you need 85, 90 goals.

Article continues below

"I use this every day, so it should not be a document in a drawer. That is winning culture, if we match what we described. We use a lot of data to see new signings match our style of play."

Sports.title: Como vs Man Utd was almost moved stadiums with clash now at risk of postponement
Sports.content:
Como vs Man Utd was almost moved stadiums with clash now at risk of postponement

Como's Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia has been hit by extreme weather ahead of Manchester United's Champions League visit

View 3 Images Como's Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia is hosting Champions League football for the first time (Image: Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Como had to make drastic changes to their stadium to avoid having to play Manchester United and their other Champions League fixtures more than 100 miles away from home. Cesc Fabregas's unfashionable side provided one of the feel-good stories of European football last season when they qualified for the Champions League ahead of the likes of Juventus and AC Milan.

‌



‌



Playing a European giant like United will be a historic moment for Como, provided Wednesday's match goes ahead as planned following intense rainfall in northern Italy. More than 6cm of rain was forecast in the 24 hours before kick-off, with an orange rain warning of "severe weather" issued by the Italian Air Force National Meteorological Service.

‌



The game could have been moved for another reason as, at the end of last season, Como's Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia didn't meet the required standard for Champions League football.

‌



If the ground wasn't updated in double-quick time, it would have meant Como playing their European games at Sassuolo's stadium, 124 miles to the south.

Cesc Fabregas already has green light for Man Utd job as he snubs Michael Carrick question READ MORE :

Man Utd's clash with Como in doubt as severe weather warning could lead to postponement READ MORE :

However, intense work has brought the stadium up to UEFA Category 4 status, with a rebuild of one of the stands and upgrades to floodlights, media facilities, toilets and security systems. The pitch was widened by two metres and relaid with new-generation hybrid grass, which aids Fabregas's fluid style of play.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



After the work was completed, Como issued a statement which said: "To meet UEFA requirements, renovation work on the stadium has been completed, including the construction of a new stand and the enhancement of infrastructure, security systems and operational facilities.

"Sinigaglia has been the home of Como 1907 for almost a century. Its role in the city and in the life of the club makes the opportunity to play these matches here particularly special.

‌



View 3 Images Heavy rain has battered the stadium (Image: @TouchlineX)

"Como 1907 would like to thank everyone who helped make this possible, as well as our fans for their patience and constant support throughout the entire process."

‌



With the overhaul completed, the issue heading into Tuesday's match is the weather. Asked if he had any concerns about the surface or even the match being impacted, United boss Michael Carrick said: "No, nothing immediate for me. We're kind of used to the rain, so we'll make the most of it."

View 3 Images Michael Carrick expects the game to go ahead as planned (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Of bigger concern to Carrick is breaking United's six-game winless run across all competitions, which has led to speculation over his future. Speaking ahead of the game, he said: "I know the role, I know my responsibilities.

"I don't need anyone else to tell me that or tell me when it's going well or when it needs to be better. I know that myself. I know the realities and I've got no problem with that. It's pretty clear."

Sports.content:
Major PSG star suffers season ending injury in huge blow to third straight Champions League win

The winger was taken off just before the hour mark in PSG's win over Barcelona

View 2 Images PSG have been handed a major Khvicha Kvaratskhelia injury blow. (Image: David Ramos - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Paris Saint-Germain have confirmed a major injury blow with key player Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffering a torn anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). The winger suffered the injury during Tuesday night’s Champions League encounter with Barcelona.

‌



‌



He appeared to twist his knee just before the hour mark. He was helped off the pitch by medical staff. PSG came out as 4-2 winners over Barcelona, thanks to goals from Desire Doue, Lucas Hernandez, Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz.

‌



It leaves them top of the Champions League League phase, having won all three of their games so far. But the injury to Kvaratskhelia will come as a big blow.

‌



Bayern Munich star Joshua Kimmich ruled out of Arsenal clash after personal tragedy READ MORE :

PSG confirmed the extent of the injury on their official website on Wednesday morning. “Having suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery in the coming days,” they wrote.

PSG suffered another double injury worry when striker Ousmane Dembélé was forced to leave the pitch in the first half, he was later joined by club captain Marquinhos. The club have confirmed that both players have suffered thigh injuries and will receive treatment over the ‘coming weeks’.

View 2 Images Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered a serious knee injury during the Champions League clash vs Barcelona. (Image: Xavier Laine/Getty Images)

‌

Giving the latest on his squad in his post-match press conference, PSG boss Luis Enrique said: "I am not the doctor. I am the coach.

‌



"The three injuries is the worst part of the game today. We will have to wait for the tests tomorrow.

“They are three very important players, so it's really bad news, of course, but that's football."

‌

Kvaratskhelia’s injury is likely to rule him out for the remainder of the season. The Georgia international has been a star of the PSG team who have won the last two Champions Leagues.

‌



He was the player who was fouled to win PSG’s equalising penalty against Arsenal in last year’s final in Budapest. He was also on the scoresheet in the team’s 5-0 win over Inter as they claimed their first Champions League in 2025.

So far this season, he has scored twice and provided one assist in 11 games in all competitions.

The French giants will now have to try to retain the title without him. They are next in European action when they travel to take on Villarreal on Tuesday, 3 November (8pm kick-off).

Sports.content:
Bayern Munich star Joshua Kimmich ruled out of Arsenal clash after personal tragedy

Bayern Munich host Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday night and will be without key player Joshua Kimmich, who is unavailable due to a death in his family

View 2 Images Joshua Kimmich has suffered a death in the family (Image: Sebastian Widmann/Bundesliga via Getty Images)

Joshua Kimmich won't play for Bayern Munich against Arsenal on Wednesday night following a death in his family.

‌



‌



Kimmich is a key player for Bayern and would ordinarily be one of the first names on the team sheet for Vincent Kompany. But the German giants confirmed on Wednesday morning that he would miss the match for personal reasons.

‌



Bayern said in a statement: "Due to a death in his immediate family, Joshua Kimmich is not in the squad today for the match against Arsenal London.

‌



"On behalf of the family, we ask that his privacy and grief be respected, and that further inquiries and reporting be refrained from. In deep sympathy, the entire FC Bayern stands by Joshua Kimmich's side."

Bayern assistant manager Aaron Danks had cast doubt over Kimmich's availability in Tuesday's pre-match press conference. "For Joshua it is personal reasons. I am not sure what it means for tomorrow," he said.

Danks faced the media due to manager Kompany struggling with illness. "Vince has had a virus, and it is important for him to rest," Danks said. "So he is at home. We are taking it day by day. He will play his role in the game whether in the Allianz Arena or not."

Bayern will also be without star playmaker Michael Olise after he was sent off in their 3-3 draw against Viking FK last week. Jamal Musiala is also unavailable due to a thigh injury, meaning Lennart Karl is likely to come into the starting line-up.

Sports.title: England star Kildunne dropped for Canada rematch
Sports.content:
Ellie Kildunne has been dropped to the bench in the England Red Roses squad to face Canada on Friday, a week on from suffering defeat in Toronto which ended a 41-match unbeaten run.

Head coach John Mitchell has made four changes to the starting XV in total, with Gloucester-Hartpury duo Emma Sing and Mia Venner coming into the back three at full-back and wing respectively, while Helena Rowland of Loughborough Lightning returns at inside-centre.

In the forwards, there is just one amendment to the team that began the second Test - Sadia Kabeya, also of Loughborough Lightning, is selected at openside flanker.

While Kildunne - 2024's World Player of the Year - and back-row Alex Matthews move to the replacements bench, wing Claudia Moloney-MacDonald and centre Tatyana Heard drop out of the squad altogether.

"Friday is our first chance to respond," Mitchell said.

"Last Friday, we lost sight of what we could control when it mattered most; that's on us to fix. This week is about getting back to who we are: hungry, accountable to each other and demanding more of ourselves than anyone outside this group ever could.

"We've earned a strong period, but nothing about it is owed to us going forward. Friday is an opportunity to apply sustained pressure, learn from what we missed and come out the other side better than we went in."

Mitchell: Kildunne going through difficult period

Speaking more about the major selection call at his pre-match press conference, Mitchell shed further light on the decision.

The head coach revealed Kildunne is "going through a difficult period" in the search for consistency:

"Well, firstly it's undisputed that she adds huge value. She's just going through a difficult period at the moment.

"It's important for us to help her through that.

Image: John Mitchell revealed the reasons for dropping Kildunne, saying she is going through a 'difficult period' in terms of consistency

"She wants to become consistent as well and she'll get back. It's also important to create competition and to recognise that you have to become more consistent, especially when you're competing in the Red Roses.

"So it's really important to reinforce the behaviours that we think are necessary to our game. And that goes for everyone."

Sports.title: VAR who wrongly awarded Haaland winner vs Man Utd set for PL return
Sports.content:
The VAR who incorrectly awarded Erling Haaland's winner in last month's Manchester derby has been reinstated to Premier League duty.

Matt Donohue and assistant Blake Antrobus failed to judge that Manchester City midfielder Enzo Fernandez was offside and interfering with play during the incident at Old Trafford on September 13.

Donohue is set to return to the Premier League and will serve as assistant VAR when Coventry host Fulham on Saturday.

He has not featured in any of the three match rounds since the incident, while Antrobus made his first appearance since the derby as an assistant referee for Newcastle's home fixture against Aston Villa last Saturday.

Donohue has officiated in the EFL since the derby, refereeing Championship matches between Derby and Wrexham on October 10 and Southampton vs Bolton last weekend.

Pro Ref's chief refereeing officer Howard Webb said Donohue developed "tunnel vision" by focusing on whether Haaland was offside, and added that the team around him should have helped pull him out of it. Sky Sports News reported United received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision.

How the Haaland incident unfolded

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Erling Haaland's controversial winner for Manchester City against Manchester United

In the 59th minute, Haaland tapped in a cross to give 10-man Man City the lead, but the goal was ruled out on-field after the assistant referee signalled for offside on the striker.

The semi-automated offside technology ruled Haaland onside, so the goal stood, but City midfielder Enzo Fernandez was clearly offside when he dived to reach the same cross.

Although he didn't touch the ball, Fernandez's movement appeared to affect Man Utd's Lisandro Martinez's defending before Haaland's back-post finish, which, under the laws of the game, should have meant the goal was disallowed.

Image: Offside law graphic shown during coverage of Manchester United's match against Man City

What happened next?

In their post on X explaining why the goal was awarded, the Premier League Match Centre wrote: "VAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside - and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.

"The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball."

However, in a statement released hours after Man City's win, Pro Ref said it had contacted Man Utd to acknowledge an "error of judgment" and that the VAR "should have recommended an on-field review" for Haaland's winner.

A Pro Ref spokesperson said: "Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal.

"The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland - that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

"In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

"Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place."

Webb: VAR had tunnel vision

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Match Officials Mic'd Up, Pro Ref chief Howard Webb said there would be a review of how the VAR process allowed Erling Haaland's goal for Manchester City against Manchester United to stand

On Match Officials Mic'd Up, Webb said he was "really disappointed" by the decision and added: "The on-field decision was not against Fernandez; it was against Haaland. When the VAR starts their check, they see that Haaland is actually onside by three centimetres.

"The VAR gets super focused on Haaland. He establishes he is onside but when he runs it through the full APP (attacking possession phase), he doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez.

"In that moment, he gets tunnel vision but it is down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel but unfortunately, that did not happen on this occasion. This goal should have been disallowed."

What the officials said at Old Trafford...

Assistant referee: "Enzo, Enzo."

Referee: "Deflection."

VAR: "Possible offside."

Assistant referee: "I'm going to go offside, Haaland."

Referee: "On-field decision is offside."

VAR: "Checking the on-field decision of offside against Haaland. He's tight. He's onside, so now we need to check the full attacking possession phase (APP).

"Haaland's in an onside position, but I need to check the full APP. Go back to see if [Iliman] Ndiaye is onside when it is flicked. Yes. Go, go, go, so it should be a goal.

"No touch there [from Enzo Fernandez], confirm no touch. Clear gap. It's not a touch there, is it? Goal.

"Michael, confirming that you need to change your decision to goal. Haaland is in an onside position. Final decision is goal; check complete."

What the pundits said

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher and former Coventry striker Jay Bothroyd analyse how VAR got Erling Haaland's winner so wrong

Sky Sports' Gary Neville predicted Pro Ref would issue a public apology for the mistake, but their statement fell short. He said: "We will see an apology from Pro Ref. There is no doubt that Enzo is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off.

"It's a really strange one. They'll recognise they got that wrong."

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher: "It's a bad one. We all look at it and it looks offside. Haaland looks offside but we know he's not. Then when you break it down, it is poor from the officials.

"It seems to me they've become obsessed with Haaland being onside. They haven't gone into as much detail with Fernandez in the middle and understanding of his impact on it."

Sky Sports' Micah Richards: "One hundred per cent [Fernandez is interfering]. It's been a bad day for referees and VAR.

"They got the Phil Foden decision wrong, and they got this decision wrong. How can you not say Enzo Fernandez is challenging for the ball? Of course he is.

"I've been in that position as a defender where any slight movement can make the difference for going for the ball or not, so of course it affects him. They've got it so wrong."

Sky Sports' Roy Keane: "Fernandez is interfering with play. Basically, United have been punished for holding a good line. When you are in that position, you are impacting the game. You're in the middle of the box, you're going for the ball.

"Their line is good. Fernandez is offside, and he goes to play the ball, so United are getting punished for good defending."

Sports.title: Wardley offered route back to world title after 'rest and recovery'
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley will be offered a route back to another world heavyweight title fight after his rematch defeat to Daniel Dubois.

Wardley was unable to regain the WBO world title after he was stopped in the second round of his second fight with Dubois at The O2 on Saturday.

But his manager Mike Ofo firmly believes that Wardley can challenge one of the other world champions after a "well-earned rest".

Ofo told Sky Sports: "Fabio has had a remarkable run, and there is no doubt that he still has a bright future ahead of him.

"Now is the time for him to enjoy a well-earned rest, to recover and consider his options. His journey has already been nothing short of remarkable, an extraordinary story of grit, determination and achievement.

"Clearly, he has never shied away from a challenge and has chosen to face the toughest opponents at every turn.

"I fully expect him to continue competing at the very highest levels of the sport and to win another world title if that is what he chooses to do."

Oleksandr Usyk's decision to vacate his world titles has opened up new opportunities as Murat Gassiev holds a WBA title, while Agit Kabayel is the WBC champion, and Filip Hrgovic holds the IBF belt.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will also fight for the WBA 'super' title in Cardiff on December 11.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WBO heavyweight rematch between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley. Video courtesy of DAZN

Promoter Frank Warren intends to steer Wardley back into world title contention.

Asked if Wardley remains a threat to the division's top fighters, Warren told Sky Sports' Toe 2 Toe podcast: "He's knocked over guys that have never been knocked over before.

"If he catches you, you're in trouble, and he's capable of doing that, but he's got to take a rest now and he's got to weigh up his chances and where he thinks he can go.

"I'm sure when he does come back, he'll have, as we call it in the trade, a warm-up fight. But if he does come back, he'll want to fight for a title again. He's a former world champion."

Wardley has reached the elite level of the sport, despite turning professional after a spell as a 'white-collar fighter' and Warren believes his remarkable success story can have another chapter.

"He'll be out for a while now and let him just rest and come back; if he does come back, and we'll see where we go with him," Warren said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Daniel Dubois stopped Fabio Wardley in the eleventh round of an incredible heavyweight battle in their first fight. Highlights courtesy of DAZN

"You've got to look at some of the wins he's had. He beat Joe Parker, who was ranked No 1 in the world and everyone was saying, 'When is he going to get his shot at a world title?'

"They were backing Joe Parker to beat Daniel and to give Usyk a real tough fight and he beat him, he stopped him. I take my hat off to him.

"All of the things you've just mentioned, he never had a single amateur fight, learnt on the job, and look where he got himself, so he should be unbelievably proud of himself.

"He's a big puncher. You look at that knockout he had with Frazer Clarke. The first fight was a good fight but the second one he knocked him out in the first round and look what he did to Justis Huni. Massively behind against a very good boxer and he knocked him over. Even with Daniel, he had him on the floor twice in their first fight. He's a dangerous man.

"You look back over the years and I'm not saying he's Lennox Lewis, but Lennox, he lost against Hasim Rahman, he lost against Oliver McCall but down the road he avenged those defeats.

"A lot of these guys have been beaten in fights over the years and this era now, there's some really good fighters out there."

Sports.title: Australia skittled for 99 as stunning South Africa comeback continues
Sports.content:
South Africa continued their remarkable Test comeback against Australia after a stellar Marco Jansen performance helped force the Baggy Greens to follow on after being skittled for just 99 on day four.

Jansen (5-33) - who had already made a sizeable contribution after making 85 off 100 with the bat - led a ferocious Proteas bowling attack, aided by important contributions by the returning Kagiso Rabada (2-33) and all-rounder Wiaan Mulder (2-14), seeing off their opponents in just 42.4 overs.

South Africa's first-innings total of 425 after declaring gave Australia a daunting 326-run deficit, leaving the tourists with an uphill battle after being forced to follow on. With a series-clinching victory now looking increasingly unlikely, Australia must focus on reducing the deficit and keeping their hopes alive.

Image: Jansen, left, celebrates the wicket of Australia's Beau Webster

Steve Smith - struggling with a neck injury throughout his innings - top-scored for Australia with a lowly 28, the only batter to score over 20 in a side that saw opener Nic Maddinson (0) and wicketkeeper Alex Carey among five of their 10 batters out for single figures.

The innings continues a sensational swing of momentum in the match sparked by South Africa skipper Temba Bavuma, who led his side from 110-6 to 425-9 with a momentous 179 off 334 balls.

The Proteas are looking to level the series after suffering a heavy defeat in the opening Test.

More to follow...

Image: Smith, centre is bowled out by South Africa's Mulder

Former Australia batter David Warner has hit out at the "pathetic" attendances in the ongoing Test series in South Africa.

South Africa lost the first Test match by 214 runs in Durban, with large sections of the Kingsmead ground empty, and the crowds haven't really picked up through the first two rain-affected days of the second Test in Gqeberha.

Sports.title: Mercedes confirm car plans for US GP after unusual Singapore split
Sports.content:
Mercedes have confirmed Kimi Antonelli and George Russell will both run their latest-specification car at this weekend's United States Grand Prix.

After a problematic debut for the team's long-awaited new aerodynamic package on F1's return to Malaysia earlier this month, only Antonelli ran the upgrades last time out in Singapore while Russell, who carried a grid penalty for the main race into that weekend, reverting to the pre-Sepang version so the team could compare the two on track.

Antonelli had started the Sprint weekend in Singapore on the back foot compared to Russell but his competitiveness improved as the event progressed and he finished third in the race, with Wolff suggesting afterwards that the team were leaning towards running both cars with the new specification in Austin.

The Mercedes team principal has now confirmed that plan in the team's event preview ahead of a race weekend that Antonelli could clinch the world title.

"Malaysia and Singapore were difficult weekends for us and we have worked hard to understand where we fell short," said Wolff.

"Austin gives us an opportunity to respond. We will run our latest update package on both cars as we continue to develop the car.

"The field is incredibly close, so we need to keep moving forward if we want to fight consistently at the front in the closing stages of the season."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell takes over from Kimi Antonelli's engineer during the Sprint rain delay in Singapore.

Despite not challenging for victory in either Malaysia or Singapore, with Max Verstappen taking back-to-back wins for a resurgent Red Bull, Mercedes remain firmly on course to secure a world championship double this year with six rounds of the season left.

Antonelli would clinch his maiden Drivers' Championship as earlier as this Sunday if he wins and team-mate Russell fails to finish in the top eight and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton is not in the top four.

Mercedes' 134-point lead over Ferrari at the top of the Constructors' Championship, meanwhile, means the Silver Arrows could be in a title-winning position for that title as early as next week's Mexico City Grand Prix.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Horner jokes that Toto Wolff's life is much easier without him in F1, reflecting on their fierce rivalry over the years.

Wolff says his team will continue to take things one step at a time.

"The United States Grand Prix begins another demanding triple-header," added Wolff.

"There is plenty at stake, but we won't get ahead of ourselves. The priority is the weekend in front of us: execute well, maximise our performance and take each race as it comes."

Mercedes will run a revised livery for the second time in three races in Austin, with blue added to the W17s to highlight the car company's MANUFAKTUR personalisation programme.
