Sports.title: 'Why me?' - PSG's Kvaratskhelia set for surgery after ACL rupture
Sports.content:
Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to have surgery after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), the French club have confirmed.

The 25-year-old, who was named the Champions League's best player last season, was injured in Tuesday's 4-2 home win over Barcelona.

The European champions have said Kvaratskhelia will have an operation "in the coming days" but gave no timeline for his recovery.

The Georgia international posted an emotional statement on Instagram, adding he has wondered 'why me' as he faces a long road to recovery.

He posted: "Many people asked me about this stand, many said that if all the footballers in the world prayed, the game would end in a draw.

"This could be true but before every game I play I ask God to leave the field healthy but in vain. It hasn't been a long time, but it's still on my mind - why me anyway? I have never missed anything probably I prepared for this game the best I have ever prepared for.

"I thought I was prepared for everything, but not, and I realize that God chose me and if I protected the players on another field, I'm ready to go through these months in labour, pain, tears.

Image: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia won the Champions League with PSG last season, beating Arsenal in the final

"I know I have to come back stronger for my people who always have my back, I won't let you down I promise I won't waste a second. Thank you all for your support see you soon."

The injury raises serious concerns over whether Kvaratskhelia will play again this season, but he will definitely miss PSG's Champions League trip to Aston Villa on December 8.

Kvaratskhelia has been nominated for the 2026 Ballon d'Or after a stellar campaign last season as he helped PSG earn back-to-back Champions League titles as well as Ligue 1 glory.

The Georgia captain's injury setback is a major blow for PSG, who are in pursuit of a third straight Champions League crown.

Kvaratskhelia has emerged as one of the world's leading forwards since joining the French champions from Napoli for £59m plus add-ons in January 2025.

Dembele and Marquinhos also suffer injuries

Image: Ousmane Dembele came off with an injury against Barca

PSG also lost Ousmane Dembele, the reigning Ballon d'Or holder, and captain Marquinhos to injury against Barca.

The French club's statement says both players have thigh injuries and "will remain under treatment for the next few weeks".

Another key player, Nuno Mendes, is also injured after missing the win over the Spanish champions following an injury in PSG's Ligue 1 win at Strasbourg on Saturday.

PSG have been in scintillating form in Europe this season since defending their title in May, beating Manchester City and Barcelona by the same 4-2 scoreline this month.

Luis Enrique's side are top of the 36-team league table after three wins from three, while they sit second in Ligue 1, level on points with leaders Lyon.

Losing Kvaratskhelia makes European domination much harder

Image: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia scored PSG's opener in a Super Cup win over Aston Villa earlier this season

Sky Sports' Laura Hunter:

PSG paid a high price for Tuesday's thrilling Champions League win over Barcelona, losing captain Marquinhos, Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to injury. Unfortunately for the latter, his season is over.

Not only is that a massive shame for the supremely talented Georgian, but a significant blow to PSG and fans of football more broadly. Kvaratskhelia is the type of player you happily pay to watch, whether you have an affinity to PSG or not.

He's played a key role for the double European champions over the past two seasons, including 16 goal involvements last year, and has earned a place on the Ballon d'Or shortlist - the recipient of the prize will be confirmed on Monday.

PSG of course have plenty of talent to cover the 25-year-old's absence. Desire Doue is doing marvellous things this season and I also like what Maghnes Akliouche offers. But this is a setback for Luis Enrique.

It won't end PSG's chances of a famous European three-peat. But it makes the task much harder.

Barca complain to UEFA over 'chainsaw' banner at PSG game

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol explains why Barcelona have complained over a PSG tifo

Barcelona have made a complaint to UEFA over a 'chainsaw' banner displayed during Tuesday night's game.

The banner, which covered almost an entire end of the stadium, bore the slogan 'Massacre, Parisian style'. It depicted a masked man wearing a PSG shirt slicing through the Barcelona crest with a chainsaw, while pyrotechnics created the effect of sparks flying as the blade made contact.

It appears to have been inspired by The Texas Chainsaw Massacre because it featured the main character from the 1974 horror film wearing a PSG home shirt.

Image: PSG fans unveil a tifo at the Parc des Princes

Sources close to Barcelona said the banner and offensive chants from the stands had been reported to UEFA's match delegate.

European football's governing body is waiting to see whether the banner is included in the official report before deciding whether to take any action.

UEFA declined to comment when contacted by the Press Association.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo asked for punishment ‘without mitigation’, then fought to cut it
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo successfully fought to reduce his punishment for walking out on a Portugal training camp, after publicly saying his sanction should be imposed “without mitigating circumstances”.

Ronaldo said in a lengthy statement on social media after he left the camp in Denmark last month that he should be punished as the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) saw fit and that his role as captain constituted “an aggravating factor”.

However, during the disciplinary council’s inquiry the 41-year-old put forward several arguments for cutting his punishment, including his clean disciplinary record in recent seasons and his services to football.

Ronaldo received a 30-day suspension and €255 (£215) fine, and the document accompanying the ruling reveals he presented three arguments in mitigation: his disciplinary record this season and in the previous three seasons, his services to football including recognition for sporting merit, and his contribution to establishing the facts of the case.

To support these arguments, Ronaldo listed the club titles he has won and his achievements with the national team: the 2016 European Championship and two Nations League titles. His individual awards were also highlighted, including the fact that the Al-Nassr forward has won the Ballon d’Or five times. Beyond his achievements on the pitch, he mentioned the honours he had received from senior state officials.

The decision-makers accepted Ronaldo’s arguments concerning his achievements and services to the country, using them to halve his suspension and fine. The punishment was then halved again because Ronaldo had accepted responsibility for his actions.

Ronaldo’s suspension will be served in a period during which there are no international matches. It is unclear whether he intends to return to the national team – or whether the coach, Jorge Jesus, will select him again.

The account of events provides a clearer picture of the circumstances surrounding Ronaldo’s departure from the training camp. After head coach Jesus held a press conference in which he reiterated that he was in charge of the team and that no player would influence his selection decisions, Ronaldo requested a vehicle from the FPF and set off for Copenhagen airport.

During the journey, he called the Portuguese federation’s president, Pedro Proença, and told him he was “not in the right frame of mind” to remain with the team.

“The defendant [Ronaldo] did not inform or provide prior justification to the federation or the men’s national team officials regarding his intention to leave the stadium and the training camp,” the ruling states. It says that between 30 September and 4 October, Ronaldo missed more than 30 team activities, including travel, training sessions and meals.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The federation says that Ronaldo’s promise on social media, after leaving the training camp, to tell his fans “the whole truth” brought further negative attention to the incident: “Given his prominence as a public figure on a global scale, the defendant could not have been unaware that his conduct, in the circumstances in which it occurred, would be subject to intense media scrutiny, as indeed it was.”

Ronaldo was therefore “expected to exercise particular caution in choosing the timing and manner in which he expressed his dissatisfaction with the manager’s decisions and conduct”. Instead, the player “further fuelled speculation and public curiosity by posting on Instagram on the very day he left Copenhagen, announcing that, ‘in due course’, he would tell ‘all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to his departure from the men’s senior national team’,” the inquiry concluded.

Portugal are scheduled to play Denmark again in their next game on 14 November in Braga.

Sports.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
Sports.content:
Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra.

I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri.

As a player and a columnist, I never had an issue with Manchester City. Precisely because, for many years, the club avoided buying the most obvious superstars. Guardiola said it himself: the most valuable of the valuable do not go to a club like City, who aren’t even the biggest football brand in their own home town.

Many became world stars in Manchester. Kevin De Bruyne had been discarded by Chelsea, Rodri’s true class was overlooked in Madrid for a long time, Gündogan’s career was on the brink after injuries, and most recently Gianluigi Donnarumma was no longer wanted in Paris. In Germany, City signed players from Hamburg, Frankfurt and Wolfsburg. Erling Haaland in 2022 was the first player they targeted who was also pursued by Bayern Munich. City did not operate like Paris Saint-Germain did in the era before Luis Enrique.

From the outside, City fundamentally did not do much differently from the other 10 or so top European clubs. But what are achievements on the pitch worth if they are accompanied by rule-breaking? The club has been found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial regulations between 2009 and 2018. It allegedly invested almost €1bn more than allowed and declared. The league leaders face potential forced relegation or having titles stripped. City continue to deny wrongdoing and are appealing against the decision.

It is right for the Premier League to crack down on unfair competition. I also appreciate that Germany is holding on to the 50+1 rule, which the federal cartel office recently upheld. It ensures that the majority of voting rights must remain with the parent club – the non-profit section of a professional club. The exceptions that have applied to Leverkusen and Wolfsburg are under review.

View image in fullscreen A Manchester City fan holds up a banner during the club’s Premier League match with Ipswich at the Etihad Stadium. Photograph: Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty Images

The bedrock of our football culture is 50+1. This rule exists only in Germany, yet it speaks to a spirit that fits perfectly with the European sports model: 50+1 maintains a balance; on the one hand it allows for investment, on the other it guarantees participation. It strengthens the rights of members and fans. Perhaps it is because of this rule that the average attendance in Germany is higher than anywhere else in the world.

What is the ultimate purpose of football? It is a business, but its infrastructure is still developed by the general public. That is how I have always understood sport. Even as a professional, it was clear to me that my privileged life was made possible by many people working on a voluntary basis. Through my role as tournament director of the European Championship, these political connections have become even clearer to me.

The stadium and football clubs can remain the final places where people gather and society debates its issues only if the elite and the grassroots stay connected, and the public is involved in the process. Football must not be detached from its roots, as was the case with Manchester City. This becomes possible when rules are enforced by an institution. Ideally, not by a commercial entity but by a non-profit one such as Uefa.

In business, as in politics, I am observing a shift in mindset. Today, it is deemed necessary to invest in non-profit institutions. More and more companies realise that football allows for a genuine exchange with the population – that it provides the perfect vehicle to set up corporate social responsibility projects.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This is what is needed in these politically turbulent times. In our fragmented world, political parties, churches and the media have lost credibility. In sport, however, people still come together. It is a tool to foster social cohesion. Therefore, I consider 50+1 to be a distinct competitive advantage for the Bundesliga.

I also welcome the fact that rules mean something in another case. Uefa is standing firm against Gianni Infantino, who recently wanted to privatise the World Cup and its profits. Along with his friend Donald Trump, he was seen by many as breaking the normal rules when Folarin Balogun’s suspension was lifted. The outcry from the global football community was loud, and it is possible that the Fifa president will fall.

When behaviour like that in Manchester and at Fifa is punished, it is a good thing. Football must prevent questionable ideas from distancing it even further from its grassroots. Only then can it drive engagement in civil society, and only then can it strengthen Europe.

Philipp Lahm’s column was produced in partnership with Oliver Fritsch at the German online magazine Die Zeit.

Sports.title: ‘A complete threat’: Rio Ngumoha’s electric display excites Van Dijk and Liverpool
Sports.content:
The shot sailed wide of Peter Gulacsi’s top corner and into the Kop, affording Villarreal much-needed respite at 4-2, but for Andoni Iraola it was a standout moment in a scintillating Champions League display from Rio Ngumoha. To a coach that called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield.

There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side ultimately won 4-3, Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with the left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game.

“I’m happy with his attitude because he’s eager to improve the things that we think he needs to improve,” said the Liverpool head coach after the comeback win against their Spanish opponents. “He has played a lot on the right lately. He’s feeling so comfortable now that he’s even adding some shots with the left. He hasn’t scored but he’s getting there, and if he can add these small things to his game it will put him in an even better position.”

Ngumoha’s 71st-minute attempt was reminiscent of Mohamed Salah in its intent, if not in execution. The Liverpool great’s final season at Anfield may have been the exception to the exceptional in terms of his own contribution but, as an education to a gifted and hungry young winger, it was not wasted.

As Virgil van Dijk noted that “a few senior players” have taken Ngumoha under their wing: “I would say Cody [Gakpo] is definitely part of that. Everyone is chipping in but for him to work with Mo last year was obviously massive. Mo was one of the best wingers at the club and experienced everything so why not soak in all the information and show it on the pitch and show your own qualities? I think he has shown it this season but there is still much more to come. He’s pretty electric at times and he showed it again. He was a complete threat constantly and their defender had a tough time.”

View image in fullscreen Rio Ngumoha proved a constant threat to Villarreal. Photograph: Richard Martin-Roberts/CameraSport/Getty Images

The Salah comparison was not the only throwback for Liverpool against Villarreal. It was a flawed performance with Van Dijk’s early mistake, Iraola’s initial formation and Liverpool’s lethargy on the ball all punished by Iñigo Pérez’s slick side. “It was a terrible start,” conceded the Liverpool captain. “I think the saying is you fight an uphill battle and as a defender it is pretty difficult to come back from it. I tried but it was a bad day at the office personally but we do it together with 11 players. We turned it around and that’s the main thing.”

The rousing recovery, the relentless high press, Iraola’s bold changes and the character required to overturn a 2-0 deficit all carried echoes of the Jürgen Klopp era. Given that was where Liverpool wished to return when replacing Arne Slot with the Basque coach this summer, Iraola’s 11th game in charge showed development is not confined only to Ngumoha.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Van Dijk said: “If you look at it from that perspective, it is like that. We train a lot, tactically as well, but because there are so many games you learn playing games and this was a test in that sense because Villarreal were good on the ball. They also rotated a lot so you have to find moments when you can press them and when you can win the ball high.

“Is this squad used to that [pressing style] because I don’t think many players have been part of that? What the manager wants us to do is something which resonates with Liverpool and it is down to us to show it in each and every game. It’s not easy, it’s demanding, but if you want to win games and win games in the Liverpool way then we have to do it. The first half was obviously not good at all and the second half was solid and we turned it around and that’s a good sign. Now we have to get ready for Brighton, a super team, which is coming.”

Sports.title: Kvaratskhelia asks ‘why me?’ after ACL rupture in most serious of three PSG injuries
Sports.content:
Paris Saint-Germain’s Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ⁠will undergo surgery after rupturing the anterior cruciate ⁠ligament in ⁠his ​right knee in the Champions League win over ⁠Barcelona.

Kvaratskhelia twisted ⁠the knee during PSG’s 4-2 ​victory on ‌Tuesday and was ‌helped off the pitch just ‌before the hour, with the Georgian unable to put any weight on his right leg.

The winger landed awkwardly after sprinting back to make a tackle on Xavi Espart and looked in severe pain as he clutched his right knee. He played a leading role in helping PSG to back-to-back Champions League titles and is one of the contenders for the Ballon d’Or, which will be awarded on Monday.

Quick Guide How do I 

“Before ‌every game I asked God ‌to let me leave the pitch healthy,” Kvaratskhelia wrote ‌on Instagram. “But it was in vain. Not much time has passed, yet one thought keeps circling in my head: why me? I never held anything back. I think I prepared for this game better than I ever had before. I thought I was ready for everything – but not for this. I know I have to come back stronger for my people, who are ‌always by my side. I won’t let you down - I promise I won’t waste a single moment.”

ACL injuries typically require a recovery period of ​at least six months.

Ousmane Dembélé had earlier been forced off with a thigh injury and the defender Marquinhos was substituted with a similar injury. PSG ⁠said both players would have treatment ​for the next ​few weeks.

The PSG head coach, Luis Enrique, used Dembélé sparingly in the French league last season and has rested him twice in Ligue 1 this campaign. The France forward, who scored six goals at the World Cup, struggled with injuries last season and had been beset by leg muscle injuries at his previous club, Barcelona.

In the 2024-25 Dembélé played 50 games in a season for the first time in his career and his performances earned him the men’s Ballon d’Or.

View image in fullscreen The ‘Massacre, Parisien style’ banner that has sparked a complaint to Uefa from Barcelona. Photograph: Mohammed Badra/EPA

Barcelona have made a complaint to Uefa over a “chainsaw massacre” banner displayed on Tuesday. The banner carried the slogan “Massacre, Parisien style” and depicted a masked man in a PSG shirt cutting through a Barcelona crest with a chainsaw, with pyrotechnics giving the effect of sparks flying as the saw made contact.

Sources close to the Catalan club said the content of the banner, and some offensive chants from the stands, were reported to Uefa’s match delegate.

Sports.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
Sports.content:
“I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.”

The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the NWSL, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.”

Success did not originally look destined, when the Swede took charge 21 months ago, at a time when San Diego Wave were enduring something of an exodus of senior players; the United States defender Abby Dahlkemper’s sale to Bay FC in August 2024 and Alex Morgan’s retirement a month later were followed by the USA forward Jaedyn Shaw’s departing for North Carolina Courage and her international teammate Naomi Girma joining Chelsea in January 2025. A reconstruction was needed.

That is why, on a video call that winter, when Eidevall spoke to his players for the first time after taking charge, he began by quoting a proverb: if you want to go fast, go alone, but if you want to go far, go together. “My ideas are not worth anything if we don’t believe and buy into them altogether,” he says. “We focused everything on just building connections as human beings.” Detailed tactical discussions were initially kept to a minimum. They spent – as he recalls – around four weeks of their six-week pre-season focusing entirely on passing out from the back, to develop their style. Fast forward to the present day and it has paid off, with the Wave defenders Kristen McNabb and Kennedy Wesley being the division’s top two players for passes completed this season. More notable, though, has been the development of young players, such as the 18-year-olds Melanie Barcenas and Kimmi Ascanio.

“From 2024, when the club was not performing well on the pitch and it led to a complete rebuild, we had to find an edge, finding players that could fit into the way we wanted to play,” Eidevall says. “Back then [it] was a bit different to many other teams in the league, because the NWSL was seen as being dominated by athleticism and transitional play, which obviously then requires really fast players and maybe didn’t put a premium on technical supremacy.”

He adds that the club therefore eyed players who are “really, really good technically. We had some young, talented players already – that has given us a really good advantage because we’ve been able to develop players in a salary cap league. That’s huge, because if you only buy readymade players, you will run out of salary cap space pretty quickly.”

View image in fullscreen Jonas Eidevall took over at San Diego Wave in January 2025. Photograph: SPP /Alamy

It is not just the salary cap that differs in the NWSL, compared to Eidevall’s previous jobs at Arsenal and Rosengård. The broad competitiveness of the American league means that, despite being second in the table, San Diego have lost almost as many games this season as Eidevall’s Arsenal across three English campaigns, and he says: “This was new for me. [In] European leagues the top teams very rarely go two games in a row without winning. Here, even the team that wins the league might go through spells where they don’t pick up points, so the way you handle those moments becomes very important.

“Training [here] is also a challenge – sometimes it’s very hard to get 22 players because you have a limited roster size. The moment you start to have injuries … there’s no real second-team academy system like we have in Europe, where you can always have the numbers that you want. Here you might not, here you would like to do something 11 v 11, but you have 18 players and you just have to be creative with how you coach.”

Trying to play entertaining football has been a target in a campaign during which they have already set new club records for regular-season wins and goals scored. They have done it with the second-highest average possession share in the division, more shots on target than any other team and while facing by far the fewest shots on target.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“That’s the most pleasing part, results through an identity rather than getting results the other way around,” Eidevall says. “The identity we have is to allow the players to be creative.”

View image in fullscreen Jonas Eidevall has overseen a necessary overhaul of San Diego Wave’s squad. Photograph: San Diego Wave

We are speaking around two years after Eidevall resigned as Arsenal’s head coach on 15 October 2024, following a disappointing start to that season. In his three full campaigns at the helm in north London he had won two League Cups, reached a Champions League semi-final and secured a second-placed top-flight finish in 2022 – but was unable to win the WSL. Reflecting on what he learned from that spell, he says: “We had a lot of fluidity with how our wide players could play in Arsenal, which at times created too few central options. So, how do we get better central connections? How do we get more players central on the pitch? That was a long-term reflection on my time at Arsenal. And that’s also led to some tactical changes that we’ve done here with San Diego.”

There is an aspect of his Arsenal tenure that he is determined to take inspiration from at San Diego, with his team having secured a home playoff quarter-final at their 35,000-seater Snapdragon Stadium. The 43-year-old fondly remembers the first sellout crowd for a women’s match at Arsenal’s 60,000-seater Emirates Stadium, for their Champions League semi-final against Wolfsburg in 2023: “We want to sell out Snapdragon Stadium and in order to do so we need to do exactly what we were doing at Arsenal – we need to create special experiences at the stadium,” he says. “That is what’s going to draw people into there. Yes, play exciting football, but we also need to play games that mean a lot to be there. The ripple effect of that, that’s so big.”

Sports.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
Sports.content:
Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game?

Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues.

Having snatched Wayne Rooney from the BBC in the summer for a Manchester United-based two-hander with the YouTuber Mark Goldbridge, last week the Overlap went daily, extending the output to 4pm Monday to Friday. An online launch had Jamie Carragher baiting Goldbridge, real name Brent Di Cesare. The former policeman shunned a “no comment” approach during his interrogation, biting back during an exchange that had Neville choking on his Huel in laughter. Clipped up, the send button pressed, job done.

The Overlap has gained a TV family dynamic, a chorus line of familiar characters. Neville and Carragher are mummy and daddy bear, football’s Richard and Judy. Jill Scott is the dotty aunt, Roy Keane the irascible uncle, smirking along with Ian Wright in picking over the latest gossip. It has been highly popular, occasionally agenda-setting, softening Keane’s image, even making a cultish figure of production hand Kiaran Saunders, supplier of biscuits and blueberries. Neville’s empire-building, though, is boundless, his tanks bulldozing into the already packed football podcast space, with newsletters to follow. The Overkill, anyone?

The family has been extended. Mondays have Steven Gerrard reviewing the weekend’s action with Becky Ives, this week offering a defence of Florian Wirtz: “Don’t give up on him.” Tuesdays have Kelly Cates and Ashley Young in tandem. Tim Sherwood and Jamie Redknapp are Wednesday’s pairing. Not the first time the Sky mainstays, one-time Tottenham midfield partners, have diversified. In the mid-2000s, they ran Icon, a lifestyle magazine initially only available to professional players. A combination of high-end advertising, onanistic photography and Redknapp’s purring interviews with A-list sportspeople fell flat, even after it became available in airport first-class lounges.

View image in fullscreen Becky Ives and Steven Gerrard breakdown the weekend’s action. Photograph: Global Media / Sky Vegas

Two decades on, such cologne-fragrant exclusivity has been swapped for the ubiquity of Bury’s most famous son piling it high. The quarter-zipped ex-Spurs duo are not alone as 1990s footballers taking the Neville shilling. Mark Crossley and Duncan Ferguson make an unlikely – but promising – pairing. Previously most famous for being the only goalkeeper to save a Matthew Le Tissier penalty, Crossley has made a successful after-dinner speaking career of Brian Clough anecdotes and “young man” impressions. “Big Dunc” completely refused to speak to the media when a player but he was a hit within ITV’s World Cup 2026 coverage.

On last week’s edition Ferguson suggested Gianluigi Donnarumma might be over the hill. “He’s 27, actually,” said Crossley before a classic game’s gone discussion of video assistant referees ruining the sacred art of smashing into the opposition at goal-kicks. Just what the listener came for, eating perhaps into the Under The Cosh’s market share of real football man podcasts. Whether Ferguson’s appointment as Glentoran manager breaks up the band is unclear, though management never halted Robbie Savage’s many media ventures.

Two further goalkeepers have signed up. Last week’s Friday edition had Joe Hart and Peter Schmeichel entering the Manchester City charges chat. While admitting to mistakenly burying the lead when Lisandro Martínez was willingly dishing the dirt on Manchester United while serving as CBS’s Champions League interviewer in Madrid last Tuesday, Schmeichel gave Hart a far harder ride. “It’s tough to be a Manchester City person,” Hart said. “I love the club … we’re in it together.” Schmeichel stayed insistent on City’s owners: “They’re letting Manchester down, they don’t understand what this place is. They have built a lot of towers and homes and all that but they don’t get this place.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I’ve worked closely with Khaldoon [al-Mubarak] and he does get this place, that’s my reference point,” said a hesitant Hart. “He’s an incredible person.” More good, strong, clip-up content.

The City affair will ask former players to intersect with uncomfortable issues for some while yet. That Neville’s further business interests include building projects running parallel to the Abu Dhabi-funded developments in Manchester is another example. Overlaps have become unavoidable in more ways than one.

Sports.title: Coach banned until 2048 for training children in DR Congo while suspended for sexual abuse
Sports.content:
A coach in the Democratic Republic of the Congo who was banned from football for 20 years by Fifa for sexual abuse of a minor has had his ban extended by five years to 2048 by the world governing body.

Jonathan Bukabakwa, known as Messi, has also been ordered to pay an additional fine of $15,000 (£11,200) after the Guardian revealed he had continued to work with young players despite his suspension.

The Congolese Association Football Federation (Fecofa) and Racing Club Baki, where Bukabakwa was coaching, have been fined $50,000 each by Fifa’s ethics committee for failing to comply with its decision to ban him for 20 years in 2023.

Quick Guide How do I 

Fecofa has also been instructed to introduce a “comprehensive education, compliance and monitoring programme for its officials, affiliated clubs and registered members” to try to ensure there is no repeat.

“The Congo DR Football Association, the club Racing Club Baki (formerly known as Esperanto FC), and the coach Jonathan Bukabakwa were found responsible for failing to comply with the decision rendered by the Fifa ethics committee on 18 October 2023,” said a Fifa statement.

Bukabakwa, who previously coached youth teams in the Limpopo and Malabo regions, was convicted of sexually abusing minors by authorities in the DRC and was released from prison last year. A Guardian investigation in August revealed there was video footage of him coaching young players at Esperanto in the Limete district of the capital, Kinshasa. Local sources confirmed he had regularly been seen taking charge of players on a school field.

Bukabakwa did not deny continuing to coach young players but claimed he had not been informed of his Fifa ban. He said he had not been questioned or received any communication from the governing body. He has denied the allegations against him.

The case has raised further questions about safeguarding in Congolese football and the ability of authorities to ensure that suspended individuals do not continue participating in the sport. Bukabakwa was provisionally suspended by Fecofa in November 2022 after media reports of alleged widespread sexual abuse in the DRC. Several other coaches were provisionally suspended at the time, although investigations into some of those other cases did not establish sufficient evidence for further action by Fecofa or Fifa.

Véron Mosengo-Omba, elected as Fecofa’s president in May, has promised to look into the previous cases once he has re-established a disciplinary committee. Fecofa was under a Fifa-appointed normalisation committee from 2023 until his election. “We will make sure that no one who is behaving like this will be involved in football in this country,” he said.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta has mastered the art of making substitutions at Arsenal
Sports.content:
They say that once is an accident, twice is a coincidence and three times is a pattern. After Mikel Arteta’s substitutes proved decisive yet again for Arsenal, we can say with certainty that his ability to change games from his bench is a pattern worth noting.

With Arsenal labouring away at Nottingham Forest and the game drifting towards a goalless draw, Noni Madueke – introduced at half-time – won the game for the visitors, shimmying inside and striking a heavily deflected right-footed shot past Matz Sels. It was hardly a glamorous goal but it secured three valuable Premier League points for Arteta’s side.

It continued a recent trend. In each of their past three Premier League victories, Arsenal have won the game thanks to winning goals by substitutes. Bruno Guimarães provided the decisive contributions against Sunderland (2-0) and Leeds (2-1), before Madueke repeated the trick against Forest.

They are the only goals Arsenal’s substitutes have scored in the league this season. Five teams have scored more goals via their replacements, with Ipswich leading the way on five, but all of Arsenal’s substitute goals have been winners.

The record for the most winning goals scored by substitutes for a team in a single Premier League season stands at six. With three in their opening seven games, if Arsenal maintain their current rate, their subs are on track to score more than 16 winning goals. That would obliterate the record. Clearly, that is not going to happen, but it does show how influential Arsenal’s substitutes have been in changing games so far this season.

Funnily enough, that record of six winning goals thanks to substitutes is held by Arsenal themselves. They hit that tally under Arteta in 2024-25. And therein lies the real pattern. This phenomenon is not confined to just this season – it is an area in which Arsenal have excelled since Arteta joined the club. Since his appointment in December 2019, Arsenal have scored more winning goals from substitutes than any other team. Over the course of the past two seasons, Arsenal substitutes have registered more goals and assists combined than any other Premier League side.

We cannot solely attribute this success to Arteta’s in-game management. When you have been given the resources Arteta has to assemble a squad as deep and strong as Arsenal have, it stands to reason that the players you are able to bring off the bench are players who would probably be starters in most other Premier League teams.

Thirteen different Arsenal substitutes have either scored or assisted a goal across this season and last, more than any other side. Having that quality available inevitably increases the likelihood of substitutes making an impact.

Arsenal’s approach to matches is also a contributing factor. They are comfortable controlling games without necessarily blowing teams away on the scoresheet. They are often happy to remain patient and lean on their exceptional defensive strength, safe in the knowledge they will eventually produce decisive moments in the opponents’ final third.

That approach naturally creates situations in which subs can thrive. A substitute introduced with the game level after an hour has a greater opportunity to score the winning goal than one entering a match that has effectively been settled already.

Close victories have been a hallmark of Arsenal under Arteta. Since his appointment, they have won by a one-goal margin 66 times – at least 13 more times than any other manager.

Nevertheless, we still have to give Arteta a lot of credit. Squad depth clearly helps, but there is undoubtedly a skill in knowing when to turn to your bench and who to bring on. You might argue that Manchester City are the only side with a squad that can rival Arsenal’s in terms of depth – yet they do not appear highly on the lists above.

One noteworthy aspect of Arteta’s management is the speed with which he makes substitutions. He has already made four half-time substitutions in the Premier League this season, a tally exceeded only by Brentford (six) and Aston Villa (five). Guimarães came on at half-time to change the game at Sunderland, and Madueke’s introduction against Forest was the latest example of that proactive approach paying off.

Arteta led the league last season for the number of times the first substitute he made in a game came at half-time (11), while on average he made his first sub after 50.2 minutes in games. That made him the second quickest to act, behind only Enzo Maresca at Chelsea (47.9 minutes).

Arteta has also not always had such a strong squad. Arsenal’s current depth is the result of years of meticulous squad-building and coaching, a process in which he has played a central role.

Perhaps the clearest indication of Arteta’s effectiveness in his use of substitutions comes when comparing him with other managers across Premier League history. Among the 81 managers who have taken charge of at least 100 Premier League matches, his substitutes have scored 12.6% of Arsenal’s goals.

That is the seventh-highest proportion in the competition’s history. And, with the possible exception of Unai Emery, the others above Arteta are less comparable in the sense that they have not had the same resources at their disposal.

For Arteta to be as high on the list as he is, despite the overall number of goals his teams have scored, shows there is more to this than simply having talented players to call upon. He has developed a knack for knowing how to change the game with his substitutes. Perhaps that could be the ace up Arsenal’s sleeve when it comes to deciding where the Premier League trophy resides in May.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: Bayern Munich vs Arsenal LIVE commentary: Harry Kane looks to continue scoring record against Gunners
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich vs Arsenal LIVE commentary: Harry Kane looks to continue scoring record against Gunners

Arsenal must contend with a familiar foe as they continue their Champions League campaign tonight.

The Premier League champions travel to Germany to face Bayern Munich for the third season running, live on talkSPORT this evening.



3 Arsenal must overcome a worrying record away against Bayern this week Credit: Getty

It follows a 3-1 home win for the Gunners during the league phase last term.

However, they have only won one of their seven away matches against Bayern including back-to-back 5-1 defeats.

Mikel Arteta's side will also come up against Harry Kane, who has scored 15 goals in 22 matches against Arsenal during his career.



The England captain has only scored more times against Leicester City (20) and Everton (16).

Kane's form against the Gunners since joining Bayern has been less prolific, though, with one goal in three matches since his move from Tottenham Hotspur.



Despite that, his nine goals in 10 appearances across all competitions this season will provide enough of a warning for the visitors.

How to follow Bayern vs Arsenal

Arsenal are in Germany tonight - Wednesday, October 21 - for their third match in this season's Champions League league phase.



Kick-off against Bayern is scheduled for 8pm, with live commentary available on talkSPORT.

Adrian Durham, Jim Proudfoot and former England captain Stuart Pearce have coverage of the match from 7pm.

3 Kane has scored 15 goals in 22 matches against Arsenal for Spurs and Bayern Credit: Getty

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.



Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

It will also be live on TNT Sports 1 from 7pm.

Bayern vs Arsenal team news

Bayern will be without France international Michael Olise on Wednesday through suspension.



The winger was sent off in their 3-3 draw with Viking last week.

Meanwhile, Jamal Musiala has been ruled out for the home side with a thigh injury.

Manuel Neuer is expected to start in goal despite doubts over a foot issue which saw him miss Saturday's win over RB Leipzig.

As for Arsenal, there are no fresh injury concerns or suspensions for the Gunners.

Arteta remains without the sidelined Piero Hincapie, William Saliba and Christos Tzolis, though.



Arsenal will be hoping to maintain their 100 per cent record in their absence after wins over Napoli and Lille already this season.

Bayern Munich vs Arsenal: Head-to-head Last five meetings November 2025: Arsenal 3-1 Bayern Munich April 2024: Bayern Munich 1-0 Arsenal April 2024: Arsenal 2-2 Bayern Munich March 2017: Arsenal 1-5 Bayern Munich February 2017: Bayern Munich 5-1 Arsenal

3 Bayern remain unbeaten in this season's Champions League league phase Credit: Getty

Arteta 'very excited' for Bayern test

Arsenal boss Arteta believes his side are ready to show their best against Bayern.

He said: "I’m really looking forward to the game, this is the stage, this is the kind of team, this is the kind of coach, this is the kind of club, the stadium, that you want to be involved in.



"We have prepared the game with lots of enthusiasm, and really thrive to come here and win the game.

"we know the kind of game we’re going to play, I think both teams are very clear on that, and we experienced that at the Emirates, and it’s going to be a very similar one in many moments.

"We have a lot of connections and positiveness in and around the team, so very excited about it.

"We have some really good players, the expectations are so big for all of them and we want more from everybody, and that’s the mindset.



"That’s what is going to make us better individually as a team so I hope that continues because that’s going to push all of us to reach different kinds of levels and be better."

Sports.title: Man City defended over 20,000 empty seats at Etihad Stadium for Champions League clash
Sports.content:
Man City defended over 20,000 empty seats at Etihad Stadium for Champions League clash

Manchester City's attendance against AEK Athens is not a 'big problem', according to Adrian Durham.

The Premier League leaders cruised to a 5-1 win in front of 40,042 supporters at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night.



4 There were more than 20,000 empty seats at the Etihad on Tuesday night Credit: PA

However, rival fans were quick to pick up on the thousands of empty seats inside the ground during their clash with the Greek champions.

City's home boasts a capacity of 61,038 following the latest expansion of the Etihad Stadium.

As a result, there were more than 20,000 seats left empty as Phil Foden's hat-trick helped the hosts to victory in the Champions League.



Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki were also on target for Enzo Maresca's side.

City now sit sixth in the league phase standings after two wins from their first three matches.



Meanwhile, their perfect start in the Premier League has seen them build a three-point lead at the summit.

City empty seats explained

Despite the reaction to the attendance, Durham believes the figure is not bad for a midweek European fixture.



talkSPORT's chief live football correspondent joined Alan Brazil and Gabby Agbonlahor on Wednesday's Breakfast show to react to the previous night's action.

Asked about the Etihad Stadium attendance, Durham explained: "It’s not a bad crowd midweek. I don’t think that’s too bad at all.

"I think sometimes, like with Wembley for example, when a stadium isn’t completely full, we tend to think there’s a big problem, but actually 40,000 on a midweek, when Man City in a normal season have a lot of games to play. There will be a lot of travelling to do.

4 City's dominant win over AEK was watched by just over 40,000 fans Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



"Alan just nailed it there, talking about Man United and Liverpool having loads of fans from all over the world coming to see random games. That’s how their seats get filled up.

"And Manchester City, they don’t really have a history of that. So I see that as the reason why, but I think there’s also a big turn-off among City fans towards UEFA.

"They’ve been booing the anthem for years because they feel they’ve been badly treated by UEFA.

"That’s now started in the Premier League because they feel, whether rightly or wrongly, they’ve been hard done by by the Premier League.



"So there’s a bit of a turn-off factor for some City fans when it comes to UEFA and now with the Premier League as well, but 40,000 isn’t bad."

City previously had a two-year UEFA ban for breaching Financial Fair Play rules overturned in 2020 by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

4 The crowd on Tuesday was not bad for a midweek fixture, says Durham Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

The club is currently appealing against a Premier League independent commission's guilty verdict in another FFP case.



It follows City being found guilty of all charges against them related to alleged breaches between 2009 and 2018.

Recent Etihad attendances

Prior to the win over AEK, more than 60,000 fans were in attendance for their matches against both Ipswich Town and Paris Saint-Germain.

Meanwhile, the attendance on Tuesday was the second lowest across nine Champions League matches played on the night.

The only fixture watched by less fans was Napoli's 4-3 win over Bodo/Glimt in front of 35,086 supporters at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.



City's most recent Etihad Stadium expansion was completed earlier this year with the construction of a new North Stand.

4 City's previous two matches against PSG and Ipswich were close to capacity Credit: Getty

Work had began in 2023 to increase the capacity from 55,100 following previous work between 2014 and 2015.

The Etihad Stadium first held 47,000 fans after it was converted from athletics to football following the 2002 Commonwealth Games.

Sports.title: Graeme Souness warned he could damage reputation as pundit over Bukayo Saka cheat claims
Sports.content:
Graeme Souness has damaged his reputation as a pundit for his dig at Bukayo Saka - rival fans wouldn't even give his view any oxygen.

That is the explosive verdict of Broadcaster and Arsenal fan Harry Symeou, who believes the harmful opinion needs calling out.



6 Saka consistently draws more fouls than the majority of his rivals Credit: Getty

Liverpool legend Souness hit the headlines this week for his explosive attack on Saka after the Gunners beat Nottingham Forest 1-0.

The 73-year-old accused the England international of being ‘a cheat’ who ‘dives all over the place’ on Piers Morgan’s Football Uncensored.

Saka cheat claim so far wide of the mark

Saka drew three fouls at the City Ground, one of which saw Neco Williams receive a caution despite making minimal contact.



However, while appearing on Rushden and Baker, Arsenal fan Symeou leapt to the defence of the 25-year-old winger.

He told talkSPORT: "To single out Bukayo Saka for this when it's something that we do have too much of in our game.



"Let's not deny that. We do see it a lot. We see players simulating in a bid to win penalties.

"We see them trying to win free kicks when they think that maybe they're going to lose the ball when they want to run the clock down.



"There are all sorts of scenarios where this type of thing comes into play. But to specifically brand Bukayo Saka a cheat, I think, is so wide of the mark it's unreal.

"It's a shame that people like Graham Souness, who I've got immense respect for based on his playing career, incredible playing career, was a really, really good pundit in my book a little while ago, but has felt the need that maybe because he's joined certain shows and certain company that he needs to be super controversial and start throwing around silly lines like that.

6 Saka is the second-most fouled player in the Premier League this term Credit: Getty

Souness has made himself look terrible

"I think he's made himself look terrible," Symeou continued.

"I think any respect that a lot of people had for Graham Souness as the pundit has maybe been damaged by this.



"You can talk to rival fans as well; it's not just because I'm an Arsenal fan - Very few would share this opinion.

"Very few would give this oxygen anyway. I just think it's crazy, to be honest."

talkSPORT co-host Charlie Baker then referenced Saka's England teammate Rio Ngumoha, who avoided going to ground while dribbling past Sergi Cardona en route to assisting Alexis Mac Allister in Liverpool's 4-3 Champions League win over Villarreal.

The question was put to Symeou whether the referee would have drawn play back for a foul had Mac Allister not found the net.



6 Ngumoha stayed on his feet to become the youngest-ever player to assist a goal for Liverpool in the Champions League Credit: Getty

He replied: "As officials, guys, they've got a responsibility to still pull up fouls even if they don't result in the player going down.

"What you need to do is essentially make players feel comfortable that even if they try and stay on their feet, if there was a foul committed, that will be punished.

"But to go back to the original point - Of all the people in the world to brand as a cheat and a simulator and a diver…to pick on Bukayo Saka, who's probably got one of the best reputations actually in English football in terms of his conduct and his personality and the kind of guy he is. I just think he's so far off the mark, it's unbelievable.



"Someone who's played the game at that level, who's been a pundit at that level, should know a hell of a lot better than that.

"And it's really, really disappointing to hear."

6 Souness branded simulation as a form of 'cheating' when hitting out at the way in which Saka wins fouls Credit: Getty

The stats also support Saka, with Arsenal's No.7 the second-most fouled player in the Premier League this term, having won 21 fouls.

That is only two behind his England teammate, Elliot Anderson, who has been on the end of 23 illegal challenges at Manchester City.



Symeou added: "I've said things in the past that have been clipped up, and they were taken out of context and turned into maybe something that they weren't.

"So I'm always really wary when something comes up like this and when I'm asked about it, about how I kind of approach it. And I always sort of look at it through that person's point of view.

"Was it a much deeper conversation from which someone's taken a sound bite, et cetera, et cetera?

"But in this instance, he had many opportunities to kind of swerve, saying essentially what he did about Bukayo Saka.



6 Arteta was asked about Souness' claims in his press conference and stated: “I haven’t heard it and I’m not going to make any comments about opinions.” Credit: Getty

"To say he went down easily in this particular scenario or in this particular situation is fine. But to make a generalisation like that, that is so wrong about a player is obviously damaging.

"I'm not saying it's just Graeme Souness. This is something that's right across the board right now.

"But as much as people kind of think, 'Oh, if I say this kind of thing, it will make me more relevant.' I'm not saying Souness isn't relevant.



"His playing career is impeccable. That's what makes this so disappointing. is that his career is worthy of him being on the telly. It's worthy of him being on the radio.

"He doesn't need to do this stuff, but you just think to yourself, 'What route do you want to go down?'

"Do you want to be clipped up? Do you want to be notorious for having silly opinions, or do you want to be respected for what you're saying? And this is where I think the struggle is for a lot of people.

"I just think in this scenario, it's so wrong. It's so incorrect.

How many times has Saka been booked for diving in his Premier League career? First Booking: October 2019 against Sheffield United. An 18-year-old Saka was cautioned by Mike Dean in the 35th minute of a 1-0 defeat at Bramall Lane. Second Booking: October 2022 against Southampton. Saka cautioned by Peter Bankes in the 29th minute of a 1-1 draw at St Mary's.

"It's so wild that this is going to do Graeme Souness more damage than it is going to potentially put him in front of more audiences.



"People are going to watch it, but their opinion of him is not going to be enhanced by it. If anything, it's going to go the other way."

Souness claim needs calling out 'because it's just so wrong'

It was then put to Symeou that the backlash may have been less severe for an Arsenal player more synonymous with the dark arts.

"This is a thing, I'm an Arsenal fan, right? And I'll always naturally defend our players and all the rest of it.

"But when I hear people say, you know, Gabriel's a bit of an S house, and Gabriel does this, and Gabriel does that...



6 Gabriel Magalhães has become a pantomime villain of sorts for rival fans of Arsenal Credit: Getty

"I don't leap to the defence of Gabriel that often because I think, well, if I was a rival fan watching Gabriel, [his antics] would probably frustrate the life out of me as well.

"And it would drive me insane. And he does play on the edge, but Bukayo Saka doesn't do any of that.

"So there are certain players that I would hear this type of thing. And I'd say, 'Look, I might not agree with you, but I don't think it's worthy of going massive on how wrong you are.'



"Whereas here, this needs calling out; this needs putting into focus with regard to how ridiculous it is because it's just so wrong."

Sports.title: Tottenham defended over £70m double exit despite pair starring for new clubs
Sports.content:
Tottenham defended over £70m double exit despite pair starring for new clubs

Tottenham Hotspur have been told not to dwell on selling Luka Vuskovic and Will Lankshear after their impressive form this season.

The pair departed the north London club for a combined £70million, including add-ons, joining Brighton and Middlesbrough, respectively.

3 Lankshear was allowed to leave Spurs for an initial £10million this summer Credit: Getty

However, fans have since questioned whether it was the right decision to let the youngsters leave amid Spurs' slow start to the campaign.

Roberto De Zerbi's side only secured their first Premier League win of the season against Coventry City on Monday.

Meanwhile, Vuskovic has helped third place Brighton keep four successive clean sheets, whilst Lankshear is the Championship's leading scorer.

Despite their immediate success upon leaving Spurs, Abbi Summers has defended the club's decision to accept bids for both players.

Should Spurs have kept Vuskovic?

Speaking on the latest episode of talkSPORT's Inside Spurs, she justified both pieces of business.

Discussing Vuskovic's exit, Summers explained: "If you’re going to get £50million for a player that hasn’t played (for you), I think it’s silly to not take it when we had to rebuild that defence.

"Of course it would have been nice to keep him, but I don’t think you could have thrown him in this season with Micky van de Ven, you couldn’t have."

The Croatia defender was sold to Brighton in July for an initial £46million plus up to £4million in add-ons.

His impressive form for the Seagulls includes a goal in their draw with Leeds United last month.

In contrast to Brighton's defensive displays, Spurs have kept just two Premier League clean sheets and have conceded 10 goals in seven matches this term.

3 Vuskovic has started all seven of Brighton's Premier League matches this season Credit: Getty

Vuskovic did not make a senior appearance for Spurs, having arrived from Hajduk Split last summer after turning 18.

His subsequent loan spell at Hamburg saw the 19-year-old named in the Bundesliga Team of the Season.

'Easy' for Spurs fans to rue selling Lankshear

As for Lankshear, Summers admitted: "It’s very, very easy (to say Spurs should not have sold him) and we could all be sitting here in another year, two years, five years and say ‘oh, we should never have sold Will Lankshear.’

"I don’t think either me or Majestic would have wanted to sell Will Lankshear. We just wouldn’t have had him as our second. Third choice? Yes.

"It’s a lot easier to go and score in the Championship because if you put (Dominic) Solanke in the Championship or you put Richarlison in the Championship, they would be bagsmen. They’d get so many goals.

"It’s a very big difference from being in the Premier League and I hope for Will Lankshear that he ends up being the next Harry Kane, I hope he has the most incredible career and he’s a Prem great.

3 Lankshear has scored 11 goals since joining Boro in July Credit: Getty

"I just think you have to look at it logically that it’s very easy to compare someone in the Championship."

Lankshear has scored 11 goals in 14 appearances for Boro across all competitions since his move to the Riverside.

The 21-year-old's initial £10million transfer includes a further £10million in add-ons.

He is currently the top scorer in the Championship with nine goals for Kim Hellberg's side.

Meanwhile, no Spurs player has scored more than twice in all competitions so far this season.

Prior to being sold, Lankshear played just 146 minutes across six first-team appearances for Tottenham.

Sports.title: Jack Wilshere explains fiery bust-up with rival EFL manager moments after final whistle
Sports.content:
Jack Wilshere has played down his post-match altercation with Barnsley manager Daniel Stendel.

The Luton Town boss became involved in a touchline melee following his side's League One win over the Tykes on Tuesday night.

3 Wilshere has played down his altercation with Barnsley boss Wilshere Credit: ITV

It came after the rival managers had shaken hands, with Wilshere appearing to take exception to actions by Stendel.

Footage of the incident showed the former England midfielder angrily turning back towards his opposite number.

Words were exchanged as players and staff from both clubs piled in to separate the pair.

A scuffle continued in front of the dugouts after Wilshere had been ushered away.

His players later gathered for a huddle on the pitch after the incident as they celebrated their narrow 2-1 home victory.

Wilshere explains Barnsley melee

Wilshere addressed his clash with Stendel during his post-match media duties.

Speaking to reporters, he explained: "Nothing but respect for them. At the end, we shook hands and it’s just passion. I want to win. He wants to win and that’s that.

"He just grabbed my hand. I think he wants to win. I want to win. I’ve got a lot of respect for him and his team.

"I watched them over the last few days, probably four or five games I’ve watched them and they haven’t got the results that they wanted, but they’re a good team and you can see that they’ve got threat.

"I thought [Patrick] Kelly was outstanding in midfield. [Reyes] Cleary’s obviously continued from last season.

3 Players and staff from both sides were also involved in the melee Credit: ITV

"So, they’re a threat and they’re also going through a transition period where they’re changing the style of play.

"They’re a high pressing team, they want to hit you on transition. I thought we managed that really well."

When asked about players and staff from both sides joining in, he added: "We have to be respectful and we are and they were as well, in my opinion, but also sometimes you can see their togetherness in those moments where we wanted to win so badly and we’ve got each other’s back."

The result leaves Barnsley 22nd in League One and a point from safety.

Luton's season so far

Meanwhile, Luton sit 13th in the third tier following their fourth win of the season.

Wilshere's side are only in the bottom half of the table on goal difference, with four points separating them from the play-off places.

3 Wilshere has been in charge of Luton since October 2025 Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

They will look to cut that gap by beating Leicester City on home soil this weekend.

The 34-year-old is into his first full season in charge at Kenilworth Road.

It follows his appointment in October 2025, his maiden senior managerial role.

Wilshere went on to win the EFL Trophy last term but was unable to guide the Hatters out of League One.

Instead, they ended the campaign in seventh, missing out on a top six berth by a single point.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham told how to win Ballon d’Or and beat Real Madrid’s heir to the throne
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham told how to win Ballon d’Or and beat Real Madrid’s heir to the throne

Jude Bellingham has been backed to blow everyone out of the water and win the 2027 Ballon d'Or - despite the inner politics at Real Madrid.

That is the verdict of Rory Jennings, who has predicted Bellingham will be the next English winner of football's top individual honour.

5 Jennings expects Bellingham to win the Ballon d'Or in the upcoming seasons Credit: Getty

The 23-year-old is currently on the Ballon d'Or 30-man shortlist for the 2026 award, set to be announced in London at the end of October.

Bellingham is a long-shot outsider for the next Golden Ball, with England teammate Harry Kane instead among the front-runners.

The former paid the price for an injury-ravaged season at club level last term, having not started a game until the end of September 2025 after missing all of pre-season.

Bellingham underwent surgery to correct a long-standing shoulder injury earlier that summer, which he put off to play at Euro 2024.

The midfielder was then sidelined for another two months following a hamstring injury sustained in February.

In his absence, Real Madrid failed to win a single piece of silverware for only the fifth time this century - having previously done so in 2004-05, 2005-06, 2009-10, and 2020-21.

However, as predicted by this talkSPORT.com writer, Bellingham came storming back into form for England at the 2026 World Cup.

The Birmingham City academy graduate scored seven goals for the Three Lions in north America, the most ever by an England player in a single edition of FIFA's greatest tournament.

Bellingham has since carried his World Cup form back into the new season, with three goals and three assists in eight LaLiga starts.

talkSPORT's Jennings believes another Champions League trophy in the cabinet of Real Madrid's No.5 could edge the Ballon d'Or race.

5 The Estadio Metropolitano, home of Madrid's rivals Atletico, has been selected as the host for the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League final Credit: Getty

"It would be very Real Madrid and very [Jose] Mourinho to win the European Cup in [Atletico's] Metropolitano [stadium], wouldn't it?

"So maybe it will be this year. And if they do… What Jude Bellingham needs is potentially international success.

"Although being English, the odds are stacked against it. And having Tuchel as his manager, the odds are massively stacked against it.

"But maybe it is a European Cup, and when you remember the final will be was at the Metropolitano it makes me think it could happen."

Jude Bellingham could blow everyone out of the water for Ballon d'Or

Bellingham was last among the favourites for the award after helping Real Madrid win the Champions League in 2024.

5 Bellingham won the Kopa Trophy, the award that goes to the best-performing player under the age of 21, in 2023 Credit: AFP

He set up Vinicius Junior's strike in the 2-0 win over his old club, Dortmund, at Wembley to cap a stunning solo first season in Madrid that saw him earn a European and LaLiga double.

Bellingham scored 23 goals and registered 14 assists in 42 appearances for Los Blancos across the 2023-24 campaign.

He then helped England to the final of Euro 2024, having scored the first goal of the tournament that kick-started the Three Lions' campaign; then he netted that bicycle kick against Slovakia, and even assisted Cole Palmer's equaliser in the 2-1 defeat to Spain.

In contrast, Vinicius was unable to prevent Brazil's dismal quarter-final exit in the Copa America that summer.

And yet when the Ballon d'Or rolled around months later, Madrid infamously threw their support behind Vini being the winner.

Asked whether the same could happen to Bellingham again, especially with Mbappe's influence now a factor as well, Jennings added: "I know what you mean. It becomes slightly political and obviously Kylian Mbappe will win his fair share of Ballon d'Ors in the next era of football.

5 Mbappe's PR machine may be hard for Bellingham to overcome if Madrid win the top honours Credit: Getty

"He is the heir to the throne, no doubt. And being in Mbappe's team, it's hard to shine.

"Jude Bellingham wasn't supposed to be England's star at the World Cup. There was a genuine conversation about whether he would go.

"Thomas Tuchel's mother called him repulsive. Thomas Tuchel wasn't picking him. There was a genuine conversation as to whether he would go. He wasn't supposed to be the star.

"The star was supposed to be Harry Kane. And Jude Bellingham blew him out of the water. Just absolutely outshone everyone.

5 Bellingham has 60 caps and 14 goals at only 23 years old Credit: Getty

"I don't think I've ever fallen in love with a footballer at an international level like that. Maybe since Gazza.

"You look at what Jude Bellingham did in the last tournament. Every time we needed a goal, he was there.

"Every time we needed leadership qualities, he was there. Every time we needed somebody to be a bit nasty on the pitch, it was him.

"So, yeah, maybe the Galacticos and maybe the politicians within the Real Madrid hierarchy, like the idea of it being Mbappe.

"And it will be Mbappe. But Jude Bellingham could just blow everyone out of the water. We've seen him do it at an international level.

"There's no reason he can't do that at club level."

Sports.title: Man United warned against hiring World Cup manager if Michael Carrick is sacked
Sports.content:
Man United warned against hiring World Cup manager if Michael Carrick is sacked

Appointing Julian Nagelsmann would not solve Manchester United's existing on-field woes.

That is according to talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook amid growing pressure on manager Michael Carrick.

4 United have been told to avoid appointing Nagelsmann as Carrick's successor Credit: Getty

The Red Devils boss has endured a poor start to the new season following his permanent appointment in May.

Carrick was rewarded for securing a third place finish and Champions League qualification with a two-year deal at Old Trafford.

However, his side have won just twice in 10 matches in all competitions this term ahead of Wednesday's clash with Como.

Nagelsmann has emerged as a candidate to replace Carrick in recent days as speculation surrounding his future intensifies.

talkSPORT understands the former Bayern Munich manager has admirers within the Red Devils hierarchy.

United given Nagelsmann warning

Crook is unconvinced by the 39-year-old, though, following his underwhelming exit from the German national team.

He also pinpointed United's lack of squad strengthening as the reason for their recent form as opposed to Carrick's management.

His stance echoed recent remarks from defender Lisandro Martinez and former boss Erik ten Hag.

Speaking on the latest episode of talkSPORT's Inside Devils alongside Flex and Angelina Kelly, Crook explained: "The standards since the start of the season have been so poor, the regression has been stark and I’m not calling for Michael Carrick to be sacked.

"But I agree with Erik ten Hag and I agree with Lisandro Martinez last week. What was the point in just rinsing and repeating?

4 Sacking Carrick is not the answer to United's problems, says Crook Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

"You sack another manager, you bring in someone like Nagelsmann, who didn’t cover himself in glory as the Germany boss and he’s also quite a combustible character.

"How’s he going to work with the likes of Jason Wilcox, who seemingly is going nowhere, and Omar Berrada?

"How’s he going to cope with what is still, I think, quite a problematic dressing room?

"So there’s no guarantee that you change the manager and you get anything other than a short-term impact because that’s what tends to happen whenever a new manager comes in and then the players revert the type.

"So I don’t think Carrick is the biggest problem at the football club. I think the summer window was an abomination and the squad is simply not strong enough to compete on multiple fronts."

Nagelsmann spent three years in charge of Germany prior to his exit this summer.

4 Nagelsmann is available after stepping down as Germany manager in the summer Credit: Getty

He departed the role following his side's penalty shootout defeat to Paraguay in the last 32 of the World Cup.

It followed a quarter-final loss to Spain for the hosts at Euro 2024 earlier in his tenure.

Who could be United's next manager?

Nagelsmann is not the only potential candidate to succeed Carrick in the Old Trafford dugout.

talkSPORT understands Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler is seen as an option by the club.

Meanwhile, Premier League title winner Antonio Conte is prepared to take charge of United.

The former Chelsea boss is currently without a club after leaving Napoli in June.

4 Conte is also a candidate to succeed Carrick if he is sacked Credit: Getty

United could face competition for his signature, though, with Juventus also interested in Conte.

He has been identified as their preferred appointment if Luciano Spalletti is sacked.

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag blames Jadon Sancho for Man United overpaying for flop
Sports.content:
Erik ten Hag has revealed Jadon Sancho caused Manchester United to overpay for Antony during his time as manager.

The Red Devils signed the winger for £81.3million in 2022, during Ten Hag's first transfer window as manager.



3 Ten Hag completed a deadline day move for Antony in his first United transfer window Credit: Getty

His arrival on deadline day made him the second-most expensive signing in the club's history.

However, Antony departed Old Trafford for just £21.6million last summer, joining Real Betis following a successful loan spell with the Spanish club.

It followed just 12 goals and five assists in 96 appearances for United.



Why did United sign Antony?

Ten Hag, who won two Eredivisie titles with Antony in his side at Ajax, has now detailed the reasoning behind bringing him to the club.

The Dutchman has revealed the late move was born out of Sancho's refusal to play on the right wing.



Speaking to The Athletic, he recalled: "There came up a problem because Sancho didn’t want to play on the right side, he said that.

"Which was very weird, he played often on the right. He said he felt more comfortable on the left. So there we had an issue and we were late."



Sancho had arrived at United from Borussia Dortmund a year prior during Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's time in charge.

He went on to feature on the left 28 times across all competitions during his debut season, compared to just eight appearances on the opposite flank.

Following Ten Hag's arrival, though, Sancho was moved to the right for the first three matches of the 2022/23 season prior to the signing of Antony.

3 Antony failed to replicate his Ajax form at United, who lost £60million on the forward Credit: Getty



Sancho's United career

However, the former England international was unable to force his way into the side on the left under Ten Hag following his request to switch flanks.

Instead, Sancho was sent on loan to Dortmund and Chelsea during Ten Hag's time as manager.

As a result, he missed out on United's FA Cup triumph in 2024, which earned Ten Hag a contract extension.

United triggered a clause in his deal which would have kept Ten Hag at the club until 2026.



He would be sacked just three months later, though, after a disappointing start to the season.

Meanwhile, Sancho was released this summer following a third loan spell away from Old Trafford.

3 Sancho's request to play on the left forced Ten Hag into the market back in 2022 Credit: Getty

Despite winning the Europa League with Aston Villa last term, the 26-year-old currently remains without a club.



Sancho was approached by Spanish club Getafe last week amid his search for a new team.
