Sports.title: England legend Sir James Anderson RETIRES from cricket at 44... after Lancashire tell him they will not give him a new contract for next summer
Sports.content:
England legend Sir James Anderson RETIRES from cricket at 44... after Lancashire tell him they will not give him a new contract for next summer

Jimmy Anderson’s long career is finally at an end at the age of 44 after Lancashire declined to offer him a new contract for the 2027 season.

Anderson, who took a record 704 Test wickets for England and this summer collected 50 wickets for Lancashire at 17 each in Division Two of the County Championship, was told earlier this week by the club’s new chief executive, Richard Kenyon, and their new director of cricket, Paul Farbrace, that his time at Old Trafford was over.

Daily Mail Sport understands that Anderson will not look to extend a county career that began in 2001, bringing to an end one of the modern game’s great fast-bowling stories.

In all, he took 1,193 first-class wickets at 24 each, as well as 358 in one-day cricket and 71 in T20s.

More to follow

James Anderson took 50 Championship wickets for Lancs at an average of 17.7 last season

Anderson was knighted by Princess Anne in 2025 for his services to cricket

Sports.title: Tragic rugby star Hyron Andrews, 31, died from a torn main artery, autopsy confirms, after he was found in locked shower cubicle
Sports.content:
The tragic circumstances surrounding the death of former Sale Sharks lock Hyron Andrews have been revealed in an autopsy report.

The 31-year-old, who played for the South African Lions, was found unresponsive in a locked shower at the Atalante-Relais Thalasso Hotel on Friday, before his club’s Champions Cup game with La Rochelle.

Emergency services arrived but were unable to save him and he was pronounced dead at the scene.

His body remains in France, where the autopsy revealed a tear in his aorta - a torn main artery.

Andrews only returned to his native South Africa to join the Lions this summer after departing English club side Sale for whom he made 45 appearances. Of those, 19 came last season.

A Lions Rugby statement read: ‘Lions Rugby Company, on behalf of the Andrews family, confirms that, following an autopsy report, Hyron’s death was found to be caused by an aortic dissection. This dissection most likely occurred on an aortic aneurysm.

‘The French authorities, who conducted the autopsy and, in whose care Hyron’s body currently remains, described the cause of death as “a tear in the aorta (due to natural causes), which led to a significant accumulation of blood within the sac surrounding the heart.”

‘The Andrews family asks for respect, privacy and patience during this difficult time as the repatriation process begins.

Hyron Andrews died in France on Friday before Lions' Champions Cup clash at La Rochelle

Clubs across Europe paid tribute to Andrews before their matches at the weekend

‘A timeline for the return of Hyron’s body to South Africa has not yet been determined. Further information will be communicated when it becomes available and under the guidance of the family.’

Lions continued to play their Champions Cup game with La Rochelle the day after Andrews' death, losing 31-14.

Andrews' former club boss, Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson, was among those who paid tribute: 'Hyron was just a brilliant guy and team-mate. He was so skilled on the field but off it, he was always someone you would want to have a beer with.

'He was funny and charismatic in his own unique, dry way and the lads, to a man, loved playing with him and being around him. It was a big move for Hyron and his wife Maiglin to come to England but he truly made a second home in Manchester and it was incredible to see how he and his family embraced the club and area.

'Most importantly, he was a loving husband and a doting father to his two gorgeous boys. It was an absolute privilege to get to know him. It’s just absolutely devastating for everyone.'

Andrews was a former South Africa Under-20 international.

Mark Alexander, president of the South African Rugby Union, said shortly after Andrews' death: 'This is terrible and distressing news. Our hearts go out to Hyron's family and the whole Lions rugby community.

'There are no words to adequately convey our shock and the depth of sympathy we feel for his wife Maiglin and for his extended family, friends, team-mates and loved ones during this time of immense sorrow.

'Hyron was a respected member of the rugby community whose contribution to the game and impact on those around him will be remembered with great fondness.

'His untimely passing is a devastating loss and we share in the grief of all who knew and loved him.

'The thoughts and prayers of the entire South African rugby family are with Maiglin and all those mourning his loss. May they find strength, comfort and peace in the memories they shared with him and in the support of those around them.'

Sports.title: The eventful life of snooker favourite Mark Allen: A high-profile relationship with fellow star, painful divorce, bankruptcy woes and new life with second wife as sporting world rallies around him after emotional interview
Sports.content:
Snooker star Mark Allen has received an outpouring of support after revealing he has been in a mental health clinic for ten weeks – a day after admitting his career could be over.

The former world No1 had been close to tears during an emotional interview after losing to Jordan Brown in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open in Belfast on Tuesday. Explaining his absence from the sport, he told TNT Sports that he has been dealing with a lot of 'problems within' that mean he is 'just trying to survive'.

And on Wednesday morning he released a lengthy statement elaborating on that interview.

'Everything I said in that interview was true. However, rest assured I’m doing my best to turn things round,' Allen wrote on social media. 'I have been in a mental health clinic for the last 10 weeks, finally discharging so I could attempt to play in Belfast.'

'I’m not OK, but I’m OK in that itself. I’ve been much worse in the last few months than you saw yesterday. I literally didn’t see a future in anything...

'I see the light now that I couldn’t see before but I do now. I also know it won’t happen overnight. I’m a work in progress!!! My fight and determination on the table has always been there to see. I need to show those same fighting qualities off it now for a while.'

Mark Allen was a downcast figure as he admitted that he might have played his last match

The former World Championship semi-finalist brushed away a tear at the end of his interview and was consoled by TNT Sport's Rachel Casey

Allen, known as The Pistol, has faced several challenges during a career which has seen him hit the heights of becoming world No1 and includes Masters and UK Championship title wins.

He has been open in the past about his lows as well, including financial problems and struggles with his weight.

In January 2021 he declared himself bankrupt – citing that he spent his £3.5million in career prize money as fast as he earned it.

'I just overspent in every aspect of my life,' he told BBC Sport in an interview in October 2022. 'Bankruptcy was the only choice. It's easy to read that I made £3.5m on the table, but I spent it as fast as it was coming in.

'It was sad saying that given what I've made in the game and how well I've done. It's embarrassing, but the priority now is to get my life in order.

'If I could go back I would be more sensible with money. If there was a car available at £50,000 I bought one at £80,000. If there was a house available at £1,500 per month, I'd spend one at £2,500.'

Back in October 2016, Allen previously gave fans a breakdown of how quickly the money he won in the sport would be spent.

He published a note that said despite collecting £2million in earnings over 12 years, he was left with an average profit of just £6,500 each year because of taxes, expenses and bills.

Allen, who was declared bankrupt in January 2021, also divorced his ex-wife Kyla McGuigan in May 2020. They had been married for seven years and share a daughter called Harleigh

Allen's financial situation was also affected by his divorce from his ex-wife Kyla McGuigan. The pair had been married for seven years and share a daughter, Harleigh, born in 2017.

'You don't put enough away for tax and everything just snowballs. All the legal stuff with the divorce, if you have to pay for lawyers and barristers, it all mounts up,' he admitted to BBC Sport.

As well as Harleigh, Allen has a daughter with his former girlfriend Reanne Evans – another snooker star.

The duo, who have publicly feuded in the past, had a three-year relationship that ended in 2008.

The former couple were paired together in the British Open in August 2021 with then 12-time women's world champion Evans refusing to touch hands with Allen as he approached her before the match began.

Evans refused Allen's attempted fist bump before she broke for the first frame of this best-of-five grudge match, which Evans won.

'It was horrible,' admitted Allen about the occasion at the Morningside Arena in Leicester. 'It was nothing I want to go through too often, but I had to remain as professional as possible.

'I can hold my head high. I treated it like any other match and showed respect where respect was due. I thought Reanne played well. She was unlucky in frame four and at that point she would have deserved to win. She played much better than me.'

Allen also has has a daughter with former girlfriend and snooker star Reanne Evans from their three-year relationship which ended in 2008

The duo haven't always seen eye-to-eye and that came to a head at the 2021 British Open

As reported by Daily Mail Sport at the time, Evans's actions were perhaps revenge for Allen's antics at the World Championships in April. The Northern Irishman was practising in the same Crucible room as Evans was working as a BBC pundit.

It prompted Allen to complain that his ex was causing a distraction and demand her removal. Organisers controversially complied, leaving Evans upset.

That spat in Sheffield only highlighted tensions that have been simmering for years and have even ended up in court.

Allen was asked by Evans to increase his child maintenance for their daughter Lauren, having become unhappy with his previous payments of around £100 per month.

Allen is now a married man once more after tying the knot with Sara Herald last year. They are understood to have first dated in 2023.

As well as finding love again, the recent years have seen Allen embark on a fitness journey – with the remarkable results seeing him lose five stone.

That health kick came after speaking to snooker legend Ronnie O'Sullivan as well as a close friend. O'Sullivan's advice prompted him to stop drinking alcohol, while his friend warned him that he may not see Harleigh get married in the future due to his lifestyle.

'I'm happier in my appearance. I don't want to do bad things to myself when I look in the mirror,' he told The Sun in the midst of his weight-loss transition in September 2022.

The 40-year-old is now re-married having tied the knot with Sarah Herald last year

Allen has also gone through a healthier phase of living - losing five stone after changing habits

'I need to lose more weight. I'm not fighting fit yet. Before I started my diet, I was 19.1 stone which is really embarrassing to say for someone of my height and age. I'm now 14st 10lbs.

'I have cut out all the fun stuff. Even if I do eat bad food, I eat so little of it. I try to cut out carbs as much as possible. Stick to stuff high in protein and fat.

'It has been hard work but I have been disciplined. I haven't gone cold turkey like with previous diets.

'One of my very closest friends said to me: "If you keep going the way you're going Mark, you won't be here to walk Harleigh down the aisle'. That was tough to hear but probably what I needed to hear.'

The former world No1 has been open about his latest challenge with Allen admitting he may have played the final match of his 21-year professional career.

'I think if I wasn't playing Jordan I wouldn't have come back,' Allen said. 'I felt like if I was going to play one last time, playing here at the Waterfront, where it all started in 2005, against one of my best mates, I thought that was a better way to sign out.

Allen played his first match since losing the World Championship semi-final to Wu Yize back in May

The Northern Irish star had missed a match winning black before going on to lose the semi-final

'I've been flooded with support but the problems are within. I just don't see a future with snooker in it, if I'm honest.

'It's sad to say, because it's all I've loved to do since I was 12 but the last few months have been really difficult and it's put snooker into perspective for me. At the minute I'm just trying to survive.'

Allen was comforted by interviewer Rachel Casey after his emotional comments, as she reassured him that many of his friends within the sport would be happy to welcome him back with open arms whenever he wanted to return.

Footage of his interview, shared by TNT Sports, has been viewed over 2.7 million times alone with Allen's candid comments receiving attention from far beyond the world of snooker.

Among those affected by the interview was his opponent Brown, who had embraced Allen after their match, and appeared emotional when he spoke to Casey moments after the interview.

‘It shows there are more important things in life than snooker, that was easily the hardest match I’ve ever had to deal with,' Brown said.

‘I don’t even know what to say, I am lost for words Rachel. I’ve missed him, I love him, just such a great guy through and through.’

Brown had expressed his worry about his close friend and regular practice partner earlier this month, after revealing he had been 'checking in on him'.

The 40-year-old's last appearance had come at the World Snooker Championships in May, when Allen agonisingly missed out on reaching the final.

Allen missed a match-winning black in the penultimate frame of his semi-final against Wu Yize, with the Chinese player ultimately winning 17-16 after reeling off the final three frames of the match.

The Northern Irish star admitted post-match to have been 'devastated to lose' but sportingly congratulated Wu, who would go on to win the final and be crowned world champion for the first time.

Allen had stayed away from the tour since, citing personal reasons, which are understood not to relate to any repercussions from the manner of his defeat at the Crucible.

Concerns had been raised by snooker fans over Allen's absence after he missed eight consecutive events, a run ended when he returned at the Northern Ireland Open, which he previously won in 2021 and 2022.

Allen has been praised by fans for his comments about his situation, after explaining that has been in a mental health clinic over the past 10 weeks and is trying to 'turn things around'

Allen explained in his subsequent update that he felt he 'owed it to everyone to speak', with the star receiving support and praise from fans for his openness.

'What a brilliant, measured and brutally honest statement. I have so much respect for such candour and virtue. Take care and get well soon, Mark,' one fan responded.

'Mark, you are legend of the game and very brave person. The night is darkest before the dawn, really hope you'll feel better,' a second replied.

Another fan added: 'You may or may not realise it. But, you’ve probably done more for mental health awareness than any ad campaign ever has before.

'This post alone shows how speaking out and seeking help in tough times, works. Thank you for sharing it and keep moving forward.'

Allen has thanked fans for their support and stated he is at the beginning of a 'new journey'.

'Thank you to every single message I have received', Allen wrote. 'I’ve seen them all but a bit overwhelmed to reply right now.

'Just know that they have helped me a lot but I’m not going anywhere just yet!!!! I have so much to live for and this is only the beginning of my new journey.'

Sports.title: Angry Barcelona launch complaint after PSG ultras displayed 'chainsaw massacre' banner before Champions League defeat in Paris
Sports.content:
Angry Barcelona launch complaint after PSG ultras displayed 'chainsaw massacre' banner before Champions League defeat in Paris

Barcelona have reported Paris Saint-Germain to UEFA for the ‘chainsaw massacre’ banner displayed during Tuesday night’s Champions League match in the French capital.

The banner carried the slogan ‘Massacre, Parisien style’ and depicted a blood-spattered masked man in a PSG shirt cutting through a Barcelona crest with a chainsaw.

Pyrotechnics gave the effect of sparks flying as the saw made contact, while the chainsaw also appeared to be covered in blood.

Barcelona have also reported offensive chants being directed towards the club during the game.

Daily Mail Sport understands UEFA will wait to see if the banner is mentioned in the match delegate's report before deciding whether to take action.

As for on the pitch, PSG ran out 4-2 winners in a thrilling game between two of Europe's most in-form sides.

The banner carried the slogan ‘Massacre, Parisien style’ and depicted a blood-spattered masked man in a PSG shirt cutting through a Barcelona crest with a chainsaw

Desire Doure, Lucas Hernandez, Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz were all on target as PSG made it three wins out of three in the Champions League this season, and firmly established their lead at the top of the league standings.

PSG manager Luis Enrique was delighted with what he saw from his players against his former club.

'What I loved is how the players were capable of playing a sensational first half defensively, winning a lot of balls with the high press and creating chances to score more goals,' he said.

'And then we overcame difficult moments in the second half when Barca had 15 minutes when they dominated and were better. But we are a team that adapts to whatever happens on the pitch.

'I think we played aggressively, strong. You can see how difficult it is to press players of this level: Pedri, Lamine, Olmo, Raphinha, (Anthony) Gordon, Espart, (Pau) Cubarsi. They are talented as individuals and as a team. This is the best level we could come up against.'

For Barca, who twice levelled through Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal, this was their first defeat of the season, bringing an end to their 11-game winning streak.

PSG have been in scintillating form in Europe this season since defending their title in May, beating Manchester City and Barcelona by the same 4-2 scoreline this month.

But Tuesday’s latest victory has come at a cost, as winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set for a long-term lay-off after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament.

The European champions confirmed Kvaratskhelia, who received extensive treatment early in the second half of the 4-2 triumph at Parc des Princes following a challenge with Xavi Espart, will have surgery 'in the coming days'.

Winger Kvaratskhelia is set for a long-term lay-off after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament

A statement on PSG’s website on Wednesday morning read: 'Victim of a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo surgery in the coming days.'

The 25-year-old Georgia captain’s injury setback is a major blow for PSG, who are in pursuit of a third straight Champions League crown.

Kvaratskhelia has emerged as one of the world’s leading forwards since joining the French champions from Napoli for £59million plus add-ons in January 2025.

The club also confirmed that France forward Ousmane Dembele and captain Marquinhos will be out of action for 'the coming weeks' due to thigh injuries.

Both PSG and Barca have big games to come in their respective leagues this weekend.

PSG face Lyon in a top-of-the-table clash in Ligue 1, while Barca host rivals Real Madrid in the Clasico.

Sports.title: How Ezri Konsa became Arsenal's 'blessing' in defence: The challenge Mikel Arteta set him to keep William Saliba out of the team, dressing-room impact and his excellent record against the world's best strikers as he faces off with Harry Kane again
Sports.content:
How Ezri Konsa became Arsenal's 'blessing' in defence: The challenge Mikel Arteta set him to keep William Saliba out of the team, dressing-room impact and his excellent record against the world's best strikers as he faces off with Harry Kane again

For Ezri Konsa, putting in a last-ditch, match-saving tackle to deny Nottingham Forest’s Liam Delap in the final minutes on Sunday was just part of his job. Nothing more, nothing less.

Mikel Arteta later paused and grinned while describing the crucial sliding challenge on 93 minutes as ‘unbelievable’, after the defender raced back to reach Delap in the nick of time and preserve a hard-fought, attritional 1-0 win – and Konsa's fifth clean sheet in nine Arsenal appearances.

A more fitting word to label the £55million summer buy from Aston Villa rests tattooed on 28-year-old Konsa’s left hand: ‘Blessed.'

For the Gunners could not have wished for more when looking for a player capable of filling the William Saliba-shaped hole in their backline.

When it emerged Saliba would be sidelined for a prolonged period because of a back injury sustained with France at the World Cup, Arsenal fretted and a like-for-like replacement became a summer priority for the team with the best defensive record in each of the last three Premier League seasons.

An Arteta team starts from a rock-solid base with multiple versatile defenders, often at the expense of frontline options.

Ezri Konsa has seamlessly filled the William Saliba void at Arsenal since joining for £55m from Aston Villa this summer

Konsa's last-ditch tackle on Liam Delap, racing back to slide in at the perfect time, preserved Arsenal's 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest on Sunday

Various right-sided centre backs who also cover right back were looked at including Jarell Quansah and even former Tottenham captain Cristian Romero, before Konsa became the one they set their sights on.

A number of factors influenced Arteta’s decision. His background checks were glowing, helped by the defender’s pre-existing ties to the England contingent at Arsenal of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Noni Madueke.

Another was his availability at Villa, making 96 per cent of the Midlands club’s matchday squads last season. For a team like Arsenal hunting down four trophies, availability is paramount. So, too, is versatility – which Konsa demonstrated by playing right back for England at the World Cup.

He has slotted in seamlessly thus far, starting six of Arsenal’s seven league matches and the two Champions League fixtures against Napoli and Lille. The statistics reflect a centre back who is Saliba-esque in his comfort with the ball at his feet – and capable of making crucial tackles in crunch moments.

Across the league’s defenders, he ranks fourth and sixth respectively for passing accuracy (96.13 per cent) and average carry distance with the ball (14.8 metres). Konsa’s ability to drive the ball high up the pitch has allowed Arteta's full backs to push on and invert effectively, meaning Ben White and Riccardo Calafiori can be extra men in the attacking line.

Konsa ranks first for interceptions (eight) and second for recoveries (20, behind Gabriel's 21) among Arsenal's defenders. Against Leeds he made three tackles and five clearances in shutting down Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and at Sunderland he was responsible for fending off the extremely physical Brian Brobbey.

On that cold night at the Stadium of Light, he stepped up on a mixed evening for his centre-back partner Gabriel, recovering from a penalty given against him for a tussle with Dan Ballard that was later deemed erroneous, and led the backline with his aerial duels and important challenges to claim another clean sheet.

And then there was the thundering tackle on former Villa team-mate Morgan Rogers to help Arsenal beat Chelsea in his first match at the Emirates Stadium and immediately endear himself to the home faithful.

Konsa's thundering tackle on a counter-attacking Morgan Rogers helped seal victory on his home debut for Arsenal

And Konsa also shut down Dominic Calvert-Lewin against Leeds in another 2-1 win

He recovered from a penalty being erroneously awarded against him at Sunderland to claim another clean sheet in what is proving to be a fantastic partnership with Gabriel

He has settled in well behind the scenes, too. Konsa is said to be very confident around the training ground with a good sense of humour, and is a proud father of young twins with his girlfriend Ronni.

His ease in adjusting to life at London Colney has been noticed by staff, and helped by those existing relationships, with Konsa especially close to Eze. There’s also a maturity he and fellow summer signing Bruno Guimaraes have brought to the squad, having operated at an elite level for a number of years. This was key in the absence of Saliba, who returned to individual training last week.

Arteta has a headache on his hands when the Frenchman is back fit, and isn’t set on a straight swap out. He’s challenged the England man privately to fight for his place.

For now, Konsa’s next task is to shackle his England skipper and Bayern Munich goal machine Harry Kane at the Allianz Arena in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Konsa boasts an impressive record against Kane, having faced him seven times. The defender has four wins against Kane’s teams and three losses, while Kane has only scored twice against him, both from penalties.

The seventh and most recent meeting came in October 2024, Konsa’s Villa beating Kane’s Bayern 1-0 at Villa Park.

‘The Villa-Bayern game… to beat them at home and keep a clean sheet… it was very special for the players and the fans,’ said Konsa. ‘I don’t really look much at those kind of stats (against individual players) but I am relishing the challenge.’

The talent has always been there. Konsa's formative years were spent at Senrab FC, in Forest Gate, London, with alumni including former Arsenal Invincible Sol Campbell and John Terry. Konsa was labelled the next Rio Ferdinand in his youth.

Konsa boasts an impressive record against Harry Kane in seven meetings, winning four of them. Kane has only scored twice against him, both from penalties

Delap was the latest to run into Konsa on Sunday and come up empty-handed

Konsa has stepped up to meet the moment throughout his career as he's risen from Brentford to Aston Villa, become an England regular and now taken to life at Arsenal with ease.

For all the attention on Kane’s extraordinary scoring record of 155 goals in 157 appearances at Bayern, Konsa has built his career on making life uncomfortable for the finest forwards in the game.

Erling Haaland, for example, has just one goal in six games against Konsa for club and country, and Delap was the latest to run into the England man's defensive wall.

On Wednesday in Munich, he has another chance to prove that his calmness and knack for a decisive intervention can carry Arsenal through their toughest test so far this season.

Sports.title: Arsenal striker Kai Havertz names ex-Spurs star Harry Kane as his inspiration as they prepare to go head to head in the Champions League
Sports.content:
Arsenal striker Kai Havertz names ex-Spurs star Harry Kane as his inspiration as they prepare to go head to head in the Champions League

Arsenal’s Kai Havertz has admitted Harry Kane is his inspiration as the pair prepare to face each other in the Champions League tonight.

Havertz pinpointed the similarities in style with the Bayern Munich forward, citing his ability to drop deep into the midfield rather than operating as a traditional No9.

When asked by Men in Blazers Media Network to name a player he has tried to model his game on, the 27-year-old said: ‘I love Harry Kane. For me he’s one of the best strikers I’ve seen in my life.

‘He’s probably also not a proper No9, but still the numbers he produces and also assists, and how he links up and helps the team when they’re deep or something is amazing – so he is definitely someone that I look up to,' said Havertz.

Kane scored 280 goals for Arsenal’s rivals Spurs and has 155 in 157 games for Bayern since his move to Germany in 2023.

But Havertz will be hoping Kane is off his game tonight as Arsenal travel to Germany to take on Bayern in the Champions League group stage. The Gunners will be looking to repeat the 3-1 victory they secured last season against Bayern.

Havertz, meanwhile, opened up on his friendship with fellow Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres as the pair continue their battle to be Mikel Arteta’s main striker.

Gyokeres signed for £67million in summer 2025 but has failed to nail down his starting role.

Kai Havertz admits he takes his inspiration from Harry Kane as a striker who also drops deep

Havertz has got the nod in eight of Arsenal’s 11 games so far this season and scored three times, while Gyokeres has been forced to settle for a bench role – starting only against Napoli, Lille and Ipswich – and is yet to get off the mark.

But despite their rivalry within the club, Havertz says their relationship is strong.

‘We connected well from day one and no-one is angry if someone else plays. I know Viktor, he wants to play every game like I do but when the referee blows the whistle or when the training session is finished we put that aside and be team-mates and achieve things together and that’s what we do. He is a top guy and a top striker.’

The pair are also padel partners and when asked who has the edge on court, Havertz added: ‘If you asked him he would say him for sure… I think he has more power but I have the better technique!’

Sports.title: Crystal Palace's nightmare start: The blunders that could cost Pierre Sage his job, how Steve Parish and Matt Hobbs sold him short in the transfer market - and why players feel worried and confused
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace's nightmare start: The blunders that could cost Pierre Sage his job, how Steve Parish and Matt Hobbs sold him short in the transfer market - and why players feel worried and confused

Pierre Sage is understandably under intense scrutiny after Crystal Palace's shambolic 5-0 thrashing by rivals Brighton.

But that must not distract from the inexcusable failures of Sage's bosses, chairman Steve Parish and sporting director Matt Hobbs, who have failed to create the conditions for him to succeed over multiple transfer windows.

It does not absolve the Frenchman of blame. He is not helping himself with how he is setting his side up defensively. But it does provide important context to the conditions he is working under.

Palace have conceded the most goals in the Premier League, 17 in seven matches. And it is not as though they have been unlucky: they have faced the most shots and shots on target of any team, conceded a league-high 252 touches in their penalty area and have the highest expected goals (xG) against. They have been inviting teams to score – and repeatedly failing to do things as basic as winning headers and clearing their lines at corners.

Ultimately, that comes down to the manager and his tactics. Sage's emphasis on an intense press is leaving an already vulnerable Palace defence exposed. In his 3-4-3 formation, both wing-backs push into extraordinarily advanced positions and desert the back three. Under Oliver Glasner last season, one wing-back would hold a deeper position when Palace attacked, ensuring four defenders were in place to cover and react to transitions.

But now, the set-up is unbalanced – allowing teams to pick Palace apart quickly and attack their fragile backline. The midfield is not helping either, with Adam Wharton increasingly isolated as Quinten Timber marauds forward. There is too much focus on being front-footed and not enough caution with the personnel Sage has to choose from.

Pierre Sage is under serious pressure at Crystal Palace after a disappointing start to the Frenchman's tenure

Palace have looked shambolic at the back, especially in their 5-0 thrashing by Brighton (pictured)

Palace have frequently tried to play out in tight areas with the back three and Wharton while the rest of the team push forward, leaving them just one sloppy pass – of which there have been plenty – away from disaster.

Palace have taken seven points from seven games this season, matching Manchester United, and have won twice. In that respect, they are not yet in crisis. But both of their victories were fortuitous. Against Nottingham Forest, they should have been 5-0 down inside the first 40 minutes and rode their luck before punishing the visitors' profligacy.

Similar could be said about their victory at Fulham, where the hosts scored twice despite having 3.14 xG and Palace overperformed theirs with freakish goals. Their defensive performances have been consistently unconvincing, to say the least.

Sources at the club have echoed that view, too. Some in the dressing room are concerned about the lack of control in games and have been left confused by Sage’s ideas. Questions have also been raised about whether Palace have done enough defensive work on the training pitch and been given enough instructions. Sage remains well-liked on a personal level, however.

Again, there is mitigation: Sage, who impressed in taking Lens to a historic second-place finish in Ligue 1 with a similar system last season, has been unable to field a consistent back three due to injuries and Axel Disasi’s suspension.

Perhaps he does not have the personnel to play how he wants at Palace, especially with a back three that lacks recovery pace to deal with counter attacks. But even if that is true, the onus is on the manager to be pragmatic and adapt. Aside from an anomaly at Leeds, where Palace kept a clean sheet and were solid defensively, there has been no sign of that.

Sage was fighting to save his job against Leeds, with Parish considering sacking him over Palace’s defensive vulnerability. Daily Mail Sport understands Parish and Sage met on the week of the game, and the Palace chairman urged his manager to concentrate on defending.

Sage's job is once again at risk and if Palace fail to improve against Besiktas on Thursday night, Parish may be forced to act. However, Sage’s saving grace could be the quick succession of fixtures, which would leave limited time to find a replacement.

Palace chairman Steve Parish (centre) must take some of the blame after appearing complacent about the club leaving their business late in the transfer window

Sporting director Matt Hobbs has also failed to give Sage the conditions to succeed

HOW SAGE WAS SET UP TO FAIL

Sage has created plenty of problems for himself and his relative inexperience has done little to help him navigate adversity.

However, the root of the problem lies with errors made by the club’s hierarchy. Sage’s predecessor, Glasner, was brave enough to call out their deficiencies in several scathing press conferences. His public criticism raised eyebrows but it was never misplaced.

Glasner grew tired of inadequate transfer business and repeatedly scolded Parish for it. Sage does not seem the type to air his dirty laundry in public, although he surely holds a similar opinion behind closed doors.

Palace are paying the price for a lack of urgency in the summer window. Glasner criticised the club for two things: late transfer business and a failure to build a deep enough squad. In fairness, they addressed the latter ahead of their second European campaign, with options in each position. But the late panic buys continued, most damningly at centre back – the position where Palace most urgently needed to strengthen.

Two centre backs arrived after the season started, despite Palace selling England international Marc Guehi in January without a replacement and losing France international Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea during the World Cup.

Not only did those signings arrive too late, leaving Sage limited time to implement his ideas amid a hectic schedule, but both represented a significant downgrade. Palace received £72million for Guehi and Lacroix but replaced them with an 18-year-old loanee in Honest Ahanor and Chelsea cast-off Axel Disasi.

Disasi, to his credit, significantly improved West Ham’s defence in the second half of last season, albeit as a wide centre back. At Palace, he has been forced into the middle simply because they lack a natural option for the role. It is, quite frankly, poor squad planning.

Ahanor is an exciting prospect but remains a work in progress. With Palace also developing their own young centre back, Jaydee Canvot, their back three lacks the experience and proven quality required at this level, as the thumping at Brighton demonstrated.

Lacroix and Guehi lifted those around them, whether Canvot, Chris Richards or both. Palace no longer have that commanding, standards-raising figure and look feeble as a result. In fact, Takehiro Tomiyasu, signed as an understudy on a comparable wage to Nathaniel Clyne, who left the club in the summer, has been Palace’s best performer in the back three when available this season. He is now sidelined with injury.

Palace have lost two high-quality international centre backs this year, and replaced them with an 18-year-old loanee in Honest Ahanor (pictured) and a Chelsea cast-off in Axel Disasi

Youngster Jaydee Canvot (left) is among the defenders suffering from a lack of experience around him and Sage's bold set-up

Parish was naive when reviewing the club’s transfer business in an interview with The Athletic last month. Five of Palace’s summer signings arrived after the season began, four of them on deadline day, denying Sage vital time on the training ground in an already curtailed pre-season because of the World Cup.

Parish claimed the fact business was done late becomes irrelevant as the season progresses, but that disregards the difficult position it places the manager in to begin with. Particularly heading into a campaign in which Palace will be playing every three days for much of the season.

Parish said: ‘The important thing is that you get to the end of the transfer window and you say: “Have we done good business for the club?” We needed to make a bit of money on transfers, we needed to strengthen the squad in a different way with loans so that we had the squad depth but we weren’t necessarily carrying that cost going forward. In three months’ time, nobody cares if you did it early.’

The reality is Palace were hamstrung this summer because they overspent in January, splashing £83m on Brennan Johnson – a Glasner request – and Jorgen Strand Larsen. And those January signings were only necessary because Palace had failed to build a deep enough squad in the previous summer window. Consistently poor planning – it has consequences.

Hobbs and Parish took the importance of recruiting genuine quality at centre back far too lightly and are now paying the price. At some point, Sage will likely be the fall guy. But at least one of the Palace chiefs should take responsibility for their errors.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez set to leave Man United in defensive overhaul, how abusive Leeds fans got to Sir Alex Ferguson despite Elland Road police guard, Harry Amass heads for exit and Kai Rooney's rapid rise: MAN UNITED CONFIDENTIAL
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s defensive rebuild next summer is set to signal the end of Lisandro Martinez’s Old Trafford career.

The Argentine landed himself in hot water after last week’s 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid when he criticised his employers over United’s transfer policy in the summer window, saying he expected more of director of football Jason Wilcox, but sources insist that would not be the reason for the defender's departure.

Martinez was fined by the club and apologised for the timing of his comments in a statement that added: ‘Everyone at the club is doing everything they can to make the team successful.'

The 28-year-old started Sunday’s 1-1 draw with Leeds at Elland Road, but came off at half-time with a thigh injury having already spent 20 months out of action during his four-year United career. When he is fit, Martinez has been a regular on the left side of central defence since moving to United from Ajax for £57million in 2022, making 115 appearances and scoring four goals.

But he will be out of contract at the end of June and is unlikely to sign a new one. United would be very reluctant to let the 2022 World Cup winner leave as a free agent, so it’s more probable that the club would trigger a 12-month extension in his contract and try to sell him in the summer.

United retain an interest in Jarrad Branthwaite having had two offers worth up to £50m rejected by Everton in 2024, and could try again in the summer.

Lisandro Martinez is set to leave Manchester United next summer to begin the club's defensive overhaul

United retain an interest in Jarrad Branthwaite (centre) having had two offers worth up to £50m rejected by Everton in 2024, and could try again in the summer

Uncertainty also hangs over the futures of Luke Shaw and Harry Maguire. Shaw is out of contract after 12 years at Old Trafford and doesn’t have an extension clause in his current deal, unlike Maguire who has a 12-month option to extend the one-year contract that he signed in April.

United have a decision to make on both players, but it's understood there are no doubts over Matthijs de Ligt's future at the club even though the Dutchman has been out of action for almost a year with a back injury that required surgery. De Ligt, who has been an unused substitute for the last two games against Leeds and Atletico Madrid, is under contract until 2029 with the option of another year.

Fergie under fire

It’s a measure of the bad blood between Manchester United and Leeds that Sir Alex Ferguson’s chauffeur-driven car arrived at Elland Road on Sunday protected by four police outriders.

The two clubs were taking no chances with Ferguson’s safety at one of the most incendiary fixtures in the English football calendar, and made sure that the legendary United boss got into the ground without any incident.

The 84-year-old is using a walking stick at the moment as he recovers from an achilles problem that has also required him to wear a protective boot.

Despite the efforts of the police and Leeds security staff, however, Ferguson was verbally abused by one fan in a video circulated on social media as he made his way from his seat in the stands – where he was sat with his former kit man Albert Morgan – to the directors’ lounge at half-time.

Ferguson dominated the rivalry with Leeds during his time as United boss, winning 20 of his 36 matches against them and losing only five.

If further evidence of the animosity between the two clubs was needed, ex-Leeds boss and current Canada head coach Jesse Marsch referred to United as ‘the scum’ when he congratulated Daniel Farke’s side on their performance in the 1-1 draw in a post on Monday.

Ferguson dominated the rivalry with Leeds when he was United manager, winning 20 of his 36 matches against them - the last of which being this 3-0 League Cup win in 2011

No Carrick summit

Contrary to speculation over summit talks between Michael Carrick and Wilcox at Carrington on Monday, Confidential understands the two men did not meet at the training ground.

Even though the players were off after Sunday's draw at Leeds before training and travelling to Italy on Tuesday for the Champions League clash with Como, Carrick and Wilcox didn't have an opportunity to get together after a tough week for both men.

Wilcox came under scrutiny in the wake of Lisandro Martinez’s bombshell TV interview in Madrid, while United’s 2-0 defeat by Atletico and a pair of 1-1 draws with Tottenham and Leeds in the Premier League left Carrick without a win in six games.

However, insiders say that Wilcox still retains the trust of minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and there is no appetite to change head coach despite Carrick overseeing United’s worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Amass heads for the exit

There is a growing expectation that Harry Amass will leave United in January after playing just 18 minutes of first-team football so far this season.

Even with a raft of injuries at left back, 19-year-old Amass has found himself on the outside looking in with right backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui and centre back Ayden Heaven all chosen ahead of him while Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu are sidelined through injury. His only appearance this season was a cameo off the bench in the 4-0 Champions League win over Sabah last month.

United were open to both a loan or permanent move for Amass in the summer, but their inability to recruit a new left back meant the club’s hands were tied. Burnley were among the teams who held talks before choosing not to proceed, and Confidential understands around a dozen Championship clubs are ready to come back to the negotiating table with the January window fast approaching.

Amass, who joined from Watford's academy three years ago, thrived on loan at Sheffield Wednesday last season, and with United out of the Carabao Cup and seemingly reluctant to use Amass even when stretched to the max in his position, expect movement for the youngster in the next eight to ten weeks.

Harry Amass is expected to leave United in January after only making one appearance this season, off the bench in the Champions League against Sabah

Tavernier a target?

United are one of the Premier League clubs being linked with a move for Bournemouth winger Marcus Tavernier in January.

However, Old Trafford sources say they are not proactively tracking the 27-year-old, who is also said to be attracting interest from Liverpool and Chelsea four years after he moved to the Vitality Stadium from Middlesbrough in a £10m deal.

Tavernier has been in fine form to start the season, scoring four times in seven league games including in Bournemouth's 2-0 win over Sunderland on Sunday that secured the Cherries their first three points of the campaign.

It’s understood rival clubs have been encouraged by Bournemouth’s willingness to consider selling players at the right price in January. England midfielder Alex Scott – who was on United’s radar before they signed Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos as part of a midfield rebuild in the summer – may be one of them if clubs offer between £80-100m.

Marcus Tavernier scored in Bournemouth's 4-4 draw at Old Trafford last season

While Wayne Rooney generates plenty of headlines behind a microphone these days, it was son Kai who made a statement on the pitch over the past week

Kai strikes right chord

While Wayne Rooney generates plenty of headlines behind a microphone these days, it was son Kai who made a statement on the pitch over the past week.

Injuries have been a source of real frustration for the 16-year-old, but he is fit again and back in the fold. Rooney made his UEFA Youth League debut for the Under 19s away to Atletico Madrid, and followed that up three days later with his Under 21s debut against Nottingham Forest.

He dropped back down to the Under 18s, also against Forest, to get himself back on the scoresheet but things are heating up nicely for Rooney who remains one of the only true centre-forward options in the academy.

Chido Obi is out on loan while Louie Bradbury has joined Stoke City. It means that Rooney takes on huge significance across the age groups, not least with United having used a false-nine system to this point in the Under 19s and Under 21s.

Sports.title: Man Utd transfer plans being put in place as injury timeline emerges for Benjamin Sesko
Sports.content:
Man Utd transfer plans being put in place as injury timeline emerges for Benjamin Sesko

As Manchester United's struggles continue to pile-up, a huge issue, which may require a transfer, is beginning to get worse

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has mounting injury issues at Manchester United (Image: Denis Doyle, Getty Images)

Manchester United may need to sign a striker in the January transfer window as a result of Benjamin Sesko's fitness issues. For the last six months, a shin problem has troubled the Slovenian.

‌



‌



He has also been forced to sit out the last five weeks as a result of a separate injury issue. United did not sign a new striker last summer, something Michael Carrick may be regretting.

‌



Recent reports have also stated Sesko is not expected to play again this year and may not return until February. If this is the case, United may need to attack the winter window to sign a new forward.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

According to the Sun, Sesko could remain sidelined for up to four months. That would rule him out until as late as February, meaning he would miss a considerable number of fixtures, reports the Manchester Evening News.

Carrick is expected to provide a clearer indication of his return date in the coming days, having indicated he would deliver a more definitive update at one of his forthcoming press conferences.

‌



When pressed on Sesko's condition, Carrick said: "We're hoping really soon that we'll have a clear picture. I'm not trying to delay it. Hopefully next time we speak.

‌



"Maybe not tomorrow, but by the end of the week, we'll have something a little bit clearer. There's a bit of work going on at the moment, so we'll see what comes out of that."

Sesko netted 12 goals last season following his high-profile switch from RB Leipzig, and has also faced stiff competition from Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo for a starting berth at the top of United's attack.

‌



So far this campaign, the striker has chipped in with two goals in six appearances across all competitions, including a powerful header in the 2-2 draw away at Everton and a finish in the 4-0 victory over Sabah.

View 2 Images Sesko's time at United has been disrupted by injuries (Image: PAUL ELLIS, AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Beyond Sesko, United are notably short of recognised centre-forwards. Rasmus Hojlund departed for Napoli this summer after the Italian club's Champions League qualification triggered a mandatory purchase clause, signing him permanently for £38m following his loan spell last season.

Zirkzee, meanwhile, has never truly been regarded as a conventional striker - he famously described himself as a "number 9.5" owing to his qualities being equally suited to both the No. 10 and No. 9 roles.

Article continues below

Last week, United were even linked with a swoop for former Tottenham Hotspur forward Troy Parrott, who has been putting in an impressive stint with Real Betis.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Fresh investigation confirmed as EFL 'ready to agree' punishment
Sports.content:
All the latest news on Manchester City's guilty verdict ahead of their appeal hearing, with the club now expected to receive a 'huge points deduction' and a fine

Hello and welcome to our live blog covering the Manchester City charges on Wednesday, October 21.

At the end of September, the Premier League confirmed that City had been found guilty on all charges relating to breaches of its financial regulations between 2009/10 and 2017/18. It was revealed that City had artificially inflated revenue by more than £900million through so-called 'sham' sponsorship deals.

City, however, have vehemently denied any wrongdoing and submitted an appeal against the ruling on October 1. In an official statement, the club maintained they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League" and claim they possess "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" to support their position.

Nevertheless, The Daily Mail have reported that the 'most likely' outcome is a three-pronged punishment for City, with the club expected to receive a 'points deduction which will guarantee relegation' and a 'huge fine'.

It's suggested that the sanction could include an additional points deduction that would virtually ensure City remain in the Championship for at least one further season, though the EFL would not be compelled to accept that penalty for one of their clubs. However, it's understood they would be prepared to agree to the points deduction.

Stay with us throughout the day for all the latest City charges news and updates...

Sports.title: Rebecca Menzies’ Breeders’ Cup dream shattered as Adonius set to miss cut
Sports.content:
Rebecca Menzies’ Breeders’ Cup dream shattered as Adonius set to miss cut

Despite his victory in a Group 2 race at host site Keeneland, the gelding is only sixth reserve for the Juvenile Turf Sprint at the same venue a week on October 30

View 3 Images Adonius: set to miss cut for Breeders' Cup (Image: PA)

Rebecca Menzies’ Breeders’ Cup dream with Adonius was shattered on Wednesday as her stable star is set to miss the cut.

‌



‌



Adonius has earned a huge following after wins at Musselburgh, twice, and Chester and second place finishes at Glorious Goodwood and York’s Ebor Festival. He then took his Durham stable to previously unscaled heights by winning the Grade 2 Indian Summer Stakes at Keeneland this month to give Menzies the biggest win of her 12 year training career with her first runner on US soil.

‌



Menzies and the American owners who had bought into the gelding expected that victory would put him in contention to secure a start in the £750,000 Juvenile Turf Sprint over the same course and distance a week on Friday.

‌



Value Scope Extra: Three jumps trainers with horses ready to strike first time out READ MORE :

But when the pre-entries were released on Wednesday, Adonius was listed as ‘not selected into the field’. As a result he has been placed on the also-eligible list as sixth reserve to get into the 12 runner final field following an assessment by a panel of international handicappers.

The horses that have made the field include Hell Of A Spin, who finished behind Adonius in the Molecomb Stakes before running third in the Middle Park Stakes. Two of the horses he beat at Keeneland are also above him on the reserve list.

View 3 Images Rebecca Menzies: hoped to run Adonius at the Breeders' Cup

‌



“Our dream looks to have been dashed,” said Menzies. “I am disappointed for the horse and the owners.

“I don’t understand why he is so far down the list and he has not been put up for winning the Indian Summer. You would have thought the course and distance win would have stood for something.”

‌



View 3 Images Adonius (nearest, red cap): gets up to win at Keeneland

She added: “This was a massive opportunity for our yard and now it looks like the trip has been cut short. We need a minor miracle to get in.”

Article continues below

Adonius has stayed in the US to prepare for the Breeders’ Cup since his victory and will continue his career in the US.

“We have a fit horse who is ready to run but nowhere to run him,” Menzies said.

Sports.title: Mark Allen bravely opens up on 10 week stay at mental health clinic after troubling TV interview
Sports.content:
Mark Allen bravely opens up on 10 week stay at mental health clinic after troubling TV interview

Mark Allen has opened up on spending 10 weeks in a mental health clinic before returning to play at the Northern Ireland Open in Belfast, sharing a candid statement after a difficult live TV interview.

View 2 Images Mark Allen has released a candid statement following his worrying interview (Image: TNT Sports)

Snooker star Mark Allen has disclosed that he spent 10 weeks in a mental health clinic before making his comeback in Belfast. The 2026 World Championship semi-finalist made his return on Tuesday before admitting that he could now walk away from the sport in a troubling television interview.

‌



‌



Allen, 40, suffered defeat at the Northern Ireland Open to close friend, Jordan Brown. It marked his return to play following his agonising semi-final defeat earlier this year, but it has now emerged he discharged himself from a clinic so that his daughter could see him in action for potentially the last time.

‌



The Pistol revealed in a post-match interview that he anticipated walking away from the sport and told TNT Sports: "At the minute I'm just trying to survive."

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The Northern Irishman appeared visibly distressed during the live television interview and, following his tournament exit, released a statement explaining why. Allen gave his thanks to everyone who had offered support and confirmed that he would continue treatment for his mental health.

"A statement on yesterday..... Everything I said in that interview was true," Allen posted on social media. "However, rest assured I'm doing my best to turn things round.

‌



"I have been in a mental health clinic for the last 10 weeks, finally discharging so I could attempt to play in Belfast I owed that to my family, in particular my daughter to see me play for what could be the last time....

"I also owed it to the fans who have supported me throughout my 21 years on tour I also owed that to World Snooker who have been amazing from day on in all this, in particular Simon Brownell and Neil Tomkins who have remained in touch regularly, even Simon paying me a visit in the clinic itself. ". "I'm not ok, but I'm ok in that itself. I've been much worse in the last few months than you saw yesterday.

‌



View 2 Images Mark Allen fell short in the World Championship semi-final (Image: Getty)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"I literally didn't see a future in anything.... My daughter kept me going, the therapists, staff and all the other patients were amazing and helped me through some really dark days I see the light now that I couldn't see before but I do now.

"I also know it won't happen overnight. I'm a work in progress!!!

‌



"My fight and determination on the table has always been there for ones to see. I need to show those same fighting qualities off it now for a while.

"Please don't detract anything from Jordan yesterday, he's been aware of my struggles and that can't have been easy to play in but he handled it with grace and skill as I knew he would. I'm proud to call him a friend.

‌



"However, rest assured I'm doing my best to turn things round... I hope the rest of the event is a success and I will continue my treatments going forward and then see what's ahead Thank you to every single message I have received on here, Instagram, Facebook, text messages and WhatsApp's, I've seen them all but a bit overwhelmed to reply right now. Just know that they have helped me a lot but I'm not going anywhere just yet!!!!

"I have so much to live for and this is only the beginning of my new journey Also, I was not made to do any interviews, I was simply given a choice and felt I owed it to everyone to speak. The media team at WST have been incredible through all this too. Thank you all x".

Article continues below

Following his win, Brown said that facing Allen was "easily the hardest match" of his snooker career. On Allen, he added: "I've missed him, I love him, just a great guy through and through. ".

While Brown continues his campaign at the Northern Ireland Open, Ronnie O'Sullivan, Judd Trump and Mark Selby have already departed the Waterfront Hall tournament, along with Allen.

Sports.title: Man Utd plot Lisandro Martinez contract extension as part of plan to land £50m star
Sports.content:
Man Utd plot Lisandro Martinez contract extension as part of plan to land £50m star

Lisandro Martinez is out of contract in the summer, but Manchester United could trigger an extension to protect their asset whilst they eye defensive reinforcements

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez is being tipped to leave Man Utd (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/the Press Association)

Manchester United could trigger the 12-month extension clause in Lisandro Martinez's contract so that they can recoup a fee for the Argentine as they prepare to rejig their backline.

‌



‌



Martinez, who has been at Old Trafford since Erik ten Hag signed him in 2022, has been heavily linked with a move away after publicly calling out the United hierarchy, accusing them of not investing heavily enough in the squad.

‌



This from a player whose own form has been criticised whilst he's spent long periods on the sidelines. United's defence has been neglected for several transfer windows and, only months into the season, it looks to be a decision that will haunt them until it is addressed.

‌



Martinez is out of contract this summer and his constant injuries, coupled with his attack on the club's bosses, had made it all but a formality that he would leave.

Atletico Madrid had been keen to land Martinez in the summer and the Daily Mail reports that United will trigger the extension clause in his deal to protect their asset, thus ensuring they will be able to land a fee for a player they spent £56million on from Ajax four years ago.

United have long had Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite on their radar and have seen offers reaching £50m previously rejected by the Toffees. They could still reignite that interest come the summer.

‌



Branthwaite has become a leading light on the blue half of Merseyside and could bolster a United backline that has seen a number of its major figures age. Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw have been stalwarts in Manchester, but may have their best days behind them.

Internally it is understood that the United hierarchy accept the summer's recruitment wasn't up to standard and missing out on a left-back may well prove costly. Shaw's injury has forced Michael Carrick into seeking makeshift solutions after he failed to sign Newcastle's Lewis Hall, who was high on his wishlist.

Sports.title: Jack Wilshere clashes with opposition manager in heated scenes after Luton win
Sports.content:
Jack Wilshere clashes with opposition manager in heated scenes after Luton win

Jack Wilshere pushed Barnsley boss Daniel Stendel after reacting to something he heard while shaking his hand following Luton's 2-1 win on Tuesday night

View 3 Images Jack Wilshere clashed with Barnsley boss Daniel Stendel after the final whistle (Image: YouTube/EFL)

Jack Wilshere sparked a touchline melee after clashing with Daniel Stendel in the aftermath of Luton's heated win over Barnsley on Tuesday night.

‌



‌



Luton picked up a much-needed 2-1 victory against the Tykes which moved them up to 13th place in League One. But the win came in controversial fashion, with Barnsley's Amani Richards booked for diving late on when he believed he was fouled for a penalty.

‌



Wilshere and Stendel were in heated discussion over the incident on the touchline and their bad blood continued after the final whistle. The former Arsenal and England midfielder went to shake Stendel's hand, only to immediately react badly.

‌



In scenes that were reminiscent of Thomas Tuchel and Antonio Conte's infamous handshake clash, Wilshere recoiled back and pushed the Barnsley boss away before pointing the finger at him.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The two were quickly separated as coaching staff from both sides piled in, with Luton goalkeeping coach Kevin Pilkington paying close attention to Stendel. The melee ended up sucking in players from both sides before eventually cooling down.

Wilshere told the BBC when asked about the heated scenes: "They want to win, we want to win. I have massive respect for them and what they're trying to do - I know they haven't got the results, but I can see what they're trying to do and they're a tough team to play because they've got some good players.

‌



View 3 Images Jack Wilshere reacted badly to the handshake (Image: YouTube/EFL)

"We got the win in the end and it got a bit heated but we shake hands in the end and everyone moves on.

‌



"Sometimes you see how together we are. We're all together. We're respectful but sometimes as well it shows everyone that we are together and a few players were in there as well. You want to be respectful but also to show togetherness."

Stendel is under mounting pressure, with Barnsley 22nd following a fifth straight defeat in all competitions, and he also tried to downplay the incident. “It was a misunderstanding between me and Jack Wilshere," he said. "But I tried to talk with him [after the game] and I think it's not a big thing.”

‌



View 3 Images Coaching staff from both sides piled in (Image: YouTube/EFL)

The Barnsley manager made three substitutions at half-time and was furious with his players. “We cannot accept the performance like in the first half. We want to do so much," he said.

Article continues below

“The atmosphere before the game in the locker room was so positive, and after one minute, the first set piece, we considered again the goal. And it's not a reason that we have not trained. It's not a reason why Luton is so good in that. It was the desire to defend the headers in this situation. And the second goal was the same. It was really frustrating in the half-time and I was a little bit louder."

Sports.title: Premier League club urged to retire mascot over 'wildlife' dispute
Sports.content:
Premier League club urged to retire mascot over 'wildlife' dispute

Crystal Palace have been asked to retire the American bald eagle that they present ahead of matches at Selhurst Park, with an animal rights charity saying the practice can be frightening

View 2 Images PETA have called for Crystal Palace to retire Phoenix, their mascot (Image: Steve Bardens - WSL/WSL Football via Getty Images)

Crystal Palace have been requested to retire their mascot, the American bald eagle Phoenix, immediately by PETA. The animal rights charity wrote a letter to the club's chief executive, Sharon Lacey, saying that 'wildlife doesn't belong in a football stadium'.

‌



‌



Phoenix participates in pre-match displays and joins supporters for photographs at Selhurst Park, and was present for the team's opening home match against Manchester City. The eagle succeeded Kayla, another American bald Eagle, who passed away in 2020 at 28 after suffering a heart attack.

‌



The south London side have been known as the Eagles since the 70s and introduced Kayla to matchdays in 2010. Phoenix first appeared ahead of a clash with West Ham in August 2024.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

PETA wrote to Lacey last month to say 'a bright stadium filled with boisterous fans is no place for animals and noting that under such conditions, birds easily become frightened, disoriented, and panicked', per the Athletic.

“When eagles are used for displays and entertainment, they are denied the opportunity to engage in their natural behaviour, resulting in frustration and stress,” the letter added. “They deserve better than to be used as an entertainment ‘prop’ to amuse the Eagles’ fans.”

‌



PETA senior corporate projects manager Dr Carys Bennett said: "Bald eagles are revered as symbols of freedom, yet Phoenix is being used as little more than a prop to entertain football fans.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



View 2 Images Crystal Palace's official live mascot American Bald Eagle "Phoenix" presented to fans (Image: Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty Images)

“ Crystal Palace already has a human mascot to energise supporters, so there’s no reason to drag a wild animal into a noisy, crowded stadium. PETA is urging the club to let Phoenix spread his wings and retire him from matchday duties for good.”

‌



The organisation claims to have records of incidents involving live mascots, including birds, being injured or killed in collisions with walls, windows and match balls.

In 2017, a Charlton Athletic fan was found guilty of attempting to punch Kayla at a League Cup match between the clubs. The incident was among those referenced by PETA.
