Sports.title: Featured Comment: Budget cap not to blame for lack of winning teams in F1 | Brief
Sports.content:
This week’s poll asks whether Formula 1 needs to rethink its budget cap as the series’ top four team have pulled further away from their rivals this year.

But reader @Skydiverian suggests it might not be realistic to expect F1 to regularly have more than four race-winning teams:

Four competitive teams has happened before but it’s still not great and the problem is as it always is, money. And I’d like to see more teams in a season have a realistic shot of winning races. It’s unfortunate that the stats are not on my side.

Pretty much since the late 80s the problem has been that the best teams could throw more money at the problem to fix it. Now, teams that are significantly behind can’t throw more money at the problem to catch-up due to the cost cap, rather than simply not having the money in the first place as was common in the 80s. (This season is interesting. It seems that Mercedes blew most of it’s cap early to get and maintain their advantage, whereas Red Bull didn’t and that’s in part why Max has had a better car the last two races. But it’s not like Williams or Aston Martin can fix their problems by spending more money to fix the deficit).

The problem is that ultimately there’s no easy fix, but spending millions to be the so-called best of the rest basically seems pointless if there is a very unlikely chance of a team outside of the top four having a realistic shot at the podium or even a win. And that’s always been a problem going back decades.

Some number crunching by looking at the history books: the 500th race was 1990 Australia, 1,100th being Vegas 2023. In those 600 races I’ve found six that were won by drivers driving for teams who finished outside the top four in the constructors championship.

That’s six of 600 races over 33 years where we had a winner driving for a team who finished outside the top 4 in that years constructors championship, 1% of all races. Seven if you count Johnny Herbert’s win at the Nurburgring which to me was a genuine surprise at the time. To me those stats aren’t good enough.

Whether that’s the fault of teams with no money, teams with too much money or teams with a cash limit so they can’t design their way out is up for debate. But my point is that I’d like to see more teams have a reasonable chance of winning. F1 has never really had that and will continue not to unless something changes (maybe by letting teams further down have a bigger budget the following season rather than just more CFD time).

I’d rather that at least 70% of drivers have a realistic chance of winning, ideally 100% of teams. It’s the reason I preferred IndyCar before Alex Palou showed up, results were unpredictable and smaller teams have a chance of getting a win or two. That’s just so rare in F1 and the current cost cap rules will continue to make unlikely.

@Skydiverian

Sports.title: Early coronation for Antonelli? Five talking points for the United States Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli could win the world championship this weekend in only his second year as a Formula 1 driver. Here are the talking points for the United States Grand Prix.

Will Antonelli clinch the title?

The odds are stacked heavily in favour of Mercedes’ new star clinching the title at some point, but most likely not this weekend. That said it is not beyond the realm of possibility team mate George Russell could have another poor weekend and come away point-less while Antonelli takes his ninth victory of the season, putting him over the line.

The title has been won at this track twice before, and both times it was by a Mercedes druver: Lewis Hamilton won the championship there in 2015 and 2019. But regardless of whether Antonelli does clinch the title this weekend it is clearly a matter of ‘when’ not ‘if’.

Verstappen dominating again?

The driver most likely to delay Antonelli’s championship celebrations is not his team mate but Max Verstappen. Red Bull have made a breakthrough with their RB22 and as well as winning the last two grands prix plus a sprint race, Verstappen could have taken victory in Baku as well with better luck.

He arrives at this weekend’s race looking like the driver to beat, with every indication he could dominate the final rounds of the season, setting himself up for a shot at the title next year.

McLaren’s driver headache

McLaren arrive in Austin in a curiously similar situation to last year: a clash between their drivers at the previous race in Singapore has created an obvious tension. What’s more, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri’s collision during the sprint race in Singapore was more costly than the one they had in the grand prix 12 months ago.

Norris’s radio messages during the grand prix gave the distinction impression he was looking for ways to make amends, having eventually accepted he was the one at fault for their collision. But above all the team will be anxious to avoid a repeat of the first-corner collision which wrecked their sprint race at the circuit 12 months ago. Particularly as a resurgent Red Bull are poised to relegate the reigning constructors’ champions to fourth place in the standings.

US teams’ driver decisions

Of the two teams competing in their home event this weekend, one has settled its driver plans for 2027. Haas has announced Rafael Camara as the replacement for Esteban Ocon, whose Formula 1 future is in serious doubt as few likely alternatives remain for next year.

Could Cadillac be one of them? F1’s new American team is yet to confirm its plans for next year. However its hopes IndyCar star Colton Herta would take Formula 2 by storm and make himself an obvious candidate for promotion have been dashed: he lies 19th in the standings, 181 points behind fellow rookie and championship leader Camara.

Are Colapinto’s die-hards paying attention?

Last week Franco Colapinto spoke out in criticism of the element of his fanbase which has sent vile abuse to his rival drivers, team members and FIA officials since he made his F1 debut this year. The Alpine driver told those attacking others in his name that they are not helping his cause in F1.

Will they take his words on board? We’ll get an indication the next time he is involved in any kind of incident on-track – however slight it may be.

Sports.title: On This Day: Ralf Schumacher wins Formula Nippon title despite spinning out | Brief
Sports.content:
30 years ago today Ralf Schumacher won the Formula Nippon title despite retiring two laps into a rain-lashed race.

Schumacher arrived at the final race at Fuji Speedway just two points ahead of team mate Naoki Hattori. But Schumacher spun out two laps into the rain-hit race (see 3’50 in the video below).

That left Hattori on course for the title, which looked increasingly secure as the laps ticked down. But conditions worsened, and seven laps from home he spun out too, handing Schumacher the 1996 title. Schumacher made his F1 debut the following year for Jordan (now Aston Martin).

Katsutomo Kaneishi won ahead of future Formula 1 driver Pedro de la Rosa. Another future F1 driver, Shinji Nakano, took fourth place behind Masahiko Kageyama. Just seven of the 26 starters were running at the finish.

Sports.title: Keith Thurman Expects Less Volume From Vergil Ortiz
Sports.content:
Keith Thurman is already spinning Vergil Ortiz Jr. as a more manageable problem than Sebastian Fundora, which tells you everything about how veteran fighters rationalize dangerous matchups.

Thurman is betting that a drop in incoming punches equates to breathing room. Trading Fundora’s exhausting, awkward flurries for Ortiz’s firepower is a terrible bargain.

Fundora drowned Thurman in non-stop punches, but Ortiz does not need triple-digit punch outputs to ruin someone’s night. He sits down on every single delivery, cuts off escape routes, and forces opponents into survival mode.

“Virgil might be holding back his volume, but his power is going to be more intense,” Thurman told MillCity Boxing. “So, once again, it’s dangerous.”

Thurman talking about Ortiz holding back volume sounds like wishful thinking from a fighter trying to talk himself into believing he will get space to operate. He even tries to compare the transition to his past fights against Shawn Porter and Danny Garcia. Porter brought a relentless dogfight, while Garcia offered pauses between exchanges that allowed Thurman to reset his feet.

“I think he’s going to be easier to match the volume, the two-punch combos, the three-punch combos,” Thurman said.

The fatal flaw in that logic is simple: Garcia let fighters off the hook. Ortiz hunts. Those quiet moments Thurman thinks he will exploit between short combinations will not be rest periods. They will be traps where Ortiz walks him into the ropes and forces him to backpedal under heavy artillery.

At 37, Thurman’s legs look gone compared to his prime. He used to circle the perimeter, plant his feet, fire a quick combination, and skip out of range before anyone could touch him. Against Fundora, he had no snap left to hold his ground, which is why he spent from rounds 3 to 6 of that fight purely in track-and-field mode.

If Thurman refuses to sit down on his shots, Ortiz Jr. will walk through him. A dangerous puncher only respects what is coming back at him. The moment Ortiz Jr. realizes Thurman is strictly on his bicycle and throwing nothing to deter him, he will pin his ears back, cut off the ring, and trap Thurman on the ropes. Without pop on his punches to gain Ortiz’s respect, running just delays the inevitable while draining Thurman’s dwindling gas tank.

The threat of a referee stoppage is very real here. Against Fundora, Thurman reached a point where he was offering zero offensive resistance, and ringside officials will step in every time if a guy looks like target practice and shows no intention of fighting back.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Backs Tyson Fury To Stop Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Frank Warren is convinced Tyson Fury stops Anthony Joshua inside the distance, pinpointing AJ’s defensive lapses during his own offensive bursts as the decisive flaw.

Fury’s timing and counterpunching remain central to Warren’s prediction. The promoter views the dynamic much like he viewed Daniel Dubois’s upset win over Joshua, even while admitting neither man is operating at their athletic peak.

“Styles make fights. I believe the same as I believed Daniel, when he fought AJ, he would knock him out and beat him. I think Tyson would do the same thing,” Warren said to Sky Sports Boxing. “I just feel that Tyson has his number, in my opinion. Maybe wrong. The one thing about AJ, as we all know, he can whack.”

Warren’s logic involves the split second Joshua commits to his combinations. While Joshua’s power creates danger whenever he fires, his delayed guard gives an elite counterpuncher clear targets before his hands return home.

“When he throws his shots, he leaves himself very vulnerable, and Tyson’s a good counterpuncher,” Warren added.

Capitalizing on those windows requires sharp reflexes, something that naturally diminishes with age. Warren admitted the bout will look different than it would have years ago, predicting a tighter, less mobile collision where neither heavyweight retreats.

“I think they’ll both be a little bit slower than they were,” Warren said. “I think it’ll be very exciting whilst it lasts.”

Warren dresses it up with complex talk about technical openings and counter angles, but the fundamental flaw is Joshua’s punch resistance. Once a heavyweight’s chin cracks, no amount of technical adjustment can compensate for it.

The warning signs were impossible to miss against Kristian Prenga. Surviving Dubois is one thing because Daniel hits with concussive force, but getting buzzed and nearly closed out by a fringe guy like Prenga signals that Joshua’s internal alarm system is permanently compromised. Every time clean contact lands, his legs betray him immediately.

Fury does not possess one-punch power, yet that makes little difference when the target crumples under ordinary pressure. With his towering frame and natural bulk, Fury merely needs to absorb the initial storm, step into the pocket, and let his hands go until something connects flush. A clean tap on a ruined chin does the exact same job as an explosive shot.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Aims To Become Undisputed Champion
Sports.content:
Las Vegas, Nevada – On Saturday night, Sebastian “The Towering Inferno” Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) defended his WBC junior middleweight championship at The Chelsea inside the Cosmopolitan Casino against the very tough and gritty Ermal “The Albanian Sniper” Hadribeaj (23-1-1, 8 KOs).

It was a much more challenging match than many expected; Hadribeaj tested Fundora on the inside by making him miss and countering him with an efficient attack. The Albanian Sniper’s total connect rate of 32.3 percent was more effective than The Towering Inferno’s 25.9

percent.

However, Sebastian did outland Ermal in total punches 202 to 144, outlanding him8 of the 12 rounds(Compubox). Fundora was able to score the finishing blow in the last second of the twelve-round fight, winning the fight by controversial knockout.

After the fight, Sebastian said, “It was an interesting fight. I had to go back and fight on the inside and show everyone again that I can still do that. It was dramatic to knock him out at the last second, but we’ll go back to the gym and fix some things.”

He added whom he’ll like to fight next by saying, “I want to go for undisputed in this division. We’ll break either Jaron Ennis or Josh Kelly down just like the last guy and the guy before that. We’ll keep breaking them down. When asked of the two whom he expects to win, Fundora answered, “I do favor Boots.” Meaning him and promoter Sampson Lewkowicz believe it will be Boots whom they’ll have to negotiate for the undisputed crown, but they appear they’ll be playing hardball in negotiations.

Lewkowicz told the media after the fight what he expects the terms of the contract to be, “It doesn’t make any difference…because we need each other. We need 50-50 because we want to unify. It doesn’t matter how many titles. I see so many st**d guys saying on the internet saying he has three belts. You have only two. People already saying he has three.

So many people saying he have three belts. Who’s he fighting? A bum? I respect boxing, and I tell you Kelly can fight.” Sampson went on to state he had already spoken to Jaron’s advisor on the expectations of terms, making it known it should be a 50-50 fight, and hopes they don’t deviate from it by requesting a higher percentage for themselves.

However, if the fight for undisputed does happen next year, the winner of the Boots-Kelly fight will be a three-belt holder bringing the WBA, WBO, and IBF titles to the table, with Fundora holding the single WBC belt. The undisputed showdown is a fight fans will want to see and will truly crown the junior middleweight king.

Hopefully both sides can come to an amicable agreement, and the fight won’t get derailed as were the contract negotiations between Boots and Vergil Ortiz Jr. For now, Sebastian will rest and wait for the Boots-Kelly winner and prepare for his next goal of becoming undisputed junior middleweight king.

Sports.title: Chris Algieri Doubts An 80% Canelo Alvarez Beats Christian Mbilli
Sports.content:
Chris Algieri argues that Canelo Alvarez must bring his absolute best to get past Christian Mbilli. His claim that Mbilli’s style naturally plays into Canelo’s hands doesn’t hold up, especially given the challenger’s relentless engine.

Algieri does give Canelo credit for stepping right into danger following surgery and significant time away, acknowledging the grueling physical test awaiting him.

“Can we give him a little respect for coming off a layoff and a surgery right into Mbilli?” Algieri pointed out to DAZN Boxing. “Yes, he has his faults. I think he falls right into Canelo’s style, but what Canelo are we getting? If Canelo is at all degraded, an 80% Canelo probably doesn’t beat Mbilli. He’s got to be top-notch for that fight.”

Even a peak version of Canelo might have struggled with this matchup. While aggressive fighters give Canelo plenty of targets, Mbilli refuses to give up the breathing room Canelo usually buys with crisp counterpunches.

Gennadiy Golovkin applied pressure behind a stiff jab, leaning on heavy single shots. Miguel Cotto relied on movement during the twilight of his prime. Neither fighter swarmed with the sustained, multi-punch bursts that define Mbilli’s game.

Canelo typically hurts opponents until they freeze. They back off, rethink their strategy, let him rest, and wait for his next opening. Mbilli simply ignores that script.

Mbilli isn’t invincible, of course. Charging forward recklessly leaves massive openings, and eating flush counter hooks could quickly check his enthusiasm. Canelo has the precision to make him pay for being aggressive. Yet landing clean shots is vastly different from dictating the tempo. If Mbilli walks through fire and keeps throwing, Canelo has to scramble back into a defensive shell before his lungs catch up with the previous exchange.

Managing that volume would test any elite fighter in his prime. Asking a 36-year-old coming off major surgery and ring rust to endure it is an entirely different proposition. Algieri is spot on about the danger here. His warning that an 80% Canelo falls short might ring true, but treating an ultra-high-volume brawler as tailor-made for him severely understates the threat.

If Canelo cannot discourage Mbilli inside the first four rounds, the math turns ugly very quickly. By round six, when Canelo’s output routinely dips and his feet go flat, he will be forced to shell up against the ropes while Mbilli pounds away at his arms, shoulders, and ribs. Heavy volume wears down legs just as fast as clean headshots, especially for an aging fighter carrying thirteen months of inactivity and repaired joints.

Surviving that kind of physical tax requires supreme conditioning and fluid defensive pivots. If Canelo is stuck playing defense just to survive the onslaught, he will not have the legs or the gas tank left to mount a mid-fight rescue. When a fighter relies strictly on finding one perfect counter shot to bail himself out, every missed swing empties the reserve that much faster.

In 2019, Canelo capitalized on a faded, battle-worn Sergey Kovalev, whose gas tank was depleted, waiting out Kovalev’s tired arm punches until round eleven to land the finishing blow. Now, the dynamic has flipped, and Canelo finds himself occupying the aging fighter’s corner against a younger, relentless pressure puncher.

Kovalev came into the fight at 36 with heavy miles and well-documented physical wear, and Canelo is carrying an even larger cumulative toll. With more than two decades in the professional ranks, chronic joint issues, and elbow surgery following a year on the shelf, the engine simply cannot turn over the way it once did.

The pattern across the Jaime Munguia, Edgar Berlanga, William Scull, and Terence Crawford bouts showed a fighter relying almost entirely on bursts, resting for extended stretches, and depending on defensive posturing to steal rounds on ring generalship. Against Crawford, the inability to sustain offense or dictate the terms of engagement laid bare what happens when elite opposition refuses to grant Canelo those customary rest periods.

Against Mbilli, relying on selective counterpunching becomes a dangerous gamble. Landing a crisp left hook or a sharp uppercut only helps if it forces the incoming fighter to step back, reset, and second-guess their entry. If Mbilli treats every clean counter as a cue to unload another four-punch salvo to the body, Canelo will never get the pauses he needs to recharge.

Sports.title: Abdullah Mason Targets William Zepeda Or Joe Cordina
Sports.content:
Abdullah Mason is targeting a December return against William Zepeda or Joe Cordina, with a lightweight unification fight or another defense of his WBO title under consideration.

Mason says nothing is signed, but those are the two names emerging for his next appearance. He is also willing to travel to the UK to face Cordina after being told visa issues prevented the British fighter from meeting him in the summer.

“Right now it’s looking like it could be a unification with Zepeda or a defense with Cordina,” Mason said to Brian Custer’s channel. “That’s what it’s looking like it could be. So I’m definitely ready to face anybody in that position.”

Zepeda would give Mason the opportunity to add the WBC belt and test himself against a pressure fighter who believes he can wear the young champion down. Asked about Zepeda’s claim that he would struggle to last 12 rounds, Mason declined to make a counterprediction.

“Two fighters got to step in the ring to really see how it’s going to go down,” he said.

That would be the harder physical test. Zepeda’s volume would force Mason to decide when to trade and when to use his feet. Mason’s willingness to fight aggressively could make it an action fight, but he would need to avoid letting Zepeda dictate how much work he does every round.

The Cordina option offers a different route, and Mason has no objection to defending on the challenger’s side of the Atlantic.

“If he’s had visa issues in the summer, I’m ready to go over there,” Mason said. “It’s a huge fight card in December in the UK. Why don’t I fight him over there if they can’t come over here?”

Mason did not identify the event or confirm a place on it. His December plans remain a target rather than a completed deal.

“Nothing confirmed, nothing signed off on, but that’s what it’s looking like, and that’s what we’re pushing for.”

Mason’s promoters at Top Rank rarely throw a young fighter into a risky fight when they can take an easier route to build an international footprint. Zepeda represents pure peril right now. His punch output breaks people down, and Top Rank knows Mason is far too young to be taking that sort of physical punishment if it can be delayed.

Letting Zepeda put more miles on the odometer before signing off on a unification makes total promotional sense.

Cordina is the soft landing spot. He gives Mason a recognizable British name to put on the record, introduces the young champion to UK fans on a big DAZN card, and presents minimal stylistic danger. Cordina likes to pick his spots from the outside and does not push a blistering pace, which plays right into Mason’s hands.

It would be a low-risk voluntary defense disguised as a big overseas trip, keeping Mason active, winning, and out of harm’s way while Zepeda’s prime ticks down.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Departure Brings Relief Within Zuffa
Sports.content:
Some inside Zuffa Boxing actually welcomed Shakur Stevenson walking away. When the planned Devin Haney matchup collapsed, the company found itself staring down massive financial obligations with zero marquee headliner to show for it.

Dan Rafael noted that parting ways worked out for both camps, despite the optics sting of Zuffa dropping a prized marquee acquisition right out of the gate.

“There are some people that are sort of relieved that they’re not going to, you know, go down that pit of that money,” Rafael said to Total Boxing.

The broadcast setup explains plenty about why Zuffa executives felt that way. Per Rafael, even if Haney versus Stevenson crossed the finish line, the US broadcast rights belonged to DAZN instead of Zuffa’s domestic partner Paramount+. Zuffa faced bankrolling an enormous purse just to drive its biggest potential viewership straight to a competing network.

Rafael pointed out that securing both men in the ring demanded north of $20 million just for the main event. Spending that kind of cash to cement Shakur as the promotion’s central figure, while asking Paramount+ subscribers to tune in elsewhere, looked like bad business.

When the Haney talks cratered, backup plans looked rough. Zuffa put a hold on Newark’s Prudential Center for January 23, but finding a credible dance rival for a hometown showcase proved tough. Footing an astronomical bill for a soft touch would leave Zuffa paying elite rates without the blockbuster that validated signing Shakur initially.

“I don’t think that everybody involved with Zuffa Boxing and/or their parent company TKO was that upset that they were able to separate because I think they might have had some buyer’s remorse,” Rafael said.

Shakur exiting before ever fighting under the banner definitely hurts Zuffa’s reputation, especially after hyping up the Haney clash. Still, the numbers explain the decision. Retaining Shakur only worked if Zuffa locked down the right opponents alongside favorable platform deals to balance the books. Once Haney slipped away, cutting ties cost far less than trying to patch up an expensive mistake.

Shakur commands elite, eight-figure purses, but his track record does not show independent pay-per-view drawing power or the ability to move tickets outside of a localized Newark gate. When a promoter guarantees that kind of money, the fighter has to generate massive subscription spikes, sell out neutral venues, or command major foreign site fees. Shakur has not done any of that on his own.

His safety-first, low-volume style makes that financial gap impossible to bridge. Fans want drama, sustained action, and knockouts. Shakur is technically brilliant, but his emphasis on distance control and minimal engagement often draws boos from casual crowds and turns off broadcast executives looking for viral, highlight-reel content. Promoting a fighter with that approach is an uphill battle, especially for an outfit tied to the UFC and TKO brand, where audiences expect relentless pressure and decisive finishes.

Paying top-dollar purses for Shakur to out-point mismatched opponents in tactical dull contests would have eroded fan interest and bled capital fast. Zuffa avoided footing the bill for an expensive, low-entertainment asset who brings little commercial leverage to the table.

Sports.title: Rafael Espinoza Wants Naoya Inoue Before Moving Up
Sports.content:
Rafael Espinoza has his sights set on Naoya Inoue, citing the Japanese superstar as his main reason to stay at 126 pounds. The WBO featherweight champion is also realistic, keeping the door open to move up to super featherweight if elite opportunities don’t materialize.

At 6’1″, the Mexican titlist wants unification honors at featherweight, knowing a win over Inoue punches his ticket straight into pound-for-pound conversations. He is even game to travel to Tokyo to make it happen.

“There’s also a big fight, the Inoue fight, and I think that’s the fight that would launch me into the world pound-for-pound rankings. That’s my dream,” Espinoza said to The Ring.

Landing the bout is another story. Espinoza presents an awkward, grueling test for anyone stepping up in weight. His height, wingspan, and relentless motor demand total focus. While Inoue possesses the timing and precision to exploit defensive holes, getting inside on Espinoza means walking through fire against a much bigger fighter.

Espinoza feels fully equipped to take the victory, even if he avoids bold knockout predictions.

“I have the qualities, the desire, and I have the reach, the height. I think I have power,” Espinoza said. “I’m not saying I’m going to knock him out. I’ve never liked talking that way, but I have a lot of hope that I can win that fight.”

Under the guidance of trainer Eddy Reynoso, Espinoza has spent recent camps dialing in his fundamentals. Rather than crowding opponents and absorbing needless shots, he has been drilling range control, leaning hard into straight punches from the outside.

The risk-to-reward ratio is completely tilted against Espinoza. Inoue gets credit for daring to be great no matter who he faces, but taking on a tall physical anomaly in his first outing at 126 offers minimal extra reward compared to the extreme stylistic danger.

Instead of Espinoza getting rewarded for ruling the division, Top Rank and Inoue’s team have plenty of reason to look elsewhere. Whether that means targeting a more conventionally sized titlist like Leo Angelo or Bruce Carrington, or grabbing the newly stripped WBA belt against an opponent with fewer stylistic advantages, Espinoza could find out the hard way that being the most dangerous man in the room often leaves you standing alone.

Sports.title: Jaron Ennis Signs Seven-Fight Extension With Matchroom
Sports.content:
Jaron “Boots” Ennis is locked in for the long haul after signing a massive seven-fight extension with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom. His eyes remain squarely set on collecting every piece of hardware at 154 pounds.

The timing couldn’t be better since IBF champion Josh Kelly signed fresh terms with the promoter on the exact same day. Because both champions share a promotional home, Hearn holds the inside track to set up an in-house unification clash. Whoever walks away with those three belts would then need only Sebastian Fundora’s WBC title to crown an undisputed king.

Ennis, now 29, picked up the WBA alongside the WBO belt after stopping Xander Zayas in Brooklyn this past July. Matchroom hasn’t announced a date or next rival just yet, but the mission statement is clear.

“I’m excited for my extended partnership with Matchroom,” Ennis stated. “Together we have aligned ourselves in all the right positions to get what I want, and that’s undisputed!” A seven-fight commitment gives Hearn plenty of runway. Still, locking down every title means hammering out contracts with rival camps, and Kelly’s signature alone doesn’t automatically settle fight terms.

Fundora brings another challenge to the bargaining table. His team wants an even split for any clash with Boots. If Ennis handles Kelly first to claim the IBF strap, he enters negotiations holding three belts, giving him total leverage to demand the lion’s share. Yet Fundora would still hold the final piece of the puzzle Ennis desires.

Ennis originally teamed up with Matchroom back in April 2024. That run saw him defend his turf in Philadelphia against David Avanesyan, beat Karen Chukhadzhian, then unify at welterweight by taking down Eimantas Stanionis in Atlantic City. Since jumping up to light middleweight, he obliterated Uisma Lima inside a single round before outclassing Zayas to become a two-division unified champ.

Hearn made his intentions clear, stating the entire Matchroom team plans to honor that loyalty by delivering undisputed opportunities on boxing’s premier stages.

Now comes the real work: turning contract ink into confirmed fight dates. Locking down Kelly gets the ball rolling toward three belts, setting up a clash with Fundora to finish the undisputed sweep.

Hearn had no choice but to lock Ennis down with a massive commitment, because letting him walk into Zuffa’s open arms would have been catastrophic for Matchroom’s stable. Dana White and the Zuffa operation are hungry for legitimate, elite names with actual substance, not smoke and mirrors. Losing Boots to that machine right when Anthony Joshua is clearly nearing the final bell would have stripped Matchroom of its true crown jewel in the United States.

The reality is that Hearn’s roster of genuine, division-ruling stars is paper thin. Ben Whittaker was hyped up as a generational sensation, but the matchmaking quickly exposed the ceiling there. When a promoter has to spoon-feed a 29-year-old fighter soft touches like Richard Rivera just to keep the show on the road, everyone sees through the packaging. Whittaker needs careful stage management and manufactured protection to stay afloat.

Ennis is the exact opposite. Boots does not need protective matchmaking or promotional smoke screens to look elite because the skill set is real. He can fight on the inside, switch stances seamlessly, punch with spite, and wipe out titleholders without Hearn having to hold his hand. While British promoters naturally lean toward homegrown cash cows, Ennis possesses the pedigree to carry the Matchroom banner globally and clean out an entire division on merit alone. Locking him in for seven bouts ensures Hearn stays relevant in the US market instead of watching Zuffa build their boxing empire around Philadelphia’s best fighter.

Ghana News.title: Court halts Common Registration Examination for 792 newly trained doctors
Ghana News.content:
The Human Rights Court 2 of the High Court in Accra has temporarily barred the Medical and Dental Council (MDC) from requiring 792 newly trained medical doctors to sit the Stage 1 Common Registration Examination (CRE) before obtaining provisional registration.

The injunction also applies to the Attorney-General and the Ministry of Health, preventing them from enforcing the examination requirement until the court hears the substantive case and an application for an injunction on notice.

The legal action was brought by the Federation of Ghana Medical Students’ Associations (FGMSA) and the affected students.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, the federation said the court’s decision effectively suspends the examination, which had been scheduled for Thursday, October 22.

The examination was a prerequisite for the affected graduates to secure provisional registration and commence their housemanship.

FGMSA has called on all parties involved to comply with the court’s directive while the legal process continues.

The federation stressed that decisions with implications for the professional careers of graduating medical and dental students must be guided by the law, fairness and due process.

It also expressed gratitude to its legal representatives, the affected graduating classes and medical and dental students for their support throughout the process.

According to the federation, further information on the case will be made available through its official communication channels.

Ghana News.title: GTA unveils December in GH 2026 calendar with 150 events
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Tourism Authority has unveiled the official calendar for this year’s December in GH, with more than 150 events registered nationwide and Accra accounting for over 100 planned activities.

The launch, held at Labadi Beach Hotel, brought together stakeholders from the tourism, culture and creative arts sectors to discuss the country’s festive season programme under the Black Star Experience.

In her speech, the Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Abla Dzifa Gomashie, urged stakeholders to focus on showcasing the country’s culture, heritage and hospitality rather than debating the name of the festive season.

While acknowledging the popularity of the term “Detty December”, particularly among young people, the Minister said emphasis should be placed on encouraging more people to Experience Ghana.

This year’s celebration is being held under the theme “Ghana to the World”, reflecting the country’s ambition to promote its cultural identity, creative industries and hospitality to international audiences.

The Minister described December as an important period for Ghana’s tourism industry and a homecoming for Ghanaians abroad, Africans in the diaspora and friends of Ghana.

She stressed that the initiative’s success should be measured not only by visitor numbers and entertainment events but also by the economic opportunities generated for local communities and investment.

Gomashie called for the benefits of the festive season to reach a broad range of businesses and professionals, including tour operators, hoteliers, content creators, musicians, fashion designers, artisans and young entrepreneurs.

The Minister also announced that Ghana is collaborating with the African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD) to host the inaugural African Festival of Arts, Culture and Creatives (AFESTACC) from 9 to 12 December 2026. The event is expected to bring together stakeholders from across Africa and the diaspora to celebrate African creativity, strengthen cultural exchange and explore investment opportunities in the creative economy.

She urged tourism and hospitality businesses to prioritise service excellence, visitor safety and reasonable pricing, noting that every interaction contributes to Ghana’s reputation as a welcoming destination.

Visitors are also encouraged to explore attractions beyond Accra, highlighting the importance of promoting tourism across all 16 regions.

In her remarks, the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA), Maame Efua Houadjeto, described December in GH as an opportunity for visitors to experience the country through its music, festivals, heritage sites, cuisine, fashion and community celebrations.

The GTA CEO urged event organisers to give Ghanaian performers and creatives prominent roles, fair compensation and opportunities to reach international audiences. She also encouraged businesses to work more closely with local suppliers and entrepreneurs to ensure that tourism spending supports livelihoods.

Houadjeto disclosed that more than 150 events had already been registered nationwide for the 2026 festive season, with Accra accounting for more than 100 planned activities.

The 2026 edition of December in GH is scheduled to run from 1 December 2026 to 3 January 2027 as part of Ghana’s broader Black Star Experience tourism initiative.

Through the campaign, Ghana hopes to strengthen its position as a destination for cultural and heritage tourism while turning the festive season into a platform for sustainable economic growth, creative expression and deeper connections with the global African community.

Ghana News.title: Mahama to appeal to Putin for ceasefire at Russia-Africa Summit
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama says he will appeal to Russian President Vladimir Putin to agree to a ceasefire when he travels to Russia for the Russia-Africa Summit next week.

Speaking at the Financial Times Africa Summit in London, President Mahama said he intended to use the visit to urge the Russian leader to halt hostilities.

“Indeed, I'm going to Russia for the Russia-Africa summit and try to convince President Putin to have a ceasefire if I can,” he said.

The President also defended Ghana’s investment partnerships with countries across the world, dismissing suggestions that competition among global powers should dictate where the country seeks investment.

“We are friends to all and enemies to none. And Ghana's policy of non-alignment has served us well. And so we welcome investors from all over the world,” he said.

He stressed that Ghana’s approach was focused on attracting investment that benefits both the country and its partners, rather than allowing geopolitical rivalries to shape economic decisions.

“It's not about competition. It's about investment and a fair return to everybody, including ourselves,” he said.

President Mahama said Ghana maintained friendly relations with the United States, the European Union, China and Russia, adding that its non-aligned foreign policy continued to guide its international relations.

President Mahama also outlined plans to end the export of raw minerals by 2030, saying the government wanted to expand local processing, create jobs and retain more value from the country’s natural resources.

He said achieving the target would require partnerships with investors to establish industries capable of processing raw materials locally.

The President argued that investment should generate wider economic benefits for surrounding communities, rather than creating isolated pockets of wealth.

“We've gone past the time where you had enclaves of prosperity and surrounded by impoverished communities. It's in the interest of the investor to have a safe environment. You cannot have prosperity in the midst of poverty. That itself is a danger to investments. And so it's a win-win. It's not a zero-sum game,” he said.

He cited gold as an example of progress, revealing that 70 per cent of Ghana’s gold is currently refined locally before export.

The government is also targeting the domestic processing of at least 50 per cent of cocoa beans produced annually.

President Mahama said expanding local processing in both sectors would support job creation, strengthen domestic industry and enable Ghana to retain a greater share of the value generated from its natural resources.

Ghana News.title: 94.7% of SHSs named in sexual abuse reports are Category B or C, amid soaring demand for Category A schools
Ghana News.content:
Almost 95% of the senior high schools named in reported sexual abuse cases since 2015 are Category B or C. The figure reflects school numbers, not a safer Category A. It comes as 313,283 candidates picked Category A first in the 2026 placement, for 76,417 declared vacancies.

JoyNews Research analysed 44 reported cases of teachers and school heads accused of sexually abusing students. Eighteen were in senior high schools, naming 19 distinct SHSs that match the Ministry of Education's 2026 Second Cycle Public Schools Register. One is Category A, seven are Category B and 11 are Category C. The data does not show why parents choose the schools they do, and it does not prove that Category A is safer.

Where the reported cases are

Category SHSs in reports Share of SHSs in reports A 1 5.3% B 7 36.8% C 11 57.9% All 19 100%

Source: Media Monitoring/JoyNews Research calculations; Ministry of Education 2026 Second Cycle Public Schools Register

Categories B and C account for 18 of the 19 schools (94.7%), largely because most schools in the register are Category B or C. Category A makes up 8.2% of schools in the register, so about 1.6 of the 19 would be expected to be Category A if reports were spread evenly. The actual count is one. That gap is less than one school, too small to suggest Category A is safer.

The only Category A school is St Louis SHS in Kumasi, where a rape-related interdiction was recorded in 2018.

Category B: KNUST SHS, Kumasi Girls SHS, Labone SHS, Benkum SHS, Okadjakrom SHTS, St Francis SHTS (Akim Oda) and Nkwatia Presby SHS.

KNUST SHS, Kumasi Girls SHS, Labone SHS, Benkum SHS, Okadjakrom SHTS, St Francis SHTS (Akim Oda) and Nkwatia Presby SHS. Category C: Ejisuman SHS, Sawla SHS, Obuasi SHTS, Dzodze-Penyi SHS, Bole SHS, Asankrangwa SHS, Assin Manso SHS, Nyankumasi SHS, Obiri Yeboah SHS, St Joseph SHS (Mampong) and Assin North Community Day.

Of the six SHS cases since January 2025, three involved Category B schools and three Category C. None involved Category A. Six cases are too few to show a difference.

Category A demand far exceeds its seats

Category First-choice candidates Declared vacancies Gap A 313,283 76,417 236,866 more candidates than seats B 176,614 250,366 73,752 vacancies beyond first choices C 123,577 468,652 345,075 vacancies beyond first choices

Source: Ministry of Education/2026 Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS)

The placement data shows 4.1 first-choice candidates for every Category A place. Category A holds 9.6% of the 795,435 vacancies declared in Categories A, B and C, yet drew 51.1% of the 613,474 first choices made across those categories. The Ministry put total declared vacancies at 859,828; on that base, Category A's share is 8.9%.

Categories B and C together declared 719,018 vacancies. That is 114,451 more than the 604,567 candidates who qualified for placement in 2026.

The Ministry said 527,932 qualified candidates (87.3%) were placed automatically. Deputy Education Minister Dr Clement Apaak said on September 8, 2026 that the remaining 76,635 were not automatically placed, largely because of high demand for Category A schools. He described the problem as a mismatch between where vacancies exist and where candidates want to go, not a shortage of places.

Vacancies are also not interchangeable: they depend on programme, boarding or day status, gender and location.

Does Category A mean safer?

The evidence does not support that assumption. Reported cases appear in all three categories, and Category A's share of them (5.3%) is in line with its small share of schools (8.2%).

Nor can the data say why candidates prefer Category A. Academic performance, reputation, facilities, boarding and perceptions of safety may all play a part. Neither dataset shows how much weight families give to each.

The central question is whether parents have access to reliable, comparable information on safeguarding in individual schools. A school’s category label does not provide that assurance. However, the concentration of reported sexual abuse cases in particular school categories could influence parental preferences and, potentially, demand for those schools. Whether it has actually done so requires further evidence.

Accountability remains a gap

The last time the Ghana Education Service published the names and schools of teachers it had dismissed was November 2018. That list named 10 teachers. Six were sacked for sexual misconduct, four of them at senior high schools, none of which is Category A.

GES has since reported more dismissals without names. On October 15, 2026, Deputy Director-General Dr Issahaque Munawaru said the GES Council had approved about 15 dismissals this month in sexual harassment cases dating back to 2021. On October 20, GES announced that 10 teachers had been dismissed and one appointment terminated for sexual misconduct. Neither announcement named the teachers or their schools.

In the cases JoyNews Research reviewed, recent SHS cases show interdictions with no public final outcome, and no SHS head has been convicted. These findings reflect the records reviewed and are not proof that no further disciplinary action has occurred.

Without names or schools, parents cannot link outcomes to the allegations they have heard about, or judge how consistently cases are handled. In a placement system this competitive, transparent safeguarding records would tell families more than a category label.

Ghana News.title: Akandoh inspects National Bed Management System to address ‘no bed syndrome’
Ghana News.content:
The Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, has inspected the National Command Centre for Bed and Referral Management at the Greater Accra Regional Hospital as part of efforts to address Ghana’s persistent ‘no bed syndrome’.

The system is designed to provide real-time information on bed availability at participating hospitals, allowing emergency response teams to identify suitable facilities for patients before dispatching ambulances.

It is also expected to improve the referral process, reduce delays in emergency care and ensure more efficient use of available hospital beds.

During the inspection, Mr Akandoh said the system would help address situations where patients are turned away from hospitals despite beds being available at other facilities.

He explained that the platform would also enable health authorities to monitor emergency patients who spend more than 24 hours on a bed and investigate the reasons for the prolonged stays.

The Minister said the initiative forms part of broader efforts to strengthen emergency care capacity at selected teaching and regional hospitals, including Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, Greater Accra Regional Hospital, the 37 Military Hospital and Tamale Teaching Hospital.

Project Lead for Bed Management, Dr Justine Osei, disclosed that more than 650 hospitals had been captured in the system, with over 5,000 beds mapped for monitoring and regular updates.

The pilot phase currently covers teaching hospitals, Greater Accra Regional Hospital and the University of Ghana Medical Centre.

Beyond tracking bed availability, the system monitors ambulance movements and helps match patients to appropriate health facilities based on available beds, medical needs and distance.

The pilot is currently supported by 10 ambulances in the Greater Accra Region and another 10 in the Ashanti Region.

The Ministry of Health plans to extend the system to all regional hospitals before rolling it out to district-level facilities nationwide.

Ghana News.title: Ghanaian jailed in US for using relative’s identity to secure job
Ghana News.content:
A 29-year-old Ghanaian, Linford Atakora, has been sentenced to approximately nine months in federal custody in the United States for fraudulently using the identity of a relative who is an American citizen to obtain employment at a home health agency.

Atakora was sentenced by US District Court Judge Daniel L. Hovland on a felony charge of misuse of a Social Security number. The sentence accounts for time already served in federal custody.

In addition to the sentence, the court ordered his removal from the United States to Ghana.

US Attorney Nicholas W. Chase announced the sentence, detailing how Atakora allegedly used his relative’s personal information and identification documents to secure employment despite lacking the necessary authorisation to work in the country.

According to court documents shared by the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of North Dakota, the incident occurred in March 2024 when Atakora applied for a job at Love & Care Inc., a home health agency located in Bismarck, North Dakota.

During the application process, he presented his relative’s driver’s licence and Social Security card, using the individual’s name, date of birth and Social Security number to establish his identity.

Atakora subsequently completed an Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Form W-4, Employee’s Withholding Certificate, and an employee information form using the same information to facilitate his employment.

Court documents indicate that Atakora did not possess a valid Social Security number and was not authorised to work in the United States.

His alleged misrepresentations had financial implications for the home health agency, which, as a result, falsely received ineligible units and claims totalling $51,435.63 from the US Department of Health and Human Services.

The case highlights the legal consequences of using another person’s identity to obtain employment and access employment-related benefits in the United States.

“This case serves as an important reminder to North Dakota workers and employers that working under another person’s identity or social security number to circumvent immigration work requirements is a federal crime,” Mr Chase said.

He added that his office would continue collaborating with state and federal law enforcement partners to investigate and prosecute similar offences.

The prosecution follows broader efforts by the US Department of Justice to address fraud involving public funds and federal benefit programmes.

On April 7, the department announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division, tasked with investigating and prosecuting individuals involved in fraud against the American public.

The initiative supports President Donald Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a government-wide effort chaired by Vice President JD Vance to tackle fraud, waste and abuse within federal benefit programmes.

Atakora’s case was investigated by the Social Security Administration’s Office of Inspector General and prosecuted by Assistant US Attorney Jonathan J. O’Konek.

The court’s order requires Atakora to be removed from the United States to Ghana following the proceedings.

Ghana News.title: Websites taken offline across UK & Europe as ‘critical’ security flaw hits dozens of government sites
Ghana News.content:
Edinburgh and Oxford Council, as well as the online home for The Traitors, were taken down, as was the Met Police website.

According to internet monitoring website Down Detector, online gaming platform Steam, Google Drive and WordPress were all down alongside a raft of local authority websites.

Error messages were displayed on the Bristol, Lambeth and Barnet council websites.

Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities.

It comes after the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) urged UK organisations to prepare for emergency updates to software used to run websites around the world, amid fears hackers could exploit the weaknesses to break into their systems.

Fixes were due to be released at 3pm BST on Wednesday, October 21, although they could arrive earlier.

The NCSC warned: “Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated.”

The flaws affect PHP, software that works behind the scenes to keep websites running, including those built using popular platforms such as WordPress.

European cyber officials have warned that the weaknesses could allow hackers to run their own commands on vulnerable systems without needing to log in. Full details of the flaws and which versions are affected have yet to be published.

The warning means some website owners could face having to temporarily take their services offline while they wait for protection to be put in place.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Russia to send first diesel tanker to the US amid Trump deal
World.content:
Russia will send on Thursday its first diesel tanker to the US to an undisclosed port.

Share Russia to send first diesel tanker to the US amid Trump deal on social media

Russia will send its first tanker of diesel fuel to the United States on Thursday, Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters amid a deal with US President Donald Trump.

The vessel will have 40,000 tonnes of fuel, but Novak, who made his remarks on Wednesday, did not name which US port the fuel would be delivered to.

Russia lifted its ban on diesel exports on October 9, which Moscow originally put in place to tackle the country’s shortages as Ukrainian-led drone strikes hindered production capacity.

The shipment comes despite setbacks for Russia’s diesel output. Earlier this month, Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence said that drone strikes knocked out at least half of Russia’s oil refining capacity, forcing cuts at Russia’s top diesel-producing refineries.

“Additional shipments will follow, of course. There were agreements reached between the two leaders. We will meet the United States’ needs, to the extent of our capabilities,” the RIA Novosti news agency quoted Novak as saying.

That was echoed by US special envoy Steve Witkoff, who has been meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin for talks in St Petersburg.

“We are preparing deliveries of several vessels, the tankers, right now. They will go one after another. The financial component should be provided,” he said, adding that Russia would also be able to supply fertilisers in “large quantities” to the US market.

US President Donald Trump had previously said that Moscow would export 300,000 tonnes, or 2.25 million barrels, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”.



US consumers have continued to face high prices at the petrol station, particularly for diesel fuel, a pressing point as the country heads into midterm elections in less than two weeks. The average price for a gallon of diesel is $6.31 ($1.70 per litre), according to the American Automobile Association (AAA). While prices remain well over the $6 mark, they are on the downturn. The average price a month ago was $6.51.

World.title: Musk pledges $10bn in SpaceX shares for US children: Who really gains?
World.content:
The pledge, which Trump says will go through accounts with his name, comes two weeks before the US midterms.

Share Musk pledges $10bn in SpaceX shares for US children: Who really gains? on social media

Elon Musk has pledged to give one SpaceX share to every child in the United States next year – a gift that could be worth more than $10bn.

“This will be the first of many,” the world’s richest man wrote on X on Monday.

About 73 million children under 18 live in the US, according to US Census Bureau data.

At Friday’s closing price of $146.03, the pledge would be worth about $10.7bn.

President Donald Trump thanked Musk on his Truth Social platform, and claimed the shares would be given to children “through TRUMP ACCOUNTS”, the tax-friendly investment accounts for children created under his signature tax and spending law last year.

The pledge comes two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections.

Musk is the biggest known donor in the run-up to those elections, having given more than $276m to Republican groups since July.

Musk has not said which children will qualify, when the shares will be handed over, or how.

So how might the giveaway work, and who stands to gain?

Here’s what you need to know:

How much is a SpaceX share worth, and how much is Musk giving away?

SpaceX, the world’s seventh-largest company, began trading on the Nasdaq in June at an initial public offering price of $135 per share.

That price has been volatile. SpaceX shares have fallen 35.3 percent since peaking days after the listing.

The shares are currently trading at around $146 a share. Every $1 move in the share price will change the gift’s value by about $73m.

Musk owns 4.8 billion shares in SpaceX outright, according to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in August.



Including unvested awards and stock options, his stake rises to about 6.4 billion shares, or 48.4 percent of the company.

Giving away 73 million shares would reduce his outright holding by about 1.5 percent, barely affecting his control of the company. That’s because his voting power, which is currently about 82 percent because SpaceX has two classes of shares, would fall by only 0.1 percentage points, according to a Bloomberg Opinion calculation.

It would be the largest single gift linked to Trump accounts so far.

How would the shares reach children?

Musk has not said.

Trump said the shares would be held in Trump accounts, and Musk thanked Brad Gerstner, the tech investor behind the accounts, for “helping enable this”.

Nearly 70 million Trump accounts have been opened, one for every child under 18 with a Social Security number, according to the White House. Investments held in Trump accounts can roll up with tax deferred until they are withdrawn when a child turns 18. Alternatively, they can be rolled into a tax-friendly IRA – a retirement account for adults – and continue with the tax-friendly status.

Under Treasury rules published on September 30, donors can now gift individual company stock to children via the accounts. Families and friends making regular contributions to a child’s Trump account are limited to investing low-risk index funds.

Families cannot refuse the shares on behalf of their children and generally cannot sell them for five years, or until the end of the year the child turns 17 if that comes sooner.

Musk cannot sell or trade most of his SpaceX shares until June 2027, the Wall Street Journal reported.

Who gains?

The accounts carry the president’s name, and Trump has tied himself closely to the gift.

He thanked Musk on Truth Social, saying the pledge was “exactly what was envisioned when we created TRUMP ACCOUNTS”.

The White House has presented the accounts as a signature achievement of Trump’s tax law, noting that “every single Democrat voted against” the legislation.

The pledge also marks a public reconciliation. Musk and Trump fell out in 2025 over Trump’s tax-and-spending bill, a rift Trump later called a “little dispute”.

Children will be gaining a share for free, but the gift could also save Musk money.

Donors who give appreciated stock to charity avoid capital gains tax and can usually claim a deduction, the US broadcaster CNBC reported.

As SpaceX’s founder, Musk paid very little for his shares, and selling $10.7bn of them could mean a tax bill of up to about $2.5bn.



It is “a popular practice for particularly high-income taxpayers that would otherwise be paying a high rate”, Will McBride, chief economist at the Tax Foundation, told the broadcaster in May.

Ann Lipton, a law professor at the University of Colorado Boulder, told Inc. magazine that millions of shareholders unable to sell would also have an interest in SpaceX’s success and in “minimising its regulatory burdens”.

For Mitchell Downey, an economist at Stockholm University’s Institute for International Economic Studies who studies political influence in the US, the more striking part of the pledge is what he called “the horseshoe aspect of this” – the idea that right-wing and left-wing policies can curve around and meet.

For decades, progressives have backed the concept of Child Development Accounts, investment accounts for every newborn designed to reduce inequality in wealth, he said. The idea was associated with groups such as the Democracy Collaborative but struggled to gain federal support. Now the idea may become more mainstream as a result of Musk’s gift and Trump accounts.

“It always felt like it might be out of reach,” Downey said. “But I don’t see how Musk’s proposal would be possible without building some infrastructure like this.”

Why is the timing important?

The pledge comes just two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the two houses of Congress. All seats in the House of Representatives and one-third of the Senate are up for re-election.
