A careful examination of the FCCPC Sales Promotion Regulations, 2026, reveals provisions that extend considerably beyond ordinary consumer protection and enter areas traditionally associated with lottery licensing, gaming supervision and the administration of games of chance.

Part I, Regulation 1 expressly extends the application of the Regulations to lotteries, digital platforms and promotional activities across all sectors of the economy.

More troubling is Regulation 3, which provides that promotions constituting lotteries under the National Lottery Act, 2005, must comply with that Act and seek the approval of the National Lottery Regulatory Commission (NLRC).

This provision is particularly objectionable.

It expressly invokes a federal lottery licensing framework whose application within the States was invalidated by the Supreme Court. It also directs promoters towards the very federal regulatory institution whose former authority over lotteries within the States was constitutionally challenged and judicially restrained.

The Federation considers this an unacceptable disregard for the legal consequences of the Supreme Court’s decision.

The contradictions extend beyond Regulation 3.

Under Part II, the Regulations introduce mandatory registration of sales promotions with the FCCPC, payment of prescribed fees, issuance of registration certificates, and powers to refuse, suspend or revoke registration.

Part VIII goes further by empowering the FCCPC to supervise prize draws, monitor winner selection, demand information concerning random selection algorithms and order a re-draw where irregularities are suspected.

These are not merely incidental consumer protection measures. Where applied to promotional lotteries and games of chance, they are substantive regulatory functions ordinarily exercised by competent gaming authorities.

Similarly, Regulation 64 expressly contemplates cooperation between the FCCPC and the National Lottery Regulatory Commission where a promotion contains elements of a lottery.

The FSGRN finds it extraordinary that a regulatory instrument introduced in 2026 would continue to present the former federal lottery regulator as the relevant institutional authority without adequately reflecting the Supreme Court’s judgment of November 2024.

The Federation rejects any arrangement that would require operators to obtain a second federal approval for lottery activities already subject to the lawful jurisdiction of State gaming regulators.

Such duplication would create unnecessary compliance costs, regulatory uncertainty, conflicting administrative requirements and avoidable barriers to investment.

More fundamentally, it would undermine the constitutional autonomy of the States.

Consumer Protection Must Not Become a Pretext for Regulatory Encroachment

The FSGRN recognises and respects the statutory mandate of the FCCPC to protect Nigerian consumers against unfair, misleading, deceptive and exploitative commercial practices.

Indeed, State gaming regulators share these objectives.

Across the Federation, gaming authorities already exercise oversight over promotional lotteries, prize draws, gaming s, player protection, fairness, transparency and the fulfilment of prize obligations.

The Federation therefore does not dispute the legitimate role of the FCCPC in addressing consumer protection concerns that fall within its enabling legislation.

What we dispute is the apparent assumption that a general consumer protection mandate confers an additional power to license or regulate activities that the Constitution places under State jurisdiction.

There is a fundamental legal distinction between protecting a consumer participating in a lottery and assuming responsibility for licensing, approving, supervising and regulating the lottery itself.

The former may fall within the FCCPC’s statutory consumer protection responsibilities. The latter, within the States, belongs to the competent State gaming authorities.

Where an activity constitutes a lottery or game of chance, its regulation must remain consistent with the applicable State gaming laws and the constitutional allocation of legislative authority.

The FSGRN consequently rejects any interpretation of the FCCPC Sales Promotion Regulations, 2026, that would permit the Commission to exercise core lottery regulatory functions under the guise of consumer protection.

President Tinubu’s Commitment to True Federalism Must Be Reflected in Federal Institutions

The Federation also considers the present development inconsistent with the broader principles of constitutional federalism long advocated by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has further demonstrated his commitment to true federalism, constitutional supremacy and the rule of law through his firm opposition to the proposed Central Gaming Bill, which sought to reintroduce federal control over an area constitutionally reserved for the States. This position reinforces the President’s longstanding conviction that the constitutional autonomy of States must be respected and that the judgments of the Supreme Court must be upheld without reservation.

Consequently, any Act of the National Assembly or regulation issued by any Federal Ministry, Department or Agency (MDA) that contravenes the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), or undermines the binding judgments and decisions of the Supreme Court of Nigeria, constitutes a direct affront to the principles of constitutional supremacy, true federalism and respect for the rule of law championed by President Tinubu.

The FCCPC Sales Promotion Regulations, 2026, must therefore be examined against this fundamental standard. No federal institution should, through administrative rulemaking or subsidiary legislation, seek to resurrect regulatory powers that the Supreme Court has already declared to be outside the constitutional competence of the Federal Government.

FSGRN Demands Immediate Review of the Regulations

In light of the foregoing, the Federation of State Gaming Regulators of Nigeria (FSGRN) demands the immediate review and amendment of the FCCPC Sales Promotion Regulations, 2026, to remove all provisions that encroach upon the constitutional regulatory powers of States over lotteries, promotional lotteries, prize draws and games of chance, including references to the invalidated National Lottery Act, 2005, and the National Lottery Regulatory Commission. The Federation insists that the Regulations must fully comply with the Supreme Court’s judgment in Suit No. SC/1/2008, particularly its perpetual injunction restraining federal interference in State lottery regulation, while preserving the FCCPC’s legitimate consumer protection mandate.

The Authority of the Supreme Court Is Not Negotiable

The FSGRN reiterates that the constitutional powers of States are neither negotiable nor subject to administrative discretion. The Supreme Court’s landmark judgment of November 2024 conclusively affirmed State jurisdiction over lotteries and games of chance and must be respected by all federal institutions.

We therefore call upon the FCCPC to align its Regulations with the judgment and urge the Attorney-General of the Federation to ensure compliance across federal agencies. While the Federation remains committed to inter-agency cooperation, consumer protection and industry development, it will not compromise the constitutional rights of its member States and will pursue all lawful measures necessary to defend them.

The Supreme Court has spoken. The Constitution is supreme. No federal agency can resurrect through subsidiary regulations powers already invalidated by the nation’s highest court. Nigeria’s federalism must be respected in both principle and practice.

Signed

Mr. Olajide Boladuro.

Director-General, Oyo State Lottery and Gaming Board

Vice Chairman, Federation of State Gaming Regulators of Nigeria (FSGRN)

For and on behalf of the Federation of State Gaming Regulators of Nigeria.

World.title: Kwara, 12 other North-central states back state policing bill
World.content:
The approval brings the number of state assemblies backing the proposed amendment to 13, according to reports.

Other North-central states that have supported it include Nasarawa and Plateau, while Taraba, Ogun, Delta, Cross River and Enugu also approved the bill.

The proposed reform seeks to amend the 1999 Constitution to provide for a decentralised policing system comprising the Federal Police Service and state police services.

The move comes as Nigeria continues to grapple with kidnapping, banditry, terrorism and communal violence, with growing calls for security agencies to respond more effectively to local threats.

Under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, a constitutional amendment requires approval by at least two-thirds of the 36 state Houses of Assembly, representing 24 states, before it can be presented for presidential assent.

With 13 assemblies reportedly having approved the proposal, the amendment remains short of the required threshold.

The Senate passed the amendment on 24 June, and the House of Representatives on 23 July, before it was transmitted to the state assemblies on 16 September 2026.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Other states back the proposal

In Plateau, lawmakers adopted an ad hoc committee’s recommendations on the proposed constitutional amendment. Lawmakers decided in plenary, presided over by Speaker Naanlong Daniel, after the committee presented its report.

In Nasarawa, the State House of Assembly also approved the proposed amendment, joining other state legislatures backing the establishment of state police.

Taraba lawmakers unanimously approved the proposal on Tuesday. The Speaker, John Bonzena, said the proposed system could help curb criminal activities, create employment and improve collaboration among security agencies.

In Ogun, lawmakers adopted the report of an ad hoc committee on constitutional review and approved the relevant clauses and amendments by voice vote.

The Cross River State House of Assembly also approved the bill, with all 22 members present voting in favour. Three members were absent.

The Speaker, Elvert Ayambem, said the state police should be implemented in line with the rule of law, accountability, and democratic principles, and that security operatives must respect citizens’ fundamental rights.

In Delta, all 23 members present voted in support of the amendment. Speaker Emomotimi Guwor directed the Clerk of the House to communicate the Assembly’s decision to the National Assembly.

Enugu lawmakers also passed a resolution backing the proposal, with Speaker Uche Ugwu announcing the decision.

Group submits draft bills

The development coincided with the Presidential Working Group’s completion of the proposed National Policing Bill.

Femi Gbajabiamila, the Chief of Staff to President Bola Tinubu and chairman of the working group, said the group had submitted the proposed legislation and 29 consequential amendment bills to the Federal Ministry of Justice for review and validation.

The submission was made to the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, in line with the group’s work plan.

According to Mr Gbajabiamila, the ministry is expected to return the validated drafts to the working group on or before 30 October.

The group will then give the bills final consideration before presenting them to Mr Tinubu for consideration and subsequent transmission to the National Assembly.

The drafting process is taking place alongside state assemblies’ consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026.

Debate over state police

The establishment of state police has been debated in Nigeria for more than two decades.

Supporters argue that decentralised policing would bring law enforcement closer to communities, improve intelligence gathering and enable quicker responses to local security threats.

However, critics have raised concerns that state governors could abuse their control over state police to target political opponents or suppress dissent.

The proposed reforms are intended to establish the legal and institutional framework for the two-tier policing system. Still, the constitutional amendment must secure the required support from state assemblies before the process can advance.

World.title: Police arrest 11 suspects for cultism, ATM fraud in Kogi
World.content:
Recover 59 ATM cards, two motorcycles, weapons

By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja

The Kogi State Police Command has arrested 11 suspects over alleged cultism and ATM card-swapping fraud in Itobe, Ofu Local Government Area, and Idah, respectively.

The police also recovered 59 ATM cards belonging to different banks, two motorcycles, an axe, a cutlass and a vehicle allegedly used by the suspected fraudsters.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Naziru Bello Kankarofi, disclosed this on Wednesday in Lokoja, saying the arrests followed intelligence gathering and surveillance operations targeting suspected criminal activities in the state.

He said eight suspected cultists were arrested on October 17, 2026, at a location behind Government Secondary School, Itobe, while three suspected ATM fraudsters were apprehended in Idah on October 20.

According to the police, operatives of the Itobe Division, working with local auxiliary forces and community leaders, raided the location at about 5.45 p.m., arresting seven adults and a 14-year-old boy.

The suspects were identified as Mutari Ahmed, 26; Mohammed Tairu, 21; Audu Moses Yahaya, 27; Peter Vincent, 28; Progress Aminu, 21; Wisdom Friday, 21; Gabriel Enema, 22; and a minor whose name was withheld.

The command said preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects had gathered to appoint a leader for a local cult group. It added that some of them allegedly admitted membership of the Aro-Baga Vikings and Aiye confraternities.

The police described the arrests as significant, citing intelligence reports of planned violent clashes between rival cult groups in Itobe and Ejule communities, allegedly fuelled by longstanding rivalries, territorial disputes and reprisal attacks.

It said security measures had been strengthened to prevent violence, protect residents and commuters, and address reported threats of reprisals against security personnel and facilities.

The case has been transferred to the Violent Crime Response Unit for further investigation, including efforts to apprehend fleeing suspects and identify other persons allegedly connected to the groups.

Three arrested over ATM card-swapping fraud

In a separate operation, the police arrested three men suspected of involvement in ATM card-swapping fraud in Idah.

The suspects were identified as Philip Akiola, 50; Ojo Thomas, 56; and Abdulrauf Suleiman, 48.

The command said their arrest followed surveillance launched after a complaint filed on May 19, 2026, by a victim who reportedly lost N1.5 million from his bank account after his ATM card was swapped.

The police said operatives recovered 59 ATM cards belonging to different banks and a vehicle allegedly used in the operation.

Preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects had allegedly operated the scheme for more than a year, targeting unsuspecting customers at automated teller machines.

According to the command, the alleged method involved one suspect observing a victim’s personal identification number (PIN) while another created a distraction, allowing them to swap the victim’s card. The suspects would then allegedly use the captured card and PIN to access the victim’s bank account.

The police said the suspects reportedly told investigators that an individual identified as “Sunday”, who was said to be abroad, introduced them to the scheme.

Their alleged operations primarily targeted ATM users at branches of First Bank, Union Bank and United Bank for Africa within their area of operation, the command added.

The case is being transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Lokoja for further investigation.

The police advised residents to shield their PINs when using ATMs, decline unsolicited assistance and ensure they retrieve their own cards before leaving the machines.

It also urged anyone who suspects an ATM card swap to contact their bank immediately to block the card and report the incident to the police.

The command said investigations into both cases were ongoing, adding that all suspects would be treated in accordance with the law and presumed innocent until proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction.

World.title: 2027: Wike asks PDP members in FCT to back Tinubu, APC candidates
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has asked members of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP in the FCT to support President Bola Tinubu and candidates of the All Progressives Congress APC in the 2027 elections.

Wike, who is the coordinator of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu/APC Presidential Campaign Council in FCT spoke on Wednesday at a political stakeholders forum in Abuja.

“I know all the PDP FCT will support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, will support Senator Philip Tanimu Aduda, will support Dr John Gabaya,” he said.

Wike pointed to an area council chairman as proof that the shift had begun. “He is of PDP, is it not correct? But you see, he has come out mobilizing for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, mobilizing for Senator Philip Tanimu Aduda,” he said.

He told the gathering that campaign logistics would be provided. “All the logistics for our campaign, you will have it. Everything you will have it,” he said.

The minister also disclosed the task he has been handed by the party. “I was even given two assignments: to coordinate for Rivers State, to make sure Rivers State is delivered to Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and to make sure FCT is delivered to Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu. And with the grace of God, FCT is for Tinubu, Rivers is for Tinubu. We must take this election very, very seriously. And that, and that, and that everybody must take it serious and come out with our Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and vote for Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu.”

Wike took a swipe at Peter Obi’s supporters. “You can vote for Peter Obi as president of social media,” he said.

He asked the youths why they are drawn to what he called pretenders. “Why do you like people who are fake? People who are not real?” he said, adding: “We prefer a president that will tell us this is white and it is white.”

Defending the removal of the fuel subsidy, Wike said every past president had called it a scam but none had acted. “There is no president that came that said fuel subsidy was not a scam. Every president said it was a scam. But nobody had that courage to say it will go. And it came, May 29th, 2023, he said, ‘Subsidy, you are gone.

“We agree that the cost of things are a bit high. By the time the reform is stabilized, the cost of living will come down. That is the sacrifice of removing the fuel subsidy,” he said.

Wike listed what he said Nigerians had gained. “Nobody goes to the bank to get loan,” he said of governors, adding: “Since three years now, has there been any strike in university? Has there been any strike? Let us just say the truth. There has been no strike. We cannot say that this administration has solved every problem, no. But within the three years they have come, they have solved a lot of problems”, he said.

On FCT, the minister assured the indigenes of a place in the administration. “Let me assure you today, in the next appointment of FCT, you will be included, because you represent a good chunk of Nigerians, and so there should be inclusivity as far as FCT is concerned,” he said.

He said Tinubu had addressed the frustration of career civil servants in the territory. “That is why today you have a head of service, you have a civil service commission, who is in charge of employing Abuja people. We have permanent secretaries now,” he said.

Wike said the president also approved a women secretariat and secretaries for youth matters. “We do not have a youth secretary before. Today, we have secretaries that take care of youth matters. That is inclusivity.

“Today, we have built twelve new police stations with residences in it, where the police people will stay in order to improve our security architecture.. Today, six area councils we have can boast of roads going to their various areas. It was not like that before,” he said.

Wike said the Apo-Karshi Road, awarded in 2010, would be commissioned soon. “By this November, we will commission that road. This December alone, we are going to commission not less than six projects in Amac alone. Our campaign is our project. Our campaign is to tell you what we have done. Our campaign is that if you give us the support, we will do more,” he said.

World.title: Otti to flag off Aba, Umuahia court complexes in November
World.content:
Abia State Governor, Alex Otti

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has announced plans to flag off the construction of ultra-modern court complexes in Aba and Umuahia in November.

Each complex, according to the governor, will have an auditorium with a seating capacity of 1,000.

Otti also announced plans to commission 15 additional court halls in phases, with 10 scheduled for commissioning after the current Legal Year programme and five before the end of the year. The remaining court hall is expected to be commissioned early next year.

The governor made the announcements on Tuesday during the 2026/2027 Legal Year Thanksgiving Service held at the Queen Elizabeth Chapel, Federal Medical Centre, Umuahia.

He said his administration was also working towards digitising processes across the executive, legislature and judiciary to improve efficiency and access to government services.

Speaking on the theme of the Legal Year, “The Bar, the Bench and the Administration of Justice: Strengthening the Courts that Bind,” Otti stressed the need for cooperation among the three arms of government while preserving their constitutional independence.

“The judiciary is a very important arm of government. There is no way the Executive or the legislature can work without the judiciary. But then, the lines are also very clear. And one thing you can be sure of with us is that we will always maintain those lines,” he said.

The governor congratulated members of the Bar and Bench on the commencement of the new Legal Year and commended their commitment to due process and the rule of law.

The Chief Judge of Abia State, Justice Lilian Abai, commended the working relationship between the executive and the judiciary, describing it as “a cord worth strengthening.”

She disclosed that the state government had installed solar power systems at the High Courts in Umuahia and Aba.

Abai also said Otti signed three laws on October 19: the Abia State Administration of Criminal Justice Law, 2026; the Abia State Restorative Justice Law No. 8 of 2026; and the Abia State Criminal Law No. 7 of 2026.

She urged lawyers to protect the integrity of the judiciary and maintain a constructive relationship with the Bench.

Earlier, the Anglican Bishop of Umuahia Diocese, Rt. Rev. Geoffrey Ibeabuchi, urged legal practitioners to discharge their duties with sincerity and accountability.

He encouraged them to emulate King Solomon’s quest for wisdom and understanding, noting that members of the public relied on the legal profession for protection against oppression.

The event was attended by dignitaries from the judiciary, government and other sectors.

World.title: 23-year-old Iranian woman sentenced to death over social media post
World.content:
Iran’s hardline judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei

Iranian authorities sentenced a 23-year-old student to death for blasphemy in social media posts, rights groups said, as the judiciary’s use of capital punishment on political charges mounts.

Najmeh Amini was arrested in February in the northeastern city of Mashhad and sentenced to death in September on charges of insulting the Prophet Mohammed, rights groups including the US-based Center for Human Rights in Iran (CHRI), Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) and the Norway-based Iran Human Rights (IHR) said in separate statements.

Iran has already hanged 34 men on charges related to the January 2026 protests. But at least eight women, as well as Amini, are facing execution on political and security charges, according to rights groups.

“I am an innocent girl. A young person with so many hopes and dreams. I have a mother and father who are waiting for me, a family who spend every night afraid of losing me until morning comes,” Amini said in an audio message from prison in September that was shared by the rights groups.

“Remember my name. Perhaps I won’t be able to speak anymore. But as long as I am alive, I have one hope: that before the rope becomes the end of my life, I will see a free and liberated Iran.”

The use of blasphemy charges, a capital crime in the Islamic republic, had been relatively rare in recent years.

Bahar Ghandehari, director of advocacy at the CHRI, told AFP the “authorities may… be using this rare and severe verdict to make an example of her (Amini) and discourage similar acts as popular discontent continues to increase”.

“Her case reflects the broader escalation of arbitrary arrests, politically motivated prosecutions, and death sentences following the bloody crackdown on protesters,” she added.

– ‘Life at stake’ –

“Amini’s life is at stake, and the international community must act urgently to stop her execution,” Ghandehari said.

The verdict is not final and still subject to appeal.

Details of her trial remain sparse, but according to reports in the regional daily Khorosan, Amini’s lawyer argued her posts were not intentional while Amini said she had been under the influence of hallucinogenic mushrooms she had consumed with friends.

The precise nature of the posts was unclear. She was sentenced to death on charges of “sabb al-nabi”, the capital crime of insulting the Prophet Mohammed, according to the CHRI.

In a separate case, the accounting student was also sentenced to 12 and a half years in prison for acting against national security.

HRANA said Amini has been tracked by Iran’s FATA cyber police after the protests, which peaked in mid-January.

Mass rallies in Mashhad and other big cities were suppressed in a crackdown rights groups say left thousands dead.

“Amini was held in prolonged isolation, subjected to physical beatings during arrest, and entirely denied access to a lawyer of her choice,” it said.

IHR director Mahmood Amiry-Moghaddam said the case “risks expanding the use of the death penalty against peaceful online expression”.

“Sentencing a 23-year-old woman to death for what she expressed on social media is an extremely alarming development,” he said.

AFP

World.title: Police arrest three suspects, recover gun in Jigawa
World.content:
police badge

By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested three suspected criminals and recovered a locally made pistol, ammunition and other weapons along the Nguru–Birniwa Road.

The command’s spokesperson, SP Lawan Shiisu Adam, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists.

He said operatives of Operation Salama arrested the suspects on October 14, 2026, at about 4:30 p.m. during a security patrol.

The suspects were identified as Bello Juli, 22; Abdullahi Yakubu, 30; and Bashir Muhammad, 25. All three are residents of Kyarana Settlement in Kiru Local Government Area of Kano State.

According to the police spokesperson, items recovered from the suspects included a locally fabricated pistol, three bullets, machetes, bows and arrows, and gunpowder.

Adam said the suspects had been charged to court following investigations by the State Criminal Investigation Department in Dutse.

Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, CP Tijjani Murtala, commended the officers involved in the operation and urged personnel across the command to strengthen surveillance and intelligence gathering to combat criminal activities.

He also appealed to members of the public to support security agencies by providing timely information about suspicious individuals and activities in their communities.

The command assured residents of its continued commitment to maintaining peace and security across Jigawa State.

World.title: UTME: Only 108 of 39,000 underage candidates scale FG’s admission hurdles
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

Only 108 out of about 39,000 underage candidates who sat the 2026 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) have survived the Federal Government’s rigorous screening for possible admission into tertiary institutions, underscoring the high academic and maturity standards imposed on exceptionally young applicants.

The candidates emerged after a stringent selection process that required applicants to demonstrate outstanding academic performance and psychological, emotional and intellectual readiness for university education.

Minister of Education Dr Tunji Alausa disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja while receiving the two highest-scoring candidates and six best-performing underage candidates in the 2026 UTME, presented by the Registrar of the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, JAMB, Prof. Segun Aina.

Alausa said the outcome followed a multi-stage screening exercise designed to ensure that admission opportunities for exceptionally gifted children would not come at the expense of their preparedness for the demands of higher education.

According to him, 2,244,149 candidates registered for the 2026 UTME, while 2,174,396 eventually sat the examination. Of these, approximately 39,000 were below the prescribed minimum admission age of 16 years.

The minister explained that candidates seeking exemption from the age requirement had to meet a series of demanding conditions, beginning with a minimum UTME score of 320 out of 400, representing 80 per cent.

They were also required to score at least 80 per cent in their post-UTME examinations, attain the stipulated 80 per cent threshold in the assessment of their O-level results and pass a screening exercise to establish their psychological, emotional and intellectual readiness for university education.

Alausa disclosed that only 391 underage candidates scored at least 320 in the UTME, with further assessments reducing the number eligible for possible admission to just 108.

He described the successful candidates as exceptionally gifted, noting that they represented approximately 0.005 per cent of the candidates who sat the examination.

“You are the geniuses in our society,” the minister told the students, stressing that the government had a responsibility to identify exceptional talents and nurture them into innovators capable of developing solutions to Nigeria’s challenges and those of the wider world.

The minister said the minimum admission age of 16 was not intended to frustrate academically gifted children or deny them opportunities to advance, but to ensure that those admitted at a younger age possessed the maturity required to cope with university life.

He said the screening exercise had yielded encouraging feedback, particularly regarding the candidates’ confidence, intellectual ability and responses to questions designed to assess their preparedness for higher education.

According to him, exceptional academic performance alone cannot be the sole basis for admitting children into tertiary institutions, as university education also demands emotional stability and the capacity to navigate its social and intellectual challenges.

Alausa urged the successful candidates to see their academic abilities as a responsibility to society, rather than merely an opportunity to secure early admission and personal advancement.

“You are the ones that will change Nigeria and change the world with your innovations,” he said.

The minister linked the recognition of exceptional young talents to the country’s broader development prospects, arguing that Nigeria’s youthful population represented a major resource that must be properly educated and harnessed.

He put Nigeria’s population at an estimated 220 million, with an average age of 18.5 years, adding that about 70 per cent of the population was below 30.

Alausa said the Federal Government’s education reforms were designed to expand opportunities for young Nigerians and strengthen the country’s capacity to turn their potential into innovations and solutions that could improve lives.

He congratulated the candidates on behalf of President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Ministry of Education, expressing confidence that their abilities could translate into breakthroughs capable of benefiting millions of people.

The eight recognised candidates, including the two highest scorers in the 2026 UTME, received plaques and certificates from the minister.

Owoeye Daniella Jesudunsin emerged as the highest-scoring candidate with 372 marks, while Enwere Kingsley Ikenna followed with 370.

World.title: FG urges self-care to contain Ebola
World.content:
The Federal Government has urged Nigerians to practise self-care, including regular hand hygiene and appropriate disinfection, to support efforts to contain Ebola virus disease following confirmation of an imported case in Abuja.

The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Iziaq Salako, made the call on Tuesday in Abuja at the inaugural National Self-Care Conference 2026, themed “Self-Care Puts Your Health in Your Hands: Test. Track. Thrive.”

Salako emphasised the importance of individual responsibility in preventing and controlling infectious diseases, urging Nigerians to adopt healthy practices and cooperate with public health officials to contain Ebola.

“Let me emphasise that self-care is also important in the prevention and control of infectious diseases, including Ebola viral disease, which Nigeria is currently working hard to contain, following one imported case that was reported.

“I therefore use this opportunity to call on the Nigerian public to observe self-care, like hand hygiene and appropriate disinfection, and cooperate fully with public health officials to contain the reported Ebola in this case,” he said.

He said self-care empowered people with the knowledge, skills and tools to take charge of their health while extending healthcare beyond hospitals and clinics into homes, workplaces and communities.

According to him, self-care complemented professional healthcare rather than replacing it or absolving the government of its responsibility to provide accessible, affordable and quality health services.

“As government, therefore, we will continue to promote investment in health facilities, skilled personnel, essential medicines, and functional referral systems,” he said.

Salako said self-care could strengthen primary healthcare, advance universal health coverage and improve outcomes in maternal and reproductive health, non-communicable diseases and mental well-being.

He explained that “Test” encouraged people to establish their health status, “Track” promoted consistent monitoring of health indicators and treatment adherence, while “Thrive” represented the goal of healthier individuals, stronger families and more resilient communities.

The minister urged state governments to integrate evidence-based self-care into health policies and programmes, while calling on healthcare professionals to guide its safe use and development partners to support sustainable financing and capacity development.

The Special Adviser to the President on Health, Dr Salma Anas, said self-care should be promoted alongside effective regulation, quality services and accountability to prevent unsafe practices and ensure people received appropriate support.

Anas said the Federal Government remained committed to achieving universal health coverage without leaving anyone behind while maintaining the quality of healthcare services.

She cited contraceptive self-injection as an example of an intervention that promoted independence and autonomy in family planning.

The presidential adviser cautioned against interpreting self-care as government withdrawal from its healthcare responsibilities.

“You can take responsibility because you have to acknowledge you are sick and acknowledge what you can do within the comfort of your home before you even reach the health services,” she said.

Anas also emphasised the importance of community participation, appropriate regulation and accountability in implementing self-care interventions.

Dr Mary Brantuo, Coordinator, Strategic Health Policy and Planning at the World Health Organization (WHO), described the conference as a demonstration of Nigeria’s commitment to empowering people to take greater control of their health.

She said self-care could help address gaps in access to services amid persistent challenges involving maternal and child mortality, unmet family planning needs, infectious diseases and non-communicable diseases.

“Self-care is not about replacing health systems but is rather about extending the reach of health systems and empowering people with the knowledge, tools, and confidence they need to make informed decisions about their health,” Brantuo said.

She identified HIV self-testing, contraceptive self-injection and self-monitoring as interventions that had demonstrated their value and acceptability in Nigerian communities.

The Group Chief Executive Officer of the Society for Family Health (SFH), Dr Omokhudu Idogho, said self-care required accurate information, quality products, affordable services and access to professional care.

Represented by Mr Emeka Okafor, Group Director, Population, Health and Community Systems, Donor-Funded Portfolio Directorate, Idogho said people made health decisions in their homes, pharmacies and communities.

He added that people also made health decisions through their phones, making reliable information and appropriate services in those spaces essential.

Idogho said SFH was using telemedicine through its Access Care initiative to bring professional advice closer to people facing distance, transport costs, time constraints and privacy concerns.

He added that the organisation’s Co-Elevate initiative highlighted the need for investment and partnerships to make technology-driven self-care services sustainable and accessible to underserved populations.

Idogho said data should be used to assess who accessed self-care services, who remained excluded and whether users received appropriate follow-up care.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that self-care is the ability of individuals, families and communities to promote health, prevent disease, maintain health and cope with illness and disability, with or without support from a healthcare provider.

Self-care interventions include contraceptive self-injection, HIV self-testing, human papillomavirus self-sampling, blood pressure checks and appropriate self-monitoring of health conditions. (NAN)

World.title: IAD endorses Obi, claims 25% voter base in 31 states
World.content:
Peter Obi

By John Alechenu, Abuja

The Igbo Agenda Dialogue (IAD) has endorsed Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for the January 16, 2027 presidential election, claiming that Igbo people constitute at least 25 per cent of voters in 31 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

The National Chairman of IAD and founder of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), Chief Chekwas Okorie, announced the endorsement in Abuja on Wednesday.

He described IAD as an Igbo political network linked to Igbo unions, market associations, women and youth groups in Nigeria and the diaspora.

Okorie traced the history of Igbo political collaboration with other ethnic groups, saying the community had consistently supported alliances aimed at promoting national unity.

He recalled that Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe led the independence struggle and that his party, the National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC), entered a coalition with the Northern People’s Congress (NPC), paving the way for Alhaji Tafawa Balewa to become Prime Minister in 1960.

He also cited the Second Republic, when Azikiwe’s Nigerian People’s Party (NPP) allied with the National Party of Nigeria (NPN) to form a government.

According to Okorie, during the transition programme of former Head of State, General Abdulsalami Abubakar, Igbo leaders met at Modotel Hotel in Enugu and invested politically in the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) after Dr Alex Ekwueme was assured of support from his northern political associates for the presidency.

He said the South-East subsequently supported the PDP across elective positions but alleged that Ekwueme was denied the party’s presidential ticket at its Jos convention.

Okorie said IAD assessed the leading contenders for the 2027 presidential election based on their records, empathy, fitness, probity and prudence before consulting widely and settling on Obi.

“We came to the unanimous resolution that it will be in the best interest of Nigeria to elect Mr Peter Obi,” he said.

He claimed Obi enjoyed support across ethnic and religious lines and was the most globally visible contender in the presidential race.

Okorie said Nigerians had long been governed by ageing political leaders and argued that the 2027 election offered an opportunity to elect a compassionate and prudent leader, despite what he described as intimidation.

On the demographic strength of the Igbo electorate, he said: “Igbo people constitute a minimum of 25% of the voting population in each of the 31 states in Nigeria and the Federal Capital Territory or the second largest population to the indigenous population of these states while constituting over 99% of the voting population in the five states in the South East.”

He also announced that Obi would run with Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, a former governor of Kano State, as his running mate.

Okorie urged other Igbo politicians to focus their campaigns on issues affecting Nigerians.

To illustrate what he described as the Igbo people’s tradition of accommodating other ethnic groups, he cited the election of Alhaji Umaru Altine, a Fulani man from Sifawa in present-day Sokoto State, as the first Mayor of Enugu under the NCNC during the First Republic.

He said Altine was re-elected as an independent candidate after losing the NCNC ticket.

Okorie also recalled that Chief (Mrs) H.I.D. Awolowo was appointed Minister without Portfolio by the then Premier of the Eastern Region, Dr M.I. Okpara, while her husband, Chief Obafemi Awolowo, was imprisoned in Calabar.

He said the appointment came with full official benefits, including a chauffeur-driven Mercedes-Benz.

Okorie said IAD would intensify its mobilisation through its networks to campaign for Obi’s victory in the 2027 presidential election.

World.title: UNODC: Africa Must Close Gap Between Evidence Generated on Substance Use, Policy Decisions
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) has said that Africa must close the gap between evidence generated on substance use and the decisions made by governments, warning that the disconnect has serious policy and human consequences.

The UNODC Country Representative in Nigeria, Dr. Akanidomo Ibanga, stated this on Wednesday in Abuja at the 16th Biennial International Conference on ‘Drugs, Alcohol and Society in Africa,’ organised by the Centre for Research and Information on Substance Abuse (CRISA) in partnership with the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

The two-day event was themed: ‘Substance Use Research and Data Systems in Africa; Advances, Relevance and Challenges.’

He questioned the value of research that does not influence decisions, data that is never used, and policies not informed by evidence, saying they are questions about lives, government priorities and the future of substance use response in Africa.

Akanidomo noted: “Africa does not lack researchers. We do not lack expertise. We do not lack institutions capable of generating knowledge. What we must continue to confront is the gap between the evidence we generate and the decisions we make.

“And that gap has consequences. When we do not know who is using which substances, where the greatest risks are emerging, who is being left behind, or whether our interventions are working, we are not simply dealing with a data problem.

“We are dealing with a policy problem, a public health problem and, ultimately, a human problem.”

Akanidomo maintained that the relevance of substance use research should not be measured by the number of surveys conducted or reports published, but by what changes because of it, including whether it helps governments allocate resources, identify underserved populations, reveal effectiveness of prevention programmes, and improve access to treatment.

According to him, research must not end when a report is launched. That is often where its most important work should begin. That evidence must reach decision-makers, service institutions, affected communities and professionals.

Akanidomo, therefore, called for reliable national data that reflects African contexts, saying Nigeria and other African countries must not be invisible in the global evidence base and should not have to make critical decisions using evidence that does not reflect their populations.

Also, the Commissioner for Human Development and Social Affairs, ECOWAS Commission, Prof. Nassirou Bako-Arifari, lamented that West Africa was shifting from being merely a transit hub for illicit drugs to becoming a growing consumer market, with serious socio-economic, public health and security implications.

Bako-Arifari, who was represented by the Head of ECOWAS Drug Prevention and Control Division, Dr. Daniel Amankwaah, said drug abuse, illicit trafficking and related crimes constitute severe challenges across several nations, including ECOWAS member states.

He cited the recently validated West African Epidemiology Network on Drug Use (WENDU) Report (2025) which underscored growing public health concerns associated with substance use in the region.

Bako-Arifari added: “Key highlights of the WENDU report – which will be presented shortly – indicate that West Africa is shifting from being merely a transit hub to becoming a growing consumer market.”

He pointed out that the changing dynamics demand enhanced international cooperation, improved treatment infrastructure and effective alternatives to incarceration.

To this end, he said the ECOWAS drug prevention and control programme continued to prioritize expansion of drug treatment and rehabilitation centres across member states.

“As of September 2026, 12 drug treatment and rehabilitation centres in 10 member states have completed renovations and received essential equipment upgrades to improve access to care for people with drug use disorders,” he said.

Bako-Arifari said that over 300 health and allied professionals have been trained as master trainers in their respective countries to champion evidence-based substance abuse prevention and treatment.

According to him, the initiatives reflect a deliberate strategic shift by the commission – moving away from a purely punitive response towards a compassionate, rehabilitative approach.

Bako-Arifari explained that another vital area of progress is the advancement of Alternatives to Incarceration (ATI), noting that traditional punitive measures often fail to address root causes of substance abuse.

“In line with this global best practice, ECOWAS has made significant strides since 2024 by advancing ATI frameworks that prioritize treatment, rehabilitation, and social reintegration. Through targeted pilot projects, ATI training has been successfully implemented in Ghana, Togo, Lagos and the Republic of Benin,” he said.

Bako-Arifari was of the opinion that emerging drug threats do not replace older ones but compound them, adding that while ECOWAS continues to combat cocaine trafficking, the escalating crisis surrounding synthetic opioids – particularly tramadol – requires member states to tackle multiple overlapping threats simultaneously.

He stressed that the ECOWAS Commission recognised the necessity of a balanced approach that addresses both illicit drug supply reduction and the public health and social consequences of substance use.

World.title: Fasoranti’s Death, a Loss to Yoruba Nation, Says Edu-Falade
World.content:
Tomisin Edu-Falade, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Akure North Constituency in the Ondo State House of Assembly, has described the death of Afenifere elder statesman, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, as a painful loss.

Edu-Falade expressed her condolences to the late statesman’s family and the Ondo State Government over his demise.

She said the death of the revered Yoruba leader was a moment of grief for his family, the people of Ondo State and the Yoruba nation.

The APC candidate extended her sympathy to the bereaved family, urging them to find solace in the life of the departed elder statesman.

She also commiserated with the Ondo State Government, expressing solidarity with it over the loss.

Edu-Falade acknowledged Fasoranti’s significance as an elder statesman and a prominent figure in Yoruba affairs.

“We mourn the passing of Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti and extend our heartfelt condolences to his family and the Ondo State Government,” she said.

She prayed that God would grant the bereaved family and the government the strength to endure the period of mourning.

Edu-Falade also prayed for the repose of the late statesman’s soul and comfort for all those grieving his death.

World.title: SWAGA’23 Mourns Fasoranti
World.content:
The South-West Agenda for Asiwaju (SWAGA’23) has mourned the death of the National Leader of Afenifere, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, describing him as a towering figure in Nigeria’s political history and a custodian of the progressive ideals of the Yoruba people.

In a condolence statement signed by its chairman, Senator Dayo Adeyeye, the group expressed deep sadness over the passing of the elder statesman, who died at the age of 100.

SWAGA’23 described Fasoranti as a teacher, educationist, former Commissioner for Finance of the old Ondo State, and a committed disciple of the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo.

The group also praised his contributions to Nigeria’s democratic development, noting that he remained a fearless pro-democracy activist who stood firmly for truth, justice and good governance during some of the country’s most challenging periods.

According to the statement, Fasoranti’s life was marked by sacrifice, integrity and selfless service, spanning his involvement in the Action Group, the Unity Party of Nigeria and his leadership role in Afenifere.

It said the late Yoruba leader consistently championed true federalism, social justice, good governance and national unity, adding that he risked his life in the struggle for the democracy Nigerians enjoy today.

SWAGA’23 also recalled Fasoranti’s support for the group during the build-up to the 2023 general elections, particularly his endorsement of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s presidential ambition.

The statement said Fasoranti received members of the group in Akure and offered his blessing, prayers and endorsement at a critical point in their political mobilisation.

“His gesture gave SWAGA’23 strength, legitimacy and confidence, and remains one of the defining moments in our movement,” the group said.

The organisation described his death as a major loss not only to his immediate family, the people of Akure, Ondo State and Afenifere, but also to the Yoruba race and Nigeria as a whole.

It further characterised Fasoranti as one of the last great figures of the Awoist tradition and a bridge between Nigeria’s First Republic and Fourth Republic.

Adeyeye, on behalf of the leadership and members of SWAGA’23 across the South-West and Nigeria, extended condolences to the deceased’s family, Afenifere, and the government and people of Ondo State.

The group prayed for the repose of Fasoranti’s soul and for divine comfort for all those mourning him, expressing hope that his legacy would endure.

“May his legacy live on forever,” the statement added

World.title: Sunbeth Activates N150b Commercial Paper Note Issuance Process
World.content:
Sunbeth Global Concepts Limited (Sunbeth) has signed the transaction documents for its N150 billion Commercial Paper note, the first series under its approved N500 billion Commercial Paper Issuance Programme.

The transaction will provide short-term working capital for Sunbeth’s cocoa procurement activities during the 2026/2027 cocoa season.

It will also support inventory requirements for the company’s 70,000-metric-tonne-per-annum processing facility, which is scheduled to commence operations in the first quarter of next year.

Speaking at the signing ceremony in Victoria Island, Lagos, Chief Financial Officer of Sunbeth Global Concepts, Adeyemi Aduwo, explained that the transaction would provide timely funding for the company’s procurement activities and broader processing ambitions.

“The 2026/2027 cocoa season presents a critical procurement window, and this transaction gives us the working capital to respond efficiently to that opportunity, supporting our transition towards greater value addition.”

Sunbeth has established a track record in the domestic debt capital market following the successful redemption of its debut Commercial Paper issuance, in which the first tranche was oversubscribed by 65 per cent.

The new N500 billion programme provides a structured framework for the company to access short-term funding in line with its seasonal working capital requirements.

The first tranche of N150 billion saw keen investor activity with an oversubscription of 45 per cent, further demonstrating Nigeria’s capital markets’ ability to provide sustainable financing models for productive activity in the agricultural sector.

Through the issuance, Sunbeth continues to strengthen its integrated agricultural platform, spanning sourcing, aggregation, and international trade, while advancing its plans to increase value creation within Africa’s agricultural economy.

The Commercial Paper issued in three series, with a minimum bid of N5 million and tenors of 180, 270, and 364 days. The timing and size of each tranche will align with cocoa procurement requirements and prevailing market conditions.

Sunbeth maintains national-scale credit ratings from established African rating agencies, with long-term ratings ranging from BBB to BBB+ and a short-term rating of A2.

World.title: UNICEF Seeks Curriculum Review to Bridge Graduate Skills Gap
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) Tuesday called for a review of Nigeria’s education curriculum to address the mismatch between graduates’ skills and labour market demands, stressing the need to equip young people with relevant digital and vocational skills.

The UNICEF Deputy Representative in Nigeria, Dr. Rownak Khan, made the call during a visit by UNICEF and Airtel Africa to schools in Agege, Lagos and Yaba College of Technology (YABATECH), to showcase their digital learning and youth skills development initiatives.

She emphasised the impact of the organisation’s partnership with Airtel and educational institutions on youth skills development.

Khan said although Nigeria had an established education system, much of its curriculum was outdated and failed to adequately prepare young people for the realities of the modern workplace.

“In many countries, and to some extent broadly in Nigeria, the education is there, but the curricula that have been followed are quite decades old. When these children come out into the real world, they are in shock because there is a mismatch between what they have learnt and what the market is asking for,” she said.

The UNICEF deputy representative stressed the need for stakeholders to work together to bridge the gap between classroom learning and industry requirements, noting that digital skills development should be linked to sustainable livelihood opportunities for young people.

According to her, the collaboration between UNICEF, Airtel and educational institutions demonstrates how partnerships can combine different areas of expertise to provide more comprehensive support for young people.

Khan described the initiative as a flagship programme, noting that its impact extended beyond digital training to preparing beneficiaries for employment and other livelihood opportunities.

She commended Yabatech for its commitment to skills development, particularly its efforts to integrate digital competencies into its programmes and provide young people with pathways to economic independence.

In her remarks, the Chief Field Office and Head of Private Sector Partnerships Unit, Celine Lafoucriere, said the telecommunications company had supported the organisation’s digital education initiatives for five years by providing connectivity to young people seeking to acquire digital skills.

The partnership, she noted, had enabled beneficiaries to access various learning platforms, including the Learning Passport and the Youth Agency Marketplace (YOMA), which provide opportunities for young people to develop skills and improve their employability.

Lafoucriere explained that UNICEF worked with different partners, each contributing expertise and resources to expand access to digital education.

She said Airtel’s contribution had been particularly significant in ensuring that young people could access skills development programmes provided through UNICEF’s network of partners.

According to her, Airtel initially focused on supporting access to the Learning Passport when it entered into a pan-African partnership with UNICEF.

However, discussions between both organisations led to the expansion of the initiative to cover other digital platforms that could benefit children, adolescents and young people.

She said Airtel subsequently agreed to whitelist the platforms, allowing beneficiaries to access the digital learning resources without the usual data constraints.

The UNICEF official expressed appreciation to the telecommunications company for its continued support, noting that the partnership had helped strengthen digital learning opportunities in Nigeria.

“The only reason why we are able to drive digital learning in Nigeria today is thanks to Airtel,” Lafoucriere stated.

She added that sustained collaboration among development organisations, technology companies and other stakeholders remained essential to ensuring that children and young people were not left behind in the digital learning ecosystem.

Also speaking, Head, Programmes, Airtel Africa Foundation, Esi Asare Prah, reaffirmed its commitment to bridging the digital divide across Africa, announcing plans to strengthen skills development initiatives aimed at equipping young people with competencies required in the labour market.

She stated that its partnership with UNICEF, backed by a $57 million investment across 13 African countries, was designed to expand access to digital education and skills training, particularly for young people who lack the opportunities to participate in the digital economy.

She added that the initiative was particularly significant in Nigeria because of its emphasis on equipping young people with practical skills they could use to secure employment and earn a living.

According to her, “Many young people graduated from schools with certificates but lacked the competencies required by employers, creating a mismatch between educational qualifications and labour market demands.”

The foundation, Prah noted, has four priority areas, with education occupying the foremost position, followed by digital inclusion.

She stated that the partnership with UNICEF remained a key part of the foundation’s commitment to addressing educational inequalities and expanding opportunities for young people across the continent.

“Our mission is to bridge that digital divide across the continent because our mother company drives the digital education agenda, and there are still a lot of young people who are left behind in that regard,” she said.

Prah also described its engagement with YABATECH as an opportunity to develop a model that could be adapted and replicated in other African countries where it operates.

“Nigerian initiative stood out because of its focus on practical skills development, supported by technical expertise to ensure that participants acquired competencies relevant to the needs of employers,” she said, adding that the approach went beyond providing access to digital learning platforms or offering training.

She stressed the importance of ensuring that the skills acquired could translate into employment and sustainable livelihoods.

The Rector of YABATECH, Dr. Ibraheem Abdul, represented by his deputy, Dr. Ismaila Badmus, said the institution was deliberate about building partnerships and strengthening town-and-gown relations.

He expressed appreciation to the partners for their support.

World.title: Movement Defends Tinubu’s  Reforms amid Hardship
World.content:
Amina Hassan in Abuja

Ahead of the 2027 general election, a group, Tinubu Must Stay Movement (TMS), has defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms amid persistent economic hardship in the country, urging Nigerians to focus on their projected long-term benefits.

The group’s Director-General, Marcel Ngogbehei, while addressing a press conference yesterday in Abuja, argued that abandoning the reforms without fixing the country’s longstanding economic challenges could leave future generations worse off.

Ngogbehei, who likened the situation to a family making sacrifices to secure its future, said Nigerians should be willing to make adjustments for the sake of their children.

He acknowledged the difficulties facing households, saying public debate should focus on the merits of government policies and possible alternatives rather than personal attacks. The director-general challenged critics to explain how they would have handled the country’s economic challenges differently.

Ngogbehei said: “Would you prefer to eat everything you have now, not caring what happens to your kids in the future? We cannot run it by propaganda, we cannot run it by lies.”

Also, the National Coordinator of the group, Ibrahim Uba, reeled out what he described as progress recorded by the administration across sectors, including economy, education, agriculture, security and infrastructure.

He noted that the economy had grown by about 4.43 per cent and claimed food prices had fallen.

Uba cited 1.5 million approvals by the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), a reported N500 billion allocation to the Bank of Agriculture to support farmers, and the absence of strikes in tertiary institutions since President Tinubu assumed office.

He further pointed to the procurement of military equipment, deployment of digital systems for security agencies and ongoing road projects as evidence of progress.

Uba urged journalists to independently investigate the government’s programmes and examine how the interventions were being implemented.

World.title: 12 Young Entrepreneurs Get N90m Grants As Kwara Empowers Business Community Again
World.content:
No fewer than 12 young entrepreneurs in Kwara State were handed N89.2 million cheques recently by the state government as grants to support their businesses, foster self-reliance and create employment opportunities for the youth.

A statement by the Press Secretary, Kwara State Social Investment Programme (KWASSIP), Bolashade Yusuf, revealed the grants were organised by KWASSIP under its Youth Entrepreneurial Empowerment Scheme.

General Manager of KWASSIP, Dr Wasiu Tejidini, who handed them the cheques in his office in Ilorin on Monday, said the government considered it necessary to empower the new starters with viable business ideas to thrive.

The beneficiaries are Firdauz Muhammed Wuraola, CEO, Drinks ‘N’ Grillz (N10 million); Nimotallah Mohammed Kpayero (Ban Shea Products) – N15.9 million; Ahmed Kuburat (Kaddy Nigeria) – N15 million; Oloyede Ikmat Omoshalewa (Kwara Souvenir Store) – N5 million; Fatigun Subomi Emmanuel ((Waka Studios) – N10 million; Anifowose Favour Boluwatife (Esthad Luxe Jewels) – N3.3 million; Ibrahim Maryam Modupeola (Kleen Klear) – N5 million; Ajiboye Opeyemi Rasheed (Tailorgang Fashion House) – N5 million; Yusuf Dolapo Azeezat (Day Varieties Enterprise) – N5 million; Akinyode Bosede Temilade (Global LightTrust Integrated Ventures) – N5 million; Badeji Sherifat Modupe (BSM Fashion) – N5 million; and Adeshewa Kolawole (Day-Yank Fashion), who received N5 million.

Dr Tejidini said the lucky 12 secured the grants on the basis of approval by Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq who went through their letters of request and details of their business proposals.

While urging them to utilise the funds responsibly to achieve the objectives outlined in their applications, Tejidini said the agency will, in six-month or one-year time, assess the impact of the funds through its monitoring and evaluation unit.

He disclosed that the government had equally supported more than 1,000 young people through its Kwapreneur programme – another flagship youth empowerment and enterprise development initiative under KWASSIP.

He defined the latest intervention by the state government as a broader strategy to encourage entrepreneurship and reduce dependence on government employment.

Tejidini commended the governor’s support for entrepreneurship skill and how his administration continues to invest in infrastructural development, healthcare, security, and education among other sectors.

Speaking on behalf of the beneficiaries, Ajiboye Opeyemi Rasheed and Mohammed Nimotallah Kpayero, appreciated the government for the financial assistance, describing it as an opportunity to expand their businesses and create jobs.

They said the support will help them acquire more equipment and improve their production capacity by employing more young people to become economically independent.

“We really thank the government. This is an opportunity for us to create jobs for people out there, including fresh graduates. They can easily learn (from us) and get the right business skills to become self-sufficient,” Ajiboye said.

World.title: Sujimoto Unveils 49-Storey Isabella Hotel, Targets Tallest Luxury Hotel in Nigeria
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

Sujimoto Group has unveiled plans for a 49-storey luxury hotel, Isabella de’ Medici, conceived to become Nigeria’s tallest and most luxurious hotel.

The project which will be in Lagos, according to the company, will combine luxury hospitality, leisure and private hotel-suite ownership, with investors able to acquire individual suites for personal use or participation in a professionally managed rental pool.

The announcement comes as Sujimoto moves towards completing its flagship Lucrezia by Sujimoto residential development on Banana Island, Lagos, where homeowners have begun taking possession of their properties.

The proposed hotel named after Isabella de’ Medici, a member of the influential Italian Medici family, draws inspiration from Renaissance Florence and is designed to position Lagos as a destination for international luxury tourism.

The Sujimoto Group stated further that the development would feature a sculptural KRION façade, a grand lobby aquarium described as potentially Africa’s largest hotel-lobby aquarium, a hanging infinity pool on the 35th floor, international restaurants, luxury boutiques, wellness facilities, a private cinema, casino, billiards lounge and sky bar.

It added that its ambition was to compete with leading international hospitality brands, including Four Seasons, while showcasing African hospitality.

Beyond hospitality, with the luxury hotel Sujimoto is introducing a private ownership model that would allow investors to own individual hotel suites rather than entire residential properties.

The company said prices for its 45-square-metre deluxe suites would begin at $150,000 during the pre-launch phase, with the price scheduled to rise to $210,000 at groundbreaking and potentially increase further as construction progresses.

According to the company, founding investors would have the opportunity to name their suites after themselves and enjoy up to 21 days of personal use annually, subject to the terms of the proposed managed rental pool.

It projected annual rental income of up to $30,000 on a $150,000 suite, representing a potential yield of 20 per cent while projecting returns on equity of up to 300 per cent by completion.

However, the company’s projected income and returns are estimates and are not guaranteed as actual performance would depend on factors including occupancy rates, operating expenses, management fees, market conditions and the final terms of the investment arrangement.

The company further outlined a proposed price progression from $150,000 at pre-launch to as much as $600,000 upon completion, depending on the stage of construction.

The Group Managing Director of Sujimoto, Dr. Sijibomi Ogundele, in a statement he personally signed, while reflecting on the challenges encountered during the development of Lucrezia, acknowledged that rising construction costs, exchange-rate volatility, borrowing obligations and regulatory hurdles had placed significant pressure on the project.

He disclosed that the group had installed 112 piles beneath the Banana Island development as part of its foundation engineering but admitted that its financing structure had not been sufficiently protected against economic shocks.

According to him, the experience had prompted it to adopt stricter financial controls for Isabella, including more prudent borrowing, aligning commitments with available funding, introducing financial safeguards at construction milestones and strengthening risk assessment.

Ogundele maintained that despite the difficulties, the group remained committed to completing Lucrezia and fulfilling its obligations to investors and homeowners.

Lucrezia is a 15-storey luxury residential development featuring four-bedroom maisonettes of approximately 600 square metres, alongside premium penthouses.

Sujimoto also cited the reported appreciation of one Lucrezia unit purchased for about ₦650 million to a current offer of ₦5 billion as an example of the potential value appreciation associated with its developments.

He said Isabella was conceived not merely as another luxury hotel but as a destination capable of attracting visitors from across the world.

The company’s vision draws on the legacy of the Medici family, whose patronage helped establish Florence as one of the defining cultural centres of the Renaissance.

According to Ogundele, the hotel’s architectural design and planned leisure facilities are intended to create a distinctive hospitality experience in Lagos.

The company said lessons from Lucrezia would inform the execution of Isabella, with a stronger emphasis on financial discipline, transparency and keeping investors informed throughout construction and eventual hotel operations.

Ogundele, who heads Sujimoto Group, has spearheaded several luxury real estate developments, including Lucrezia by Sujimoto, Leonardo by Sujimoto, the Sujimoto Twin Tower and Queen Amina by Sujimoto.

The proposed Isabella de’ Medici project represents the company’s latest ambition to expand beyond luxury residential real estate into large-scale hospitality and investment-driven developments.

While the company has outlined its architectural vision and investment projections, the project’s delivery timeline, financing arrangements and the independent verification of its projected returns remain important considerations for prospective investors.

World.title: Thinking of adopting a rescue dog? Here’s what it really costs in South Africa
World.content:
Adoption fees at most South African SPCAs range from about R900 to R1,400. Image: Pexels

Deciding to adopt a rescue dog is one of the most rewarding choices a family can make.

But the adoption fee is only the start.

Food, vet visits and flea treatment all add up.

And for first-time owners, those ongoing costs can come as a surprise.



Here’s what it really costs: adoption fees at most South African SPCAs and animal welfare organisations range from about R900 to R1,400, and usually include sterilisation, a first vaccination and a microchip.

After that, you’ll need to budget for food, regular vaccinations, parasite control and vet visits.

HOW MUCH ARE ADOPTION FEES?

Fees vary between organisations and regions. Here are some examples of published adoption fees for dogs:



Bloemfontein SPCA: R1,400

R1,400 Animal Anti-Cruelty League, Johannesburg: R1,240

R1,240 SPCA Randburg: R1,000 for adult dogs, and R1,100 for puppies under six months

R1,000 for adult dogs, and R1,100 for puppies under six months Animal Anti-Cruelty League, Cape Town: R1,000

R1,000 Vereeniging SPCA: R900, including a non-refundable R100 administration fee

WHAT DOES THE ADOPTION FEE INCLUDE?

You’re not paying for the animal itself.

According to the Vereeniging SPCA, the fee covers the expenses the SPCA has already paid, such as sterilisation, the first vaccination, deworming, an ID disc and a microchip.

Some organisations also include flea treatment or a collar.



The Durban and Coast SPCA says the adoption fee is heavily subsidised, and that the cost of vaccinations alone at a private vet is more than its fee.

WHY ADOPTING IS GOOD VALUE

Sterilisation is one of the biggest savings.

At a private vet, sterilisation can cost between R2,500 and R3,500 for a female dog, and between R1,800 and R2,500 for a male dog, according to industry estimates.



Since most adoption fees include sterilisation, adopting can save you more than the fee itself.

OTHER ONCE-OFF COSTS

Some organisations charge extra for:

Home inspections. The Animal Anti-Cruelty League in Johannesburg charges R88 for inspections within 40km of Johannesburg.

The Animal Anti-Cruelty League in Johannesburg charges for inspections within 40km of Johannesburg. Additional vaccinations, if your dog needs more than one at adoption.

You’ll also need to buy basics, such as a bed, bowls, a lead and toys.



ONGOING COSTS TO BUDGET FOR

Once your dog is home, you’ll need to budget for:

Food, which depends on your dog’s size, age and diet.

which depends on your dog’s size, age and diet. Booster vaccinations, usually once a year.

usually once a year. Deworming and flea and tick treatment, which need to be repeated regularly.

which need to be repeated regularly. Vet visits, for check-ups and unexpected illness or injuries.

for check-ups and unexpected illness or injuries. Grooming, especially for long-haired breeds.

TIPS TO KEEP COSTS DOWN

Ask your SPCA about low-cost services. Some SPCAs offer vaccinations, deworming and sterilisation at lower prices than private vets. The Bloemfontein SPCA, for example, lists sterilisation at R900 for a female dog and R600 for a male.

a copy of your ID ,

, proof of residence ,

, proof that pets are allowed, if you rent,

and a home inspection.
