World.title: Medium-term budget in a nutshell: Everything to know in 30 seconds
World.content:
Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana announced temporary fuel levy cuts, billions in additional funding for social services and new resources to fight crime. Image: X @GovernmentZA

Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana has announced temporary fuel levy cuts, billions in additional funding for social services and municipalities, and new resources to fight crime as government seeks to ease pressure on households while stabilising South Africa’s public finances.

Delivering the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement (MTBPS) in Parliament on Wednesday, 21 October, Godongwana said the government’s fiscal consolidation measures were beginning to deliver results, despite weaker economic growth and ongoing global uncertainty.

“The difficult choices of the past few years were made for a purpose. To restore stability today so that we can build a faster-growing, more inclusive and more resilient economy tomorrow,” he said.



However, South Africa’s economic growth forecast for 2026 has been revised down to 1.2%, from the 1.6% projected in February, reflecting pressure from higher fuel prices, geopolitical conflict and the effects of El Niño.

Growth is expected to improve to 1.6% in 2027 and reach 2% by 2029.

Tax revenue boost helps turn debt tide

One of the key developments is the improvement in government’s debt trajectory.



The debt-to-GDP ratio stabilised at 78.4% in the 2025/26 financial year and has started to decline, marking a milestone after years of rising public debt.

The budget deficit is expected to narrow to 3.9% of GDP in the current financial year, better than the 4% forecast in February. It is projected to decline further to 2.5% by 2030.

Meanwhile, the primary budget surplus – the difference between government revenue and expenditure before debt-service costs – is expected to rise from 1.7% of GDP to nearly 3% by 2030.



Tax revenue estimates for 2026/27 have been revised upwards by R17.1 billion, supported by corporate income tax, VAT and stronger commodity prices.

Government expenditure is expected to increase from R2.7 trillion this year to R3 trillion by 2029/30.

The improved revenue outlook gives Treasury some room to provide targeted relief, although the government remains focused on containing borrowing and keeping debt on a sustainable path.



Fuel levy cuts offer temporary relief

One of the most immediate announcements for consumers was a temporary reduction in the general fuel levy worth R10 billion.

From 4 November to 1 December 2026, the levy will be reduced by:

Petrol: R1.50 per litre

R1.50 per litre Diesel: R3 per litre

The second phase will run from 2 December 2026 until 5 January 2027, with smaller reductions:



Petrol: R1 per litre

R1 per litre Diesel: R1.50 per litre

The funding will come from R10 billion in revenue overruns from the 2025/26 financial year that had been transferred to the Central Energy Fund. The money will be returned to the National Revenue Fund to finance the relief.

“This intervention will help ease cost of living pressures without compromising the sustainability of the budget,” Godongwana said.

The reductions are intended to cushion motorists and businesses against elevated fuel costs. Lower fuel levies can also help moderate transport and distribution expenses, although the final pump price will still depend on other fuel-pricing components.



Social grants and child nutrition receive support

Social spending remains a major part of the government’s budget, accounting for 60% of non-interest expenditure.

Government funding supports 18.1 million social grant beneficiaries through programmes including old-age, disability and child support grants.

More than 11 million households also benefit from free basic services, including water, electricity, sanitation and refuse removal.



The MTBPS includes R1.6 billion over the medium term for child nutrition, with a focus on maternal care and the first 1 000 days of a child’s life. The programme aims to help prevent malnutrition and stunting during a critical period of development.

Billions allocated to fight crime and GBVF

Government has reprioritised R3.8 billion over the 2027 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework period to appoint 3 552 social workers, strengthening the response to gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF).

A further R186 million has been allocated to improve forensic and investigative capacity.



Godongwana also announced plans to increase the number of sexual offences courts from 55 to 101 and expand Thuthuzela Care Centres supporting rape survivors from 72 to 80 by 2028/29.

An additional R157.4 million will go to the Department of Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities to strengthen national coordination of the GBVF response.

Beyond gender-based violence, R810 million has been allocated to recapitalise the South African Police Service vehicle fleet. A further R823 million has been set aside for military deployments targeting gang violence and illegal mining.



The allocations are intended to strengthen law enforcement and improve support for vulnerable communities.

HIV and AIDS services get additional funding

The budget also addresses the financial pressure on HIV and AIDS programmes following the withdrawal of funding from the United States President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR).

Government will reprioritise R556.7 million over the medium term to sustain HIV and AIDS services. This will supplement R3.8 billion reprioritised through the district health programmes grant.



The funding is intended to help maintain essential services as South Africa adjusts to the loss of external support.

Municipalities receive billions for basic services

Local government is also set to receive additional support.

Municipalities will receive an additional R3.5 billion over the medium term for smart meter rollouts, aimed at improving billing accuracy and helping municipalities manage electricity distribution.



The local government equitable share will receive a further R21.8 billion to support basic services.

Godongwana stressed that funding must translate into visible improvements for residents, including more reliable services and better municipal management.

The challenge will be ensuring that the additional allocations result in practical improvements on the ground.



New digital platform planned for government services

Government also plans to spend R150 million developing the MyMzansi app, a digital platform intended to give citizens access to government services through their smartphones.

The initiative forms part of efforts to improve access to public services through digital channels.

Its impact will depend on how effectively the platform is implemented and whether people can access the services they need through it.



What the MTBPS means for South Africans

The 2026 MTBPS presents a balancing act for government.

Stronger tax revenue and a stabilising debt trajectory offer some encouragement, while the temporary fuel levy cuts provide immediate assistance to households and businesses facing high costs.

At the same time, billions have been directed towards social workers, crime prevention, health services, child nutrition and municipal infrastructure.



However, the downgraded growth forecast highlights the scale of the economic challenge. Sustained improvements in employment, investment and household living standards will depend on whether fiscal stability can be translated into stronger economic growth and better public services.

For now, motorists can look towards temporary fuel relief from November, while the longer-term test will be whether government can maintain its fiscal gains and deliver tangible improvements for South Africans.

World.title: Government to spend R3.8 billion to protect women in South Africa
World.content:
Government has reprioritised R3.8 billion to appoint 3 552 social workers as South Africa steps up its response to gender-based violence. Image: SA Govt news website

Government has reprioritised R3.8 billion over the 2027 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) period to appoint 3 552 social workers as South Africa steps up its response to gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF).

Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana announced the funding during his Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement (MTBPS) address to the National Assembly on Wednesday, 21 October.

READ | R38 billion by 2030: What MTBPS said about SASSA grants



The allocation comes amid growing concern over the murders and attacks on women, with government also committing additional funding to strengthen criminal investigations and support survivors of sexual violence.

Godongwana said the measures give effect to President Cyril Ramaphosa’s announcement on the unacceptably high levels of GBVF in South Africa.

R186 million to strengthen criminal investigations

Alongside the social worker appointments, government has allocated R186 million to strengthen forensic and investigative capacity within the criminal justice system.

The funding is intended to improve the state’s ability to investigate cases and respond to crimes involving gender-based violence.

Godongwana also announced plans to expand specialised support for survivors of sexual offences.

“We are expanding sexual offences courts from 55 to 101 and increasing the number of countrywide Thuthuzela Care Centres that provide support to rape victims, from 72 to 80, by 2028/29,” he said.



The expansion would increase the number of dedicated courts and care centres available to assist victims and support the handling of sexual offences cases.

More funding for GBVF coordination

Government has also allocated an additional R157.4 million to the Department of Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities.

Godongwana said the money would improve national coordination and oversight of government’s response to GBVF.

The measures form part of a broader effort to strengthen support services, improve the criminal justice response and address the persistent threat of violence against women.

R556.7 million to support HIV and AIDS services

The MTBPS also addressed funding pressures facing HIV and AIDS programmes following the withdrawal of funding from the United States President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR).

Godongwana said R556.7 million would be reprioritised over the MTEF period to sustain HIV and AIDS services.

This funding will supplement the R3.8 billion already reprioritised through the district health programmes grant.

The allocation is intended to help maintain essential services as South Africa responds to the loss of external funding.

What the allocations mean

The funding commitments announced in the MTBPS cover several areas of public service delivery, from appointing social workers and strengthening forensic investigations to expanding courts and supporting HIV and AIDS programmes.

For South Africa’s GBVF response, the planned appointments and additional criminal justice resources are intended to strengthen the support available to survivors and improve the handling of cases.

The effectiveness of these measures will ultimately depend on how quickly the funding translates into appointments, expanded services and stronger investigative capacity across the country.

World.title: Rulani Mokwena breaking and setting new records at Pyramids
World.content:
Former Mamelodi Sundowns coach Rulani Mokwena is breaking and setting new records at Pyramids FC.

Mokwena joined the Egyptian outfit at the start of the current season, and he is already proving to be settling in well.

He is slowly making the likes of Al Ahly and Zamalek look ordinary teams in this early stages of the campaign.



As things stand, Pyramids lead the standings with 21 points from their opening seven games, and they followed by Al Ahly and Zamalek who are both on 16 points.

RuLANI MOKWENA MAKING WAVES WITH PYRAMIDS IN EGYPT

Now, overall, Mokwena has been in charge of 11 competitive games since joining Pyramids, and he won all of them.

The former Wydad Athletic mentor is the FIRST coach in the history of the club to win 11 games in a row at the start of a season.

There are two coaches who previously went 11 games unbeaten at the start of the season with Pyramids but they were not all wins.

Current Egypt national team coach Hossam Hassan and Argentine mentor Ramon Diaz were also unbeaten in 11 opening games with during their stints with Pyramids.

World.title: ‘Increase the grant’: Pensioners call for more as SASSA brings November payday forward
World.content:
Pensioners are expressing frustration over the value of their monthly grant. At the same time, SASSA has made an important change to their November payment.

Grant recipients shared their concerns in the comments section of The South African’s Facebook page. Many said the Older Persons Grant no longer covers their basic needs.

Donovan Serfontein said government has turned its back on older South Africans.



“People died poor with nothing left for their children and yet the Government is not concern or worried about the nation,” Serfontein wrote.

November SASSA grant moves forward

Pensioners will not have to wait for the first week of November to get paid. Under SASSA’s revised arrangements, the Older Persons Grant will be paid on Friday, 30 October, with the Disability Grant following on Monday, 2 November and the Children’s Grants on Tuesday, 3 November.

The agency said the revised schedule follows consultations with stakeholders to keep grant payments running efficiently and securely during the Local Government Elections on 4 November. SASSA has also set aside Thursday, 5 November, for beneficiaries whose grants are under review.



The agency urged beneficiaries not to visit its offices unnecessarily, as payments will be processed according to the announced schedule.

Early money, longer wait

An early payment may feel like relief, but it comes with a catch. December’s Older Persons Grant is expected on 2 December. That leaves pensioners stretching their November money over more than a month.

This is the same grant that many pensioners already say is too small. The Older Persons Grant pays R2 400 per month to recipients 60 and older.



Pensioners who plan their spending carefully in the first week will be better placed to reach December without running short.

Calls for more support continue

The date change does nothing to address the main concern raised by grant recipients. Many want either more money or lower costs.

Enock Thembekile Jakeni wants SASSA to step in at the till.



“SASSA should issue card to pensioners to get 25% discount in stores & Supermarket,” Jakeni wrote.

Shipho Khosi said government should choose one of two options.

“Either discount at shopping stores or increase in the pension,” Khosi wrote.



SASSA has not announced plans for either proposal.

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: R38 billion by 2030: What MTBPS said about SASSA grants
World.content:
Millions of recipients of SASSA grants were waiting with bated breath to glean any positive news from today’s (Wednesday 21 October) 2026 MTBPS. And Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana debuted a new term we’ll probably be hearing a lot: ‘targeted and responsible savings.’

2026 MTBPS ON SASSA GRANTS

On top of the R12 billion identified for SASSA grants in the February 2026 Budget, Treasury has unlocked a further R38 billion over the 2027 medium-term period. For clarity, this period spans a three-year fiscal horizon from 2027/28 through to 2029/30. Moreover, the minister says R13 billion of that is to come from ‘reducing fraud.’

From there, the 2026 MTBPS shares little detail on where and how this additional money will be allocated. Nevertheless, on a straight-line basis, R13 billion spread over three years is about R4.3 billion a year. And let’s not forget R1.33 billion in irregular payments was flagged by the Auditor-General this past financial year. Our takeaway is that South African Social Security Agency reviews, eLife certification and biometric matching will not only stay, but increase in voracity, to meet these targets.



SOUTH AFRICA’S SOCIAL SAFETY NET

More will be spent on the first 1 000 days of children’s lives through feeding schemes. Image: File

Godongwana reiterated that South Africa’s social wage is one of the most comprehensive on the continent. Spending on healthcare, education, SASSA grants, social development and housing, makes up 60% of government non-interest expenditure. “The budget funds a comprehensive social safety net for old-age, disability and child support to 18-million ‘core’ beneficiaries,” he said.

Moreover, government is allocating R1.6 billion over the 2027 medium-term period (till 2030) to focus on prebirth care. This means the first 1 000 days of life, aimed at tackling stunting and malnutrition. It isn’t a grant increase per say, but it does mean more help to Child Support SASSA grants.

TACKLE HIGH COST OF LIVING

While not directly related to SASSA grants, a few measures to tackle the high cost of living crushing South Africans were addressed. Specifically, the fuel levy will be cut by R3 a litre for diesel and R1.50 for petrol from November to December 2026. Then by R1.50 for diesel and R1 for petrol until January 2027. That’s R10 billion in forgone revenue for the Central Energy Fund (CEF).



Frustratingly, 2026 MTBPS made no mention of the ‘expanded SRD grant’ that’s supposed to morph into some kind of Basic Income Support for the nation’s unemployed. Even though Godongwana kicked that can down the road back in February 2026. As we know, the ‘temporary’ R370 grant is funded only until 31 March 2027. Perhaps the R38 billion allocation in his speech is what it’s earmarked for? And finally, no word on the potential trajectory of future grant increases in 2027 either …

But what do you think? Do you like what you heard from the minister about SASSA grants in his 2026 MTBPS? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Explainer | What Kaizer Chiefs need to do to reach CAF group stage
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs face a decisive 90 minutes on Friday as they attempt to overturn a 1-0 first-leg defeat to Zambia’s Red Arrows. Image: X @KaizerChiefs

Kaizer Chiefs face a decisive 90 minutes on Friday as they attempt to overturn a 1-0 first-leg defeat to Zambia’s Red Arrows and secure a place in the 2026/27 CAF Confederation Cup group stage.

Amakhosi host Red Arrows at the Moses Mabhida Stadium in Durban on Friday, 23 October, at 18:00, knowing their continental campaign is on the line.

A goal down after the first leg, Kaizer Chiefs must find a way past the Zambian side while remaining alert to the threat of an away goal.



What Kaizer Chiefs need to do

Red Arrows won the first leg 1-0, giving them a narrow advantage heading into the return fixture.

Here is how the different results could affect Kaizer Chiefs’ qualification hopes:

Kaizer Chiefs win 1-0: The aggregate score would be level at 1-1. The tie would go to extra time and, if necessary, a penalty shootout

Kaizer Chiefs win 2-0: Amakhosi would qualify with a 2-1 aggregate victory

Kaizer Chiefs win 2-1: The aggregate score would be 2-2, but Red Arrows would advance under the away-goals rule

Kaizer Chiefs win 3-1: Kaizer Chiefs would qualify with a 3-2 aggregate victory

Kaizer Chiefs draw or lose: Red Arrows would progress to the group stage

Why keeping a clean sheet is crucial

The away-goals rule adds another layer of pressure for Kaizer Chiefs.

Because Red Arrows scored once at home in the first leg, an away goal in Durban could prove decisive if the aggregate score is level.

For example, a 2-1 Kaizer Chiefs victory would leave the teams level at 2-2 overall. Red Arrows would progress because they scored in South Africa, while Kaizer Chiefs failed to score in Zambia.

That means a 2-0 victory is enough to send Kaizer Chiefs through, while a 2-1 win would not be sufficient.



If Red Arrows score twice, Kaizer Chiefs would need to win by at least two goals to qualify automatically.

Match details

Fixture: Kaizer Chiefs vs Red Arrows

Competition: CAF Confederation Cup, second preliminary round, second leg

Date: Friday, 23 October

Kick-off: 18:00

Venue: Moses Mabhida Stadium, Durban

First-leg result: Red Arrows 1-0 Kaizer Chiefs

Tickets are available through Computicket and at Shoprite and Checkers outlets nationwide for R80, while hospitality tickets are available at R1 699 and R2 899.

Suite tickets can be purchased through the Moses Mabhida Stadium hospitality team by emailing MMS.Hospitality@durban.gov.za or calling 031 322 3115.

Will Kaizer Chiefs do enough to progress to the CAF Confederation Cup group stage?

Let us know by clicking on the comments banner below …

World.title: Godonwana signals further work on proposed online gambling tax
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - South Africans who gamble online could soon see changes as government explores the proposal of a national online gambling tax.

However, authorities have not yet signed on the dotted line yet.

Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana said consultations are underway around this proposal; including the proposed tax design, its linkages to the existing regulatory framework and the implications for provinces and the currently regulated market.

READ | Godongwana eases fuel pain as growth slows

Godongwana, who delivered the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement in Parliament on Wednesday, said the final design will be made in the February 2027 Budget.

“The submissions received generally recognised the need to address the growth of online gambling and its associated harm,” he said.

The proposal follows a discussion paper published by National Treasury last year.

The discussion paper stated that, due to the surge in online gambling and its impact on society, Treasury proposed that a 20% tax be applied to gross gambling revenue from online betting, including interactive gambling.

READ | SARS rakes in more tax revenue than expected

Meanwhile, Treasury has reported a stronger-than-expected revenue outlook for the current financial year, 2026/2027.

According to Godongwana, gross tax revenue for this year has been revised upwards by R17.1 billion compared with the February estimate.

The increase is largely due to higher collections from corporate tax, dividends tax and VAT.

Additionally, a larger portion of this improvement was attributed to higher commodity prices,.

Treasury said overall, gross tax revenue is projected to increase from R2.14 trillion this year to R2.53 trillion in 2029/30.

World.title: Slight relief at the pumps as Godonwana announces fuel levy cuts
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - For many South Africans, a trip to the petrol station has become another strain on the budget, but there is some good news for your pockets.

Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana has announced a temporary relief to ease the pressure of rising fuel prices on households and businesses.

Delivering the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement on Wednesday, Godongwana said the diesel levy will be cut by R3 per litre, while the petrol levy will be reduced by R1.50 per litre.

The minister said the reduction is expected to take effect from 4 November 2026 until 1 December 2026.

But that is not all.

Godongwana said the relief will then continue at lower rates until 5 January 2027, with diesel reduced by R1.50 per litre and petrol by R1 per litre.

“These measures will provide R10 billion in support, at a fiscal cost of R10 billion in foregone revenue,” he said.

According to the minister, to fund the relief, the R10 billion that was transferred to the Central Energy Fund will be returned to the National Revenue Fund and put into the Contingency Reserve.

World.title: Godongwana cuts GDP growth forecast to 1.2% for 2026
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana has cut South Africa's growth forecast to 1.2% for this year, down from February’s 1.6% projection.

Presenting the Medium-Term Budget in Parliament on Wednesday, Godongwana warned domestically risks remain elevated.

This as he cited prolonged conflict in the Middle East, alongside El Niño and its likely impact on producer costs and output, which he believes could weaken domestic growth.

"Domestic economic activity has already lost some momentum, especially in export-linked sectors." he said.

Godongwana further noted that growth remains sluggish, even as fiscal stability improves.

As such, he said government is betting on structural reforms, stronger state capacity, and infrastructure investment to accelerate growth.

“If we stay the course, growth could exceed 3 per cent per annum,” Godongwana added.

World.title: Police launch manhunt after twin brothers shot dead in Bloemfontein
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Two businessmen, identified as twin brothers and owners of Ekhayeni Lounge Bar, were shot dead in their Ford Ranger in Bochabela on Wednesday.

Police have launched a manhunt for suspects following the fatal shooting of twin businessmen.

The brothers, identified as 52-year-old Kegomodicoe Lekone and Keabecoe Lekone, were gunned down at the gate of a premises on Ramatsoele Street on Wednesday morning.

According to a statement from the office of the Free State Provincial Commissioner, Mangaung police received a report of a shooting in progress from radio control at about 8.51am.

Officers arrived at the scene at approximately 9am, where they found the two victims inside their charcoal-coloured Ford Ranger.

“Both the driver and the passenger suffered gunshot wounds,” police said.

ER24 paramedics declared both men dead at the scene.

The victims were identified as the owners of Ekhayeni Lounge Bar.

A witness told police that he heard gunshots from upstairs in the double-storey building before rushing outside to investigate.

The witness allegedly saw a man running towards a white Chevrolet Aveo hatchback, which then sped away.

“He didn't see if the male person had an object in his hands,” the statement said.

Police believe there may have been two other occupants already inside the vehicle when the man approached it.

The Provincial Serious and Violent Crimes, Murder and Robbery Unit has launched an investigation into the double murder.

Police have appealed to anyone with information that could assist in identifying and locating the suspects to come forward.

Members of the public can contact Colonel Msokoli Bolsick on 082 466 8530, report information at their nearest police station, submit a tip through the MySAPS app or call Crime Stop on 08600 10111.

The investigation is ongoing.

World.title: Jansen takes five for Proteas as Australia forced to follow on
World.content:
GQEBERHA - Marco Jansen took five wickets as Australia collapsed to 99 all out in reply to South Africa's 425-9 declared first innings on the fourth day of the second Test at St George's Park on Wednesday.

With a first innings lead of 326 runs, South Africa enforced the follow-on despite fast bowler Anrich Nortje being out of action with a groin injury.

Tall left-armer Jansen struck with his first ball of the innings when he had nightwatchman Scott Boland caught behind in the second over of the day.

He followed up with the wickets of Travis Head, Matt Renshaw, Alex Carey and Beau Webster as Australia collapsed.

Steve Smith, who twice needed treatment for what appeared to be a neck injury, top-scored for Australia with 28 before being bowled by Wiaan Mulder.

Brief scores:

South Africa 425-9 declared.

Australia 99 (K. Rabada 2-33, M. Jansen 5-33, W. Mulder 2-14).

Match situation: South Africa lead by 326 runs on the first innings and have enforced the follow-on.

World.title: WATCH | Godongwana delivers Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana tables his Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement.



South Africans struggle with soaring fuel prices, stubborn inflation, and rising borrowing costs.



All eyes now turn to Godongwana.



Economists want proof government can rein in debt and steer through the cost-of-living storm.

World.title: Rhodes University hit with 'stomach bug' outbreak
World.content:
MKHANDA - A stomach-related outbreak has hit Rhodes University in Makhanda, in the Eastern Cape.

Over 100 students have been affected and the university says they are closely monitoring reported cases.

Affected students have been receiving medical attention. Cases have also been reported in other parts of Makhanda as well.

World.title: SAFTU calls for plans to tackle unemployment, poverty
World.content:
PRETORIA - The South African Federation of Trade Unions (SAFTU) says the country can become like Spain and France if the country ignores its economic realities.

France has been plagued by social unrest over the last few weeks and SAFTU says South Africa is on the cusp of similar events.

SAFTU is demanding urgent action on unemployment and poverty. They are demanding Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana to table a three-year plan to address the crisis.

Godongwana will be delivering his Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement on Wednesday in Parliament.

"We need a plan," says SAFTU's Zwelinzima Vavi.

"Some of us have been warning about the ticking time bomb, in France it has imploded," he says.

World.title: Mudavadi, Wetang'ula walk out as Sifuna addresses mourners at memorial
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula walked out of the requiem mass of former lawmaker Burudi Nabwera after Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna was invited to address mourners.

In a clip that has since gone viral, the two senior government officials are seen walking towards the entrance of Friends Church in Lang'ata on Wednesday, the venue for the memorial service, while Sifuna took the stage.

Sifuna appeared to acknowledge the departure with "this is Nairobi" quip that drew laughter from mourners.

The incident appears to lay bare the deepening political divisions ahead of the 2027 General Election.

The two leaders’ departure came as Sifuna used the funeral gathering to condemn tribal politics, lament the breakdown of political friendships and pledge to restore the spirit of national unity that defined Kenya at independence.

“At the beginning of this country, when we got independence, we were all Kenyans; there was nothing like tribalism and everyone of us should be available to all of us to sell our policies,” he said.

The senator appeared to take a swipe at those seeking to restrict political associations along regional lines, saying leaders were being judged based on whom they were seen with.

“Some people saw me somewhere with someone and somehow they are telling us that there is a region in this country where none of us is supposed to associate with,” Sifuna said.

The sentiments appeared to castigate government leaders who he said "are not happy" with his association with former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua.

This happened just hours after he met the Democracy for the Citizens (DCP) party leader at his Wamunyoro home in Nyeri on Tuesday, in the company of other Linda Mwananchi movement leaders.

He pledged that, in honour of Nabwera, he would work towards reviving the spirit of unity that characterised the country at independence in 1963.

“I want to make assurance here, in honour of Burudi Nabwera, we will restore that feeling that was there at the beginning of our country in 1963, that all of us, irrespective of our tribe, are Kenyans and we all belong to this society,” he said.

Sifuna, also used the opportunity to woo the Nabwera's nephew, Nabii Nabwera, who is Lugari MP, with whom they have "shared a long political history."

Sifuna also expressed regret that political divisions had separated him from Nabii, whom he described as a friend with whom they journeyed together in ODM.

“Our politics is so petty that being seen with some of us, you are branded and told you are hanging out with Sifuna, you are now a bad person,” he said.

“I miss Nabii Nabwera. You know the things we have done together. You know the journey we have walked together in ODM. I want you by my side on this journey towards the presidency,” he said.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
