World.title: An unusual die-off of southern right whales in Argentine Patagonia alarms scientists
World.content:
An unusual die-off of southern right whales in Argentine Patagonia alarms scientists

21st Wednesday, October 2026 - 14:44 UTC Full article

Neither researchers nor the provincial government will give an official figure until the season ends; unofficially, more than 300 dead whales are being mentioned

Scientists monitoring the southern right whale population at Península Valdés, in Argentina’s Chubut province, have recorded since July an unusual number of deaths among calves and adults which, they expect, could make this the worst year on record. They are investigating the role of a bacterium and of a toxic algal bloom known as “red tide”.

Neither researchers nor the provincial government will give an official figure until the season ends; unofficially, more than 300 dead whales are being mentioned. Until now, the highest figures recorded by the health monitoring programme run by the Whale Conservation Institute since 2003 were 113 dead calves in 2012 and 28 adults in 2022.

In calves, the deaths have been linked to the bacterium Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, which causes erysipelas and can enter through wounds, such as gull bites, or through feeding, explained Mariano Coscarella of the Centre for the Study of Marine Systems at the National Scientific and Technical Research Council (Conicet). In adults, the cause is still under study, although red tide, which caused the 2022 peak, is suspected. According to Coscarella, no evidence has been found that direct human activity caused the deaths, although climate change or El Niño may have influenced ocean conditions.

The health monitoring programme, led by veterinarian Marcela Uhart of the University of California, Davis, is carrying out necropsies and analyses and will add sampling of water and shellfish in the Nuevo and San José gulfs.

Península Valdés is South America’s largest sanctuary for southern right whales. The population visiting it grew from about 500 whales in the late 1990s to a peak of 2,110 in 2025; this year 1,375 were recorded, including 409 calves. The Whale Conservation Institute warned that, as this is a long-lived species, the consequences of a die-off “are not immediate and cannot be measured from isolated figures”.

World.title: Milei calls Sánchez an “unpresentable dictator” in Madrid in the middle of Spain’s election campaign
World.content:
Milei calls Sánchez an “unpresentable dictator” in Madrid in the middle of Spain’s election campaign

21st Wednesday, October 2026 - 14:31 UTC Full article

Milei explained why he has not met Sánchez on any of his seven visits to Spain as head of state: “I’m not going to see a criminal thief like Pedro Sánchez”

Argentine President Javier Milei on Wednesday called Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez an “unpresentable dictator”, “corrupt” and “authoritarian”, and urged Spaniards to “kick the socialists out” of power, at his first public event in Madrid, just over a month before the snap general election on November 29.

At a breakfast organised by the Nueva Economía Forum, Milei explained why he has not met Sánchez on any of his seven visits to Spain as head of state: “I’m not going to see a criminal thief like Pedro Sánchez because I’m not willing to have to sew my pockets shut so I don’t get robbed.” He added: “Wherever there is an enemy of freedom, I will go and confront him.” Of Madrid regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso, whom he will meet in the afternoon, and Vox leader Santiago Abascal, he said they “have healthy and positive ideas to lift Spain out of decline”.

The Socialist Party greeted him with a banner on the façade of its headquarters: “Hello Milei, we lefties welcome you to Spain, the fastest-growing country in Europe.” Sánchez released a video in which he says “I am a leftie”, in a reference to the term Milei uses to insult his left-wing opponents. In May 2024, Spain withdrew its ambassador from Buenos Aires after remarks by Milei about Sánchez’s wife.

The Argentine president linked his trip to his campaign for re-election in 2027. “If we are re-elected, the following four years will be unforgettable,” he said, inviting Spaniards to invest and settle in Argentina, which he said would become “the promised land where good business flows”. He also called the Argentine newspaper Clarín “corrupt” and its journalists “serial liars”.

Milei attributed not being received by King Felipe VI to scheduling problems. According to Royal Household sources quoted by El País, a meeting with the monarch must necessarily be accompanied by one with the prime minister. The Argentine president did not say whether he will attend the Ibero-American Summit, to be held in Madrid on November 4 and 5.

World.title: Lula ramps up public handouts in the final stretch of Brazil’s presidential campaign
World.content:
Lula ramps up public handouts in the final stretch of Brazil’s presidential campaign

21st Wednesday, October 2026 - 14:21 UTC Full article

The largest items are the Bolsa Família increase and subsidies for taxi drivers, ride-hailing drivers, truckers and transport operators to renew their vehicles

Some 20 million Brazilian families begin receiving this week a 15% increase in the Bolsa Família social programme, the centrepiece of a broad package of aid, subsidies and tax cuts announced by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the final stretch of the campaign for Sunday’s runoff, in which he faces Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in a statistical tie.

According to calculations by the newspaper Folha de S.Paulo, the measures announced by Lula over the past year, accelerating during the campaign, add up to almost 300 billion reais, about US$57 billion, over the rest of 2026 and 2027. The largest items are the Bolsa Família increase and subsidies for taxi drivers, ride-hailing drivers, truckers and transport operators to renew their vehicles. After the first round, the president also promised a payment of 5,000 reais to micro-entrepreneurs and partial forgiveness of their debts, scrapped taxes on fuel and pledged free public transport at weekends. Earlier he had launched a new personal debt renegotiation programme and banned online betting.

“This is my last campaign for president and I want this term to be historic,” Lula said on Tuesday at a rally in São Luís. The president, who is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, also challenged his rival to lift secrecy over his family’s assets and phone records, as he has pledged to the electoral court to do for his own.

Bolsonaro promises sharp cuts in public spending, which he put at 250 billion reais in Sunday’s debate, and says he will maintain Bolsa Família and other social programmes, though he has not explained how he will reconcile both goals. Brazil’s public debt stands at around 82% of GDP.

The measures have barely moved the polls, which still show a statistical tie with a slight edge for Bolsonaro, who won the first round with 47.03% of the vote against Lula’s 45.16%. The two candidates will face each other on Friday in their second and final debate, on TV Globo.

World.title: Amazon fires rise 62% in October as deforestation falls to a record low
World.content:
Amazon fires rise 62% in October as deforestation falls to a record low

21st Wednesday, October 2026 - 13:29 UTC Full article

Satellites detected 9,045 fire hotspots in the Brazilian Amazon in the first half of October, 62% more than in the same period last year, amid a drought aggravated by El Niño. The increase contrasts with the fall in deforestation, which over the past year reached its lowest level since 1988.

The situation is particularly serious around Manaus, the capital of Amazonas state, home to more than two million people, which has been covered in smoke for weeks with air quality among the worst in the world. On Saturday, civil defence sent a “severe alert” to residents’ mobile phones urging them to stay at home, and classes were suspended at some schools. The federal government deployed more than 300 firefighters and 11 aircraft to support the fire services.

According to Ane Alencar, director of science at the Amazon Environmental Research Institute, most of the fires are set deliberately, generally to clear land for cattle, and the drought has turned the forest into a tinderbox. Alencar noted that September was the second month with the fewest fires on record and that the situation changed after the first round of the presidential election on October 4, and suggested as a hypothesis that the expectation of a change of government may have played a role: “I think the prevailing thought is ‘we won’t be punished’.” The head of the federal environment agency Ibama, Jair Schmitt, told the newspaper Folha de S.Paulo that the police and the intelligence agency are investigating whether there is “something orchestrated and structured”.

Between August 2025 and July 2026, 3,355 square kilometres of the Amazon were deforested, 42% less than in the previous period and the lowest figure since 1988, against 11,600 square kilometres in 2022. Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government has set a target of zero deforestation by 2030.

The campaign of opposition candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, who faces Lula in Sunday’s runoff, has used the smoke to criticise the government’s record. His programme proposes eliminating illegal deforestation by 2029 using artificial intelligence and satellite imagery. He has not responded to the researcher’s hypothesis.

World.title: The area of Antarctic ozone hole during September reached 15 million km2, says Copernicus
World.content:
The area of Antarctic ozone hole during September reached 15 million km2, says Copernicus

21st Wednesday, October 2026 - 13:01 UTC Full article

“CAMS provides high-quality data, forecasts and analyses needed to understand the state of the ozone layer and track its long-term recovery,” Laurence Rouil said

The Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) (*) has found that the 2026 Antarctic ozone hole reached a significant size threshold slightly earlier than average, aligned with 2025. It has also stayed ahead of average, unlike the previous year.

The 2026 Antarctic ozone hole has been developing at a typical rate since the second half of August, consistent with the previous 46 years. The area of this ozone hole reached 15 million km2 – more than the area of Antarctica, 14.2 million km2– by the end of August 2026, which was slightly earlier than average and similar to development of last year’s ozone hole, which reached the same area on 30 August 2025.

In the first half of September, the area of this year’s ozone hole increased sharply, to an estimated 25 million km2 on 12 September – around 5 million km2 above the average for this period – with forecasts showing a possible further increase in area in mid-September. Ozone depletion in the Southern Hemisphere stratosphere occurs as cold temperatures allow the formation of polar stratospheric clouds, which play a role in activating the chemical removal of ozone via halogens in the presence of sunlight during the austral Spring (August to November). The rapid development of the 2026 ozone hole coincided with a sudden decrease in the minimum temperature at approximately 20km above the South Pole (50 hectopascal / hPa).

However, other ozone hole diagnostics monitored by CAMS, including the ozone column minimum value within the defined area of the ozone hole and the ozone mass deficit, remained close to the average values.

“The Antarctic ozone hole’s development can vary considerably from year to year, depending on a range of atmospheric and chemical factors. While we have seen its area increase rapidly in early September this year, other indicators remain close to historical averages. These findings highlight the importance of monitoring the complicated interaction between human-made disturbances and natural factors. CAMS provides the high-quality data, forecasts and analyses needed to understand the state of the ozone layer and track its long-term recovery,” according to Laurence Rouil, Director of CAMS.

The ozone layer protects life on Earth against harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation, a major cause of skin cancers, by absorbing much of it. Over almost half a century, human-caused emissions5 have resulted in the thinning of this protective layer, putting people at risk. Additionally, global warming tends to cool the stratosphere, which favors the formation of polar stratospheric clouds which, in turn, play a key role in ozone depletion. The thinning of the ozone layer is most pronounced over the Antarctic – where the area of low pressure and cold air (polar vortex) and stratospheric winds are more stable – with the ozone hole there opening each year during the austral Spring.

The Antarctic ozone hole, which has been monitored by ground-based and satellite observations since the late 1970s, spanned a record 29.6 million km2 on 9 September 2006. It also covered its largest average area over a consecutive multi-week period in that month. However, recent years have seen smaller and shorter-lived ozone holes, indicating recovery.

(*) Copernicus is the Earth observation component of the European Union’s Space program, looking at our planet and its environment to benefit all European citizens. The program is coordinated and managed by the European Commission and implemented in partnership with the Member States and European organizations.

The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) is both a research institute and a 24/7 operational service, producing global numerical weather predictions and other data for our Member and Co-operating States and the broader community. It operates a world-class supercomputer facility for weather forecasting and holds one of the largest meteorological data archives.

World.title: Falklands: UK Statement at the UN Fourth Committee on Decolonization
World.content:
Falklands: UK Statement at the UN Fourth Committee on Decolonization

21st Wednesday, October 2026 - 10:15 UTC Full article

“Hydrocarbon activities on the Falkland Islands continental shelf are regulated under Falkland Islands law and conducted in full accordance with international law, including UNCLOS”

Statement by Ambassador Kate Foster, UK Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN, at the UN’s Special Political and Decolonization Fourth Committee. “The United Kingdom has no doubt about its sovereignty over both the Falkland Islands, and South Georgia, and the South Sandwich Islands, and their surrounding maritime areas”.

“Nor do we have any doubt about the Falkland Islanders’ right of self-determination.”

“This is enshrined in the UN Charter and in Article One of both UN covenants on human rights, by virtue of which they are free to determine their political status and pursue their economic, social, and cultural development.

“In the 2013 referendum, which was conducted in line with international standards and was observed by independent, international observers, 99.8 per cent of those who voted wanted to remain their current status as a British Overseas Territory.

“Argentina’s decision to initiate arbitration against the United Kingdom under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) is the latest attempt to undermine the rights and livelihoods of the people of the Falkland Islands.

“The people of the Falkland Islands have freely and democratically chosen their future, and they have every right to develop and manage their natural resources without intimidation, coercion, or interference from others.

“Hydrocarbon activities on the Falkland Islands continental shelf are regulated under Falkland Islands law and conducted in full accordance with international law, including UNCLOS.

“The United Kingdom will continue to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with the Falkland Islands Government and the Falkland Islanders.

“We will robustly defend their wishes, their economy, and their right to determine their own future”.

World.title: Argentina and the UK to face off in Hamburg on November 10 over Falklands oil
World.content:
Argentina and the UK to face off in Hamburg on November 10 over Falklands oil

21st Wednesday, October 2026 - 01:46 UTC Full article

Argentina submitted its request on October 13, pending the constitution of the arbitral tribunal under Annex VII of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea

The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea will hold hearings on November 10 and 11 on Argentina’s request for an order requiring the United Kingdom to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands. The dates were set by the tribunal’s president, Judge Maurice K. Kamga, in an order dated October 20.

The case, officially named the Case concerning hydrocarbon exploitation in the South-West Atlantic Ocean (Argentina v. United Kingdom), will be heard in the main courtroom of the Hamburg-based tribunal. The hearing will be public and broadcast live on its website, where verbatim records will later be published. The detailed schedule of sittings will be announced later.

Argentina submitted its request on October 13, pending the constitution of the arbitral tribunal under Annex VII of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. It seeks four provisional measures, including that the United Kingdom prevent the commencement or continuation of hydrocarbon exploitation through Sea Lion and refrain from granting new permits. To prescribe them, the tribunal must consider that the arbitral tribunal would have prima facie jurisdiction over the dispute and that the situation is urgent.

The United Kingdom has said it will take part in the proceedings, challenge any attempt to use them to settle sovereignty over the archipelago and regard any provisional measures prescribed as binding. Sea Lion, operated by Navitas Petroleum and Rockhopper Exploration, expects first oil in 2028.

World.title: A Russian satellite shadows a US one for days in an unprecedented manoeuvre
World.content:
A Russian satellite shadows a US one for days in an unprecedented manoeuvre

20th Tuesday, October 2026 - 16:10 UTC Full article

The Russian craft carried out “a series of deliberate manoeuvres” around Iceye-X36 between October 15 and 19, alternating between positions ahead of and behind it

A Russian military satellite, Kosmos-2612, manoeuvred for several days at close range to a commercial satellite operated by a US company that supplies images to Ukraine, coming within less than five kilometres, in what space-tracking specialists describe as an unprecedented approach between active satellites belonging to different owners.

According to orbital tracking company LeoLabs, the Russian craft carried out “a series of deliberate manoeuvres” around Iceye-X36 between October 15 and 19, at an altitude of about 540 kilometres, alternating between positions ahead of and behind it. It came within five kilometres on October 16 and then withdrew in a controlled manner; it is now more than 100 kilometres away. LeoLabs says it had never before observed a deliberate approach of this kind sustained over several days.

Short time-lapse of part of this morning’s first pass of ICEYE-X36 (59103) and COSMOS 2612 (68762) over South America under partly cloudy skies. https://t.co/t8RhwmKcV4 — s2a systems (@s2a_systems) October 18, 2026

“This looks like an unprecedented step by Russia, if correct,” wrote astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell, a specialist in tracking space activity, for whom it would be the first known encounter in low Earth orbit between two active satellites without the consent of one of their operators. The head of Germany’s Space Command, Michael Traut, said the Russian satellite was “chasing” the US one and warned that such manoeuvres force satellites to adjust their orbits, consuming fuel and shortening their working lives.

Iceye-X36 belongs to the US subsidiary of Finnish company Iceye, which builds radar satellites capable of imaging at night or through cloud and has worked with Ukraine since 2022. “We are aware of the situation and are monitoring it closely,” the company said. Russia has not explained the mission of Kosmos-2612, launched in April with three other satellites that, according to the US Space Force, approached a Western spacecraft in May.

The episode comes a month after US Air Force Secretary Troy Meink acknowledged that the United States has “space control weapons in orbit”. The 1967 Outer Space Treaty prohibits placing weapons of mass destruction in orbit but not conventional weapons.

World.title: 30 years after the Zapatistas shook Mexico, Indigenous leaders confront an unfinished struggle
World.content:
Thirty years ago, Comandanta Ramona — a diminutive Tzotzil woman representing the Zapatista movement — marched into Mexico City with her masked delegation and helped launch a national Indigenous political space that would become the Congreso Nacional Indígena (CNI).

This October, the CNI returned to the capital for its 30th anniversary inside another potent symbol of Indigenous defiance: a former federal Indigenous affairs building seized six years ago by Otomí women and transformed into the Casa de los Pueblos y Comunidades Indígenas “Samir Flores Soberanes,” named for the Indigenous land and water defender assassinated in Morelos in 2019.

The symbolism was difficult to miss. So was the water.

Across three days of testimony and debate, water surfaced again and again — polluted rivers in Veracruz, depleted aquifers and dirty tap water in Jalisco, wells contested in Puebla, megaprojects and mining threatening communities from Oaxaca to Sonora.

What had begun three decades earlier as a struggle for Indigenous autonomy was now being fought, increasingly, through one of Mexico’s most basic necessities.

‘Why walk alone?’

The CNI traces its birth directly to the political earthquake set off by the Zapatista Army of National Liberation, or EZLN, which rose up in Chiapas on Jan. 1, 1994, demanding land, democracy and Indigenous rights.

Two years later, after the San Andrés dialogues between the Zapatistas and the federal government, Indigenous peoples from around the country took an already growing Indigenous rights movement to the next level, building a national space of their own.

María de Jesús Patricio Martínez — better known as Marichuy, a Nahua traditional healer from Jalisco and longtime CNI spokeswoman who in 2017 became the first Indigenous woman to seek Mexico’s presidency — recalled those beginnings at the opening plenary.

Communities barely knew one another then, she said, but quickly discovered how much they had in common: land disputes, poor health and education services, internal divisions often fueled from outside.

“If our problems are the same, why walk alone?” she recalled them asking.

The answer became the CNI: not a political party or government body, but an autonomous gathering of Indigenous peoples, nations, tribes and communities committed to defending territory and exercising self-determination on their own terms.

For the anniversary gathering, that autonomy was visible in the architecture of the event itself. Indigenous delegates met privately in working groups inside the building. Outside, beneath a vast tent spanning the closed-off street, invited allies — students, feminists, environmentalists, human-rights defenders, families of the disappeared and other organizations — held separate discussions about how to support the CNI without trying to direct it.

At public plenaries, the two groups came together to compare conclusions. Then the Indigenous delegates went back inside to continue their own deliberations, while a music and art festival and street fair unfolded under the big tent.

Water as a warning

If one issue linked the wildly different geographies and populations represented at the gathering, it was water.

Cecilia Sánchez Martínez, of the Veracruz collective Mujeres que Luchan por la Vida, described communities resisting megaprojects that, she said, leave few jobs but contaminate “our rivers, our beaches, our lagoons and all the bodies of water we have.”

Wixárika delegates from western Mexico spoke of aquifers threatened by mining and industrial agriculture. Participants from Puebla described communities confronting police and machinery over wells. Others spoke of dams, tourism developments, industrial corridors and urban expansion.

Carlos Beas Torres, a longtime non-Indigenous ally of the CNI and veteran organizer, argued that such conflicts are precisely why the Congress matters beyond Indigenous communities.

“The message the Congreso Nacional Indígena is sending is not for Indigenous peoples,” he said. “It is a message that goes beyond.”

One of the clearest expressions of the broader crisis, he said, is water — pointing to Guadalajara, where hundreds of thousands of residents have been receiving discolored, tainted water.

Buying another garrafón may get a family through the day, he said, but it does nothing to resolve the underlying problem.

The same pattern surfaced repeatedly during the gathering: seemingly local conflicts over a spring, aquifer, forest or river leading back to larger questions about who gets to decide what happens to a territory — communities, governments or corporations.

‘With or without a law’

The anniversary soon turned into a direct challenge to the Sheinbaum government.

The administration has celebrated the 2024 constitutional reform recognizing Indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples as subjects of public law as a historic advance. But CNI delegates were deeply suspicious of the proposed law intended to put those rights into practice — both because of what it contained and because of how Indigenous communities were being asked to review it.

Ramón González López, a Wixárika former communal land commissioner from Tuxpan de Bolaños, described communities being handed a massive document and asked for an opinion almost immediately.

“They arrive all of a sudden and say, ‘Here, we have this law, and we need you to review it and tell us whether it’s good or bad,’” he said. “Almost overnight. That’s not right.”

Then he held up the scale of the task: “This huge book, more than 450 articles. Who wrote it? How did they write it? Why did they write it? Why weren’t we invited when they were writing it? … You can’t review something like that in one or two days.”

By the second day, representatives of 35 Indigenous peoples had reached a near-unanimous position: reject the proposal.

Reporting back to the plenary, delegates declared: “With law or without law, we will continue exercising our free self-determination according to the different territories we inhabit.”

The final pronouncement went further.

Carlos González, an Indigenous attorney from Jalisco, founding member of the CNI and one of Mexico’s leading legal voices on Indigenous rights, read the closing declaration.

“Indigenous consultation is a power belonging to our peoples, not to the state or to corporations,” it stated.

Communities themselves, through their assemblies and customary systems, must decide whether consultation is appropriate, the document continued.

“The occupation of our territories and the destruction of our peoples are not matters for consultation.”

The declaration called on the CNI to strengthen and expand its presence across Mexico and urged participating communities to carry the agreements back to their own assemblies. It also demanded action on disappearances, political prisoners and attacks on land defenders while reaffirming support for Zapatista autonomy.

Resistance — and joy

For all the grim testimony, the gathering itself was remarkably buoyant.

Music filled the courtyard at night. Murals were painted. Workshops ranged from political education to composting the waste generated in the dry toilets set up to accommodate the gathering. Children ran between meetings. Young people played pelota, the prehispanic predecessor to soccer, in the cordoned-off street. Steaming and delicious food appeared in enormous pots, piled high into bowls served by Otomí women in their colorful pleated collars.

One working-group report captured that contradiction: resistance, it said, was not simply saying no to megaprojects or government laws, but continuing “through love, through hope, but also through rebellion.”

There was also a clear sense of generational handoff.

Some of the veterans who helped build the CNI are now elderly. Younger delegates, women and first-time attendees were everywhere.

Noé Valentín Aguilar Rojas, from the Indigenous community of San Lorenzo de Azqueltán in Jalisco, was attending the national CNI gathering for the first time with his 22-year-old son Fernando, now serving in his community’s highest position of authority as communal land commissioner. His community has been engaged in a historic struggle to recover their stolen lands, a struggle that led to last year’s assassination of one of their leaders. Hearing so many stories of dispossession and resistance was overwhelming, he said — but also strangely reassuring.

The details differed from place to place, but “the struggle of everyone is the same,” he said. “One person’s path belongs to all of us.”

1 of 5

A building changes hands

The CNI formally closed its anniversary gathering shortly after 2 p.m. on Oct. 12.

Then the Otomí women who had hosted the Congress took the microphone.

Six years earlier, they had occupied the headquarters of the federal Indigenous affairs agency and refused to leave, turning it instead into housing, an organizing center and a meeting place for movements far beyond their own community.

Now, invoking Comandanta Ramona and the Zapatistas, they announced that the Casa de los Pueblos would become patrimony of the CNI and the EZLN.

Thirty years after Ramona marched into Mexico City to help create a national Indigenous movement, another group of Indigenous women stood on a stage in front of a government building they had claimed for themselves and handed it, symbolically, to that movement.

The anniversary was over.

The unfinished struggle was not.

World.title: Mexico suspends chicken imports from Brazil over Newcastle disease outbreak
World.content:
Mexico on Monday suspended chicken imports from Brazil, the world’s largest chicken meat exporter, following reports of a Newcastle disease outbreak in that country.

Mexico’s National Service for Agrifood Health, Safety and Quality (Senasica) halted imports of chicken meat, all live birds and fertile eggs to prevent the spread of Newcastle disease to Mexico, a measure that will apply to commercial imports and products carried in by tourists.

Newcastle disease is a highly contagious respiratory infection in birds that can cause neurological disorders, reduced egg production and high mortality rates, according to the World Organization for Animal Health. It poses no serious risk to humans.

Brazilian authorities first detected an outbreak of the disease at a commercial turkey farm in southern Brazil on Sunday, Brazil’s public news agency reported.

Brazil’s Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock then confirmed the presence of the disease at a commercial broiler chicken farm in the municipality of Nova Itaberaba, Santa Catarina state, on Monday.

The agency reassured the public that the facility had been closed and that measures had been implemented to control and eradicate the outbreak.

Brazil exports a massive 30% of its chicken production, according to official figures, and, in 2025, Mexico was Brazil’s seventh-largest poultry buyer.

This is the second time in 17 months that Mexico has suspended the import of poultry products from Brazil. In May and June 2025, Mexico, China, the European Union and other Latin American countries halted imports of Brazilian chicken due to an outbreak of avian influenza.

The last outbreak of Newcastle disease in Brazil occurred in July 2024 in Santa Catarina’s neighboring state of Rio Grande do Sul. During that period, chicken exports fell by about 25%, or 100,000 metric tonnes, according to estimates by analysts at JPMorgan. However, trade quickly rebounded as markets reopened.

The current outbreak is not expected to cause lasting damage to Brazil’s poultry industry so long as authorities can contain it quickly, according to analysts.

With reports from Noticias DW and Reuters

World.title: Mexico’s economy grew 3.7% last month, compared to September 2025
World.content:
Mexico’s economy grew 3.7% year over year in September, according to preliminary seasonally adjusted data published on Tuesday by the national statistics agency INEGI.

The annual growth rate is the highest of any month so far this year, exceeding July’s 3.3% expansion and a 3.2% estimated increase in August.

INEGI also published preliminary data on Tuesday that showed that Mexico’s economy grew 0.1% on a month-over-month basis in September. That growth rate is significantly lower than the 0.5% month-over-month expansion in August, according to INEGI’s latest estimate.

Both the annual and month-over-month growth rates for September are subject to revision. Final data for the month will be published in late November.

Services sector growth hits 4%

INEGI’s preliminary data shows that Mexico’s tertiary, or services, sector recorded 4% year-over-year growth in September, up from a 3.7% expansion in August.

The secondary sector — which includes manufacturing, construction, mining and electricity generation — expanded 3.6%, according to the preliminary data, on par with the growth rate in August.

INEGI didn’t publish preliminary data for the primary sector.

Analyst: Annual growth in Q3 could exceed 3%

In an X post on Tuesday, Banco Base’s director of economic analysis, Gabriela Siller, wrote that GDP data for the third quarter of 2026 “could show” quarter-over-quarter growth of 0.99% and annual growth of 3.04%.

En México, el PIB del tercer trimestre podría mostrar un crecimiento trimestral de 0.99% y anual de 3.04%, de acuerdo a las cifras del indicador oportuno de la actividad económica (IOAE). Esto se debe a que el IOAE de agosto fue revisado al alza, de un crecimiento mensual de 0.14% a 0.47%. Por su parte, en septiembre el IOAE mostró un crecimiento mensual de 0.09%. — Gabriela Siller Pagaza (@GabySillerP) October 20, 2026

An annual growth rate of 3.04% would represent a significant improvement from the expansions recorded in the first and second quarters of the year. Mexico’s economy grew 0.4% in annual terms in Q1 and 1.9% in Q2.

On a quarter-over-quarter basis, Mexico’s economy contracted 0.6% in Q1 and grew 1.4% in Q2.

Annual GDP growth in 2025 was just 0.8%.

In a separate X post on Tuesday, Siller wrote that there are “three factors that support greater economic growth in Mexico this year.”

Those factors, she wrote, are “the downward revision of GDP in the second quarter of 2025” as well as “greater public spending on physical infrastructure, which has a multiplier effect on the economy,” and “the high growth of computer equipment exports, reaching 209.75% annually in the cumulative total through August.”

Earlier this month, the International Monetary Fund revised its 2026 growth forecast for Mexico’s economy to 1.5% from a previous prediction of 1.2%.

World.title: Music, masked dancing and Afro-Mexican coastal traditions took center stage at Oaxaca’s first Afro Guelaguetza
World.content:
Twelve delegations brought music, masked dancers and coastal traditions to Oaxaca’s first Afro Guelaguetza on Monday, celebrating Afro-Mexican heritage and highlighting communities that officials said had long lacked recognition.

La Rejunjuneada — loosely meaning “the get-together” — took place in Chacahua Isla, a community on Oaxaca’s Pacific coast that has a predominantly Afro-descendant population. It lies in the Costa Chica, a coastal region spanning Oaxaca and Guerrero and a historic heartland of Afro-Mexican culture.

The festival marked Oaxaca’s Afro-Mexican People’s Day, an Oct. 19 observance established in 2013. A procession along the lagoon and through local streets preceded performances on a stage beside Chacahua Lagoon.

Afro-Mexican communities already participate in Oaxaca’s better-known July Guelaguetza, which showcases traditions from across the state. For example, Collantes, an Afro-Mexican town on Oaxaca’s coast, sent its Dance of the Devils delegation to this July’s festival.

The distinction is the focus: La Rejunjuneada gave those Afro-Mexican traditions and others their own dedicated festival rather than only a place in the broader statewide celebration.

Oaxaca Gov. Salomón Jara Cruz said recognizing communities’ histories must also translate into rights, justice and opportunities.

Villa de Tututepec Mayor Eder Muñoz Peña described the municipality’s Chatino, Mixtec and Afro-Mexican roots, saying the celebration represented historical justice as well as cultural pride.

The host delegation opened with the Fandango de Varitas. Another community performed the Turtle Dance, plus there were two interpretations of the Dance of the Devils — a highly representative expression of Afro-Mexican culture, with dancers wearing horned masks stomping and leaping to the music.

Enid Azucena Torres Agustiniano also participated. This summer, she was the first Afro-Mexican woman ever chosen as Goddess Centéotl — the main Guelaguetza’s cultural ambassador.

In Mexico’s 2020 census, 8.6% of Guerrero residents and 4.7% of Oaxaca residents identified as Afro-Mexican or Afro-descendant, compared with 2% nationwide, according to figures from Conapred, the federal anti-discrimination agency.

With reports from Quadratin and La Razón

World.title: Man arrested at Oaxaca International Airport with more than US $366K in undeclared cash
World.content:
Federal agents at the Oaxaca International Airport seized US $365,865 and nearly 6,000 pesos ($326) that a passenger arriving from Dallas, Texas, was carrying in his luggage.

Personnel from the National Customs Agency of Mexico (ANAM), the Navy Ministry, the National Guard and the federal Security Ministry (SSPC) participated in the operation.

➡️ En el Aeropuerto Internacional de Oaxaca, autoridades detuvieron a una persona procedente de Dallas, Estados Unidos, que transportaba sin declarar más de 365 mil dólares y 5 mil 900 pesos mexicanos. https://t.co/cjasoLY581 — IMER Noticias (@IMER_Noticias) October 20, 2026

The unidentified passenger stated to customs officials that he had nothing to declare, but the detection dog “Cinta” alerted its handler to the man’s baggage.

As a result, customs personnel carried out a physical inspection of the four suitcases and a backpack the traveler was toting, eventually locating several packages with dollar bills and national currency hidden among the contents.

In a press release, ANAM said that given the possible commission of a crime, the National Guard was notified and their agents seized the cash and carried out the count.

The Navy and the SSPC then arrested the suspect and informed him of his rights, after which he — and the seized money — were placed at the disposal of the Federal Attorney General’s Office, which will determine his legal status.

The newspaper Milenio reported that this was the first significant incident involving undeclared cash at a Mexican airport since members of the National Guard seized 16 million pesos (then worth about US $750,000) and arrested two at the Mexico City International Airport more than six years ago.

On Feb. 24, 2020, National Guard personnel found 14 million pesos in a suitcase and a backpack after an X-ray inspection, while 2 million pesos were confiscated from another passenger’s hand luggage after a routine inspection uncovered envelopes containing hundreds of peso notes of varying denominations wrapped in transparent plastic.

Visitors to Mexico are permitted to enter the country with cash totaling less than US $10,000 (or the equivalent in other currencies) without declaring it. However, customs officials must be notified upon arrival if carrying more than that.

With reports from El Universal, Línea Directa and Milenio

World.title: Morena is the clear favorite in Mexico’s 2027 midterm elections, say the (very) early polls
World.content:
Mexico’s midterm elections are set for June 2027, and the ruling party Morena has a commanding lead in national electoral preferences with 46% of voter intention, according to an Oct. 19 poll by the newspaper El Financiero.

In the poll, which measures generic party preference and not individual races, the National Action Party (PAN) is a distant second with 8% of respondents saying they would vote for the party. Although it may be more meaningful to give second place to “no preference,” which accounted for 31% of the responses, leaving room for some preference shifts down the line.

Following the PAN’s 8% are the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) with 6% and Citizens’ Movement (MC) with 5%. Meanwhile, the Green Party (PV) and Labor Party (PT), both allied with Morena, received 2% and 1% of voter intention, respectively.

The two new parties — PAZ and Somos — are still stuck in neutral, each garnering less than 1%.

In addition to measuring voting intention, the poll asked respondents for their opinion of each party. Here, Morena swept again. Not only did it record the highest favorable rating at 55%, but its two electoral partners finished second and third with 31% (PV) and 29% (PT).

The PAN earned a positive opinion from just 26% of eligible voters and the PRI 21%. More significantly, those two parties — the previous two to hold power before Morena — are burdened with negative ratings of 64% and 70%.

The 17 governor races are not all so cut-and-dry

A recent report by Político MX measured party support in the 17 state governorships up for election in 2027, using a variety of early polls. Here again, the results favor Morena but not quite as decidedly as the national poll.

Poll data is shaky at this point, but here’s the picture so far:

In Baja California, Guerrero, Tlaxcala, Campeche, Colima, Nayarit, Quintana Roo and Zacatecas, candidates from Morena or its allied bloc lead comfortably across all the polls reviewed, often by double digits.

In Sinaloa and Michoacán, Morena’s lead is less solid. One poll even showed the upstart candidate Grecia Quiroz, widow of the slain mayor of Uruapan, in the lead.

The northern states of Baja California Sur, Chihuahua, Sonora and Nuevo Léon, are toss-ups, with the PAN in the first three and the PRI and MC in Nuevo León challenging Morena.

In three El Bajío states, Morena could be the underdog. Querétaro and Aguascalientes are leaning toward the PAN, and in San Luis Potosí the incumbent PV has split from Morena and will run its candidate against its former electoral partner.

With reports from El Financiero and Político

World.title: UN chairman brings missing persons crisis in Mexico before General Assembly committee
World.content:
A U.N. committee responsible for monitoring the International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance again pressed the General Assembly to take up the issue of disappearances in Mexico.

The chairman of the Committee on Enforced Disappearances on Tuesday presented the annual report to the General Assembly’s Social, Humanitarian and Cultural Committee (Sochum), reiterating its assertion that the situation in Mexico ought to be categorized as crimes against humanity, a proposal that Mexico has rejected.

Mañana compareceré ante la Tercera Comisión de la Asamblea General de la @ONU_es para presentar el informe anual del Comité contra la Desaparición Forzada @UNTreatyBodies. Esta comparecencia tiene una relevancia particular. Por primera vez desde la entrada en vigor de la Convención, el Comité ha recurrido al artículo 34 para llevar una situación a la consideración de la Asamblea General. Este procedimiento excepcional abre una oportunidad para movilizar la cooperación internacional en materia de búsqueda, investigación, esclarecimiento de la verdad y protección de las víctimas. También informaré sobre los avances de nuestro trabajo y las graves consecuencias que la crisis financiera de las Naciones Unidas está teniendo para el cumplimiento de nuestro mandato. En un momento especialmente difícil para el sistema internacional de derechos humanos, resulta fundamental que los mecanismos de protección puedan cumplir eficazmente las responsabilidades que los Estados les han confiado. 📅 Martes 20 de octubre, 15h00 (Nueva York). 🔴 Transmisión en vivo:

https://t.co/GLbxtfZ0Ax #UNGA81 #CED — Juan Pablo Albán (@JuanPablo_Alban) October 19, 2026

Sochum is one of six permanent U.N. committees that include representatives of all 193 member states.

“[G]iven the existence of well-founded indications that enforced disappearances have been and continue to be perpetrated in [Mexico],” Juan Pablo Albán Alencastro of Ecuador, the chairman of the Committee on Enforced Disappearances (CED), urged the General Assembly to formally take up the matter.

This marks the first time since the entry into force of the International Convention against Enforced Disappearances (CPED) that the committee in charge of monitoring compliance has recommended that the situation in a specific country be examined by the General Assembly. Albán had initially brought the issue to the Assembly’s attention in April.

The submission of CED’s annual report does not mean a resolution has been issued regarding Mexico, however, nor does it imply that a judgment has been made.

“This exceptional procedure opens an opportunity to mobilize international cooperation in the search for the missing, the investigation of cases, as well as truth-telling and protection of victims,” Albán said.

The goal, Albán said, is to provide support “for the adoption of preventive measures that will enable Mexico to tackle the crisis effectively.”

On Friday, Mexico’s Interior Ministry presented the U.N. with a progress report on the National Strategy for the Search for Missing Persons, while declaring that more than 16,000 people had been located this year.

Mexico also said a group of national and international specialists, with the support of the U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights, is reviewing the methodologies of the National Registry of Missing and Unlocated Persons.

The International Federation for Human Rights, which requested the U.N. activate CPED procedures, thanked the committee for its actions in a press release.

The decision “acknowledges the existence of international crimes that are emblematic of what victims are experiencing in [Mexico] and seeks to contribute to the adoption of measures aimed at preventing, investigating, punishing and eradicating such conducts,” it said.

With reports from El Universal, Aristegui Noticias and Milenio

World.title: MND Local BCS: Upcoming one-of-a-kind events in Los Cabos
World.content:
A little over two weeks after the return of high season in Los Cabos, the event calendar is already in full swing. Highlights so far include Sammy Hagar’s 36th edition of his annual birthday bash at the iconic Cabo Wabo Cantina in Cabo San Lucas, and Bisbee’s Los Cabos Offshore fishing tournament, with its robust prize pool exceeding US $2.39 million.

Over 100,000 requests were received for the 1,600 available tickets to attend “The Red Rocker’s” 79th birthday celebrations at Cabo Wabo on Oct. 9, 11 and 13. Joining him on stage were long-time collaborators like guitarist Vic Johnson (a bandmate of Hagar’s in The Waboritas and Sammy Hagar and The Circle) and drummer Kenny Aronoff (a bandmate in Chickenfoot) — as well as the always highly anticipated special guests. Notable among the latter category was Jerry Cantrell of Alice in Chains, who joined in on a version of his own band’s hit “Man in the Box,” plus the Van Halen classic “Ain’t Talkin’ ‘Bout Love” during the Oct. 11 show.

Unrehearsed and unpredictable

“That’s part of the charm of the Birthday Bash,” Hagar told Billboard. “It’s not rehearsed, and we never know really what we’re gonna do. I don’t invite people; I just invite kind of a house band, you might say. I’ve got a repertoire of about 400 songs, and if somebody says they know one of them, we throw it together real quick and go out and do it.”

As for Bisbee’s Los Cabos Offshore, over 122 teams competed during the three days of fishing, and there was more than one winner: Team Tikki Perro caught the biggest fish, a 350-pound blue marlin that narrowly beat the 347-pound blue marlin caught by Team Loose Crew on the final day of fishing. Those teams finished first and second in the standings, but due to timing and jackpots, the biggest winner monetarily was the third-place finisher, Team Trixie, who walked away with an oversized check for US $1,589,0007 for reeling in a 334-pound black marlin the day previous, and sweeping all daily jackpots.

But this drama was merely a prelude to the world’s most lucrative fishing tournament, which takes place this week.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bisbee’s Offshore Tournaments (@fishbisbees)

The biggest single event on the Los Cabos sports calendar, Bisbee’s Black and Blue marlin fishing tournament has been a local institution since its founding in 1982. Its impact, however, is global: No fishing tournament on the planet has ever topped the record US $11,651,300 prize pool offered by the Black and Blue in 2022.

As the name suggests, blue and black marlin are the most valuable catches — provided they meet the minimum 300-pound limit. In 2025, three teams earned checks totaling upwards of US $1.7 million for boating blue marlin, with the two largest in excess of 450 pounds.

This year, for the first time, Bisbee’s has added a fourth event to its Baja California Sur schedule: Mag Bay Mania in Bahía Magdalena, Comondú municipality. The format is also novel, with teams given the entire month of November to choose three days to fish, with 100 points each garnered for all virtually verified catches and releases of qualifying billfish (including blue, black and striped marlin, sailfish and spearfish).

The other three events — the East Cape Offshore, Los Cabos Offshore and iconic Black and Blue — all take place in Los Cabos. The prize pool for the 2026 Black and Blue, aka “The Super Bowl of Fishing,” is US $7.4 million.

Dates: Oct. 19-24

Location: Boats depart from the Cabo San Lucas Marina, with fishing permitted within a 50-nautical-mile radius.

Cost: Base entry is US $5,000 per team, or US $84,500 “all-in” to include daily jackpots.

Founded by Latitude 38 publisher Richard Spindler back in 1994, this epic annual 750-mile cruisers rally from San Diego to Cabo San Lucas celebrates its 32nd edition in 2026. This year’s sail, however, will be the first without Spindler as “Grand Poobah” of the proceedings, as he stepped down and sold Baja Ha-Ha LLC after last year’s event, citing age as the reason (he’s 78).

San Diego Sailmaker Chuck Skewes is the new Grand Poobah, or “Newbah,” and has stated he plans no major overhauls. A nine-time participant himself, he also has the expertise of longtime Assistant Poobah Patsy Verhoeven, a veteran of 20 Baja Ha-Has, to lean on. Boats will depart San Diego on Nov. 2 following the pre-launch costume party, with two stops planned along the way before scheduled merrymaking in Cabo San Lucas — including the “Can’t Believe We Cheated Death Again” dance party at El Squid Roe on Nov. 13, and an awards banquet at Mango Deck on Nov. 14, with awards given out in categories such as “most miles sailed” and “biggest fish caught” along the way.

Dates: Nov. 2-14

Location: Departs from San Diego, California, and arrives in Cabo San Lucas following stops at Bahía Tortuga and Bahía Santa María.

Cost: Entry fee is US $595.

Fishing and hunting-focused publication Western Outdoor News (WON) has a long history with Los Cabos, dating back to the halcyon days of Baja columnist and “The Sea of Cortez” author Ray Cannon, who helped put the area on the travel map in the 1950s and 1960s — largely because of its superb sportfishing.

The Los Cabos Tuna Jackpot was first organized by WON in Cabo San Lucas in 1999, and by 2019 it had crossed the million-dollar prize pool threshold. Now recognized as the richest tuna fishing tournament in the world, the 2025 prize pool exceeded US $1.4 million (just shy of the 2022 record of US $1,533,800), with Team North Star pocketing a cool US $572,225 for reeling in a 253-pound yellowfin.

But it’s not all about the money, as the tournament motto (“fish hard, party harder”) makes clear.

Dates: Nov. 4-7

Location: Cabo San Lucas Marina, with no off-limits boundary line for fishing.

Cost: Base entry is US $1,000 per team, or US $50,500 to include all daily jackpots.

The only PGA-sponsored golf tournament in Los Cabos — and one of only two in Mexico — returns to the Tiger Woods-designed El Cardonal course at Diamante for its 20th edition this year (the fourth based in Cabo San Lucas after 16 years on the Riviera Maya).

The last two tournament winners, Austin Eckroat (2024) and Ben Griffin (2025), have both confirmed they’ll return this year. However, since players aren’t required to commit until Oct. 30, the rest of the field is mostly still unknown, outside fan favorite “Cashmere Keith” Mitchell, Mexican invitee Álvaro Ortiz and Mexican qualifiers Alejandro Madariaga and Jorge Villar.

For the first time, both of Mexico’s PGA tournaments — the VidantaWorld Mexico Open in Nuevo Nayarit and the World Wide Technology Championship — will appear back-to-back on the schedule as part of the FedExCup Fall series.

Dates: Nov. 5-8

Location: El Cardonal Golf Course, Diamante, Cabo San Lucas

Cost: General admission tickets are US $139 for the four-day tournament, with daily tickets available from US $35. Access to VIP hospitality areas, however, runs significantly higher. The Skybox overlooking the 18th green, for example, costs US $1,499 for the duration of the tournament.

Chris Sands is a writer and editor for Mexico News Daily, and the former Cabo San Lucas local expert for the USA Today travel website 10 Best and writer of Fodor’s Los Cabos travel guidebook. He has also contributed to numerous other websites and publications, including The San Diego Union-Tribune, Marriott Bonvoy Traveler, Forbes Travel Guide, Porthole Cruise and Travel, and Cabo Living.

World.content:

CHILE · CONCERTS

Key Facts — The night Hawaii-born singer-songwriter Jack Johnson plays Santiago on Wednesday 10 February 2027.

— Where it is The Movistar Arena, renamed Santander Arena in September 2026, in Parque O’Higgins, Santiago.

— How to buy Tickets are sold through Puntoticket, the venue’s only official seller; general sale opened on Friday 10 July 2026.

— What it costs Prices run from 42,600 Chilean pesos (US$43) to 111,600 pesos (US$114), service fee included.

— Start time Puntoticket and the arena’s own listing say 21:00 (9 in the evening); the artist’s page differs, and doors are not confirmed.

— For US visitors No visa is needed for tourist stays of up to 90 days on a US passport.

— Power Index Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 63.6 points (October 2026 edition).

The Jack Johnson Santiago concert is set for Wednesday 10 February 2027 at the arena in Parque O’Higgins, formerly the Movistar Arena. It is a chance for US fans to see a Hawaii-born surf-folk star in the middle of the Chilean summer.

Tickets for the Jack Johnson Santiago night go through Puntoticket, the arena’s only official seller, from US$43 to US$114 with fees included. The singer plays Buenos Aires five days earlier, so a South American trip is easy to plan.

Who Jack Johnson Is and Why This Show Matters

Jack Johnson is an American singer-songwriter born in Hawaii, known for relaxed acoustic songs and a surfer’s outlook. The Clinic, a Chilean outlet, says he has sold more than 25 million records worldwide.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Chile ranks 3rd of 14 with 63.6 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (86); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (38). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

His catalogue includes eight studio albums and three live albums. Fans will expect classics such as “Better Together” and “Sitting, Waiting, Wishing”.

The tour behind the Santiago date is called SURFILMUSIC, like his documentary about his path from surfer to filmmaker to musician. He scored it with the Hermanos Gutiérrez duo, and the film and soundtrack came out on Friday 15 May 2026.

On stage, Johnson is joined by Adam Topol, Merlo Podlewski and Zach Gill, according to the Chilean broadcaster 24horas. The Jack Johnson Santiago show is billed as a celebration of two decades in music and surf.

Chilean outlet El Dínamo counts this as his fourth visit to Chile. The artist’s tour page also lists Buenos Aires on Friday 5 February and Rio de Janeiro on Tuesday 16 February 2027.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Tickets, Prices and How to Buy

Puntoticket is the official seller for the Jack Johnson Santiago concert, and the arena names it as its only one. Tickets cost 42,600 to 111,600 Chilean pesos (about US$43 to US$114), service fee included.

The cheapest seat is the Tribuna, at 37,000 pesos plus a 5,600-peso fee, or 42,600 pesos in total (about US$43). Platea Alta Silver costs 48,300 pesos in total (about US$49).

Platea Alta Golden and the standing Cancha floor both cost 54,100 pesos in total (about US$55). Platea Baja Silver costs 94,300 pesos (about US$96), and Platea Baja Golden costs 111,600 pesos (about US$114).

Puntoticket also lists universal-access places for wheelchair users and a companion seat, both at 54,100 pesos (about US$55). All dollar figures in this article use 981 Chilean pesos per US dollar, the rate on Wednesday 21 October 2026.

A Banco de Chile presale ran from Wednesday 8 July 2026, and general sale opened at noon on Friday 10 July. Puntoticket sets a limit of 10 tickets per buyer, and there is no age restriction, with children paying from age 2.

The Venue and How to Get There

The Jack Johnson Santiago show takes place inside Parque O’Higgins, a large public park in central Santiago, at Avenida Beauchef 1204. It carried the Movistar name for years, and Banco Santander took over the naming rights in September 2026.

CNN Chile reports the new name was presented on Saturday 5 September 2026. Tickets and listings may still say Movistar Arena, so treat both names as the same building.

CNN Chile puts the maximum capacity at about 15,500 people, depending on the stage layout. The operator, Arena Santiago, is controlled by Live Nation, according to the same report.

The simplest route is the Santiago Metro, Line 2, to the Parque O’Higgins station, a short walk from the arena. Ride-hailing apps and regulated taxis also work, but expect traffic around the park after the show.

Cars enter only with a prior parking ticket sold through Puntoticket, at the gate on Avenida Viel or Tupper street. Pedestrians enter from the Parque O’Higgins Metro side or from Tupper street.

Tips for US and Foreign Visitors

For the Jack Johnson Santiago trip, US citizens need no visa for tourist stays up to 90 days, the State Department says. Your passport must be valid for the whole stay and have a blank page for the entry stamp.

On arrival you receive a Tourist Card, which you must hand back when you leave. At the arena, the venue asks for your ticket plus an ID card or passport.

The State Department rates Chile Level 2, exercise increased caution, in its advisory of 19 August 2026. It names crime, unrest and health as the main risks.

The arena bans bottles, food, drinks, umbrellas and professional cameras, and every fan passes a security check. Use regulated taxis with orange or yellow plates, or a legal ride-hailing app.

Chile has frequent earthquakes, and wildfires peak from December to March, the State Department says. Follow SENAPRED, the national disaster agency, and obey local instructions.

Demonstrations can happen with little notice and often disrupt buses and the Metro. Check the situation on the day, and keep the US Embassy number, +56 2 2330 3000, in your phone.

Santiago is large, so a hotel near a Metro line makes the trip home after the show easier. For city costs and areas to stay, see our Santiago expat guide and our Chile safety guide for expats.

What Is Not Confirmed Yet

The start time of the Jack Johnson Santiago show is not settled, since Puntoticket and the arena’s calendar both list 21:00. The artist’s tour page instead gives doors at 19:00 and the show at 20:00.

No support act has been announced, and the promoter has not published a door time or any rules specific to this date. Check Puntoticket and the arena’s website nearer the show.

Puntoticket still offered tickets for sale on Wednesday 21 October 2026, but it does not say how many remain. Availability in each zone is not confirmed.

The artist’s tour page also lists a Surfestival date in Pichilemu on Saturday 13 February 2027. The festival’s own website did not confirm that booking on that day, so it stays unconfirmed.

The last Metro train time for that night is also not confirmed. Check the Santiago Metro website before the show, because a 21:00 start may end close to closing time.

What Comes Next

After the Jack Johnson Santiago night, the city’s concert calendar stays busy, including Jay Wheeler on Saturday 22 May 2027. Rock fans can also read our guide to Slipknot at the Estadio Nacional.

If a short trip turns into a longer stay, see how to get residency in Chile. It is worth reading the rules before you book a long stay.

More: Chile news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Jack Johnson concert in Santiago?

The Jack Johnson Santiago concert is on Wednesday 10 February 2027 at the arena in Parque O’Higgins. Puntoticket lists the start at 21:00.

How much are Jack Johnson tickets in Chile, and where do I buy them?

Puntoticket, the official seller, lists tickets from 42,600 pesos (about US$43) to 111,600 pesos (about US$114), fees included. Check Puntoticket for availability, since what is still on sale is not confirmed.

Do US citizens need a visa to see the show in Santiago?

No, not for tourist stays of up to 90 days, according to the US State Department. Your passport must be valid for the whole stay.

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Wednesday, 21 October, 11:00 a.m. ET · Source: Palver polling institute, TSE registration BR-04612/2026

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What happened On Wednesday 21 October, the Palver polling institute published an online runoff survey showing a technical tie.

The numbers Flávio Bolsonaro has 50% and Lula 48%, which works out to about 51% to 49% of valid votes, with a 2.4-point margin of error.

The change Palver’s previous survey, published on 15 October, had Flávio at 50% and Lula at 49%.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 78% chance of winning the 25 October runoff (21 October, 10:58 a.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 78% and Kalshi at 79% (Lula: 23% and 23% ), as of 21 October, 11:00 am ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Brazilian polling institute Palver says Flávio Bolsonaro leads President Lula by 50% to 48% in its new runoff survey, a technical tie. Palver published the results on Wednesday 21 October, four days before the Brazil election 2026 vote.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 51.0 %, Lula 49.0 % 31 national polls from 18 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

The survey was taken online and adds to the Brazil election polls that show a race inside the margin of error. Flávio is a senator for Rio de Janeiro and the conservative candidate, while Lula leads the left-wing Workers’ Party.

What the Palver Poll Found

Palver interviewed 5,000 voters online between 18 and 20 October, Exame reported. The institute paid for the survey itself, and the margin of error is 2.4 points at a 95% confidence level.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Flávio Bolsonaro has 50% and Lula has 48%, with 1% blank, null or not voting and no undecided voters, according to Terra. Leaving out blank answers, our calculation puts the split near 51% to 49% in Flávio’s favour.

The survey is registered with the electoral court (TSE) as BR-04612/2026, Congresso em Foco noted. The 15 October Palver survey had Flávio at 50% and Lula at 49%, so Lula slipped one point.

Why an Online Poll Is Different

Palver recruited its respondents through social media advertising, not by phone or in person. Statisticians call this a non-probabilistic sample, meaning not every voter had an equal chance of being asked.

That is why such polls are read with more caution than in-person surveys. The stated margin of error is the institute’s own estimate, and a two-point gap sits inside it.

How It Compares With Other Polls

Datafolha, a major pollster linked to the newspaper Folha de S.Paulo, had Flávio at 51% and Lula at 49% of valid votes on 15 October, as we reported in our earlier poll report. Quaest, another leading institute, published a survey on 21 October with Flávio at 45% and Lula at 44%.

All three surveys point the same way: a one- to two-point gap that no pollster can separate from chance. The race has no clear leader with four days left.

What It Means for US Readers

If you hold Brazilian stocks, bonds or US-listed shares of Brazilian companies, a race this close can bring sharp price swings until the result is known. The winner will also set Brazil’s course on trade and diplomacy with Washington for the next four years.

Treat one online survey as a single data point. The Brazil runoff poll tracker lists every pollster side by side so you can compare methods.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, traders give Flávio Bolsonaro about a 78% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula about 22% (21 October, 10:58 a.m. ET). The market has seen about US$190 million in trades, and prices from Kalshi, a market regulated in the US by the CFTC, are on our Brazil election odds page.

Prices are bets, not polls, and they can move within minutes of new surveys. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

The survey does not say which undecided or wavering voters will turn out on 25 October, or which way they will go. Because respondents joined online, it is also unclear how well they mirror all Brazilian voters.

Any poll measures opinion during its fieldwork days and does not forecast the result. Official results come only from the TSE.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who leads Brazil’s latest runoff poll from Palver?

Flávio Bolsonaro leads with 50% against 48% for Lula, a technical tie. Palver published the survey on Wednesday 21 October.

What is the margin of error in the Palver poll?

The margin of error is 2.4 percentage points at a 95% confidence level. A two-point gap sits inside it.

How was the Palver poll conducted?

Palver surveyed 5,000 voters online between 18 and 20 October. Respondents were recruited through social media, so the sample is not random.

How did the Palver poll change from last week?

On 15 October, Palver had Flávio at 50% and Lula at 49%. Flávio held steady while Lula slipped one point.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October, four days after this poll was published. The winner takes office as president for a four-year term.

World.title: Mexico Retail Sales Rise 1.2% in August
World.content:
Rio Times Markets · Mexico

Key Facts —Who. INEGI, Mexico’s statistics agency, counts monthly sales at shops, supermarkets and online stores. —What. Retail sales rose 1.2% in August from July, four times the 0.3% that analysts expected. —Year on year. Sales were 3.3% above August 2025, against a forecast of 2.0%. —Why it matters. Strong spending gives Mexico’s central bank less reason to cut its 6.50% interest rate. —What to watch. Inflation data for early October are due on Thursday 22 October at 12:00 UTC. —Prediction markets. Polymarket prices no Banxico change in November at 68.5%, a cut at 30.1%; Kalshi 61% and 35% (10:33 a.m. ET). —Power Index. Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index, with 71.4 points (October 2026 edition).

Mexican shoppers spent more in August than analysts expected, which gives the central bank one more reason to keep its interest rate at 6.50%.

Mexico’s retail sales rose 1.2% in August from July, four times the 0.3% that analysts expected, the statistics agency INEGI reported on Wednesday 21 October 2026. Compared with August 2025, sales were 3.3% higher, against a forecast of 2.0%.

The data matter to US readers because a stronger Mexican shopper leaves the central bank less room to cut interest rates, and rates drive the peso and Mexican bonds. They also give an early guide to household spending in Mexico.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 with 71.4 points. Strongest pillar: economic relationships (90); weakest: state capacity & security (46). Alignment group: Hedging. Watch21 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.7 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What INEGI Reported

INEGI measures the real income of retail companies, which means their sales revenue after removing the effect of inflation. The monthly figure of 1.2% is seasonally adjusted, a method that smooths out regular calendar swings such as holidays.

The rise followed two small falls. Income fell 0.2% in June and 0.1% in July.

The yearly rate of 3.3% compares August 2026 with August 2025, and it is up from 1.8% in July. Forecasters in the RT economic calendar had expected 2.0%.

A strong month after two weak ones is good news, but it is still only one month. The forecasts quoted here are the consensus in the RT economic calendar.

A stall at the Coyoacán market in Mexico City, photographed in 2019. File photo. (Photo: EmilioMV11, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

We send a confirmation link first, and the same address then receives The Rio Times Brief, our daily briefing. Unsubscribe with one click at any time; see our privacy policy. Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

Online Sales and Health Products Led

Among product groups, online, catalogue and television sales grew fastest, up 17.6% from a year earlier. Health-care products followed with 9.3%.

Hardware, paint and glass rose 8.3%, and household appliances, computers and decor rose 6.2%. Clothing, footwear and accessories gained 5.6%.

These annual rates are INEGI figures as relayed by the broker XTB and trading-data services. They show that growth was broad, not limited to one kind of shop.

In Plain English INEGI. Mexico’s national statistics agency. Real income. Sales revenue after removing the effect of inflation. Seasonally adjusted. Smoothed for regular calendar swings. Banxico. Mexico’s central bank, formally the Banco de México.

What It Means for Interest Rates

Banxico held its target interest rate at 6.50% on Thursday 24 September 2026, its third hold in a row. The minutes of that meeting, published on 8 October and reported by El Financiero, showed three of five members saying a cut could be discussed, while the others urged caution.

Strong retail sales lean against a cut, since steady demand can keep inflation from falling. Retail data are only one input, and inflation figures and US interest rates weigh more on the peso and on Banxico.

Inflation stood at 3.45% a year in September, with core inflation, which leaves out volatile prices, at 3.75%. The next reading covers the first half of October and is due on Thursday 22 October at 12:00 UTC (8:00 a.m. New York time).

The RT economic calendar shows forecasts of 3.6% for headline inflation and 3.7% for core, against 3.42% and 3.79% in the first half of September. Those are forecasts, not results.

What to Watch Thursday 22 October, 12:00 UTC. Mexico’s inflation for the first half of October (forecast: 3.6%). Thursday 5 November, 19:00 UTC. Banxico’s next interest-rate decision. November. INEGI’s retail survey for September.

The Peso Weakens on the Day

The dollar traded above 18.5 pesos on Wednesday, against 18.43 at Tuesday’s close, according to RT market data. One peso is worth about US$0.054 at that rate.

The broker XTB names the risk of higher US interest rates as the main pressure on the peso. It is not possible to separate the effect of the data from other news on the day.

The US dollar in Mexican pesos, daily, May to 21 October 2026. (Chart: The Rio Times)

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket is a platform where users trade contracts on real events, and its market on Banxico’s November decision has US$85,241 traded. As of 10:33 a.m. ET on 21 October 2026, traders price no change at 68.5% and a 25-basis-point (0.25 percentage point) cut at 30.1%.

Kalshi, regulated in the US by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), shows no change at 61% and a 25-basis-point cut at 35% (42,450 contracts traded). Each outcome is quoted separately, so Kalshi’s prices do not add up to exactly 100%, and all these prices are bets, not polls.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

For US investors in Mexican stocks, bonds or the peso, the data point to firm consumer spending and a central bank in no hurry to cut. Companies that sell to Mexican shoppers, such as Walmart de México, which the US retailer Walmart controls, operate in a market that is still growing.

For residents and visitors, inflation of 3.45% means everyday prices are rising at a moderate pace. At about 18.5 pesos per dollar, US$100 buys roughly 1,850 pesos.

What Is Not Known

Details on retail jobs and pay in the August survey are not covered here, and it is not yet clear whether the rebound will last. The September survey, due in November, will show whether August was a turning point or a one-off.

What supports spending is inflation of 3.45%, a moderate level that does not quickly eat into household budgets. What could reverse it is a weaker peso that lifts import prices, and a central bank that stays at 6.50% for longer.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much did Mexico’s retail sales grow in August 2026?

Mexico’s retail sales rose 1.2% from July, seasonally adjusted, and 3.3% from August 2025, the statistics agency INEGI reported on 21 October 2026. Forecasters had expected 0.3% and 2.0%.

What does the retail sales figure measure?

It measures the real income of retail companies, which means their sales revenue after removing the effect of inflation. It covers retail businesses such as shops, supermarkets and online stores.

Will Banxico cut interest rates after this data?

The data lean against a cut, but retail figures are only one input. Banxico held its rate at 6.50% on 24 September 2026, and its next decision is on 5 November.

What do prediction markets say about the November rate decision?

On Polymarket, traders price no change at 68.5% and a 25-basis-point cut at 30.1%, while Kalshi shows 61% and 35%. These prices are bets, not polls.

What does this mean for the Mexican peso?

Strong spending can support the peso by reducing the chance of rate cuts. On the day, however, the peso weakened, and the broker XTB names the risk of higher US interest rates as the main pressure.

World.title: Why Britain Keeps Changing Prime Ministers
World.content:
EUROPE’S POLITICAL CRISIS · BRITAIN

Britain has had six prime ministers since the 2016 Brexit vote, and the latest change shows both the revolt against the old parties and their way back.

Andy Burnham became Britain’s prime minister on 20 July 2026, after Keir Starmer resigned as Labour leader under pressure from his own MPs. He is the sixth person to take the job since the Brexit referendum of 2016, and the fifth to arrive without first winning a general election as leader.

For Americans the churn matters because Britain is Washington’s closest ally, a nuclear power and one of the world’s largest financial centres. It is also the clearest test in Europe of whether an old party can win back voters who drifted to an insurgent.

Key Facts — New leader Andy Burnham, Greater Manchester’s former mayor, became prime minister on 20 July 2026.

— How He was elected Labour leader unopposed after Keir Starmer announced his resignation on 22 June.

— The revolt In March 2026 Reform UK led YouGov’s poll on 25%; Labour was tied third on 17%.

— The recovery On 18 and 19 October YouGov had Labour 27%, Conservatives 23%, Reform 22%.

— Next vote The next general election is due by 2029; no date has been set.

— Prediction markets Kalshi: Labour 38% and Reform 37%, roughly level, to win the next general election (21 October, 10:27 a.m. ET).

In Plain English Labour Britain’s main centre-left party, in government since July 2024.

Britain’s main centre-left party, in government since July 2024. Conservatives The main centre-right party, in power from 2010 to 2024.

The main centre-right party, in power from 2010 to 2024. Reform UK Nigel Farage’s anti-immigration party, which won five seats in 2024.

Nigel Farage’s anti-immigration party, which won five seats in 2024. Plaid Cymru The Welsh nationalist party, now the largest in the Welsh parliament.

The Welsh nationalist party, now the largest in the Welsh parliament. By-election A one-off vote to fill a single vacant seat in Parliament.

Six Prime Ministers in Ten Years

Theresa May, 2016 to 2019 Conservative; took over after the Brexit vote.

Conservative; took over after the Brexit vote. Boris Johnson, 2019 to 2022 Conservative; won the 2019 election.

Conservative; won the 2019 election. Liz Truss, 2022 Conservative; resigned within two months.

Conservative; resigned within two months. Rishi Sunak, 2022 to 2024 Conservative; lost the 2024 election.

Conservative; lost the 2024 election. Keir Starmer, 2024 to 2026 Labour; won the 2024 election by a landslide.

Labour; won the 2024 election by a landslide. Andy Burnham, since 20 July 2026 Labour; elected party leader unopposed.

File photo: the Palace of Westminster, seat of the British Parliament. (Photo: Christian David, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)
