A Landslide Built on a Third of the Vote

Labour won 411 of 650 seats in July 2024 with about a third of the vote, because Britain’s first-past-the-post system rewards the party that comes first in each seat. Reform UK won about one vote in seven but only five seats.

That gap between votes and seats fed Reform’s complaint that the system shuts out its voters. By mid-March 2026 YouGov had Reform on 25%, the Greens on 19%, and Labour and the Conservatives tied on 17%.

The May Elections and Wales

The local and devolved elections of 7 May 2026 turned the polls into seats. In Wales, where Labour had led every government since devolution in 1999, Plaid Cymru won 43 of the Senedd’s 96 seats, Reform 34 and Labour only 9.

File photo: the Senedd, the Welsh parliament, in Cardiff Bay, where Labour fell to nine of 96 seats in May 2026. (Photo: Rosser1954, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Welsh Labour’s leader and first minister, Eluned Morgan, lost her own seat. Plaid Cymru’s Rhun ap Iorwerth became first minister at the head of a minority government.

How Starmer Fell and Burnham Rose

Burnham, who had spent nine years as mayor of Greater Manchester, won a seat in Parliament at the Makerfield by-election. On 22 June 2026 Starmer announced outside Downing Street that he would resign as Labour leader.

“I have heard the answer of my parliamentary party to that question, and I accept that answer with good grace.”Keir Starmer, Downing Street, 22 June 2026

When nominations closed in July, Burnham was the only candidate, and Labour declared him leader on 17 July. He became prime minister three days later, on 20 July 2026.

File photo: 10 Downing Street, the office of the British prime minister. (Photo: Peter McDermott, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

The Argument: No Mandate

Nigel Farage, Reform’s leader, demanded an immediate general election in July, saying Burnham had no mandate for power. His argument fits the wider European complaint: the establishment changes its leaders inside the party while voters who want a different party wait years for a say.

British law supports the government on the procedure. A prime minister needs the confidence of the House of Commons, not a personal election, and the next general election is due by 2029.

The Counter-Evidence: Labour’s Recovery

Since the change at the top, Labour has climbed back. YouGov had Reform and Labour tied on 22% in late July, and on 18 and 19 October Labour on 27%, the Conservatives on 23% and Reform on 22%.

In YouGov’s poll of 11 and 12 October, Reform’s 21% was its joint-lowest of this parliament. In our reading, Britain is therefore Europe’s clearest counter-example to the idea that voters, once lost to an insurgent, never come back.

The recovery is fragile, though. The three leading parties are within five points of each other, and a Pew Research Center survey this spring found 51% of Britons dissatisfied with how their democracy works.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Kalshi, regulated in the US by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, traders give Labour a 38% chance and Reform 37% of winning the next general election, with the Conservatives on 21%. More than 261,000 contracts have been traded on that question, as of 21 October at 10:27 a.m. ET.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for Americans

A stable Britain matters to Washington on defence, intelligence and trade, and frequent changes at the top make long-term deals harder. A Reform victory, which the markets now price at roughly one in three, would put an anti-immigration party in charge of a G7 economy.

For investors, political churn has already cost Britain once, when markets turned on Liz Truss’s 2022 budget plans. Any sign of fiscal drift under a new leader is watched closely in the bond market.

What Is Not Known

Nobody knows when Burnham will call an election, and he does not have to before 2029. It is also unclear whether Labour’s recovery will survive his first budget.

Britain is one of five countries in our explainer on why Europe’s politics are breaking. For the opposite approach to an insurgent party, see why Germany’s top party in the polls is kept out of power.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is the prime minister of Britain now?

Andy Burnham of the Labour Party became prime minister on 20 July 2026. He replaced Keir Starmer, who announced on 22 June that he would resign as Labour leader.

Why did Keir Starmer resign?

His MPs withdrew their support after Labour’s heavy losses in the May 2026 elections. He said he accepted their verdict with good grace.

Did Andy Burnham win an election to become prime minister?

No general election was held. He was elected Labour leader unopposed in July, and a prime minister needs the confidence of the House of Commons, not a separate vote.

When is the next UK general election?

It must be held by 2029, and no date has been set. Reform UK’s Nigel Farage has demanded an immediate election.

Is Reform UK ahead in the polls?

Not in the latest YouGov poll. On 18 and 19 October Labour had 27%, the Conservatives 23% and Reform 22%, after Reform had led YouGov’s poll in March 2026.

More: Why Europe’s politics are breaking, our guide to the crisis from France and Spain to Germany, Romania and Britain.

World.title: Ukraine Peace Talk Odds Jump to 64%
World.content:
File photo: the Kremlin in Moscow at night.

RUSSIA · UKRAINE · PREDICTION MARKETS

Key Facts — Prediction markets Polymarket: talks by 31 December 64%, up 27 points in 24 hours (21 October, 10:31 a.m. ET).

— Trigger On 21 October Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff and agreed in principle to resume talks after 10 November.

— Next date Talks could restart after 10 November; no venue has been announced.

— Near term The same market gives talks by 31 October only 7.1%, down 4.5 points.

— Volume About US$1.74 million traded in all; about US$110,000 in the past 24 hours.

Traders now bet that Russia and Ukraine will sit down for peace talks before the year ends, after the Kremlin said it would resume negotiations.

Polymarket traders now put the chance of new Russia-Ukraine peace talks by 31 December at 64%, up 27 points in 24 hours. Our report of 17 October put the same market at 36%, so the price has swung back sharply in four days.

It matters to US readers because any talks involve the US directly. Washington is the mediator, and sanctions, military aid and energy prices all depend on whether the war moves toward a deal.

In plain English Trilateral talks means three-way negotiations between the US, Russia and Ukraine. A prediction market is an exchange where people bet real money on events, and the price shows the crowd’s implied chance. Witkoff is Steve Witkoff, President Donald Trump’s special envoy for the war.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a crypto-based exchange, lists the question “Russia x Ukraine peace talks by…?” with one contract for each date. Each contract pays out if the two sides hold peace talks by that date.

31 December: 64%, up 27 points in 24 hours and 17.5 points in a week; about US$27,900 traded in 24 hours, so this line is thinly traded.

64%, up 27 points in 24 hours and 17.5 points in a week; about US$27,900 traded in 24 hours, so this line is thinly traded. 30 November: 55.5%, up 25 points in 24 hours and 21 points in a week; about US$37,200 traded.

55.5%, up 25 points in 24 hours and 21 points in a week; about US$37,200 traded. 31 October: 7.1%, down 4.5 points in 24 hours and 7.5 points in a week; about US$44,700 traded.

Across all contracts on the question, about US$1.74 million has traded, including about US$110,000 in the past 24 hours. Individual lines trade only tens of thousands of dollars a day, so a few large orders can move the price, and it moved several points while we were checking it. Kalshi, which is regulated in the US by the CFTC, did not list a contract on peace talks by a date when we looked; its nearest contracts ask whether Zelenskyy and Putin will meet.

The price is a bet, not a poll and not a forecast by this newsroom. You can follow live prices on our Prediction Markets page.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why the Odds Moved

The timing fits one event. On 21 October, Putin met Witkoff for about three hours at the Konstantin Palace in Strelnya, outside St Petersburg, according to the Associated Press. Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov said Putin agreed “in principle” to resume trilateral talks after 10 November.

Ushakov said the talks would focus on “building a security system for Russia and Ukraine after the conflict ends.” Kirill Dmitriev, Russia’s presidential envoy, joined the meeting, and Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner took part by video link, the AP reported.

The visit had been signalled a day earlier. The Kyiv Independent reported on 20 October that Witkoff would travel to St Petersburg after speaking with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, citing Norway’s prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre.

Kyiv has not signed on to a date. Zelenskyy said that only a summit of leaders can break the impasse and that freezing the fighting is the minimum step, according to the AP.

Context matters here. Three rounds of US-Russia-Ukraine talks were held earlier this year, in Abu Dhabi in January and February and in Geneva on 17 and 18 February. We found no later round.

Traders have not said what moved them, so the link between the meeting and the price is our reading, not a claim from any source. The 31 October contract fell at the same time, which suggests traders read the “after 10 November” wording as ruling out talks this month.

What It Means for US Readers

The first link is diplomacy. Washington is the go-between, since Trump’s envoy met Putin in person, so a date for talks is a test of US mediation.

The second is sanctions and money. Our reporting on the EU’s frozen Russian assets and the US$78 billion Ukraine funding gap shows how much Ukraine’s budget depends on Western decisions that talks could change.

For investors, our analysis is that energy, defence and European shares often react to peace headlines. A 64% price for talks is a bet on a meeting, not on a deal, and the same market shows how fast it can reverse.

What It Means for Latin America and Africa

Our analysis, not a claim from the sources: the main channel is energy. Latin American buyers of Russian fuel were left exposed by a US sanctions waiver, as we reported in Russia Sanctions Waiver Leaves Latin American Buyers Exposed, and any shift in sanctions would reach them first.

Latin America’s gas exporters also have a stake. Europe’s plan to end Russian gas is the opening described in Can Latin America LNG Replace Russian Gas in Europe?, and a peace track could change how fast that demand grows.

For African importers of wheat and fertiliser, the effect would come through grain and fuel prices. We have no market data on that link today, so we do not put a number on it. See our Latin America odds page and Africa odds page for regional markets.

What Is Not Known

It is not known where or when the talks would be held. Ushakov gave only “after 10 November,” and no venue has been announced.

It is not known whether Kyiv will attend on Moscow’s terms. Zelenskyy has called for a leaders’ summit and a freeze, and the AP report does not say that Ukraine accepted the Kremlin’s framework.

It is also not known what a meeting would produce. The three rounds held earlier this year did not end the war, and individual lines in the market trade only tens of thousands of dollars a day.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are prediction markets saying about Russia-Ukraine peace talks?

Polymarket prices new talks by 31 December at 64% as of 21 October, 10:31 a.m. ET, up 27 points in 24 hours. It prices talks by 31 October at 7.1%.

Why did the odds jump on 21 October?

Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff that day and agreed in principle to resume trilateral talks after 10 November, according to Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov. Traders have not said what moved them.

What are trilateral talks?

They are negotiations between the US, Russia and Ukraine. Three rounds were held earlier in 2026, in Abu Dhabi and Geneva, and we found no later round.

Has Ukraine agreed to the new talks?

Not publicly, as far as we could confirm. President Zelenskyy has said a leaders’ summit is needed and that freezing the fighting is the minimum step.

Does a market price mean talks will happen?

No. Prediction market prices are bets by traders, not forecasts by this newsroom or any government, and they can reverse as news arrives.

World.title: Drone Strike on Border Market Kills 153
World.content:
Sudan War · Breaking

Published Wednesday, 21 October, 10:26 am ET (4:26 pm Port Sudan) · Source: Abyei administration via AP and Reuters

A drone strike on a fuel market in the disputed border region of Abyei has killed at least 153 people, a local official says.

Key Facts —What happened. A drone strike hit Amiet Market on Monday, 19 October 2026, about 11 a.m. local (5 a.m. ET). —Who says so. Abyei’s caretaker information minister put the toll at 153, up from 73. —Who is blamed. Abyei officials blame Sudan’s army. An army officer says it hit fuel tankers. —What is next. Recovery of bodies is continuing, and the toll may rise further. —Prediction markets. Polymarket puts a Sudan ceasefire by 31 December 2026 at 8%, as of 10:24 a.m. ET, 21 October (4:24 p.m. Port Sudan).

This story is part of our coverage of the sudan war. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Where Sudan's Refugees Have Gone, Country by Country

In plain English Sudan’s army and a paramilitary group, the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), have been at war since April 2023. Abyei is a small oil-rich area that both Sudan and South Sudan claim, so a strike there can pull in a second country.

Abyei officials say at least 153 people died in a drone strike on Amiet Market on Monday, 19 October 2026, around 11 a.m. local time (5 a.m. ET). The toll rose from 73 reported the same day, according to Yohanna Akol Ngor, the caretaker information minister of the Abyei administration, speaking to the Associated Press and Reuters.

The attack is part of the Sudan war, which has spread into the border regions. We reported the first count of 73 on Monday.

What We Know

Ngor said the death toll “was continuing to rise as the fire burned,” according to the Associated Press. The market sits north of Abyei town, and South Sudan’s foreign ministry summoned Sudan’s ambassador to protest the attack.

Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said it was treating more than 20 wounded at Ameth Bek Hospital. Several were in critical condition, and some had burns.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Is Blamed

Abyei officials blame the Sudanese Armed Forces, the national army led by General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan. An unnamed senior Sudanese officer told the Associated Press the army struck “fuel tankers arriving from South Sudan” that he said were bound for the Rapid Support Forces.

The officer added, “We do not target civilians.” Three diplomatic sources, an aid worker and a conflict expert told Reuters the strike hit a fuel depot in the market that the RSF had used before.

Why Abyei Matters

Abyei is an oil-rich area on the border between Sudan and South Sudan. Both countries have claimed it since South Sudan became independent in 2011.

It borders Kordofan, now a major front in the war, and Reuters reported that recent drone strikes have pushed total deaths past 250. Our Sudan war news hub tracks each development.

What Prediction Markets Say On Polymarket, traders priced “Yes” on a Sudan civil war ceasefire by 31 December 2026 at 8 cents, an implied probability of 8%. That contract had about US$15,000 in trading volume as of 10:24 a.m. ET on 21 October 2026 (4:24 p.m. Port Sudan). Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

The attack hit a fuel supply route, and fuel is what keeps drones, trucks and aid convoys moving in this war. American donors and aid groups working in the region face a more dangerous operating picture as strikes move toward border trade hubs.

A dispute over who controls Abyei also gives South Sudan a direct stake in the fighting next door, and it has already summoned Sudan’s ambassador.

What Is Not Known

The toll is an official’s claim and has not been independently verified. Eye Radio and Sudans Post report Ngor later citing more than 220 dead, a figure we could not confirm independently, and it is unclear how many of the dead were civilians, and the army has not said publicly what it targeted.

Recovery work is still under way, so the final number is likely to change. We will update this report when official counts change.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people died in the Abyei market strike?

Abyei’s caretaker information minister, Yohanna Akol Ngor, said at least 153 people died, up from 73 earlier. He said the count was still rising as fires burned. Eye Radio reports he later cited more than 220. Neither figure is independently verified.

Who carried out the strike?

Abyei officials accuse the Sudanese army. An unnamed senior Sudanese officer told the Associated Press the army struck fuel tankers bound for the Rapid Support Forces and said, “We do not target civilians.” The army has not issued a public statement.

Where is Abyei and why is it disputed?

Abyei is an oil-rich region on the border between Sudan and South Sudan. Both countries have claimed it since South Sudan became independent in 2011.

What are Rapid Support Forces?

The Rapid Support Forces (RSF) are a paramilitary group fighting Sudan’s army in a war that began in April 2023. They hold large areas of western Sudan.

What do prediction markets say about a Sudan ceasefire?

On Polymarket, traders priced a ceasefire by 31 December 2026 at 8% on 21 October 2026. That is a bet, not a poll or a forecast by experts.

Sources: Associated Press; Reuters; Doctors Without Borders (MSF); Polymarket; The National; Eye Radio; Sudans Post.

World.title: Why Romania’s Court Cancelled a Presidential Election
World.content:
EUROPE’S POLITICAL CRISIS · ROMANIA

In December 2024 Romania’s top court cancelled a presidential election won in its first round by an outsider, and the country is still arguing about it.

Romania’s Constitutional Court annulled the country’s presidential election on 6 December 2024, two days before the runoff, after declassified intelligence reports alleged a hidden online campaign for the first-round winner, Călin Georgescu. The vote was rerun in May 2025 without him, and the centrist mayor of Bucharest, Nicușor Dan, won.

For Americans the case matters because it became a flashpoint between Washington and Europe, and because Romania is a NATO member on the border with Ukraine. It is also a rare example of a court changing who could compete for power in an EU country.

Key Facts — What happened The Constitutional Court annulled the whole 2024 presidential election on 6 December 2024.

— Why It cited intelligence reports alleging online manipulation and undeclared campaign funding.

— The outsider First-round winner Călin Georgescu was barred from the 2025 rerun.

— The rerun Nicușor Dan beat the nationalist George Simion by 53.6% to 46.4% in May 2025.

— The money Romania ran the EU’s largest budget deficit in 2025, 7.8% of GDP.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives a 2.4% chance that President Dan leaves office in 2026 (21 October, 10:16 a.m. ET).

In Plain English Constitutional Court (CCR) Romania’s court for constitutional questions, which also validates presidential elections.

Romania’s court for constitutional questions, which also validates presidential elections. Central Electoral Bureau (BEC) The body that registers candidates and counts the national vote.

The body that registers candidates and counts the national vote. Călin Georgescu A little-known nationalist outsider who won the first round in November 2024.

A little-known nationalist outsider who won the first round in November 2024. George Simion Leader of the nationalist AUR party, the runner-up in May 2025.

Leader of the nationalist AUR party, the runner-up in May 2025. Nicușor Dan The former mayor of Bucharest, a centrist independent, president since May 2025.

What Happened, Step by Step

24 November 2024 Georgescu, who had averaged about 5% in polls, wins the first round with about 23%.

Georgescu, who had averaged about 5% in polls, wins the first round with about 23%. 4 December 2024 Intelligence reports on the campaign are declassified.

Intelligence reports on the campaign are declassified. 6 December 2024 The Constitutional Court unanimously annuls the whole election, two days before the runoff set for 8 December.

The Constitutional Court unanimously annuls the whole election, two days before the runoff set for 8 December. December 2024 The European Commission opens formal proceedings against TikTok over election risks in Romania.

The European Commission opens formal proceedings against TikTok over election risks in Romania. March 2025 The European Court of Human Rights rejects Georgescu’s complaint; the electoral bureau then bars him from the rerun.

The European Court of Human Rights rejects Georgescu’s complaint; the electoral bureau then bars him from the rerun. 4 and 18 May 2025 Simion leads the first round with 40.96%; Dan wins the runoff with 53.6%.

Simion leads the first round with 40.96%; Dan wins the runoff with 53.6%. 22 May 2025 The Constitutional Court unanimously rejects Simion’s request to annul the result.

What the Court Said

In its ruling number 32 of 6 December 2024, the court said the electoral process had been marred at every stage by multiple irregularities and breaches of electoral law. It pointed to voter manipulation through aggressive, non-transparent promotion on social media, and to campaign funding from undeclared sources.

The ruling never names Georgescu and refers only to “one of the candidates”, who had declared a campaign budget of zero. It annulled the whole process, including votes already cast abroad in the runoff, and kept the sitting president in office until a successor was sworn in.

Călin Georgescu (front) and George Simion at a polling station on 4 May 2025, the day of the first round of the rerun. (Photo: AUR Alianța pentru Unirea Românilor, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Why Georgescu Was Barred

When Georgescu tried to stand again, the Central Electoral Bureau rejected his candidacy on 9 March 2025. It said he had breached the duty to defend democracy that applies to every candidate, and the Constitutional Court rejected his challenge days later.
