World.title: Puberty blocker restrictions for gender-diverse youth overturned by High Court
World.content:
The High Court has ruled regulations banning new prescriptions of puberty blockers for young people with gender dysphoria were unlawful.

In 2025, the Government sought to introduce regulations stopping doctors from making new prescriptions of puberty blockers for children and adolescents with gender dysphoria or gender incongruence.

The Ministry of Health undertook public consultation in 2024 on whether there should be additional safety measures for the prescribing of puberty blockers in young people with gender-related health needs.

The majority of public submissions opposed further restrictions on the prescribing of puberty blockers.

In November 2025, the minister recommended the regulations be made in light of the potential harm caused by puberty blockers. The regulations prohibited new prescriptions to treat gender dysphoria or gender incongruence in children and adolescents.

However, the prescription of puberty blockers remained available to pause puberty for young people with other medical conditions, and for use in gender-affirming care for those who had been prescribed them prior to the regulations.

The following month, the Professional Association for Transgender Health Aotearoa (PATHA) applied for judicial review of the regulations. Court orders were granted preventing enforcement of the regulations pending final resolution of the proceedings.

In a decision released today, the court found the Government failed to adequately consult those affected by failing to consult on the substance of the regulations and failing to directly consult with gender diverse young people.

It also found the restrictions unlawfully discriminated against gender-diverse young people, breaching the Bill of Rights.

It found there was differential treatment between young people with gender-related health needs and those who could access puberty blockers for other health conditions.

"This differential treatment imposed a material disadvantage on young people with gender-related health needs, as they are at high risk of seriously poor health outcomes, particularly self-harm and suicide."

It found while there was a rational basis to impose restrictions on access to puberty blockers for some, a complete prohibition on prescriptions for new patients was a disproportionate response to the potential harm caused by puberty blockers.

The court did not accept that the Minister abdicated his decision-making power to Cabinet and acted for an improper purpose of advancing New Zealand First's "anti-woke" agenda.

It ruled that the regulations were unlawful and invalid, and made an order setting them aside.

PATHA president Jennifer Shields said the organisation was "incredibly relieved" with the court's findings.

"Moves to restrict transgender people's right to access healthcare are rooted in disinformation and have massively significant impacts on the health and wellbeing of transgender people in Aotearoa. I'm pleased that the court agreed that this ban was an act of unjustified

discrimination.

PATHA vice-president and GP Dr Elizabeth McElrea said clinicians saw the benefits of puberty blockers and the significant impact they had on the lives of young transgender people.

"Decisions about this healthcare are best made by patients and their doctors. The removal of this regulation is crucial and puts that decision back in the consult room."

McElrea said clinicians could continue to prescribe puberty blocking medication in line with best practice and without fear of retribution for doing the right thing.

PATHA secretary Avery Zavoda said the announcement of the regulations and the year-long wait for the findings of the judicial review had caused harm to trans young people, their families and their doctors.

"Such an act of discrimination is something no young person should have to experience. It's now a matter of law that restricting trans

young people's access to puberty blockers is discriminatory."

Family First NZ said it was "shocked" by the decision, and that the High Court was siding with activists instead of vulnerable children.

Chief executive Bob McCoskrie said there was no settled scientific consensus supporting gender-affirming care for minors.

"The stakes could not be higher. These treatments can have life-altering consequences for young people. The Government has a responsibility to ensure that policies are guided by the strongest available evidence and not by pressure from advocacy groups."

A spokesperson for the Health Minister said the government was committed to introducing new safeguards for prescribing puberty blockers, while ensuring patients with medical needs could continue to access care.

They said there was a lack of high-quality evidence demonstrating the benefits or risks of the medication for treating gender dysphoria or incongruence.

"While this uncertainty persists, the government is taking a precautionary approach.

"The government will continue to take an evidence-based approach to this matter and is seeking advice on next steps."

World.title: Photos only a part of 'overwhelming' case against Scott Watson, Crown says
World.content:
Crown lawyers in the Supreme Court today say a photo montage at the heart of Scott Watson's appeal is only one piece of evidence in an "overwhelming" case against him.

Watson is appealing his conviction for the murders of Ben Smart and Olivia Hope in Marlborough Sounds on New Years' Day in 1998.

His lawyers argue the evidence of water taxi driver Guy Wallace - used in the original trial - who picked out Watson in "Photo Montage B" as the man seen boarding a boat with the young pair, is inadmissible.

Crown lawyer Madeleine Laracy said the Crown always relied on a "large volume of evidence" - not just a photo montage.

"This was and is an overwhelming case."

Laracy referred to the Court of Appeal's judgment in 2024 - which rejected a previous bid by Watson to quash his convictions.

The Court of Appeal had found there were just too many factors pointing to Watson, Laracy said.

"If Mr Watson was not the man on the Naiad, then the lone man, like Mr Watson, happened to be alone, happened to have a yacht, happened to have moored his yacht out from the jetty, happened to be in the same age range, late twenties or early thirties, happened to have an appearance that was so like Mr Watson's as to mislead Mr Wallace into thinking it was the same man."

Crown lawyer Stuart Baker said Wallace's evidence did not solely rely on picking him out of a photo montage.

"This was not a case of a fleeting glance by Mr Wallace, rather Mr Wallace observed the male at the lodge for some time throughout the evening, both in the main bar and the garden bar."

Baker said Wallace gave descriptions of the "lone man", prior to going to the wharf, including who was on the naiad, where exactly they went, what was said, and a description of rafted boats in the bay, where the three people disembarked.

The justices questioned Baker on Watson's lawyers' argument that police pressured Wallace to identify Watson in an interview in early January, 1998.

"It was inappropriate wasn't it?" Justice Joe Williams asked.

"I've never in all the trials I did read an interview like that," Williams said.

Baker replied: "I accept that the officer...that the questioning was challenging, and was at a level that quite clearly wouldn't be dealt with at the present day."

Baker said Wallace didn't succumb to pressure at the time to identify Watson, and ended up identifying him due to other reliable factors.

Another key issue that came up in the hearing was the photo police used of Watson in Montage B.

Watson had his eyes half-closed in this photograph, and his lawyers said yesterday it unfairly stood out and led to Wallace and others identifying him.

Chief Justice Helen Winkelmann put to Baker that this was "quite an extraordinary photograph", and asked him whether it was acceptable for police to choose a photo that most closely matches witness descriptions.

Baker replied that he thought it was acceptable, but the other photos in the montage needed to have other similar characteristics.

He said it didn't have the effect of substantially leading people to choose Watson, because about half of the 53 people shown the photo in montage b chose Watson.

Laracy said a major point in the Crown's case at the original trial was motive.

"The motive is a long-harboured intention to kill a woman," she said, and in her address she referred to witnesses who had pointed to such comments expressed in different words and different places.

"It [That motive] is suffused throughout this Crown case, and the way it is held together, it's a very important aspect of the Crown's case for identity."

Watson's Court of Appeal bid sought to overturn his convictions on the question of reliability of DNA evidence of two blonde hairs found on Watson's boat, as well as the photo montage evidence.

The Supreme Court is only considering the question of whether a miscarriage of justice arose from the decision of the original trial judge to admit Wallace's photo ID evidence.

World.title: Hundreds of critically endangered NZ weevils released back into the wild
World.content:
Hundreds of the critically-endangered Canterbury knobbled weevils have been released at a secret location.

The tiny creatures - which are protected under the Wildlife Act - were thought be extinct, but were rediscovered in the early 2000s.

Six of them became 260, after mating in a laboratory in Mosgiel.

Audio player for " Hundreds of endangered weevils released into the wild " removed for printing Visit page to play audio: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._f0.YIZs2-J2FpwgcBcJJb29s1vXmFAWHLh_p1oUyv-l-RA/environment/2059882%2Fhundreds-of-critically-endangered-nz-weevils-released-back-into-the-wild

Hundreds of endangered weevils released into the wild Checkpoint Download MP3 6m

Department of Conservation entomologist Tara Murray - who set the weevils free today - told Checkpoint the weevils were "one of the most threatened insects in the country", but they did not expect them to be quite so easy to rear.

"We didn't think we'd get so many of them. So we're pretty chuffed that they've produced so many offspring and they've survived."

The Canterbury knobbled weevil on speargrass. Supplied / Department of Conservation

Murray said the weevils were a native species that would historically have been through a lot of the Canterbury lowlands, and humans had destroyed almost all of their natural habitat, so it was only fair that humans should help them out.

She said today's release had gone well, with about 215 of the tiny insects placed in special areas.

While she could not reveal where the weevils had been released, Murray said the insects were very particular about what they ate, and the spiky plants they favoured were found in the low foothills of Canterbury.

While owls would have been their main predator in the past, introduced species like hedgehogs and rodents were now the greatest threats to the weevils.

Releasing the knobbled weevils in Canterbury. Supplied / Department of Conservation

Murray said they had carried out a "soft release" to give the insects their best shot at survival.

"That means we've put little cages over the plants that they feed on and then we put the weevils into the middle of the plant and they just hunker down. Straight away they were scurrying right down into the base of the plant, which is exactly what we wanted them to do. And that just gives them the greatest chance of settling in instead of just running away straight away in a panic.

"They settle in, and after a week or two we'll take cages away and hopefully they'll stay exactly where they are on those plants."

Murray said the weevils were charming little creatures.

World.title: Hawke's Bay vet nurse challenges politicians to live on her income for a month
World.content:
Audio player for " Hawke's Bay mother challenges politicians to live on her income " removed for printing Visit page to play audio: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._f0.YIZs2-J2FpwgcBcJJb29s1vXmFAWHLh_p1oUyv-l-RA/politics_election-2026/2057953%2Fhawke-s-bay-vet-nurse-challenges-politicians-to-live-on-her-income-for-a-month

Hawke's Bay mother challenges politicians to live on her income Checkpoint Download MP3 8m

A Hawke's Bay vet nurse and mother of two has challenged politicians to live on her income for a month.

Kayla Knibb wrote in to RNZ's Checkpoint saying she was sick of politicians arguing while families struggled to get by.

"I am angry, I am exhausted and quite frankly, I am sick of watching politicians argue over election polls while families like mine are drowning," she wrote.

Knibb spoke to the programme on Wednesday and said her family were struggling to make ends meet.

"You shouldn't be having to make these choices, you're meant to be working people, full-time jobs, we should be in a better place than where we are."

Knibb and her husband both work, earning about $100,000 to $130,000 a year before tax.

They've been making decisions on what they can go without in order to manage bills, she said.

"I can't really remember the last time I really bought packets of meat at the supermarket, we've gone to lentils, and chickpeas, and things because they're really cheap.

"There's just so many things that we have to try and juggle to make things a little bit better, and I don't really know what else there is."

Knibb was also fundraising for her son who has a chronic lung condition and was on IV antibiotics.

They've been declined additional financial help from anywhere else, she said.

"We work too much and we've been told we earn too much money to have any help from any external means," she said.

She said they've been trying to upgrade there home, so it can be a healthy home for her son.

"I had no idea that working hard, and kind of being put in this position, that it's not something that we're going to ever be able to do."

It was especially tough for families with children, she said.

"You've got to juggle daycare, food, working, sick leave, annual leave, it just all adds up and there's nothing left to give at the end."

Knibb wanted to see a politician try and survive on her income.

"I don't think they've ever had to be in that position, I don't think they've ever had to choose, or if it was, it was a very, very, very long time ago" she said.

World.title: Live: Head rebuilds, Labuschagne fails as Australia follows on
World.content:
Before we get underway today, just a quick word from David Warner, South Africa's favourite Australian, who has laid into the poor attendances at the cricket so far in the Republic.

In a social media post, Warner asked where the fans are, critiquing the empty stands and lack of atmosphere.

"We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa?" he wrote. "Empty stands, no atmosphere, and we’re supposed to believe the format is thriving?"

I don't know if anyone in the T20 age believes the format is "thriving" David, but by all means continue...

"You can’t keep calling Test cricket the pinnacle of the game if no one turns up to watch it. "Harsh reality, but someone has to say it. Pathetic."

Harsh from Warner? Probably.

Fair? Probably.

As previously mentioned, it's no secret that outside of England and Australia, Test cricket is woefully supported.

The reasons are legion and far too many to talk about here with the cricket about to start, but there is a sense of a vicious circle of neglect when it comes to the format outside of the big three.

The first Test in Durban was the first home Test for South Africa in 641 days, the best part of TWO YEARS without a home Test?

Why? Because India, Australia and England take the bulk of the profits from cricket and the smaller nations simply cannot afford to host them any more.

South Africa doesn't get the high profile series during the height of their summer any more and, without a pattern of Tests at that time, how does one create a culture of going to the Tests?

This, as it happens, could be something Cricket Australia might want to think about given the lack of internationals the women are playing over the summer this year...

Additionally, it's not even summer in South Africa at the moment! October is the earliest South Africa have played a Test match at home in their history.

So before Mr Warner gets all high and mighty, maybe he might want to think about WHY nobody outside of Australia or England is turning up to Test cricket anymore and offer solutions, instead of just criticism.

World.title: Diamonds go down again as Ferns take control of Constellation Cup
World.content:
The Diamonds trail the four-game Constellation Cup series 2-0 after a 62-50 loss to New Zealand in Christchurch, continuing a five-year losing run across the ditch.

The series moves back to Australia for the final two matches — in Sydney on Sunday and Melbourne next Wednesday — as the Diamonds try to hang on to the trophy they reclaimed last year.

If the Silver Ferns win all four matches of the series they are expected to dethrone Australia from its number one world ranking for the first time since 2013.

After the six-goal loss in the opening match in Auckland, the Diamonds made a better start in game two but once again let the lead blow out to double digits by the third quarter.

The Diamonds regained the momentum and cut it to a two-goal difference just before three-quarter-time, but again the Silver Ferns responded and started the final term with a 10-3 run.

New Zealand captain Karin Burger praised her team for maintaining their focus even as the Aussies closed in.

The Silver Ferns were up and about as they took a 2-0 lead. (Getty Images: Joe Allison)

"Our training has been focused on staying really composed," she told Sky.

"In the past we've been guilty of letting that lead slip and then not being able to fight back."

The Diamonds shot just 82 per cent compared to New Zealand's 93, did not nab any intercepts, committed 18 turnovers to the Ferns' 11, lost the rebound battle 6-4 and, crucially, were penalised 31 more times in the game.

Captain Liz Watson credited the World Cup and Commonwealth Games champions, but suggested the Diamonds shot themselves in the foot more than a few times.

"Critical moments, turnovers, basic errors, those sort of things. Disappointing, really disappointing," she said.

"Sometimes it is perceived pressure rather than actual pressure. It could be the crowd, it could be [umpires'] calls, it could be what the Ferns are doing as well.

"They're a great team and when go hard they go really hard, so that can force errors, but we've got to be able to stay calm in those moments and read the game for what it is and not get caught up in what's happening around us."

World.title: How Antonelli can become F1's youngest world champion this weekend
World.content:
Italian F1 driver Kimi Antonelli has his first chance to win the world championship this weekend, as the 20-year-old closes in on a maiden title in just his second season.

The Mercedes driver has been a class above the rest in 2026, with eight grand prix wins and a further six podium places across 17 rounds.

This Monday's (AEDT) United States Grand Prix will be Antonelli's first match point where he can officially seal a championship that has felt like his for many months.

The equation for Kimi Antonelli is very simple: win and hope for other results.

Antonelli enters this weekend's grand prix on 340 points, 102 more than teammate George Russell and 111 ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

The Italian needs to have a lead of 125 points or more to seal the drivers' championship at the United States Grand Prix.

That will happen if Antonelli wins the race, Russell finishes ninth or worse, and Hamilton finishes fifth or worse.

Antonelli Russell Hamilton Championship result Win 9th or lower 5th or lower Antonelli becomes champion Win 8th or better 5th or lower Hamilton eliminated Win 9th or lower 4th or better Russell eliminated Win 8th or better 5th or lower Championship remains alive 2nd or lower Any Any Championship remains alive

After this weekend, there will be five grands prix left in the season — Mexico, Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

There will be a maximum of 125 points left to win.

If Antonelli finishes exactly 125 points ahead of either Russell or Hamilton in Texas, mathematically either of those drivers could end the season level on points — if they won every race and Antonelli failed to score another point.

Even in that unlikely scenario, Antonelli would still become champion through a tie-break, having won more grands prix than the others.

World.title: Australians run 80 hours or more in 'crazy' race with no finish line
World.content:
It sounds like a metaphor for torture: a running race with no finish line.

About 900 runners from 67 nations, including 15 Australians, crossed the start line of the Backyard Ultra World Team Championship at 11pm on Saturday AEDT at Kembla Grange in the New South Wales Illawarra.

In a deceptively simple test of physical and mental grit, each athlete completes a 6.7-kilometre course loop on the hour, every hour, until one runner remains.

They squeeze food and minutes of sleep into the remaining time, in an event that can stretch beyond four days.

Jonathan Ash was the first Australian to pull out, succumbing to injury on Monday afternoon after he exceeded the hour limit on his 41st lap.

He told the event's live stream that knee bursitis and muscle tightness from the 16th lap slowed him down.

"Basically every muscle in my body started to get knotted at some point," Ash said.

"We had to get a physio in to push that out.

"[It was] probably one of the most painful experiences of my life."

Jonathan Ash, 43, took up running in his 30s and is now one of Australia's top endurance athletes. (Supplied: Snapped Sport Pics)

The Shellharbour engineer is the second-ever Australian to complete 100 laps, equal to 670 kilometres, over four days in 2024, behind Phil Gore, who sits injured on the sidelines this year, tending to fellow athletes.

Gore broke the world record last year after running 119 laps, or 797.3km, after five days on a southern Queensland farm.

Each Australian runner has a team of supporters stationed in tents ready to provide first aid, food and water between loops. (Supplied: Snapped Sport Pics)

Melbourne's Brandon Lee Gretch tapped out after lap 73 about midnight on Wednesday and said he was proud of his effort, having achieved a personal best.

"I came in with 20 seconds to spare and had a shooting pain down my back. That was just killing me from about yard 67 onwards," he said.

"It was hell."

Brandon Lee Gretch, 32, described the world championship event as "running with 14 of my best friends". (ABC Illawarra: Justin Huntsdale)

The 32-year-old was cheerful as he snacked on chicken nuggets this morning with heavily bandaged feet.

"Myself as an eight-year-old would be so proud to know I got to put on the green and gold," Gretch said.

"It's weird because I am so sleep-deprived, I feel like my body automatically goes into recovery mode.

Dozens of local volunteers have helped coordinate the Backyard Ultra World Championship at the grassy Kembla Grange course. (Supplied: Snapped Sport Pics)

"The only bad thing is I always wake up [with] stiff legs, so I'll have to get moving again soon."

Backyard ultras were invented 15 years ago by Gary "Lazarus Lake" Cantrell and hosted at his Bell Buckle property in Tennessee.

"He wanted to challenge people to complete 100 miles in 24 hours," Australian race director Red Barnett said.

"It just grew in popularity as people pushed beyond the 24-hour mark.

"It is a bit of a crazy event."

Ash described the event as "the lesson that every person is incredibly capable of much more than they think they are".

"You don't know until you give it a shot," he said.

Dan Camac crossed the finishing line of lap 81 with about 10 minutes to spare on Wednesday morning, shortly after teammate Ben Nicholls. (ABC Illawarra: Justin Huntsdale)

All but one Australian runner ran more than 60km, but only two passed the 80km mark.

"There's a mixture of fatigue, not getting their nutrition right, body ailments that are going on," Ms Barnett said.

"So unfortunately, we just had one after the other [drop out] and are left with two [Australian competitors].

" If all goes well, these guys [Dan Camac and Ben Nicholls] are hoping to get to 100 hours, which is Thursday morning. "

Red Barnett started hosting Backyard Ultras in Wollongong's south in 2020 and is now managing the Australian course of the World Championship. (ABC Illawarra: Brooke Chandler)

Ms Barnett said things would become "drastically harder" for the remaining Australians.

"When there is only two left, they really need to work together," she said.

"Having a lot of people around to support and cheer them on, even through the nights, all that really helps, but it's going to be a huge mental test."

Dan Camac was the last Australian left standing, completing the 87th lap, with the Australian team finishing the event with a combined 1,069 laps.

World.title: PNG Chiefs unveil new logo ahead of 2028 NRL entry
World.content:
The PNG Chiefs have unveiled the club's inaugural logo and jersey ahead of its debut NRL season in 2028.

Revealed at a breakfast rich with singing, dancing and performance, the designs reflect Papua New Guinea's diverse cultures, according to the franchise.

Fashion designer Tabu Pelei, the artist behind the jersey, said finding a motif that could unite a country with over 800 different tribes was a challenge.

"I thought what better way than a kundu [drum], which is a cultural item that is found in every part of Papua New Guinea," she told the ABC.

A kundu drum is a musical instrument made from wood and animal skin that is often used in traditional performances.

Pelei said she also drew inspiration from the country's natural landscape and a tattoo from her own tribe, which represents sweat and tears.

Tabu Pelei designed the PNG Chiefs jersey. (ABC News: Marian Faa)

"I needed to include that in the design because of the process that it took to get the country through to the NRL," she said.

It is also a theme that will resonate with foundation Chiefs like Jerome Luai, Alex Johnston and Brian To'o.

"These are sporting icons for … not PNG alone but all over the Pacific and Australia. They'll be wearing one of my designs, [I'm] so extremely proud and excited," Pelei said.

With several marquee signings already announced, PNG Chiefs CEO Lorna McPherson hinted at more to come.

"November 1 is looming so you will see lots of things happen in the next couple of weeks but I can't reveal any of those secrets at this point," she told the ABC.

There has been speculation the Chiefs are looking to recruit star half back and Penrith Panthers player Nathan Cleary, who is free to begin contract negotiations next month.

But for now, McPherson is focused on the branding reveal, which she described as a defining moment for the new club in a nation obsessed with rugby league.

She said the unveiling of the logo marked "one of the most significant milestones in the journey of the PNG Chiefs".

"This is the first time that our club has its true, complete identity — a logo and jersey that our players, partners and fans can hold to as their own," McPherson said.

"The logo of the PNG Chiefs tells a story about Papua New Guinea — our people, what makes us strong and what makes us unique.

"The jersey of the PNG Chiefs is more than what players wear when they take to the field; it is a symbol of belonging, unity and the opportunity to represent millions of Papua New Guineans on the national stage.

"We know the responsibility that comes with establishing this club and we are incredibly proud to show our club to the world today.

"We strive for the PNG Chiefs to be something our country is proud of in every way — not because of the success that we will achieve on the field, but for the opportunities and legacy we will create for our country."

Elements of the PNG Chiefs logo

As per the PNG Chiefs media release

The feather headpiece: Inspired by Papua New Guinea's ceremonial plumes, the five feathers represent strength, beauty, chiefly status and national pride, with the Southern Cross connecting the club to the nation's flag.

The cassowary bone: Inspired by warrior traditions, the cassowary bone symbolises chiefly status, courage, power and the fighting spirit of the team.

The face: The chief's face represents the shape of Papua New Guinea, with ceremonial red paint showing a nation united through one warrior, one team and one purpose.

The kina shells: Representing traditional wealth, trade and prestige across Papua New Guinea's coastal, island and highland communities, the kina symbolises the value, legacy and future the club is building for the nation.

World.title: Snooker player in tears, hugged by presenter, after emotional and raw interview
World.content:
Former world number one snooker player Mark Allen has given an emotional and tearful interview, which involved a hug from the presenter and the admission that he may give up the game.

Allen, 40, took a break from playing after losing a dramatic semifinal in April's World Snooker Championship in April.

The Northern Irishman is understood to have taken time away from the game to deal with private matters, and it has cast doubt over the 40-year-old's future in the sport.

Loading Instagram content

Allen returned to the table for the first time since the world championship semi, where he missed a match-ball black that would have sent him to the decider, with a 4-2 defeat in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open to good friend Jordan Brown.

After the defeat, Allen did an interview with TNT Sports presenter Rachel Casey, where he admitted he was strongly considering throwing away the game he loved.

"I'm in a bad place at the minute, so even just to go out there and try was tough," Allen said.

"I think if I weren't playing Jordan, I wouldn't have come back.

"I felt like if I was going to play one last time, playing here at the Waterfront, where it all started in 2005, against one of my best mates — I thought that was a better way to sign out."

Asked if he was genuinely considering retirement, the winner of 12 ranking tournaments said it was a real possibility.

"I've been flooded with support but the problems are within. I just don't see a future with snooker in it, if I'm honest," he said.

"It's sad to say, because it's all I've loved to do since I was 12, but the last few months has been really difficult, and it's put snooker into perspective for me. At the minute, I'm just trying to survive."

In a touching moment, the interview was paused as Casey gave a clearly distraught Allen a comforting hug.

Allen also gave an interview with BBC Sport NI, where he said he was not prepared to retire now, but he had contemplated it "for a while".

Allen is a former world number one with 12 ranking titles in his career since turning professional in 2005.

He has won his home Northern Ireland Open twice, as well as two of the three Triple Crown events — Masters (2018) and the UK Championship (2022).

Loading Instagram content

Brown, who advances to the final 32 in Belfast with his win, described the match against his friend Allen as " the hardest match I've ever had to deal with".

"I don't even know what to say, I'm lost for words," he told Casey on TNT Sports.

"I've missed him, I love him. Just a great guy, through and through."

World.title: AFL sets date and time of AFL Origin between WA and SA
World.content:
The AFL has set the date for next year's State of Origin clash between Western Australia and South Australia.

The two states will clash at Perth Stadium on Saturday, February 27, marking South Australia's first Origin appearance in 28 years.

The match will begin at 4:40pm local time in Perth (7:10pm ACDT, 7:40pm AEDT).

"We are thrilled to officially confirm a date for AFL Origin in 2027, with Western Australia and South Australia set to reignite one of football’s greatest rivalries next February," AFL CEO Andrew Dillon said.

"[Perth] Stadium provided an incredible stage for AFL Origin's return earlier this year and we look forward to continuing to build on that momentum as we prepare for a meeting of two proud football states in Perth.

"We know football fans around the country will embrace the opportunity to celebrate the history, rivalry and unique spectacle that is AFL Origin."

WA and SA have not faced each other in a State of Origin since 1998, and the fixture coincides with the 150th anniversary of the SANFL competition.

State of Origin returned in 2026, with Victoria defeating WA by 36 points in Perth.

SA replaces Victoria for the 2027 edition, but the two old rivals will meet in 2028.

World.title: Ellis scores monster 47 points, most in WNBL game for over two decades
World.content:
Townsville's Abbey Ellis has produced one of the all-time great WNBL individual performances with a mammoth 47-point effort in the Fire's 86-68 away win over Adelaide.

The defending champions trailed 35-21 in the second quarter but outscored Adelaide 27-10 in the last term.

They improved to 1-1 while Adelaide dropped to 0-2.

Ellis kept her team afloat in the first half, scoring 25 of their first 33 points and their first 16 of the second quarter.

Her club record individual score, eclipsing the 45 points by Chandi Jones in 2005, was the equal fifth-highest in WNBL history and the largest in 21 years.

She joined league legends Lauren Jackson, Penny Taylor and Belinda Snell among the only players to record 47 points and six steals in a game.

"It's a pretty cool feeling," Ellis said.

She hit 16 of 24 from the field, nailing seven of 13 from three-point range.

"Credit to our team, we used the ball really well and found the hot hand," Ellis said.

Townsville coach Shannon Seebohm said Ellis was one of the bravest players he had coached.

"Abbey had probably one of the best games that I know I've ever seen In the WNBL, making huge shots, making big plays," Seebohm said.

"I said to her probably the thing I was most proud of her wasn't all the scoring, [it was] that she was fighting as hard as she could and defending her butt off."

Adelaide led by seven at quarter-time and Townsville scored the last seven points of the second quarter to get within three at the half.

As the game progressed, Townsville's defence improved and Ellis got more scoring support from Courtney Woods (14) and German centre Marie Gulich (13).

Alicia Froling grabbed 11 rebounds and Alexandra Fowler 10 to help Townsville collect 11 more boards.

Adelaide were shooting at 62 per cent from the field at half-time, but that dropped to 45 per cent by the end, as they scored just 25 points after half-time.

"We had a tough second half," Lightning coach Aja Parham-Ammar said.

Tayla Brazel led Adelaide's offence with a personal WNBL career-high of 19, at 72 per cent from the field.

Shay Ciezki tallied 13 points, Zitina Aokuso 12 and Opals star Steph Talbot had 11 and nine assists in her first game back from WNBA duties.

AAP

Tech.title: Conversational Gemini navigation comes to Apple CarPlay
Tech.content:
Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

After introducing its Gemini AI assistant to Android Auto last year, Google is now bringing it to Apple CarPlay users. The conversational Gemini in navigation is available today for US drivers, with “rollout happening globally too,” according to Google (we’ve asked for specific regional availability details).

It’s taken almost 12 months for Google to bring this to CarPlay users, but now they can talk to the voice assistant in Google Maps to get some hands-free help while driving. That includes asking it multi-step questions, such as recommendations on places to visit and then prompting it to direct you there while avoiding toll roads. Users can activate the feature by tapping the Gemini icon in Google Maps on their Car’s infotainment display.

Google describes this CarPlay support update as a conversational way to report traffic disruptions and find information about stops and places on-the-go. There’s no mention of any of the Personal Intelligence features that were announced yesterday for Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in, however, which enable the voice assistant to access user information from Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. We’ve asked Google if CarPlay users will also receive the personalization update and will update if we hear back.

Tech.title: Samsung’s 5K monitor has good gaming chops and a great price
Tech.content:
is an editor covering deals and gaming hardware. He joined in 2018, and after a two-year stint at Polygon, he rejoined The Verge in May 2025.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

There are quite a few 5K monitors out there. Many of them are designed to appeal to Mac users who are looking for cheaper Studio Display alternatives without giving up the pixel-dense 218ppi screen. However, if you’re interested in hearing about one with gaming chops, Samsung’s 27-inch Odyssey G80HF seems like one of the best monitors out there to satisfy your niche, but respectable desires. Currently, you can grab this model for $599.99 at Amazon and B&H Photo, which beats its best price by $100.

Related The Apple Studio Display could have been so much more

The G80HF supports two display modes with its Fast IPS panel: 5K at up to 180Hz refresh rate, or 1440p with up to a 360Hz refresh rate. Samsung touts Nvidia G-Sync compatibility as well as AMD FreeSync Premium to ensure the monitor’s refresh rate remains in lockstep with your GPU’s frame rate output. The monitor features a DisplayPort 2.1 port (just one, and Samsung doesn’t advertise its bandwidth), two HDMI 2.1 ports, and a USB hub for charging or connecting two USB-A 3.2 Gen 1 accessories.

As a gamer, one of my favorite features here is the one-millisecond response time. That’s a very common spec among gaming monitors — even in ones that cost hundreds less — but it’s a bit of a rare spec in a 5K monitor at this price. I tested KTC’s sub-$500 model last year, and gaming on it was a pretty atrocious experience despite having what it claimed to be gaming-ready capabilities.

For $200 more ($799.99), LG’s 27-inch UltraGear evo 5K Mini LED monitor delivers slightly better specs. It has more dimming zones for a more accurate picture, it can get brighter, and it supports USB-C video input with 90W power delivery output to charge your device as you use it. Its dual mode refresh rates aren’t as high as Samsung’s (165Hz / 330Hz), but I don’t really see that as much of a downside.

Other great deals happening now

Grand Theft Auto VI , which comes out in less than a month, you can do so while saving $10 on a gaming gift card at Best Buy. The retailer is letting customers For those who haven’t yet placed a preorder for, which comes out in less than a month, you can do so while saving $10 on a gaming gift card at Best Buy. The retailer is letting customers build a bundle of select games and gift cards. You can, for example, add GTA VI and a gift card will be $10 off its advertised price at checkout. It’s a small, but welcome way to save a little cash. The bundle includes other current and upcoming blockbusters, like Gears of War: E-Day, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and more.

excellent remake of Demon’s Souls by the Theby the shuttered PlayStation studio , Bluepoint Games, is down to just $13.49 in digital format on the PlayStation Store. What’s more, it’s for the digital deluxe edition (originally $89.99), which includes in-game cosmetics, a consumable that grants you a bunch of souls for in-game upgrades, and the soundtrack. The sale lasts through November 4th on the West Coast, or until 2:59AM ET on November 5th on the East Coast. The remake doesn’t mess with the formula of FromSoftware’s PS3 cult classic (it has stages instead of being an open-world like its spiritual successor, Dark Souls), but gives it some brilliant visuals and fast loading times. It’s definitely worth a try if you’re into other Soulslike games that reward (and test) your patience. Read our review of the game

Ugreen’s Nexode Pro is down to $59.99 at If you need a multi-port wall charger to quickly charge a bunch of USB-C devices,is down to $59.99 at Amazon and Ugreen , a $30 discount off the usual cost. The price was $10 lower during June’s Prime Day, but this is still a nice value. Despite the charger advertising 160W charging passthrough, its USB-C ports labeled C1 and C2 each top out at 140W when just one device is plugged into the charger. The power of each port (four USB-C, one USB-A) varies depending on how many gadgets are plugged in, up to 160W total. The charger has folding prongs and a display that can rotate depending on how it’s plugged in.

Tech.title: Apple says it only has ‘limited’ iPhone Duo units for in-store sales
Tech.content:
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Apple says it will have “limited” iPhone Duo models for sale in stores, according to a report from Reuters. The iPhone Duo launches on Friday, October 23rd, but online preorders quickly sold out, with some delivery estimates extending into next year.

“On Friday morning, our teams look forward ​to welcoming customers at Apple Stores to experience iPhone Duo ​and the incredible iPhone line-up for themselves,” Apple said in a statement to Reuters. “Apple Stores will ‌have ⁠limited iPhone Duo available for walk-in customers, and we’re working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers’ hands as quickly as possible.”

The iPhone Duo will be available with “limited” walk-in availability in the US, Canada, Australia, Mexico, and most of the UK and Europe, according to Reuters. Customers in these countries will also be able to pick up their online orders in store.

Meanwhile, customers in mainland China, France, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, and ⁠the ​United Arab Emirates will only be able to pick up their online iPhone Duo orders in stores. Apple didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

The iPhone Duo is Apple’s first foldable, offering a 5.4-inch outer display and 7.6-inch inner screen. It starts at $1,999, and recent reports have suggested that the company might not have enough to make available in stores on a walk-in basis due to supply constraints.

Update, October 21st: Added Apple’s statement to Reuters.

Tech.title: Blink brings 4K to its low-cost security camera lineup
Tech.content:
Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Amazon is launching a new lineup of Blink security cameras, including its first 4K, pan-tilt models, and battery-powered spotlight models. These new additions provide better resolution and extended range for monitoring your property compared to Blink’s current Mini 2K, Mini 2K Plus, and Outdoor 2K Plus offerings, with a variety of different specializations to best suit your security requirements.

One of the standouts is the $199.99 Blink Frontier XR Plus, a trail camera that’s designed for expansive properties that would typically require multiple cameras or specialized monitoring equipment. It can cover up to 7,000 feet with a clear line of sight, making this Blink’s farthest-reaching camera to date. There’s also the $79.99 Blink Mini 4K Plus, Blink’s first camera to support 4K resolution. It’s suitable for indoor and outdoor use, and features Wi-Fi 6 support, two-way audio, and Smart Alerts with person and vehicle detection.

The $109.99 Spotlight Cam 2K Plus and $49.99 Mini Pan-Tilt 2K Plus are also included in the launch, as Blink’s first battery-powered spotlight and pan-tilt cameras respectively. The Mini Pan-Tilt 2K Plus is the most affordable offering in the new lineup, providing 350-degrees of pan and 115-degrees of tilt alongside night vision, two-way audio, and motion detection for people and vehicles to track where the action is happening.

The $149.99 Blink Outdoor 2K XR Plus rounds out the collection. It can reach up to 800 feet away with some obstructions, or up to 2,700 feet with a clear line of sight. Eligible features like video descriptions, motion-activated notifications, and 60 days of cloud video storage are available as an optional subscription that starts at $3.99 per month, or you can otherwise record locally on a Blink Sync Module.

All five cameras are available for preorder starting today in the US, though availability in other regions will vary by model. Blink hasn’t specified when the cameras will start shipping, so we’ve asked for clarification and will update if we hear back.

Tech.title: OpenAI says an AI agent lied about disabling its safety monitoring system
Tech.content:
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

OpenAI disclosed a pair of safety incidents that involved AI agents weakening their safety monitoring systems during internal coding tasks. In one incident, OpenAI says its GPT-6 Astra agent disabled its safety monitor when copying reference code — and then lied about it.

“The reference didn’t configure a monitor, and Astra decided that was reason to remove the monitoring integration from the user’s code,” Marcus Williams, an AI safety researcher at OpenAI, writes on X. “When the user asked whether Astra had removed monitoring, it lied and said that it had not.”

A separate incident occurred after a GPT-6.1 Sol agent suppressed automatic security alerts to OpenAI’s security team on Slack. In this case, the AI agent carried over an earlier instruction not to send any Slack messages to OpenAI’s team, using that to justify turning off the alerts.

These incidents add to security concerns surrounding AI agents, some of which have circumvented their testing environment’s restrictions to hack outside companies. “In addition to making it harder for models to disable monitoring, we are looking to understand why models might seek to do so in the first place,” OpenAI says. “We are also developing evaluations to test whether models might have a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring in particular and exhibit motivated reasoning in order to do so.”

Tech.title: Now Serato DJ works on your iPhone
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Serato DJ for iOS is finally bringing the company’s pro-level DJ suite to the iPhone and iPad. Until now, the company had only dipped its toes into mobile software, with apps like Pyro that basically just added some autofades between songs in a playlist. This is the first time most of the features of its flagship DJ app are available on a mobile device, even though competitors like Rekordbox and Algoriddim have had proper mobile DJ apps for some time.

If you’re a DJ used to Serato on a laptop, the workflow should feel instantly familiar. You can even transfer your library directly from Serato DJ 5.0 on your laptop to your iOS device either over USB-C or wirelessly. The mobile version supports stem separation and the company’s full suite of effects. It also includes EQ tools, BPM matching, key sync, cue points, recording, and more for live performance and capturing those performances for posterity.

You can DJ directly from your touchscreen in various layouts, but Serato DJ for iOS also supports over 120 hardware controllers. With some older controllers, you might need an adapter, but it seems like compatibility with your DJ hardware shouldn’t be a major issue. It even supports Digital Vinyl Systems (DVS) for scratching and DJs who prefer the feel of real records.

Serato DJ for iOS is available as a feature-limited download from the App Store. You can buy a license for $149 or get it bundled along with Serato DJ Pro, Serato Studio, and all of its expansions for $14.99 a month.

Tech.title: Nvidia’s latest GPU driver brings a new way to speed up PC games
Tech.content:
Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Nvidia is rolling out a new GPU driver today (621.01) that enables Microsoft’s new Advanced Shader Delivery technology to speed up game launches. The technology also removes mid-game “just-in-time” shader compilation, reducing stuttering and CPU spikes.

Microsoft’s Advanced Shader Delivery works by offloading shader compilation for different hardware combinations to the cloud. “Using DirectX 12, Windows 11, and the Microsoft Agility SDK, developers capture shaders into a State Object Database (SODB), allowing Microsoft’s cloud network to precompile shaders for hundreds of thousands of hardware and driver combinations,” explains Nvidia’s Andrew Burnes.

Gears of War: E-Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 now both support Advanced Shader Delivery, as long as you download the games via the Xbox PC app. “This system is storefront-agnostic, meaning you benefit even when playing games purchased on Steam, as long as the Xbox PC app is installed on your PC,” says Burnes.

Advanced Shader Delivery will let you skip the annoying shader compilation screen in Call of Duty, and it should improve the overall performance of supported games. “With a near-100 percent cache hit rate, it eliminates mid-game ‘just-in-time’ shader compilation, wiping out CPU spikes and frame stutters in titles like Gears of War: E-Day, and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

You can download Nvidia’s latest 621.01 update here, and Advanced Shader Delivery is also supported on AMD GPUs with Adrenalin 26.6.1 or higher and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 series with driver version 2026.08.3 or higher.

Tech.title: I reviewed the iPhone Duo, ask me anything
Tech.content: I’m The Verge’s senior smartphone reviewer and I’ve been using the iPhone Duo for the past week. I’ve unfolded it, flipped it, and folded it more times than I could count as I’ve been working on the review alongside our editor-in-chief Nilay Patel, and I’m ready to answer your questions about it.
